**Validation.** Every `door: true` piece resolves closed and open state art plus its own 4-step swing sprite (variant-matched) at its class rate, and open draws a different frame from closed in every rotation. The step sequence is 1, 2, 3, 4, then end art for opening and 4, 3, 2, 1, then end art for closing, with 62.5 ms frames (16 fps) and about 91 ms frames (11 fps) checked at the boundaries. First sight, breach, and repair snap; a re-entered door is a first sight; a mid-swing reversal continues from the current step. The Canvas2D renderer draws closed, then the swing frames from the render clock, then open. The sound key is chosen per piece class and exists in `bank.json`; toggling a placed garden gate's attachment plays `door.open.gate` / `door.close.gate`, and the initial snapshot is silent. `splitStreamPages` keeps the 1024 pages at 4 per layer and moves the 2048 swing sheets to their own pool.

## ADR-315: Bigger claim areas with a radius preview, a per-player border toggle, and no overlapping claims (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** A Claim Flag (ADR-310) claimed radius 12, too small for a homestead with a garden, pens and outbuildings. Players could not see a claim's extent before or after placing. A new flag was only refused when a *foreign* zone came within r + R, so own and clan claims could overlap freely, and every zone lookup queried the shared entity hash out to the maximum radius.

**Decision.**
- **Radius 32** (`claim_totem.privilegeRadius`, was 12). That is one world chunk (`CHUNK_SIZE` 32), so one flag covers a 64-tile-wide homestead. That is ~7× the old area and roughly a screen at default build zoom. It is still small enough for several neighbours to fit side by side within a short walk. 40 would make one claim wider than the view and leave little room between non-overlapping claims. `MAX_PRIVILEGE_RADIUS` (zone-grid bound) is 40, and a test asserts every piece stays within it.
- **Zone grid** (`building/zones.ts`). Every zone is bucketed into 32-tile cells covering its largest possible disk. `zonesAt` reads one cell for a point and a few for a disk, then re-checks live radius and position. The grid rebuilds only when zone membership changes: the new `ComponentStore.membership` counter is bumped on add-new and remove, never on field writes. A zone found away from its bucketed spot forces a rebuild, so answers always match a full scan (tested).
- **No overlap, touching allowed.** A flag's disk may overlap no claim of any owner (own, clan, or foreign): `distance < r1 + r2 − 0.001` fails with the new `BuildFail.ClaimOverlap = 27`, HUD text "Claim would overlap another claim". Rims may touch, so clanmates can bump their land edge to edge. A flag *centre* inside a foreign claim stays `NoPrivilege`. `zoneOwnedBy` is unchanged, so clan members still build inside each other's claims.
- **Multiple flags per player are allowed.** Under the no-overlap rule, extra flags only add disjoint land, each costing a flag's materials and carrying its own `maxPiecesPerZone`. Tests cover this.
- **Ghost preview.** A Claim Flag hologram carries `preview.claim = { radius, overlap? }`. The new claim overlay (`apps/client/src/claim-overlay.ts`, a pointer-events-none canvas under the ADR-196 snap overlay) draws the claim at the ghost. It is green when valid and red on overlap, and the overlapped claim's border turns red too. Nearby borders (rim within 24 tiles) show own and clan claims in cyan and foreign claims in dashed amber. For readability on any ground, each line has a dark halo under a bright stroke, a faint fill, and rim points lifted to the terrain height under them. A ghost that overlaps by ≤ 4 tiles is pushed out to touch the claim (`bumped`).
- **Placed flags: default off, with a 6 s fade after your own placement** (`CLAIM_FLASH_MS`). Permanent borders around every flag would clutter the screen. The brief fade confirms what you just claimed.
- **Use / hand toggles a flag's border.** `interactPanel` adds `{ panel: "claim" }` for the nearest flag in build reach (any owner, so you can plan against a neighbour), competing by distance like doors (ADR-303). The ADR-212 hand icon shows over the flag (`CLAIM_HINT_KIND`). Keyboard and gamepad Interact and a touch tap on the hand all toggle `ClaimView`, which is client-local and per player: never sent or replicated. Use on a flag never opens inventory.
- **AI humans.** `pickBaseSite` accepts a site only if an own or clan claim already covers it, or if a new flag beside the hut (4-tile slack) overlaps no claim and no other agent's planned site (2R + 4 apart unless same tribe). When the local ring is all claimed, it tries tangent spots just outside the blocking claims, nearest first. The flag slot is chosen by the same `validatePlacement`, so it cannot overlap. Hire relocation (ignoreClaim) still rebuilds under the owner's claim. A worker's own flag that would overlap it is now skipped (its salvage stays in the manifest). Abandoned-site reclaim keeps `hasOwnClaim`.
- **Saved claims.** Loaded flags with the old radius grow to 32 on load (`growLegacyClaims`). Each stops where its rim meets another party's claim and never shrinks, so a reload cannot lock anyone out of land they built on.

**Not changed.** ADR-310 claim requirement, `zoneOwnedBy` / `hasPrivilege` semantics, ZoneFull, flag cost, compass, graphics, art.

**Validation.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr315_claims.test.ts` covers the following:
- the radius value and bound;
- clanmates touching (allowed);
- overlap rejected for clan, own, and foreign claims;
- foreign centre → NoPrivilege;
- multiple own flags;
- clan building inside;
- hologram radius, ClaimOverlap with the overlapped zone, and the bump;
- grid = scan over 3000 random claims, add and remove tracking, and 40k lookups with no rebuild (perf sanity);
- legacy growth;
- AI site and flag slot clear of a foreign claim;
- two agents' sites a claim apart.

`apps/client/test/adr315_claim_view.test.ts` covers the following:
- ghost ring green with own and foreign neighbours;
- red ghost and red overlapped border;
- nothing drawn by default;
- terrain-lifted rim;
- Use at a flag picks the claim toggle (hand icon) and never a panel;
- a closer box still wins;
- the toggle is local and forgets destroyed flags;
- the post-placement fade;
- main.ts wiring.

Updated tests (deliberate changes):
- ADR-310: radius 12 → 32.
- task5: the lone-floor probe moved out of the bigger claim.
- adr252 live fight fixture: the arena is now the spawn point farthest from both bot bases, because bases sit a claim apart and one can land beside the fixed spawn point the fixture assumed was clear.

## ADR-316: Demolish mode without a hologram, touch select + confirm (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Demolish (ADR-136 / ADR-302) only existed inside placement: a player had to pick a piece, carry its ghost, then aim at the piece to remove and press X twice. On touch the contextual Demolish button acted on whatever the ghost-lifted touch point happened to hit, with no way to pick a piece directly.

**Decision.**
- **`BuildMode.startDemolish()`** opens a Building session with no selection: no hologram, no preview queries, only the target under the aim. The aimed (KBM / pad cursor) or tapped (touch) piece gets the ADR-302 amber footprint outline (`targetOutline`), and the HUD strip shows its name · tier · hp, the refund ("Refund: 10 Sticks, 6 Fiber (100%)", ADR-317) and, when it can't be demolished, the reason ("You don't have permission to demolish here") with Demolish disabled. Exiting returns to normal play.
- **Entry points.** New append-only action `ToggleDemolish`: KBM `Delete` / `Backspace` (every letter key is already a gameplay, build or UINav hotkey: K = Character, L = Clan), gamepad `LB+B` (free in Gameplay and Building; shadows QuickUse / Build.Cancel through modifier shadowing, like LB+Y), and on touch the Build menu's new "Demolish / Move" entry (pad-navigable like every menu button) plus a "Demolish" button on the placement chip. Pressing it while placing switches to demolish mode; pressing it in demolish mode exits. `Build.Cancel` (Esc / B / ✕) also exits.
- **Desktop and gamepad keep the armed step**: `mouse.left` / `pad.a` (and `X`) arm, a second press within 3 s demolishes; hold `pad.x` confirms at once (ADR-136). Floor PgUp/PgDn / LT+D-pad work as in placement.
- **Touch.** A tap on the world selects the piece under the finger (no ADR-136 finger lift, no drag), another tap on another piece changes the selection, a tap on empty ground clears it. The strip sits at the HUD's fixed top-centre spot and shows "Confirm demolish" (one tap demolishes, as does the layout's ✓), "Deselect", and the chip's "Exit".
- Repair / Upgrade / Reclaim / Move stay available on the selected piece in demolish mode.

**Not changed.** Placement flows, ADR-302 outline art, compass, graphics, art. No new glyph art (the generated glyph map is not extended).

**Validation.** `apps/client/test/adr316_demolish_mode.test.ts`: Delete / Backspace / Esc on KBM (no preview, outline, refund text, arm + confirm), switching from placing, a foreign-claim piece (highlighted, reason, disabled, nothing sent), LB+B on gamepad with QuickUse shadowed (A arm/confirm, hold X, B exit), touch select / change / deselect / empty-ground clear / one-tap confirm / Exit, touch bindings. `build_platforms.test.ts` gains the Move action in the strip.

## ADR-317: Demolish refunds by builder, and a claim-permission gate for players and AI humans (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Demolish refunded `demolishRefund` (50%) × hp fraction for everyone (pickup pieces 100% × hp fraction), so tearing down your own fresh wall lost half of it. Permission was the generic `hasPrivilege` on the tile.

**Decision.**
- **`PieceBuilder {player}`** (networked, persistent, appended component) records the PlayerId that placed the piece (0 = worldgen). A builder entity without a PlayerId records nothing (unknown). Reclaim (ADR-300) changes owner and tribe but never the builder, so reclaimed ruins are not the reclaimer's build. STRC v6 saves `PieceOwner` and `PieceBuilder` (flag 64); v5 saves load with the builder unknown. Unknown builders count as the actor's when the piece carries the actor's tribe, so pre-ADR-317 bases still refund in full to their tribe.
- **Refund** (`demolishRefund`, `building/edit.ts`): your own build (or your hired worker's, or for a hired worker its employer's) refunds 100% of the *current* tier's cost regardless of damage; anything else refunds 50%, floored per resource with a minimum of 1. Pickup pieces (ADR-250) follow the same rule (contents still drop as a loot bag).
- **Permission** (`demolishPermission`): every claim covering the piece must pass `zoneOwnedBy`: own claim, clan claim (clan ranks gate through the existing "base" rank permission, which is what gives a member the clan Tribe), or a hired worker's employer's claim. In the wilderness, worldgen ruins (tribe 0) and your own pieces may go; another tribe's piece may not. Failure is `BuildFail.NoDemolishPermission = 28`, "You don't have permission to demolish here". Claim Flags sit inside their own zone, so only the owner or clan can take one down.
- The check runs on the server for every Demolish intent, so AI humans (which use the same intent) can never demolish a foreign piece; the client mirrors it to disable the button and explain why.

**Validation.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr317_318_demolish_move.test.ts`: own build 100% when damaged, upgraded tier, clanmate 50% (min 1), reclaimed 50%, hired worker both ways, STRC round-trip + legacy fallback, outsider refused (28) / clanmate allowed, claim flags, wilderness ruins vs foreign piece, unhired vs hired AI. `apps/server/test/adr318_mp_move.test.ts`: over the network an outsider's Demolish is refused, a clanmate gets 50%, the builder 100%. Updated: `adr250_basic_storage_box` (own damaged box now refunds in full).

## ADR-318: Moving placed pieces (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Re-arranging a base meant demolishing (losing materials and contents) and rebuilding.

**Decision.**
- **`MoveCmd {target, x, y, level, rot}`** (append-only, after ReclaimCmd; `IntentAction.Move = 16`) re-slots the *same entity* in one server step (`movePiece`): validated with the piece lifted out of the structure index (`StructureIndex.lifted`), then committed. Identity and all state stay: BuildPiece (hp, tier, paint, tint), Tribe, PieceOwner / PieceBuilder, and every attachment (storage contents, fuel, door state, lights) whose Transform / PieceLink follow. Small decor on a moved surface is re-seated. No cost, no refund. Emits `PieceMoved`.
- **Allowed** only when the piece is fully repaired (`NeedsRepair` 29, "Repair it first"), belongs to the mover (same tribe: own personal tribe or clan; owner / builder pid; a hired worker's employer — else `NotYours` 30, "Not yours"), the mover has privilege at the source and the destination (`NoMovePermission` 33, "No permission here"), the piece type is movable (stalls, planters, terrain ladders, shaft hatches: `NotMovable` 31) and nothing rests on it (`HasDependents` 32: structural dependents or decor on a surface). The destination goes through `validatePlacement` (reach, support, overlap, claim) with `ignoreCost`; a moved Claim Flag ignores its own zone (`ignoreZone`) but still respects ADR-315 no-overlap.
- **Atomic / cancel.** The client never removes anything: Move lifts the piece into the normal hologram (`BuildSelection.moving`; the ghost preview lifts it the same way so its own cell doesn't block), the amber outline stays on the original, piece / tier cycling is off. Confirm sends one MoveCmd and returns to demolish mode; Cancel (Esc / B / ✕ / "Cancel move") just drops the hologram — the piece never left.
- **Controls.** `Build.Move` (append-only): KBM `F`, gamepad hold `Y` (tap Y stays Upgrade), touch the strip's "Move" button; available on the targeted piece in demolish mode and while placing.
- **Replicas.** Pieces replicate their Transform; on non-authority peers `structureIndexSystem` re-indexes a piece whose Transform changed to a different slot, so the client's index (targets, previews, outlines) follows a server move.

**Validation.** `adr317_318_demolish_move.test.ts`: move keeps entity / hp / tier / tribe / builder / contents and re-slots the index; damaged, foreign and no-permission refusals; clanmate allowed; validateMove leaves everything unchanged; occupied destination; structural dependents refused; flag move ignores its own zone and fails ClaimOverlap. `adr316_demolish_mode.test.ts`: F lifts, wheel can't change the piece, Esc restores with nothing sent, click sends MoveCmd; damaged → "Repair it first"; pad hold Y / B. `adr318_mp_move.test.ts`: a stocked box moved over the network keeps its contents and moves on every client's replica and structure index; an outsider's MoveCmd changes nothing. Server command tail tests list `MOVE_COMMANDS`.

## ADR-319: Mounts — taming, riding, realistic scale (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Crossing the map on foot is slow (walk 2.9, sprint 4.64 tiles/s). Players asked for rideable animals that are tamed, ridden, shown with the rider on them, sized realistically next to the 1.75 m player (t362u, t363). Art delivered dedicated true-scale sheets in fafe447e (`docs/ART_KEYS_MOUNTS.md`).

**Decision.**
- **Data.** `packages/gameplay/data/mounts.json` (`mount_defs.ts`): seven species (append-only order = `Mount.species`), per-species speeds, acceleration, turn rate, hp, taming difficulty, food preferences, traits, art key and a real-world **size** block. Every walk beats an on-foot sprint; every gallop differs.

  | Species | Wild archetypes | Walk | Gallop | Accel | Turn | HP | Tame diff. | Foods (taming) | Traits |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Horse | `animal_horse` | 5.4 | **9.6** | 4.0 | 5.5 | 180 | 1.0 | carrot (love), apple (love), hay (like), wheat (like), berries (ok) | fastest gallop |
  | Donkey | `animal_donkey` | 4.9 | **6.9** | 3.0 | 6.5 | 150 | 0.7 | carrot (love), hay (love), apple (like), wheat (like), berries (ok) | sure-footed: +1 safe drop tile; low enough to ride through doorways |
  | Deer | `animal_deer`, `animal_red_deer`, `animal_stag` | 5.5 | **9.1** | 5.0 | 7.0 | 90 | 1.3 | apple (love), berries (love), carrot (like), wheat (ok) | quickest to accelerate; skittish (spooks more while taming) |
  | Elk | `animal_elk` | 5.2 | **8.5** | 3.5 | 5.0 | 160 | 1.2 | apple (love), hay (like), berries (like), wheat (ok) | sturdy |
  | Moose | `animal_moose` | 5.0 | **7.8** | 2.5 | 3.8 | 240 | 1.6 | apple (love), berries (like), hay (like), wheat (ok) | strong swimmer: crosses deep water; kicks while being tamed |
  | Buffalo | `animal_bison` | 4.9 | **8.0** | 2.5 | 3.5 | 260 | 1.5 | hay (love), wheat (love), carrot (like), apple (ok) | toughest hide; kicks while being tamed |
  | Yak | `animal_yak` | 4.8 | **6.4** | 2.6 | 4.2 | 220 | 1.1 | hay (love), wheat (like), berries (like), carrot (ok) | cold-hardy pack animal; sure-footed: +1 safe drop tile |

  New wild archetypes `animal_horse`, `animal_donkey`, `animal_yak` (ai.json append; spawns: horse grass, donkey sand / grass, yak stone / grass). They have no wild sheet, so `sprite_fallbacks` maps them to their own `mount_<art>` sheet (idle / walk / gallop only: hit / death / eat fall back to idle).
- **Realism table** (player 1.75 m = **52 px** doll at 1x → 29.714 px/m, z step 16 px; the same table as Art's `mount_anchors.json`). Drives the sheets' authored size (render scale 1), the rider seat fallback (when a frame has no `seat` anchor), the collision radius and the clearance checks:

  | Species | Sheet | Withers m (×player) | Head/antler/hump top m | Length m | Width m | Seat m (×player) | Rider head m | Doorway (≤2.0 m) | Deck ceiling (≤2.4 m) | Body radius | Withers / top / length / seat px (1x) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Horse | `mount_horse` | 1.60 (0.91) | 2.25 | 2.4 | 0.65 | 1.45 (0.83×) | 2.30 | no | yes | 0.375 | 47.5 / 66.9 / 71.3 / 43.1 |
  | Donkey | `mount_donkey` | 1.20 (0.69) | 1.75 | 1.8 | 0.5 | 1.10 (0.63×) | 1.95 | **yes** | yes | 0.3 | 35.7 / 52.0 / 53.5 / 32.7 |
  | Deer | `mount_deer` | 1.35 (0.77) | 2.10 | 2.0 | 0.5 | 1.25 (0.71×) | 2.10 | no | yes | 0.3 | 40.1 / 62.4 / 59.4 / 37.1 |
  | Elk | `mount_elk` | 1.45 (0.83) | 2.60 | 2.4 | 0.6 | 1.35 (0.77×) | 2.20 | no | yes | 0.35 | 43.1 / 77.3 / 71.3 / 40.1 |
  | Moose | `mount_moose` | 2.00 (1.14) | 2.70 | 2.9 | 0.75 | 1.85 (1.06×) | 2.70 | no | **no** | 0.425 | 59.4 / 80.2 / 86.2 / 55.0 |
  | Buffalo | `mount_bison` | 1.80 (1.03) | 1.90 | 3.0 | 0.95 | 1.55 (0.89×) | 2.40 | no | yes | 0.48 | 53.5 / 56.5 / 89.1 / 46.1 |
  | Yak | `mount_yak` | 1.55 (0.89) | 1.70 | 2.6 | 0.85 | 1.40 (0.80×) | 2.25 | no | yes | 0.475 | 46.1 / 50.5 / 77.3 / 41.6 |

  Tamed mounts draw on `mount_<art>` at scale 1 (true scale). Wild deer / elk / moose / bison keep their shipped `animal_*` sheets and scale (Art's decision in fafe447e); they switch to the true-scale sheet when tamed. Fallback seat lift = `(seatM − 0.45 m) × px/m ÷ 16`. Rider head = seat + 0.85 m. Collision radius = clamp(width/2 + 0.05, 0.3, 0.48).
- **Components** (appended): `Mount {species, kind, owner, tribe, riderNetId, saddle, saddleItem, saddleDur, hp, len, name[16]}` (networked + persistent; `kind` rebuilds `Animal` after a load), `Riding {mountNetId, species, speed, hurt}` (networked, not persistent), `MountTaming {progress, by, lastTick}`. All replicate to everyone ("all") so every peer draws the rider on the mount.
- **Taming.** Unlock node **Horsemanship** (husbandry branch, tier 0, `mount:tame`) gates taming and riding. Feed a liked food (`MountFeedCmd`): progress += gain(love 25 / like 15 / ok 8) × (1 + tame mod) ÷ difficulty; each feed may spook (chance = 0.18 × difficulty × (1 − progress/100) × pref multiplier × (1 − tame mod)): −15 progress, then a kick (6 damage) for species with an attack, else it bolts. Progress decays after 20 s without food. At 100 the animal becomes a `Mount` owned by the tamer (a hired worker tames for the employer), with the tamer's tribe. A wild mount-species animal is lured (no flee / charge) by someone holding a food it eats.
- **Riding.** `MountRideCmd` / `MountDismountCmd`; who may ride = owner, tribe / clan mate, or a worker of the owner. Movement runs through the shared `applyMovementInput` (`applyRidingInput`, so client prediction and AI humans use the same code): speed ramps from 0.6× walk by species accel, decel 2.5× accel, species turn rate, a sharp reverse drops to the pivot speed, Sprint (or the ADR-289 auto-sprint warmup) gallops, roads and swimming apply, a mount below 30 % hp runs at 0.75×. Collision uses the species body radius; only swimmers enter deep water. `rideClearanceBlocked`: riders taller than a doorway cannot pass an edge-piece opening; riders taller than a deck ceiling cannot ride under a deck one level up. Terrain ladders over 3 refuse riders; falls are taken with the species' safe bonus and the mount is hurt too. While mounted: gather / build / repair / demolish / move / doors / fire / attack / reload are cleared (`mountGateSystem`); eating, crafting and containers still work. A hit on a rider is split: the mount takes 40 %. Death, disconnect, entering a vehicle or a stale link dismount; the mount stays put.
- **Controls.** `Mount.Menu` (append-only): KBM `U`, pad `LB+X`, touch ♞ "Mount" (shown near a rideable animal or while riding) opens the mount panel (status, speeds, hp / tame / saddle bars, tame-with-food, Ride / Dismount, Saddlebag, Rename, saddle actions; all gamepad-navigable buttons). `Interact` dismounts while riding and mounts the nearest own free mount on foot; Use never opens the saddlebag (ADR-303).
- **Rendering** (`view.ts syncMounts`, `mount-render.ts`, on every peer from replicated Mount / Riding). The mount takes the rider's predicted / interpolated pose, so it never slides under them. Gait idle / walk / gallop comes from `Riding.speed`; the render `Run` chain now tries `gallop`. The rider's Sit chain becomes `ride_idle` / `ride_walk` / `ride_gallop`, falling back to `vehicle` → `sit` → `idle`, and restarts on the same tick as the mount so frames stay 1:1. The rider is placed on the current mount frame's `seat` anchor (`dirFrameAnchors`, index frame × 8 + facing), and the doll's own ride / vehicle `seat` socket lands there (the sprites.ts seat rule is extended to `ride_*`). Layers draw `mount_<art>` → `mount_saddle_<art>_<tier>` (ADR-320) → rider → `mount_<art>_fore` (only while ridden). They are ordered by screen-neutral depth shifts: each layer moves along the view diagonal and up by the same screen amount, giving sort keys +0.01 / +0.02 / +0.03, and this holds in all four ADR-253 view rotations. Hp bars sit over the real head height.
- **AI humans.** Bot intents `tameMount`, `rideMount`, `dismount`, `saddleMount`; riding AI moves at mount speed through the same movement code. No autonomous planner policy yet (hook only).

**Validation.** `adr319_mounts.test.ts` (species list, speeds > sprint, withers / seat ratios, pixel targets vs Art's `mount_anchors.json` heights, wild archetypes + spawns, seat lift, body radius, doorway / ceiling lists, taming + needs_skill, worker / AI ownership, permissions, ride / gallop / dismount, gate, mount_busy, disconnect + link heal, death drop, replication scopes, chunk save / load + Animal rebuild, doorway clearance). `adr319_mount_bindings.test.ts`, `adr319_mount_render.test.ts` (every sheet / fore / saddle key exists, screen-neutral shifts in 4 rotations, rider on the seat anchor, gait), `adr234_skill_audit` (+ `mount:` token), touch layout ids.

## ADR-320: Saddles (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Bareback riding has no storage and no protection; saddles should add both, scaling per tier, and show on the mount (t362u).

**Decision.**
- **Items + recipes** (append-only ids): 

  | Tier | Item | Slots | Defense | Durability | Recipe (station) | Unlock node |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | Leather Saddle `saddle_leather` | **3** | 10 | 300 | leather 4, rope 2, thread 2 (workbench) | Saddler (tier 1, 1 pt) |
  | 2 | Reinforced Saddle `saddle_reinforced` | 5 | 20 | 450 | hardened leather 4, leather 2, rope 2, nails 4 (workbench) | Harness Maker (tier 2, 2 pts) |
  | 3 | Iron Saddle `saddle_iron` | 7 | 32 | 600 | iron ingot 4, hardened leather 3, leather 2, rope 2 (anvil) | Iron Saddler (tier 3, 2 pts) |
  | 4 | Steel Saddle `saddle_steel` | 9 | 45 | 800 | steel ingot 4, hardened leather 4, thread 4, rope 2 (anvil) | Master Saddler (tier 4, 3 pts) |

  Bareback: 0 slots, 0 defense. Saddlery nodes are unlock nodes with `item:<saddle>` tokens (husbandry branch); crafting checks `recipeOutputUnlocked` (craft queue reason `recipe_locked`, "🔒 learn it in the skill tree"), repair checks `itemRepairUnlocked` (ADR-310).
- **Equip.** `MountSaddleCmd {target, slot}` puts a saddle from the player's inventory on; a swap returns the old saddle with its wear; a smaller saddle needs its extra bag slots empty (`bag_too_full`). `MountUnsaddleCmd` needs an empty bag. The saddlebag is the mount's `Container` (slotCount = saddle slots), opened through the normal OpenContainer / storage panel only with a saddle on and permission (ADR-303: a container, but distinct from mounting).
- **Defense.** `armorOf` adds the saddle defense to the mount, and to the rider while riding. Hits on the rider or mount wear the saddle (max(1, round(dmg × 0.5))); at 0 durability it gives no defense. `MountRepairCmd` costs 30 % (rounded up) of the recipe.
- **Death.** A dead mount drops its saddle (with wear) and saddlebag contents in an owner-tagged loot bag.
- **Rendering.** Saddle overlay `mount_saddle_<art>_<leather|reinforced|iron|steel>` (28 dedicated sheets, Art fafe447e), drawn between the mount and the rider with the mount's anim and facing. Saddle icons: `saddle_<tier>` in nature_icons.

**Validation.** `adr320_saddles.test.ts` (tier table, 3-slot basic, rising stats, items + recipes; bareback; equip → 3 slots + 10 armor on mount and rider; stranger can't open the bag; swap returns the steel saddle with its durability; bag_too_full / bag_not_empty; unsaddle; wear; broken = no defense; repair cost + restore; rider / mount damage split; recipe + repair gating; node names).

## ADR-321: AI humans tame, ride and keep mounts on their own (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-319/320 let AI humans tame and ride through the same commands as players, but no behaviour used them. The question "can AI humans decide to tame and ride on their own?" needs utility behaviours in the existing survivor planner, not a new AI.

**Decision.** `packages/gameplay/src/ai/mount_behaviors.ts`, built like `vehicle_behaviors.ts`:
- **Sensors** (`fillMountSensors`, run after the plan sensors in `buildAgentView`): `mount` (own mount: hp, saddle, wear, free bag slots, riding / busy, a liked food when it is below `feedBelowHp`), `mountSkill` (Horsemanship), `tameMount` (best wild target), `saddleUp` (next saddle step) and `invFree`. "Own" means `Mount.owner === mountOwnerIdFor(self)` (the employer for a hired worker) and `mayUseMount`. Tribe-mates' and strangers' mounts are never treated as own.
- **tame_mount**: needs no mount, Horsemanship, a liked food in the bag, and calm (hp ≥ `minHp`, fed, no zombie within `safeTiles`).
  - Picks targets with a spatial-hash radius query (`seekRadius` 24), at most every `scanEveryTicks` (40). Score is gallop + hp/60 − 0.15 × distance, ties broken by entity id.
  - Skips kickers (species with an attack) while hp < `kickerMinHp`. Also skips animals inside a claim it does not own, and animals someone else is taming.
  - It holds the food (`equip`, which lures), walks up and sends `mfeed` every `feedEveryTicks`.
  - When progress drops (a spook) it steps back for `backoffTicks`. When kicked to low hp it gives up.
  - After `giveUpTicks` (60 s) it gives up and bans the animal for `banTicks`.
  - Its single consideration is weighted `tameUtility` 1.3, so a calm bot takes the chance before another resource trip.
- **mountPolicy** wraps every survivor behaviour, next to `stancePolicy`. `goTo` records the nav goal (`navGoal*` bb).
  - **Mounting:** it mounts when the goal is > `longTripTiles` (25) away and its mount is within `fetchRadius` (8, detouring to it) and not the wrong way. It also mounts when fleeing with the mount within `fleeMountRadius`.
  - **Dismounting:** it gets off on arrival (< `arriveTiles` 4, or still for `idleDismountTicks`). It also gets off before a base-interior goal, when `rideClearanceBlocked` is hit ahead (doorway / low ceiling), at once for sleep / rest / vehicles, within `taskDismountTiles` for task behaviours, and on any foot action (gather / attack / craft / build / door …).
  - After a dismount it waits `remountCooldownTicks` before mounting again. Fleeing riders stay on.
- **saddle_up**:
  - Equips a better saddle from the bag (never downgrades).
  - Otherwise crafts the best unlocked saddle it can pay for in its bag, here or at its base station (`craft:`).
  - Otherwise repairs a saddle below `repairBelow` when `checkRepair` allows.
- **tend_mount**: feeds a hurt mount, and fetches a mount more than `homeRadius` from home (walks to it, rides it home, gets off). With ≤ `bagOverflowFreeSlots` free slots it deposits surplus into the saddlebag (`copen` / `cdeposit` / `cclose`). A dead mount drops out of the sensors, so `tame_mount` replaces it.
- **Commands:** action strings `mfeed:<t>:<item>`, `mride:<t>`, `mdismount`, `msaddle:<t>:<slot>`, `mrepair:<t>` become the ADR-319 / ADR-320 net commands (`agent_output.ts`). The server re-validates everything (reach, skill, ownership).
- **Determinism and budget:** no rng, tick cooldowns on the bb, sorted candidates. Own-mount lookup is cached (rescan every `ownScanEveryTicks`); the saddle plan is cached `saddleScanEveryTicks`.
- **Tuning:** all knobs live in `data/mounts.json` → `bots` (`MOUNT_BOTS`).
- **Bandits:** gameplay has no hostile-human faction yet. Any future one inherits the same rule: only mounts `mayUseMount` allows.

**Validation.** `adr321_ai_mounts.test.ts`:
- action strings, and the behaviours in the registry;
- end-to-end seek → lure → feed → tame, plus the same through the full `survivorController`;
- determinism; species preference, the hurt-kicker skip, foreign claims, and skill / food gates;
- spook back-off and the give-up timeout with ban;
- long-trip auto mount → faster arrival → dismount, staying on foot for short trips, no far fetch, and the flee mount;
- the doorway clearance dismount and remount cooldown, a donkey riding through, and the building dismount; task dismounts but no flee dismount;
- saddle equip with no downgrade, craft at the workbench, then equip and repair; saddlebag overflow;
- strangers' and tribe-mates' mounts ignored, a worker using and taming for its employer;
- feeding a hurt mount, fetching a strayed mount home, and replacement after death.

## ADR-322: seated rider poses, mount actions and lazy ride pages (SurVivaZ)

Context: Art & Assets shipped `ride_idle` (4f@4) / `ride_walk` (6f@8) / `ride_gallop` (6f@12) on every doll layer (pages
`cz_ride_<slot>_<n>`, ~111 MB) and hit (3f@10) / death (6f@8, no loop) / graze (4f@4) on every mount, fore and saddle
sheet, plus moose swim (6f@8), with `mount_anchors.json` (riderSeat, seat, riderOffset, actSeat, acts.riderAnim,
moose swimWaterY). See docs/ART_KEYS_MOUNTS.md.

Decision:
- Rider chain is `ride_<gait>` -> slower ride_* -> idle; the ADR-319 vehicle / sit fallback is gone. sprites.ts still lands the
  body's ride frame `seat` socket (frameMeta df:i, body only; layers follow) on the mount seat, so doll pivot = mount pivot +
  seat - riderSeat (= riderOffset). On a gait the rider VAnim start tick equals the mount's, so rider frame fi = mount frame fi.
- Mount actions come from the mount's view anim state (`mountActOf`): 4 hit, 5 death, 8/9 graze, 14 swim (only on a sheet with
  swim, i.e. moose). hit / graze / swim: the rider plays ride_idle on its own clock (start tick = when the act began), pinned
  each tick to that act frame's seat anchor (actSeat). death: the rider is not seated (the server dismount follows).
- Moose swim: `riderClip` binding = water row as px above the seat pivot (`swimClipPx` = seat.y - water.y); the sprite shader
  clips the doll below it without the swim sink / bob (aJ.y < 0 flag).
- Graze: standing, unridden tamed mounts and the wild archetypes on a mount sheet (horse / donkey / yak, no wild sheet:
  sprite_fallbacks animal_<k> -> mount_<k>) graze when fed (Eat / Graze) and on a deterministic idle duty cycle
  (GRAZE_ON 5 s of every GRAZE_CYCLE 12 s, phase hashed per entity). STATE_ANIM_TABLE already mapped Hurt/Die/Graze/Swim.
- Streaming: `cz_ride_*` pages are never body (eager) pages; they join the lazy wear pool and load when a ridden frame needs
  them (the body shows idle until the page is ready). prefetch-art skips them (`shouldPrefetchAtlas`).

Tests: apps/client/test/adr322_mount_acts.test.ts (anchor pairing for all species x gait x frame x facing, male and female,
body frameMeta seat = riderSeat, frame / fps pairing, act -> rider map vs acts.riderAnim, actSeat = sheet seat anchors,
act sheets on mount / fore / saddles, wild mount-sheet archetypes, swim water anchors + clip), packages/render/test/
adr322_ride_lazy.test.ts (real registry: every cz_ride page lazy, none eager, none prefetched).

## ADR-323: AI humans stock mount food from allowed storage and plan saddle materials (SurVivaZ)

Context: ADR-321 bots only tamed / fed with liked food already in the bag and only crafted a saddle with every ingredient
on hand.

Decision:
- Food (mount_behaviors foodSensors / fetch_mount_food): when taming (a tameable animal is near but no liked food is on hand)
  or feeding the own hurt mount, the bot looks for its species' liked foods (love > like > ok) in base storage within
  `storageRadius` (scan every `scanEveryTicks`, cached) and withdraws only `tameFoodCount` / `feedFoodCount` + `foodBuffer`
  minus what it carries (ADR-250 open -> withdraw -> close; the server re-checks reach and ADR-207).
  `mayTakeFromStorage`: inside a claim every covering zone must be zoneOwnedBy the bot (its own claim, its clan / tribe's, or
  its employer's for a hired worker) and canUseBaseStorage must agree; an unclaimed box counts only within
  `homeStorageTiles` of its own planner base, or of the employer's work home (Worker.homeX/Y) for a hired worker.
  Everything else (strangers' claims, stray boxes) is never touched. With nothing stored, the liked foods go into the bot's
  gather needs (bb "mountNeeds" -> computeGoalSensors), so the normal gather / harvest pick forages them.
- Saddle chain (saddleGoalPass + planner): with an own mount and a base, every `saddleScanEveryTicks` the bot picks the best
  unlocked saddle tier whose recipe chain only needs stations the base already has (chainStations, depth-capped) and that
  the planner can resolve within `planMaxDepth`. The goal goes to the planner as a priority item goal right after the
  survival pre-goals (PlanInput.priority / maxDepth), so the existing behaviours do the work: withdraw from own base storage,
  hand / station crafts (craft, base_work), gather leaves and hunt. When the saddle is in the bag, ADR-321 saddle_up equips it.
  Timeout (`saddlePlanTimeoutTicks`) bans the tier for `saddleTierBanTicks` (falls back a tier); danger / low needs (hp <
  minHp, hunger or thirst < 30 %, zombie within safeTiles) abandons it for `saddlePlanRetryTicks`, and
  `saddleAbandonsToFallback` abandons of one tier ban it too. Hired workers do not run the chain (they work their job).
- Deterministic (no rng, tick cooldowns, sorted storage), budgeted (storage scan and tier pick on cooldowns; one planner pass
  per tier candidate per scan). Knobs: mounts.json "bots".

Tests: packages/gameplay/test/adr323_ai_mount_supplies.test.ts.

## ADR-324: AI humans travel the whole world (clan attachment is a preference)

Context: AI humans were held near their spawn. The limits found were:
- HOME_MAX_DIST 48: the home was re-anchored to the current position past 48 tiles.
- The base was forgotten past 4 x 48 = 192 tiles.
- The ADR-279 trip radius was 36 tiles.
- The local nav goal range was about 24 tiles.
- The unloaded/idle view was the only sim far from players (no world-scale goal, no long path).

Decision (packages/gameplay/src/ai/travel.ts, data/travel.json):
- Long-range goals (pickTravelGoal, deterministic: seed + travel count):
  - explore a hashed direction 200 to 800 tiles out;
  - every third goal, a POI (AbandonedSite) or trade stall (StallHeader) within poiSearchTiles in an unvisited region;
  - relocate the homestead every relocateEvery trips (free AIs only);
  - "sent" when ordered (orderTravel);
  - "return" for roamers.
- Hierarchical routes:
  - A* over a coarse region grid (regionTiles 16, 8-neighbour, binary heap, node budget maxRegionExpand).
  - Region cost comes from sampled water and is cached with a TTL.
  - The route is region-centre waypoints plus the exact goal, and the local nav (goTo) walks each leg, so path length is unbounded.
  - requestRoute allows at most maxPlansPerTick plans per world tick; there are no full-world searches.
  - The ADR-321 mount policy treats the trip goal as the ride goal, so mounted bots ride long legs.
- Attachment (travelMode):
  - Hired worker: "worker", stays with the employer unless sent.
  - No clan: "free".
  - Clan member: "stay" when roamPreference(traits) < roamTraitMin or under a BuildBase/Defend clan order; otherwise "roam".
  - Stay bots only take trips within clanStayRadius of the clan anchor. Roamers go out and return after roamReturnTicks.
- The base and home are kept while on a trip's corridor (travelKeepsHome). A relocation trip drops the base on arrival.
- Off-screen sim (apps/client/src/local.ts and GameServer.setStreaming):
  - A bot with a route and no human within offscreen.fullSimTiles gets no view or controller and stops being a chunk source.
  - Every offscreen.stepTicks it moves along its route at walk or mount speed (offscreenStep), with needs floored at needsFloor.
  - When a human comes near or it arrives, it streams again and resumes full sim once its chunk is active.
  - The state lives in AiMemory (identity.ai), so position and leg continue across reloads.
  - It is server-authoritative: the Transform moves on the authoritative world, so net relevance works as usual.

Tests: packages/gameplay/test/adr324_world_travel.test.ts.

## ADR-325: AI humans spawn all around the world, not by the players

Context (old behaviour):
- Seed spawn points: computeSpawnPoints (ADR-106) gave only four starter points, one per quadrant, about 48–144 tiles from the origin on the starter biome. Players join at the least crowded of those four.
- Host bots (createLocalServer `bots`, the settings value) joined through the same player path, so they landed at a starter point.
- Population bots (spawns.json "humans": minPlayerDistance 10, maxPlayerDistance 40, global caps) were triggered in player-active chunks but placed by pickSpawnPoint at the least crowded of the same four points.
- Respawn (ADR-153 installBedRespawn): own bed, else the nearest of the four.
- Result: AI humans always started and came back where the players are.
- Abandoned sites (planAbandonedChunk) are a pure function of the seed but were never used as spawns.

Decision (packages/gameplay/src/ai_spawn.ts, data/ai_spawn.json):
- World-wide AI spawn points from the seed (computeAiSpawnPoints):
  - a Vogel spiral of `count` points between minRadius and maxRadius, each snapped to the nearest clear 3x3 walkable patch with no resource node;
  - plus up to `abandonedSites` spots beside seeded abandoned buildings;
  - plus the four starters, which count as player areas.
  - The set is built lazily on the first bot spawn.
- pickAiSpawnPoint:
  - A seeded (world.rngFor) weighted pick, 1 / (1 + crowd)^crowdPow. Crowd counts the live humans and bots within crowdRadius plus spawns already handed out.
  - The point must be at least minPlayerDist from every human player and every starter point.
  - With probability nearPlayerShare (0.05) a nearer point is allowed, but never within onScreenTiles.
  - Claims, water and decks are skipped. If nothing qualifies, the farthest free point is used.
- Population bots, host bots (markVirtual) and AI respawns all use it. GameServerOptions.aiSpawn "starters" keeps the old placement; only fixtures use it.
- Respawn: own bed, then home (the remembered base via the setAiHomeLocator host hook) when homeFirst, then a distributed point. Hired workers and clan members keep the ADR-153 rule.
- A bot that spawns or respawns more than offscreen.fullSimTiles from every human starts in the ADR-324 off-screen sim:
  - it has no view and no chunk streaming;
  - offscreenPlan picks its own travel goals on the cooldown and plans routes within the per-tick budget;
  - it hands back to full sim (and the flag clears) when a human comes near.
- Caps are unchanged (maxBots, spawns.json caps), and netcode relevance is unchanged.

Tests:
- packages/gameplay/test/adr325_ai_spawn.test.ts
- apps/client/test/adr325_ai_spawn_live.test.ts
- The ADR-202/203/252 fixtures pin aiSpawn "starters".

## ADR-326: Safe spawn radius around world-wide AI spawn points (SurVivaZ)
- Problem: Task 33 put a 20-tile safe radius (SAFE_SPAWN_RADIUS) around the four installed starter spawn points only — no aggressive spawns inside, zombies / aggressive animals do not acquire or engage survivors inside, horde zombies exempt. ADR-325 added world-wide AI spawn points (up to 40 Vogel-spiral points plus up to 12 beside abandoned sites), and those had no safe zone at all: an AI human spawning at a world point could land straight into zombies or a wolf pack.
- Decision: the same 20-tile radius, same rules, extended to the ADR-325 points. No new knob: the radius is the shared SAFE_SPAWN_RADIUS in spawn_points.ts, not a second value in data/ai_spawn.json, so the two point sets can never drift apart (the JSON $comment records this).

Mechanism (packages/gameplay/src/spawn_points.ts, packages/gameplay/src/ai_spawn.ts):
- spawn_points.ts owns an "extra safe centres" resource (setExtraSafeSpawnPoints / extraSafeSpawnPoints). inSpawnSafeRadius now checks the installed starter points plus the extra centres.
- ai_spawn.ts setAiSpawnPoints forwards its points into that resource — eagerly when installed eagerly, or lazily through the same builder when installed lazily. A lazy set is therefore protected from the first spawn check, not only after the first bot spawns (the builder runs once, on first read, and is cached).
- The resource lives in spawn_points.ts rather than ai_spawn.ts because ai_spawn.ts imports spawn_points.ts: a resource key defined in ai_spawn.ts would need a second defineResource call here, and resource keys are object identity, so it would never match.
- No enforcement site changed: the legacy zombie spawner, zombie acquire, the population spawn gate and animal engage all already read inSpawnSafeRadius, so they all pick up the AI points with no edits (zombies.ts, population.ts untouched).
- Bare worlds are unchanged: with no points installed anywhere there is still no safe radius (Task 33 rule); AI points that fall back to the starters add nothing beyond the installed starter points.

Tests:
- packages/gameplay/test/adr326_ai_spawn_safety.test.ts (9 tests): the predicate covers world / site / starter-source AI points out to 20 tiles and nothing beyond, with no starter points installed; a lazy install is protected before any bot spawns and builds once; the legacy zombie spawner spawns around but never inside a world point; a zombie does not acquire a survivor inside; a horde zombie still chases inside (exempt); a wolf does not engage inside (with a no-AI-points control that does attack); the population spawner spawns nothing in a chunk fully covered by AI points (with a control that does spawn).
- Neighbouring suites re-run green: adr325_ai_spawn, task33_craft_death_safe_water, animals, population, spawn_points, task35_seed_safe_zone, task35_water_resources (51 tests).

## ADR-329: Route water sampling uses seeded terrain for unloaded regions (SurVivaZ)

Context (ADR-324): regionCost sampled water through inWater, which reads the loaded TileMap: an unloaded chunk
returns tile 0, and a world with no TerrainRes at all returns false, so both read as dry land. Region routes
therefore planned straight across unloaded lakes and through unloaded regions as if they were cheap dry land, and
only discovered the water when the chunk streamed in and the local nav had to cope.

Decision (packages/gameplay/src/ai/travel.ts, no travel.json change):
- Each region-cost sample resolves through regionSampleWater: loaded terrain wins (a TerrainRes with a loaded()
  hook — terrainFromTileMap — is consulted first, so shovel edits and flowing water, which only touch loaded
  ground per ADR-263, are honoured), and unloaded terrain is read from the seeded ProceduralGenerator instead of
  assumed land. A TerrainRes without a loaded() hook (test stubs, replicas) is treated as loaded, as before.
- The generator is `new ProceduralGenerator({ seed: world.seed })` with the default bands — the same generator the
  server builds its chunks from (apps/server/src/game.ts) — cached per world, so its tileAt is the generated tile
  at any (tx, ty) whether or not the chunk is loaded. Water is the movement swimTiles set (data/movement.json
  [1, 8]); worlds without a GameplayConfig fall back to that same set.
- Nothing else changes: the 5 samples per 16-tile region, the 1 + waterCostMul x wet-share cost (Infinity when
  all 5 are wet), the regionCostTtlTicks cache, the region-grid A* and the per-tick plan budget are untouched, so
  routes stay deterministic (no rng: same seed -> same route) and budgeted. A re-plan after the TTL picks up a
  chunk that has since loaded, with any edits in it.
- Honest cut: the seeded lookup is the generated terrain, not player edits in unloaded (persisted) chunks — edits
  can only be made on loaded ground, so an unloaded chunk has no edits a route could miss while it stays
  unloaded; once it loads, the loaded path (and the TTL expiry) takes over.

Tests: packages/gameplay/test/adr329_route_water.test.ts (a seeded all-water region costs Infinity with no chunk
loaded; every unloaded region's cost matches the seeded terrain, never silently cheap dry land; a route across a
seeded lake detours around the all-water region; loaded terrain wins over the seed in both directions; same seed
-> same route and costs on fresh worlds). The ADR-324 off-screen test now measures coarse progress along the route
instead of x displacement, because a detouring route advances the same 2.6 tiles/s along its legs while its x lags.

## ADR-328: gate_clan door swing last-frame pop (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-314 swings doors on the render clock (11 fps for `gate_clan`: swing1..4, then the piece's own open art). The swing step math is exact — steps change at 0 / 91 / 182 / 273 ms and the rest frame shows at 364 ms — and the frame geometry is identical across closed, swing1, swing4 and open (same 160x256 rect and anchor in every rotation), so the pop was not an off-by-one in frame indexing, an easing overshoot, or an art mismatch. What was seen instead, on the last frame of a `gate_clan` swing, was the gate blinking out and fading back in as open. The cause is one layer down, in the static chunk buffers (`SpriteBatch`, `packages/render/src/sprites.ts`): a swinging door is drawn dynamically, so it leaves its chunk's static list, and a newly created chunk fades in from alpha 0 over `chunkFadeIn` (0.35 s) from its `born` clock (`drawStatic`). A clan gate stands alone at a claim perimeter, so it is the piece most likely to be the only static piece in its 32x32 chunk; doors in walls share a chunk with other pieces and never hit this.

**Root cause.** During the swing the gate's chunk has an empty scratch list, and the rebuild loop deleted every chunk with an empty list as demolished. The chunk (with its `born`) was therefore gone by the second swing frame. When the swing ended and the gate returned to the static path, the chunk was recreated with `born = now`, so `drawStatic` drew the open gate at alpha 0 on that frame and ramped it to 1 over 0.35 s — the last-frame pop. The same blink would hit any lone piece that goes dynamic and returns (a faded occluder, a lit fire going out), not only swinging doors.

**Decision.** `SpriteBatch` now tracks, per gather, the chunk keys that had a piece drawn dynamically (`dynamicChunkKeys`, cleared each frame, recorded before the off-screen skip). In the rebuild loop, a chunk whose list is empty but whose key is dynamic is kept alive but empty (count 0, checksum updated, `maxZ` 0, `seen` refreshed, `born` preserved) instead of being deleted; its key stays in scratch, so it keeps its `seen` while the swing plays. No VBO re-upload is needed for the empty chunk — a count of 0 draws nothing, so the stale buffer contents are never visible. A chunk emptied by demolition (no dynamic piece) is still deleted in the same frame as before, and a genuinely new chunk still fades in from `born`. No change to swing timing, door art, the swing tracker, or the Canvas2D path (which has no static chunks and was never affected).

**Validation.** New `apps/client/test/adr328_gate_clan_pop.test.ts` drives `SpriteBatch.prepare` + `drawStatic` with a mock GL that captures the `uAlphaMul` uniform, a lone `gate_clan` and a `DoorView` swing: it failed before the fix (alpha 0 on the frame the swing ends, opening and closing) and passes after, and also asserts the swing actually played (dynamic instances visible through swing4) and the gate returned to static. The harness itself is validated by the baseline frames (a brand-new chunk fades in from 0; a settled chunk draws at 1). `apps/client/test/adr314_doors.test.ts` 10/10 and the full `packages/render/test` suite 475/475 pass; typecheck with the pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 is clean for `packages/render` (the client typecheck shows only the pre-existing local better-sqlite3 gap in `packages/persist`).

**Not changed.** Swing steps and timing, door art and frame geometry, the chunk fade-in for genuinely new chunks, demolition chunk deletion, and the Canvas2D renderer. Not verified visually — no GL in the VM; the numeric alpha test is the verification, and the user's eyes on the live build are the real check that the blink is gone.

## ADR-330: vehicle_net convergence flake (SurVivaZ)

**Test.** `apps/server/test/vehicle_net.test.ts`, "driver predicts its vehicle; converges to the server under latency, jitter and 10% loss" (ADR-102): a client drives a `car_offroad` at full boost for 80 ticks under `{ latencyMs: 80, jitterMs: 20, loss: 0.1 }` and asserts the client's predicted position never strays more than 4 tiles from the server's (`maxErr < 4`), then converges to < 0.05 with 0 snaps after coasting to a stop. CI failed it intermittently at ~4.22.

**Reproduction.** Reproduced locally on the first run (4.224988912613346), and in 5 of 20 repeated runs of the single test pre-fix — every failure the bit-identical value 4.224988912613346, 15 passes. An instrumented copy of the test (temporary file, deleted after use) sampled the error per tick: maxErr takes only the values 2.535 / 3.38 / 4.225 across 14 runs — exactly 3 / 4 / 5 ticks of travel at top speed. The better-sqlite3 server-test load gap did NOT block this test locally: it loads and runs.

**Diagnosis — two causes, neither a netcode bug.**
1. The bound was inside the model's own range. One tick at top speed is `13 tiles/s x 1.3 boost x 0.05 s = 0.845` tiles. The client's steady-state lead is the round trip: `(80 + 0..20) ms` each way, so RTT 160–200 ms = 3.2–4 ticks; the measured plateau is exactly 3.38 tiles = 200 ms x 16.9 tiles/s. On top of that the server applies one input per tick with no catch-up (ADR-191), so a loss burst or late snapshots leave its input queue 1–3 ticks deeper — each extra tick adds 0.845 tiles. The observed worst case is 5 ticks = 4.225 tiles, above the limit of 4. Prediction/reconciliation itself is exact: the final convergence (< 0.05) and `snaps == 0` assertions passed in every trajectory, failing runs included — the client is correctly ahead by RTT + queueing, not diverging.
2. The run-to-run flip is wall-clock chunk loading shifting the loopback RNG. `ChunkManager.update()` budgets loads by wall time (`performance.now()`, `maxLoadTimeMs: 2`, `apps/server/src/game.ts`), so which tick each chunk loads (and streams to the client via TileSync) varies with machine load. The `LoopbackNetwork` shares one seeded RNG across all links, so a one-message difference in per-tick traffic (observed: 54–57 messages sent before the drive; three distinct RNG states at drive start) re-rolls every later jitter/loss draw, and the lead lands on 3, 4, or 5 ticks. Two runs with the identical RNG state at drive start still diverged mid-drive (3.38 vs 4.225), because chunk streaming continues as the vehicle moves into new chunks. The chunk time budget is intentional production frame pacing and was not changed.

**Fix (test only).** `expect(maxErr).toBeLessThan(4)` → `toBeLessThan(6)`, with the derivation in the test comment. 6 tiles is ~7.1 ticks of lead at top speed: RTT-max (4 ticks, 3.38 tiles) plus 3 ticks of loss/queue excursion, covering the observed 5-tick worst case (4.225) with 2 ticks of headroom. A real prediction failure would be far larger and would also trip the independent final-convergence (< 0.05) and `snaps == 0` assertions, so the test still guards what it claims to guard. No production code changed.

**Validation.** Full `apps/server/test/vehicle_net.test.ts`: 9/9 pass. The fixed test repeated 10/10 pass (pre-fix it failed 5/20). Typecheck with the pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 for `apps/server`: 8 errors, all pre-existing local-environment gaps (missing `@types/ws`, missing `better-sqlite3` types) in files this change does not touch; zero errors in `vehicle_net.test.ts`.

**Honest cuts.** The wall-clock chunk-budget nondeterminism remains, so the test's maxErr still varies run to run (2.535–4.225 observed); the bound absorbs it rather than removing it. The bound is set from the observed worst case plus the mechanism, not an exhaustive sweep: a pathological alignment (RTT-max plus a 4-tick excursion, ~6.76 tiles) could in principle exceed 6, but it was never observed in ~35 runs and would need a multi-packet loss burst at top speed.

## ADR-327: Hired workers run the saddle-material chain (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-323 left hired workers out of the saddle chain ("they work their job"): a hired worker never
planned saddle materials, even though unhired AI did (liked-food fetch plus saddle-material planning with a
tier pick, a depth cap, timeout fallback and danger abandon). A second part of the gap: an affordable saddle
tier needs every station already at the base — for a hired worker, that base is the employer's, not its own.

**Decision.** A hired worker runs the saddle chain as a LOW-priority goal, only when it has no pending job
work and its survival needs are met, and it never abandons or delays employer job work for the chain:
- **Idle gate** (`fillHireSensors`, `view.hire.idle`): no pending job work — no defend / farm / repair target,
  no craft recipe or craft-supply fetch, no Maintain shelter / earth plan with a step or leaves, and no wanted
  gather node for a Gather / Craft job (a node wanted only for saddle leaves is the chain itself, not job
  work) — and needs met on the same danger thresholds ADR-323 abandons on (hp < `minHp`, hunger or thirst
  < 30, zombie within `safeTiles`). A Follow worker is never idle: its duty is proximity, so any saddle trip
  would abandon the owner.
- **Employer's base:** `buildAgentView` now runs `fillHireSensors` before `fillMountSensors`, so the saddle
  tier pick (`saddleGoalPass`) reads the hire sensors and the employer's base scan (`view.base` / `view.bs`
  re-anchored by `fillHireSensors`) — stations must already stand at the employer's base, and the plan's
  stock counts are the employer's storage. The saddle plan itself is built in `fillHireSensors` (on the
  employer's base), because that function deletes the planner's own-base plan for hired workers; when the
  worker is not idle, or the goal is unresolvable, no plan is left behind.
- **Same rules as unhired bots:** storage access still goes through `mayTakeFromStorage` (own / employer /
  clan storage only — a stranger's claimed box is never counted or withdrawn from); the timeout
  (`saddlePlanTimeoutTicks` -> tier ban -> fall back a tier) and the danger / low-needs abandon
  (`saddleAbandonsToFallback` abandons -> fall back) run on the existing `saddleGoalPass` paths unchanged.
  Danger / low needs also drops the hired worker's saddle plan the same tick, because the idle gate in
  `fillHireSensors` re-checks needs before building it.
- **Gather leg:** the early `fillHireSensors` call in `computeGoalSensors` now runs for every hired worker
  (it previously ran only for Maintain), so an idle worker's saddle leaves reach the gather pick like job
  items (added to `needs` / `jobItems`, and the hired gather guard lets saddle-leaf nodes through for
  Defend / Farm jobs — Follow never has a saddle plan, so the exception is vacuous there). No new knobs in
  `data/mounts.json`, no new commands.

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr327_hired_saddle_chain.test.ts` (12 tests): an idle hired
worker with the employer's mount plans saddle materials from the employer's stations + storage and runs the
chain end to end (withdraw hide -> craft rope / leather / thread / saddle -> equip); no stations at the
employer's base means no goal; pending Craft work, a Defend zombie at the anchor, and Follow all block the
chain; a stranger's claimed box is never counted (hide becomes a gather / hunt leaf instead) while the
employer's box is withdrawn from; timeout falls back a tier; danger abandons the goal and the plan, retries
later, and falls back after repeated abandons; determinism and the `planMaxDepth` cap. One existing
assertion updated for the intentional sensor change: `task22_recruitment.test.ts` now expects `hire` to
carry `idle: true` for an idle Gather worker. Full `packages/gameplay/test` suite 1564 passed / 3 skipped;
typecheck with the pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 is clean for `packages/gameplay` (the client typecheck shows
only the pre-existing local gaps — missing `peerjs` / `ws` / `better-sqlite3` types — in files this change
does not touch).

**Honest cuts.** Follow workers never run the chain (a deliberate call, not an oversight — see above). The
gather leg only serves saddle leaves while the saddle plan is active; a hired worker whose job work appears
mid-gather finishes the current think tick's walk before the job behaviour retakes over (the plan itself is
dropped at once). Not verified on a live server with players or on a real phone — the end-to-end test drives
the behaviours through the same commands a live worker would send, but no live playtest has watched a hired
worker saddle its mount.

## ADR-332: Minify shipped JSON manifests at build/copy time (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The Pages artifact is ~891 MB; shipped JSON is 79.3 MB in the baseline dist (83,202,610 bytes across 146 files), most of it pretty-print whitespace in pack manifests and atlas layouts. Source files stay pretty-printed for editing; only the dist copy needs to be compact.

**Decision.** `apps/client/vite.config.ts` gains an exported `copyArtFile(src, dst)` used by the `closeBundle` art copy: `*.json` files are re-stringified compact (`JSON.parse` then `JSON.stringify` with no whitespace) as they are copied into `dist/art`; non-JSON files copy verbatim with `cpSync`. A JSON that fails to parse fails the build here rather than shipping corrupt data. The dev server still serves the pretty source files unchanged, and `manifests.index.json` keeps its 1-space indent (it is generated, not copied).

**Validation.** New `apps/client/test/adr332_json_minify.test.ts` (3 tests): `copyArtFile` compacts `pack/manifest.json` with parsed output equal to parsed source, no newlines, smaller file; non-JSON files copy byte-identical; every JSON served by the art mounts minifies to the same parsed value — compared with a recursive `===` comparator because the source contains `-0` values (`JSON.stringify(-0)` is `"0"`, and `-0 === 0` for every consumer; vitest's `toEqual` distinguishes them). Real `vite build` (BASE=/SurVivaZ/, VITE_DEFAULT_OFFLINE=1): dist 988,942,726 → 947,540,750 bytes (−41,401,976, ~39.5 MiB); JSON bytes 83,202,610 → 41,800,634. The build itself still fails at rollup on the known sparse-checkout gap (`assets/ui/input/atlas/input_glyphs.json` missing, `src/tutorial/overlay.ts`) after the art copy runs, so the measured dist is art-only — same failure mode as the clean-base build. Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `vite.config.ts` clean; `apps/client` project typecheck shows only the 3 pre-existing `src/tutorial/overlay.ts` errors from the missing `input_glyphs.json`.

**Honest cuts.** Minification saves bytes on disk and over the wire only; parsed data is identical, so no runtime behaviour change. Nothing verified on a real phone.

## ADR-331: Test coverage for off-screen hand-back, bot restore, homestead relocation, long-trip riding and spread spawns (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Grok's ADR-324/325 handoff listed five areas as untested: the live off-screen hand-back after
a far respawn; restoring a saved bot account over the new spawn placement; relocated homesteads being rebuilt;
mount riding on long trips; multiplayer with several humans and spread AI spawns. This ADR adds the coverage
only — no production behaviour was intended to change — and the live tests caught one real bug (below).

**Tests.**
- `packages/gameplay/test/adr331_open_items_coverage.test.ts` (8 tests):
  - *Far respawn hand-back (gameplay half):* a bot that dies and respawns at a distributed point far from every
    human steps off-screen along its route (offscreenPlan picks the goal, offscreenStep moves it), then hands back
    when a human comes near — `spawnedOffscreen` clears, the same route object and leg continue in full sim, and
    the bot walks it to the goal.
  - *Saved bot restore:* a JSON-restored identity keeps its base, travel route/leg and off-screen flag; respawn
    honours the restored home (bed -> home -> distributed point) and, with no restored home, lands on a
    distributed point, never a starter.
  - *Relocated homestead rebuild:* a free AI's relocate trip (picked every `relocateEvery` explorations) drops its
    old base on arrival and bumps `stats.relocations`; the next sense picks a new site 5..9 tiles from the new home,
    and the planner rebuilds the campfire -> basic storage box -> workbench ladder there (claim planted first, ADR-310).
  - *Long-trip riding:* a bot with its own horse mounts at once (inside `mountReach`) and rides for the bulk of a
    400-tile trip (`rode / samples > 0.8`), dismounting on arrival; a short trip does not mount (`longTripTiles`);
    a riding horse is stopped and dismounted at a doorway edge (`dismountReason` "clearance", donkeys still fit).
  - *Spread spawns:* with four humans spread across the world, 120 picks still spread over >= 90% of the eligible
    world-wide points (high entropy, bounded pile-ups), stay >= `minPlayerDist` from every human (or >=
    `onScreenTiles` for the low near share), never use a starter point except in the near share, and cover >= 6 of
    8 sectors; deterministic for the same seed and human spread.
  - *For-hire respawn regression (the bug below):* a Worker record with `owner: 0` still gets the distributed
    respawn; only `owner != 0` (actually hired) keeps the ADR-153 nearest-starter rule.
- `apps/client/test/adr331_open_items_coverage.test.ts` (2 live tests on the real local server):
  - *Live hand-back after a far respawn:* a bot is killed, respawns far from the human (retrying a near-share pick),
    starts off-screen (`spawnedOffscreen`, no chunk streaming); a human teleporting next to it hands it back
    (flag clears, chunk streams again), and it keeps travelling in full sim (along-route progress / displacement;
    strict route/leg continuity is the gameplay test's job — a live bot also gathers and may be out of stamina, so
    the live tail waits for progress, not speed).
  - *Live saved-account restore:* a bot's AiMemory base is saved, the server restarts on the same store, the
    restored bot keeps its base, does not land on a starter point, and respawns at its remembered home.

**Bug found by the live tests (fixed here, one line).** `aiRespawnPoint` (`packages/gameplay/src/ai_spawn.ts`)
returned undefined for any bot carrying a Worker record, intending "hired workers keep the ADR-153 rule". But
`recruitmentSystem` gives *every* AI human a Worker record with `owner: 0` (for hire, not hired), so on a live
server no bot ever took the ADR-325 distributed respawn — every bot respawned at the nearest starter point. The
live tests failed exactly there (respawn on top of the human; 809 tiles from the restored home). The guard now
requires a non-zero owner, matching every other "hired" check in the codebase (`travelMode`, `fillHireSensors`,
`mount_behaviors`), and the for-hire regression test pins it. No other site used the bare `has(e, Worker)` test.

**Validation.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr331_open_items_coverage.test.ts` 8/8; `apps/client/test/adr331_open_items_coverage.test.ts`
2/2 (twice); neighbours re-run green: adr324, adr325, adr326, adr327, adr325 live, task33 safe spawn, spawn_points,
population, adr321, adr323, task22 recruitment, adr259 worker orders, adr252 (155 tests across those suites).
Typecheck with the pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean; `apps/client` shows only the pre-existing
local gaps (missing `peerjs` / `@types/ws` / `better-sqlite3` types, `input_glyphs.json`), zero errors in the new files.

**Honest cuts.** The live hand-back test waits for route progress rather than asserting speed: a live bot gathers
en route and can be out of stamina, so its along-route advance varies run to run (chunk-load timing shifts the
loopback RNG, as ADR-330 describes). Nothing was verified on a real phone.

## ADR-334: Ship m4a audio only, drop ogg (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The Pages artifact is ~891 MB; dist audio is ogg 21.8 MB + m4a 19.6 MB. The ADR-117
mixer tried ogg first with m4a fallback, so both copies shipped. No re-encoding: the m4a files
already exist.

**Coverage (the gate).** `packages/assets/pack` holds 741 ogg (732 under `audio/`, 9 under
`vehicles/audio/`) and 706 m4a. The bank (`apps/client/src/audio/bank.json`) references 706
files — every one has an m4a twin (706/706). 35 ogg files have no m4a twin; per the ADR's STOP
rule none of them is dropped: 26 sit under `pack/audio/` and 9 under `pack/vehicles/audio/`.
The 9 vehicle files never shipped anyway (the vite MOUNTS filter's vehicles branch only allows
manifest + atlases). The 26 are referenced only by the legacy
`packages/assets/pack/audio/manifest.json`, which no client code reads — the ADR-117 bank is the
only runtime loader path, and no `src` file constructs an `.ogg` URL outside it.

**Decision.** `bank.json` formats `["ogg", "m4a", "mp3"]` → `["m4a", "mp3"]`, so
`SoundBank.urlsFor` / `resolve` emit `.m4a` first and never `.ogg`; the stale
"ogg/opus first" comment in `bank.ts` is corrected. The generic `AudioFormat` union and MIME
map are left alone (format vocabulary, still used by ordering tests with ogg fixtures) — the
loader can only request formats listed in the bank. The vite MOUNTS filter change IS in
this commit (applied by the coordinator after ADR-332/333 landed): it drops ogg generally but keeps
the 26 twin-less ogg files shipping by name, so the shipped set loses exactly 706 ogg files
(22,372,623 bytes, ~21.3 MiB) and keeps 464,873 bytes of legacy ogg. Full m4a-only shipping
needs those 26 re-encoded to m4a or confirmed dead and removed from the legacy manifest —
out of scope here. Note: `bank.json`'s header says it is generated by
`scripts/gen-audio-bank.mjs`, but that script no longer exists in-repo, so the file was edited
directly; the $comment records that.

**Validation.** New ADR-334 tests in `apps/client/test/audio_bank.test.ts` (3 tests): shipped
formats are exactly `["m4a", "mp3"]`; every bank file's first resolved URL ends `.m4a` and no
URL ends `.ogg`; every bank-referenced file has an m4a twin on disk. Audio suites green
(audio_bank 9/9, audio_events 12/12, audio_mixer 8/8, audio_spatial 5/5 — 34/34 across the four suites). Typecheck with pinned
TypeScript 5.9.3: `apps/client` shows only 3 errors, all pre-existing in `src/tutorial/overlay.ts`
(`input_glyphs.json` import + `unknown` locals; also present in the pre-change baseline run, which
showed 14 including transient `peerjs` / `@types/ws` / `better-sqlite3` module-resolution errors
that cleared between runs), zero in the touched files.

**Honest cuts.** A real Safari listen test is impossible in this VM — m4a/AAC is Safari's native
format and the mixer falls back to the synth placeholder if a file fails to decode, but the
user should confirm sound on Safari (and on Chrome/Firefox, which now fetch m4a instead of
ogg) on the live build. Nothing was verified on a real phone.
## ADR-333: Exclude customization_v2_sample from dist (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The Pages artifact is ~891 MB; the dev-only v2 character-art sample (`packages/assets/pack/customization_v2_sample`, 26,877,721 bytes in the baseline dist) ships to every player even though only the opt-in `?charArt=v2s` preview ever fetches it. Default players (v1) never fetch it: `packages/assets/src/manifest-index.ts` appends the fragment only when `charArt` is v2s/v2s-all (`withCharArtFragment`, called from `apps/client/src/view.ts`), and it is not in `MANIFEST_INDEX`, so `manifests.index.json` never lists it.

**Decision.** Remove `customization_v2_sample` from the pack-mount filter alternation in `apps/client/vite.config.ts`, so the sample is neither copied into `dist/art` nor served by the dev server. The files stay in the repo for dev. Accepted consequence (user-approved): the opt-in `?charArt=v2s` preview breaks — with v2s enabled the client will request the fragment and get a 404 instead of the sample art.

**Validation.** New `apps/client/test/adr333_v2_sample_excluded.test.ts` (3 tests): the sample files still exist in the repo; `artServed`/`artFile` return false/undefined for the sample manifest and atlases; neighbouring pack mounts (`pack/manifest.json`, vehicles, task34, customization) are still served. Clean rebuild (`rm -rf dist`, then `vite build` with BASE=/SurVivaZ/, VITE_DEFAULT_OFFLINE=1): dist 947,540,750 → 920,676,753 bytes (−26,863,997, ~25.6 MiB); `dist/art/pack/customization_v2_sample` absent; JSON count 146 → 145. Note the build still fails at rollup on the known sparse-checkout gap (`assets/ui/input/atlas/input_glyphs.json` missing) after the art copy runs, so the measured dist is art-only — and that a failing build does not empty `dist`, so the delta was measured from a clean rebuild, not the incremental one (whose stale v2 files survived). Combined with ADR-332, dist is 988,942,726 → 920,676,753 bytes (−68,265,973, ~65.1 MiB). Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `vite.config.ts` clean; `apps/client` project typecheck shows only the 3 pre-existing `src/tutorial/overlay.ts` errors from the missing `input_glyphs.json`.

**Honest cuts.** Default (v1) players lose nothing — the sample was never fetched for them. The v2s preview is gone until/unless the sample is re-included or served another way. Nothing verified on a real phone.

## ADR-339: AI humans tame a mount of their own choice (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-321/323 gave AI humans tame/ride/saddle/look-after-mount behaviour, and mounts can die;
the missing piece of the user's Task 37 question 4 was "of their choice" — no preference existed, so a
bot tamed whichever rideable animal scored best on gallop/hp/distance. Feeding preference already
existed (`bestMountFood` is love-first) and no re-tame gap existed (`fillMountSensors` only computes
`tameMount` in the no-own-mount branch), so the only gap was the tame-target pick itself.

**Decision.** `packages/gameplay/src/ai/mount_preference.ts` derives a bot's liked species deterministically
from its own PlayerId (`fnv1a("mount:<playerId>")` over `MOUNT_SPECIES`, plus the species' first love
food), stored as a tuning knob `preferredSpeciesBonus: 10` in the `bots` section of
`packages/gameplay/data/mounts.json`. `pickTameTarget` in `ai/mount_behaviors.ts` takes a
`preferredSpecies` parameter (default 0 = no bonus, old behaviour) and adds the bonus to the ADR-321
score; both call sites (`tameTarget` and the `foodSensors` pre-fetch) pass
`preferredMount(playerIdOf(world, self)).species` — the bot's OWN taste, while tames are still
recorded under the employer via `mountOwnerIdFor`, so a hired worker keeps its own preference. The
bonus (10) provably dominates the max inter-species score spread (gallop 3.2 + hp/60 2.83 + distance
3.6 = 9.63), so a liked species in `seekRadius` always wins; the fallback is unchanged when the
liked species is absent. No keep-alive guard and no feeding change were needed (verified: no re-tame
gap; love-first feeding already exists). No new `AgentWorldView` field.

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr339_mount_preference.test.ts` (11 tests) for the
preference derivation and scoring; new `packages/gameplay/test/adr339_mount_wiring.test.ts` (3 tests)
proving the wiring through `fillMountSensors`: liked species wins at equal distance, plain ADR-321
pick when the liked species is absent, no tame target while the bot's own mount lives and a liked
target again after it dies. Neighbours re-run green: adr321/adr323/adr327 (38/38). Typecheck with
pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** A bot whose liked species never spawns near it tames exactly as before (no
preference is visible). Nothing verified on a real phone.
## ADR-336: AI humans have their own lives, wants and moods when idle (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Bots already had goals/planner, homesteading, travel, clan-stay vs roam — but no
wants/aspirations/personality layer: nothing made one bot differ from another when it had nothing to
do, and nothing let a bot act like a person (eat a favourite food, make a keepsake, visit water,
socialize, tend a garden, rest). The user's Task 37 questions 1–2.

**Decision.** `packages/gameplay/src/ai/life.ts` + data `packages/gameplay/data/ai_life.json` add:
personality derived deterministically from the bot's stable identity id (core traits from
`rollTraits` + curiosity/rhythm/favourite food/keepsake from `fnv1a` streams — same technique as
the Task 25 dye colour and Task 22 recruitment wanted-item; the local `fnv1a` copy was replaced
with the identical one from `@engine/core` because `vehicle_craft.ts`/`vehicles.ts` already
export that name); six data-driven wants (favourite food, keepsake craft, visit water, socialize,
tend garden, rest); pure moods (`deriveMood`: weary > lonely > restless > cheerful > content);
routines gated by rhythm → day-phase. The layer runs ONLY when the bot is otherwise idle: hired
bots only under the ADR-327 `view.hire.idle` flag, unhired bots only when `makePlan` returns
`"idle"` with no step/leaves/hunt, no danger within 12 tiles, and hunger ≥ 55 / thirst ≥ 55 /
hp ≥ 0.5, not cold. Wired in `packages/gameplay/src/agents.ts`: `fillLifeSensors` is the LAST
sensor in `buildAgentView` (it must see the final `view.plan` / `view.hire.idle` / `view.travel` /
`view.farm` / `view.mount`) and `lifeBehaviors()` (`life_want`) joins `survivorRegistry` after
`hireBehaviors()`. Persistence is a separate `identity.aiLife` record (`lifeStateOf` /
`flushAiLife`, 300-tick debounce) flushed from `apps/client/src/local.ts` next to
`flushAiMemory`/`flushSocialMemory` (removal, periodic, shutdown); `game.agents.put`
shallow-merges partials so `{ aiLife }` never clobbers `ai` / `social`. No `planner.ts` change was
needed. Behaviours only move the bot and emit the action strings / commands a human client sends;
the server validates reach, recipes and costs as for players.

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr336_ai_life.test.ts` (33 tests) for personality
determinism, moods, routines, the idle gate, want picks and the persistence round-trip; new
`packages/gameplay/test/adr336_life_wiring.test.ts` (4 tests) proving the wiring through the real
view: an idle hired worker gets `eat_favourite` and `life_want` emits `eat:<slot>` (completion
recorded in life state), a Follow worker gets no want, the registry carries `life_want`.
Neighbours re-run green: adr252/adr327/adr259/task22 recruitment (61/61). Typecheck with pinned
TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean; `apps/client` shows only the 3 pre-existing
`src/tutorial/overlay.ts` errors from the missing `input_glyphs.json`, zero in `local.ts`.

**Honest cuts.** `visit_water` rarely fires for spawn-homed bots: a step-2 scan of [-150,150]² in
the seed-42 test world found no `nearWater` tile, so bots homed near spawn have no water within
the search radius (the slice tests use a fake lake). Nothing verified on a real phone.
## ADR-338: AI humans defend their own claimed territory with barbed wire and turrets (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The Defend job existed and `barbed_wire` + arrow/bolt/flame turrets existed as pieces,
but AI humans had no claims of their own and never chose to build defences — the user's Task 37
question 5. Defence is deliberately NOT in `makePlan` (planner.ts was off-limits for this slice);
`planDefence` + `hasSurplus` are reusable if that changes later.

**Decision.** `packages/gameplay/src/ai/defence.ts` + data `packages/gameplay/data/ai_defence.json`
add: threat as a pure `assessThreat` over sightings (1) / kills (2) / livestock losses (3) / recent
close attack (+2) in a 1-day window (24000 ticks), levels from thresholds [1,3,6]; builds only at
level ≥ 2 AND with surplus (after paying cost, reserve wood 12 / stone 8 / planks 4 remains, and no
cost item on the plan's gather leaves). Wire first along the claim perimeter (max 8, ring at
radius − 2), then one turret of each kind cheapest first (arrow → bolt → flame, max 3, diagonal
offsets around the base anchor). Every candidate passes a ghost preview (`snapPlacement` +
`validatePlacement`, cost/range ignored). Hired workers and bots without their own claim get no
target. Wired in `packages/gameplay/src/agents.ts`: `fillDefenceSensors` runs after
`fillHireSensors` (it needs `view.base` / `view.bs` / `view.plan` and skips hired workers) and
`defenceBehaviors()` (`build_defence`) joins `survivorRegistry` after `hireBehaviors()`; the
behaviour withdraws missing materials from base storage first, then emits the standard `build:`
action, and scores only when a target exists, the planner has no step, the bot is not hired, and
no zombie is close. Threat memory is a separate `identity.defence` record (`defenceMemoryOf` /
`flushDefenceMemory`, 300-tick debounce) flushed from `apps/client/src/local.ts` next to
`flushAiMemory` / `flushSocialMemory` / `flushAiLife`. Two real bugs were fixed in-slice: a missing
`cclose` after the final withdraw, and close being bare `cclose` (not `cclose:<id>`).

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr338_ai_defence.test.ts` (27 tests) for threat
assessment, surplus gating, wire-before-turret ordering, placement inside the bot's own claim,
one-piece-at-a-time and no-claim → no-plan; new
