`packages/gameplay/test/adr338_defence_wiring.test.ts` (7 tests) proving the wiring through the
real view: a threatened bot with its own claim and surplus gets a `barbed_wire` target, no target
at level 0/1, none without a claim, none when hired, the registry carries `build_defence`, and
threat events persist through `flushDefenceMemory`. Neighbours re-run green:
adr252/adr310/adr315/adr259/adr221 (70/70). Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3:
`packages/gameplay` clean; `apps/client` shows only the 3 pre-existing
`src/tutorial/overlay.ts` errors from the missing `input_glyphs.json`, zero in `local.ts`.

**Honest cuts.** Defence is not in `makePlan`, so it cannot compete with planner goals — it only
fires when the planner has no step. No turret ammo stocking; kills only count when witnessed;
livestock loss is a head-count drop. Nothing verified on a real phone.
## ADR-337: AI humans claim and build — repair/rebuild abandoned structures or build their own home (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Seeded abandoned structures (ADR-300/301), the Claim Flag (ADR-310/315) and the
build systems (`BASE_SLOTS` 2×2 hut, `pickBaseSite`) all existed, but no AI ever used them — the
user's Task 37 question 3. Hired bots never claim.

**Decision.** `packages/gameplay/src/ai/claim_build.ts` + data `packages/gameplay/data/ai_claim.json`
add: `chooseClaim` is deterministic — nearest suitable ruin within 12 tiles (unclaimed, intact ≥ 0.5,
damaged ≤ 0.7, no claim overlap via `siteClaimOk`, ghost-placeable flag slot), else `pickBaseSite`
new site with a per-bot variant (`homestead` / `garden` / `fenced` / `workshop`,
`variants[PlayerId % 4]`), far ruin as fallback. The stage machine is recomputed per sense tick:
ruin = flag → reclaim → repair (hp < 60%, own-claim + skill gate, exact server repair cost) →
rebuild from the regenerated planned layout (`planAbandonedSite` pure in seed/origin/kind/rot;
20-tick cache) → done, `BASE_SLOTS` fallback when no rotation matches. New = flag →
`mem.base` handoff to the planner (ladder builds hut) → variant extras → done. Ruin homes never
get `mem.base` (the planner would build `BASE_SLOTS` over the ruin); the ruin marker is the home
record. Flag cost is 10 wood + 10 stone + 2 dye (`pieces.json`), not "10 logs" as the brief said.
Wired in `packages/gameplay/src/agents.ts` (`claimBuildBehaviors()` after `autonomyBehaviors()`),
`packages/gameplay/src/ai/autonomy.ts` (`fillClaimSensors` in `computeGoalSensors` after
`bindAgentWorld` and BEFORE the `fillPlanSensors` block, its leaves merged into `needs` after it;
`"claimTarget"` / `"claimPlan"` added to `SENSOR_KEYS`; the legacy reclaim sensor is gated so it
does not double-drive a ruin the claim layer owns) and `packages/gameplay/src/ai/base_behaviors.ts`
(claim materials merged into the planner priority chain after the saddle goal).
Coordinator fix (caught by the ADR-252 live test during the full gate): the wiring as first
landed starved the homestead ladder two ways, and the live bots built no campfire/box/workbench,
no earthworks and no 2×2 base in 3000 ticks. (1) Claim materials fed into `makePlan`'s priority
chain became the plan GOAL — the bot's goal read "dye" (flag) then "clay" (flower-bed extra) and it
wandered gathering while its hut stayed unbuilt. The priority merge is removed: claim materials
join the gather `needs` only (the sensor still publishes them on the `claimPriority` blackboard,
pinned by the slice test), and the flag is still built promptly by the planner's own flag-first
rule plus `claim_build` when the materials are in hand. (2) Variant extras are decoration, not
shelter: `planOwnHome` now returns the extras plan with no step until the hut (`BASE_SLOTS`)
stands, so a bot never spends homesteading ticks on fences / garden beds / a flower bed before
its hut and bed exist. The slice test for flag → extras was updated to raise the hut first (and
pins the waiting state: stage "extras", no step, before the hut). With both fixes the ADR-252
live test passes 8/8 again. (3) Coordinator fix (caught by the ADR-321 long-trip ride test in the
full gate): `chooseClaim` anchored its new-site pick on the bot's current position while the
planner anchors every site pick on `view.home` — a bot 70 tiles from home claimed the ground
under its feet, the adopted base made `return_home` walk to the base's porch 7 tiles away instead
of riding home, and `wantsRide` never fired (trip < `longTripTiles`). `chooseClaim` now takes an
optional home anchor and `fillClaimSensors` passes `view.home`; the ruin scan uses the same
anchor. Pinned by a new wiring test (bot at (0,0), home (70,0): claim and adopted base within 12
tiles of home, `return_home`'s navGoal > 30 tiles out, `wantsRide` true). Neighbours re-run green:
adr300/adr301/adr311/adr252/modular_building/adr331 (61/61) — the ADR-331 relocated-homestead
test failed once during wiring (see the coordinator fix above) and passes with it. Typecheck with
pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** Ruin homes have no full base behaviour yet (planner flag in `planner.ts` not
built). Nothing verified on a real phone.

## ADR-340: Ruin homes get full base behaviour (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-337 deliberately withheld `mem.base` from ruin homes (the planner would build
`BASE_SLOTS` over the ruin), so a bot living in a reclaimed ruin got none of the base ladder: no
furnishing, no hearth, no bed, no upgrades, no base storage through the planner path.

**Decision.** `PlanInput` gains `ruinBase` (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/planner.ts`), set by
`fillPlanSensors` from the new `ruinHomeAnchor(world, self, agent)` in
`packages/gameplay/src/ai/claim_build.ts` — the ruin centre minus 1 (anchor+1 = ruin centre, the
hut anchor convention), defined only once the bot owns the ruin and it is reclaimed (claimedBy =
own PlayerId, `siteUnclaimed` false); during flag / reclaim, or for hired bots (whose target the
sensor clears), it is undefined. `makePlan` reads one `home = base ?? ruinBase` anchor: the
`piece` (campfire / storage / workbench / furnace / anvil), `furnish`, `bed`, `upgrade`, `cook`
and winter / evening fuel pre-goals run against it, while the `base` goal still requires `p.base`
and never fires for a ruin home. Details: the hearth goal is satisfied by any campfire station in
the ruin scan (the ladder's campfire piece goal builds one first; the HEARTH slot is the second
chance when every campfire spot has failed); the bed uses `BED_SLOT` with no `complete` gate (the
spare spots around a ruin are bare ground and all fail the ghost check with NoSupport — a bed
needs a deck, and the ruin floor is the deck); the upgrade goal scans tiered pieces within
`upgradeRadius` of the ruin centre instead of `bs.pieces` (ruins have no `BASE_SLOTS` pieces in
the scan). `fillPlanSensors` (`base_behaviors.ts`) passes `ruinBase` + the ruin scan to `makePlan`
and sets `view.bs` to the ruin scan (so warm_up, sleep-by-fire and the Task 30 `lowFire` refuel
behaviour see the ruin's stations / storage / fires), while `view.base` stays unset — goTo's door
logic, `insideBase` and sleep-in-bed all key on the 2x2 hut geometry, which a ruin does not have.
A dropped ruin home deletes a stale `view.bs`. The freezing / fuel-need checks read the merged
`homeBs` scan. Tuning knobs (`furnishRadius`, `upgradeRadius`) live in the new
`packages/gameplay/data/ai_ruin.json`. The ADR-337 stage machine, the `mem.base` handoff for new
builds and the claim layer's flag → reclaim → repair → rebuild → done flow are untouched; the
earthworks ladder/light path still requires a real base (earth slots are relative to the earth
anchor, which a ruin anchor must not reinterpret).

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr340_ruin_base.test.ts` (15 tests): the adoption
gate (undefined until claimed + reclaimed, anchor centres the ruin, hired / taken / new-home bots
adopt nothing); the ladder walks straight past `base` to `bed`; the ruin bot builds its campfire
inside the ruin, never plans a redundant hearth (the HEARTH-slot fallback is pinned with all
campfire spots failed), beds on the ruin floor then furnishes (a standing table satisfies the
goal), ruin storage counts toward goals and bed materials withdraw from the ruin box, the upgrade
goal targets the lowest-tier ruin wall at the max tier; wiring through `buildAgentView` (plan +
`view.bs` set, `view.base` / `mem.base` unset, no competing site after the cooldown), a lit low
ruin campfire is the Task 30 refuel target, and the new-build `mem.base` handoff is unchanged.
Two real findings while writing the tests, both fixed in the slice: the bed cannot go on spare
spots (NoSupport — bare ground), so it uses `BED_SLOT`; and the test rig's 99 x 25 stock overflowed
the 24-slot player bag, so the walk stocks lean (8 types x 20) and consumes craft ingredients.
Neighbours re-run green: adr337 / adr252 / adr331 / adr321 (8 files, 82 tests). Typecheck with
pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** A ruin whose `BED_SLOT` is occupied retries the bed 6 times then gives up (the
same fails mechanism as a blocked bed in a built hut) — no fallback spot search. A ruin bot with
stale `mem.earth` from a destroyed built home keeps the old earthworks plan (pre-existing; the
earthworks path only guards the ladder/light build against a ruin anchor). Nothing verified on a
real phone.
## ADR-341: Defence wired into makePlan as a first-class plan goal (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-338 deliberately kept defence out of `makePlan`: `fillDefenceSensors`
planned a target only when the planner had no step, so defence could never compete with
planner goals. The user asked for it wired in (the Task 37 follow-up).

**Decision.** `makePlan` gains a `defence` goal (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/planner.ts`,
`GOAL_LADDER` after `bed`, before `furnish`) that calls ADR-338's `planDefence` with the
same gating: threat level ≥ 2, own claim, surplus after the data reserve (wood 12 / stone 8 /
planks 4, no cost item on the plan's gather leaves), wire first along the claim perimeter
(max 8), then one turret of each kind cheapest first (max 3), every candidate through the
ghost preview. Ranking: defence sits after tools / fire / storage / workbench / base /
hearth / bed, and acute hunger (cook), freezing (emergency wood/stone) and winter/evening
fuel are pre-goals that jump the queue anyway, so defence never starves shelter / food /
water / fire — it competes with furnish and progression after that. Thirst is served by the
`drink_water` behaviour, not the planner (unchanged). The goal emits one `build` step (the
piece's cost joins `plan.keep`, so its materials are never junk-dropped or stashed while the
goal is live); `buildsPiece` includes it, so a locked earlier build goal still holds it.
`PlanInput` gains `threat` + `defenceMem`, passed by `fillPlanSensors`
(`packages/gameplay/src/ai/base_behaviors.ts`, from `assessThreat` over
`identity.defence`); the branch also skips hired workers itself, and needs a home anchor
(built base or adopted ruin). Ownership: the planner owns the target. `fillDefenceSensors`
(`packages/gameplay/src/ai/defence.ts`) still records threat events (sightings / kills /
livestock / close attacks) and still owns `identity.defence` persistence, but no longer
calls `planDefence` — it translates the planner's defence step into `view.defenceTarget`
for `build_defence`, or clears it when the plan is doing anything else, so a threatened bot
never plans two defences. `build_defence` stays the executor (withdraw from storage, then
the standard `build:` action, `DefenceMemory` fails routing); its `planFree` consideration
now allows the planner's own defence step, and `base_work` skips defence plans
(consideration + run guard). Ruin homes defend too: `fillPlanSensors` publishes
`view.ruinBase` (added to `PlanSensors` / `SENSOR_KEYS`, `view.base` stays unset per
ADR-340) and the sensor reads `view.base ?? view.ruinBase` — without it a ruin defence
step would be orphaned (base_work skips it, build_defence would have no target). No new
data knobs: the goal reuses `ai_defence.json` (`buildThreatLevel`, `maxWire`,
`maxTurrets`, `surplusReserve`, ring / offsets) as-is.

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr341_defence_plan.test.ts` (18 tests): ladder
position (defence after bed, before furnish); defence appears at threat ≥ 2 with surplus
(one build step, wire inside the own claim, cost items in `plan.keep`); none at level 0/1,
without surplus, without a claim, or when hired; ordering pinned (hungry → cook, freezing
→ wood, unsheltered → base, thirst signals still reach `drink_water` under a defence plan);
one step at a time (after the wire stands, the next plan is the next wire slot); a ruin
home plans defence; `base_work` scores nothing for a defence plan while `build_defence`'s
`planFree` allows it; wiring through the real view (plan + translated target identical in
slot / x / y, stable across sense passes, no target while the plan is busy with the
campfire, ruin home defends with no `mem.base` / `view.base`). Two ADR-338 tests updated
to the new contract (the sensor no longer plans: the slice sensor test now asserts events
+ translation from a defence plan; the wiring test snoozes the pre-defence ladder goals so
the plan IS defence). Neighbours re-run green: adr338 / adr337 / adr340 / adr252 / adr321
(9 files, 121 tests — same as the pre-change baseline). Typecheck with pinned TypeScript
5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** In-planner, the `hasSurplus` leaves check sees the current pass's gather
leaves, which are empty by construction (any unmet earlier goal returns first) — later
comfort goals do not reserve materials against defence, by design; the data reserve is the
floor that protects them. A defence step's threat is the sensor's fresh level, which can
differ by one sense pass from the level the planner used (events are recorded after the
plan is made). No turret ammo stocking (ADR-338 cut, unchanged). Nothing verified on a
real phone.

**Coordinator fix (caught by the full gate).** The `planner.ts -> defence.ts` import
created an ESM import cycle: `recruitment.ts` (entry) -> `planner.ts` -> `defence.ts` ->
`base_behaviors.ts` -> `input.ts` -> `recruitment.ts` (still evaluating, so
`WORKER_COMMANDS` was undefined and `COMMAND_RATES` threw "Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'map')" — `esm_import_order.test.ts`, recruitment entry, failed
standalone and in the gate). Fix: the pure planning layer moved to a new leaf module
`packages/gameplay/src/ai/defence_plan.ts` (threat, memory, `planDefence`, turret ammo
picking; imports only leaf modules, never `input.ts`), `planner.ts` and
`base_behaviors.ts` import from there, and `defence.ts` keeps only sensors + behaviours
and re-exports the moved names so existing `import * as D` users keep working.
`fillTurretAmmoSensor` stays in `defence.ts` (it is a sensor, not pure planning).
`esm_import_order` passes 136/136 after the fix; neighbours re-run green (15 files,
326 tests). No behaviour change: the moved code is verbatim.
## ADR-342: Turret ammo stocking (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Turrets (arrow / bolt / flame) existed and fired, but nothing ever stocked them:
each turret consumes one ammo item per shot from its own 4-slot storage Container (the piece's
Storage attachment; `defenseSystem` spends the first matching item in slot order, no ammo = idle),
and no bot or player flow loaded them. Investigation findings: arrow_turret shoots flint_arrow /
iron_arrow / fire_arrow, bolt_turret iron_bolt / steel_bolt, flame_turret crude_oil / lamp_oil
(`pieces.json` `features.turret.ammo`); the target count 20 fills a single stack for every kind
(maxStack 20–50). There was no stock/load interaction to reuse — a player loads a turret through
the ordinary container panel (`copen` / `cdeposit` / `cclose` on the piece, the server resolving
it to the Storage attachment), and the bot does the same, mirroring the Task 30 refuel deposit
into a fire's container.

**Decision.** `packages/gameplay/src/ai/defence.ts` + data `packages/gameplay/data/ai_defence.json`
add `stock_turret` next to `build_defence` (same registry, `defenceBehaviors()`), with
`fillTurretAmmoSensor` called from `fillDefenceSensors` (after the hire sensors, so the employer's
base / `hire.idle` are available). `pickTurretAmmo` picks one turret: neediest first (least ammo,
then nearest), below `ammoLowFraction` (0.25) of `ammoTargetCount` (20) rounds, capped by the
turret's free stack room (a kind already inside tops its stack up; a new kind needs a free slot).
The kind is the turret's first listed kind with surplus — only the surplus above the per-kind
`surplusReserve` (flint/iron arrow 10, fire arrow 5, iron/steel bolt 10/5, crude/lamp oil 5) is
deposited, and a kind on the plan's gather leaves is skipped for the next kind, so the bot never
gives away its last arrows or spends what the ladder still needs. The source is the bag, else the
base storage box — and only when the storage rule allows it. The rule itself moved to the storage
API: `storage_api.mayTakeFromStorageAt` (own / clan / employer claim via `zoneOwnedBy`, or
unclaimed within `ammoHomeTiles` of home, plus the ADR-207 `canUseBaseStorage` gate), with
`mount_behaviors.mayTakeFromStorage` kept as a thin wrapper resolving the home from the agent, so
ADR-323/327 keep their exact signature and behaviour (no new import cycle: `storage_api` takes
`building/place.js` + `building/actions.js`, neither of which imports any `ai/*` module).
Gating (the no-starvation rule): only with surplus, never while a survival need is unmet
(Survival hunger / thirst < 30, the ADR-327 floor), never while the planner wants anything (any
step, gather leaf or hunt target — a leaves-only plan is still planner work, caught while writing
the wiring test), and for a hired worker only while `hire.idle`. One trip per turret
(`ammoCooldownTicks` 600 after a trip or an empty source). The behaviour withdraws the shortfall
from the box first (same container sequence as `build_defence`, including its pending-`cclose`
dance), then deposits, tracking the open deposit in `ammoSeq` so the sequence finishes even
though the turret reads full once the deposit lands. The target earmarks its ammo (the kind joins
`plan.keep` and leaves `view.surplus`) so the bot neither junk-drops nor stashes the rounds it is
about to load. Hired workers stock the employer's turrets from the employer's box (the claim check
`ownClaim` / `zoneOwnedBy` covers the employer's claim); they still build nothing.

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr342_turret_ammo.test.ts` (24 tests): data knobs and
each turret's ammo, `turretAmmoState` counts / free slots, per-kind choice and fallback, surplus
above the reserve only, leaves veto, low / half / full thresholds, free-slot vs stack top-up,
neediest-first, foreign box never a source (fabricated scan + `mayTakeFromStorageAt`), sensor
gating (busy step, gather leaves, hungry, cooldown, no claim), hired worker stocks the employer's
turret (real employer-owned claim) and not when idle is false or absent, behaviour considerations,
the full bag-deposit and box-withdraw-then-deposit sequences (open / deposit-or-withdraw / close,
cooldown set, turret at 20), no-ammo cooldown, full turret left alone. New
`packages/gameplay/test/adr342_turret_wiring.test.ts` (4 tests): the target appears through the
real `buildAgentView` for an idle bot (ladder snoozed) and for a hired idle worker, none for a busy
planner, and the registry carries `stock_turret` next to `build_defence`. Neighbours re-run green:
adr341 / adr338 / adr337 / adr340 / adr252 / adr321 / adr323 / adr327 (12 files, 162 tests).
Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** The reserve can leave a turret half-full when the bot holds exactly one load
(20 arrows = reserve 10 + deposit 10) — the bot has no ladder goal to gather more arrows, so a
turret it cannot fill stays at what the surplus allowed. A deposit sequence open on a turret the
sensor stops targeting (e.g. the turret is demolished mid-trip) is closed by the behaviour, but a
withdraw sequence abandoned the same way relies on the pending-`cclose` dance on the next run.
Nothing verified on a real phone.

## ADR-343: Resource expeditions — AI humans travel far for the resources they need (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** World-wide travel already existed (ADR-324: hierarchical region routes, riding long
legs, budgeted deterministic off-screen sim), but a bot that needed a resource it could not see
never went and got it. The investigation found the real bottleneck was not the travel range: the
planner DOES ask for far resources (its leaves), but the gather sensor only sees agent memory
(`sightRange` 12 tiles, `memorySeconds` 20), and the only resource-seeking movement was the
local `trip` — 18–36 tiles, a 3600-tick (3 min) cap, random direction — after which the goal
snoozed half a day (`GOAL_PATIENCE` 6000). Travel explore (200–800 tiles) is random-direction
and never resource-directed, and off-screen bots never perceive, so a far trip only ended in
gathering when the destination happened to be the resource. Verified non-bottlenecks, unchanged:
`goalTimeoutTicks` 72000 (a 1200-tile off-screen leg is ~9k ticks), off-screen speeds 2.6 / 5.4
tiles/s, `poiSearchTiles` 400 (POIs, not resources), `homeMaxDist` 48. Two arbitration flaws
stood in the way as well: the local `trip` (~1.0 utility) out-scored `travel` (0.55) while
`tripWanted`, so it would hijack an expedition into 36-tile loops, and `return_home` pulled a
far bot home at night mid-trip.

**Decision.** New `TravelKind` `"resource"` (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/travel.ts`): when a
free/roaming bot has a fresh unmet need (`m.resourceNeed`, recorded by `noteTripWanted` in
`packages/gameplay/src/ai/base_behaviors.ts` from the plan's leaves, cleared when the leaves
empty), `pickTravelGoal` prospects the seeded world for the nearest node of that kind and
travels to it — a round trip: on arrival the bot surfaces to full sim to gather (`endTravel`
sets `m.resourceReturn` and clears `spawnOff`), then the next goal is a `return` home.
Prospecting (`prospectResource`): placed nodes first (live, skips amount-0 depleted); else a
seeded ring scan via the new `nodesInChunk` (`packages/world/src/generator.ts`, which mirrors
`load()`'s node loop exactly — same order, same rng draws, same guarantee pass — so placements
agree exactly). First ring with a hit wins (nearest within a chunk diagonal). Bounded by
`prospectMaxChunks`, cached per (start chunk, kinds, excludes) with a TTL, deterministic (fixed
ring / in-chunk order, no rng). `resourceKindsFor` maps items to node kinds via yields ≥ 0.15
(iron_ore → iron_vein + chromite_vein). `fillTravelSensors` ends a resource trip early when its
recorded items no longer intersect the live need — but NOT while a plan step is executing
(leaves are transiently empty during build/craft steps; the planner reports only the first
unmet goal). A failed resource trip bans its destination (cap 4) so the next prospect takes the
next-nearest node. `travelKeepsHome` now measures the corridor to the leg segment (previous
waypoint / origin → current waypoint) instead of the waypoint points, same limit (2 ×
`regionTiles` = 32) — a strict relaxation, teleports still detected. Arbitration: the `trip`
`want` consideration returns 0 while a travel route is active and ends any in-progress
`bb.trip` (a stale trip cannot hijack the return leg); `return_home`'s `farFromHome` returns 0
while a route is active (the logistic curve's floor is ~0.07, still far below travel's 0.55).
Clan-stay bots and hired workers get no expeditions (stay → short loop; worker → undefined).
New knobs in `packages/gameplay/data/travel.json`: `resourceMinTiles` 48 (trip range 36 + sight
12; nearer nodes are the local trip / gather's job), `prospectMaxTiles` 1200, `prospectMaxChunks`
256, `resourceNeedTtlTicks` 36000 (30 min), `prospectCacheTtlTicks` 6000. `AiMemory` gains
`resourceNeed`, `resourceBanned`, `resourceReturn`; `TravelState` gains `items`.

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr343_resource_expeditions.test.ts` (17 tests):
`nodesInChunk` == `load()` (seeds 42 + 7, 6 chunks each); prospecting (placed / nearest /
depleted / generator-deterministic / copper-undefined); goal selection (resource pick, near-node
exclusion, stale need, ban → next-nearest, stay / worker exclusion, `noteTripWanted` record /
clear); a 1200-tile route with a lake-wall detour; full-sim controller (the bot follows the
resource route past 100 tiles, the trip never starts); off-screen: an 800-tile expedition to a
resource the plan genuinely needs reaches it deterministically (same seed → same arrival) and
comes home; early-end (a) ends a stale trip, (b) survives a mid-craft step; `travelKeepsHome`
segment behaviour; trip / `return_home` scoring with and without a route. Three real findings
while writing the tests, all test bugs except the last: `WOOD_RESERVE` (8) means a fresh bot's
axe goal still leaves wood as a leaf (the craft-step rig needs 12 wood); wood yields from 10
node kinds, not 2; and the trip's `day` consideration zeroes it at night by design, so the
scoring test splits day / night contexts. Neighbours re-run green: adr324 / adr339 / adr341 /
adr342 (4 files, 62 tests) + adr321 / adr323 / adr327 / adr336×2 / adr337×2 / adr338×2 /
adr339-wiring / adr340 / adr341 / adr342×2 (14 files, 201 tests) — 263 passed, 0 failed.
Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** Journey preparation (food / water / gear by distance) and water navigation (AI
humans swimming / fording, or routing around water) are separate later ADRs — this slice is
distance only. Prospecting cannot find kinds the generator never places in the live bands
(copper / tin appear only in `worldgen.json` bands, used by tests — so the bronze chain's ores
fall back to explore; a pre-existing game gap, out of scope) or depleted nodes in unloaded
chunks (banned + re-prospected on arrival). Iron needs a tier-2 pickaxe, so the planner
backward-chains an iron need through the bronze chain before iron_ore itself becomes a leaf.
Nothing verified on a real phone.

## ADR-344: Distance-based journey preparation — AI humans pack for the trip (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-343 sends bots on long resource expeditions, but they set out with whatever
happened to be in the bag — a bot could walk 800 tiles for iron with no food, no water, and no
pickaxe, and die pointlessly en route. This slice prepares the bot for the journey, sized to the
distance, before it leaves.

**Decision.** New pure planning leaf `packages/gameplay/src/ai/journey.ts` (data in
`packages/gameplay/data/ai_journey.json`; no new art, no binaries), wired in `ai/travel.ts`:

- **Estimate** (`estimateJourney`): route length via `routeTiles` (round trip ×2 for a resource
  expedition, one-way otherwise) at the off-screen speeds from `travel.json` (foot 2.6, mounted
  5.4 tiles/s), plus budgeted rest stops (`restEverySeconds` 300 s, each +60 s). Rests are
  budgeted time in the estimate, not simulated stops. Riding is assumed via `willRide` (already
  riding, or own mount + mount skill + route > `longTripTiles` 25, mirroring ADR-321 mountPolicy
  minus the fetch-radius detail).
- **Pack** (`planJourneyPack`, pure: bag + storage counts in, pack list out): gear first, then
  water, then food. Needs come from the vitals drain rates (hunger 0.05/s, thirst 0.08/s) ×
  `safetyMargin` 1.25; the bag's contents count first, then the highest-value healthy items in
  storage (health ≥ 0 only; never food with negative thirst, e.g. bread / jerky). Only surplus
  above the data reserve (`reserve` per item key, else `defaultReserve` 1) — the ADR-338/341
  discipline, so the base is never starved. Never an item on the planner's gather leaves. Capped
  by free bag slots (a kind not carried needs a free slot per stack). Gear is the required tool
  for the destination node kind (`TravelState.nodeKind`, recorded by `pickTravelGoal` from the
  prospect hit; fallback is the lowest tier of any node yielding the item) — the lowest adequate
  tier, one each. Iron needs a tier-2 pickaxe, chromite a tier-4; the node-kind rule is what keeps
  an iron trip from demanding a steel pickaxe.
- **Departure gate.** A long trip (≥ `minPrepTiles` 100 tiles) does not start until `tr.journey`
  is recorded (`journeyResolved` in the travel behaviour's goal consideration). The
  `prepare_journey` behaviour (second in `travelBehaviors()` — travel stays first, ADR-324/331
  tests depend on the order) walks to the box (`packRadiusTiles` 8, door-aware `goTo`) and
  withdraws the pack one `containerSeq` cycle per item; the pack list is recomputed every sensor
  pass from live bag + storage counts, so each landed withdraw shrinks it until it empties and
  the journey records. A `journeyPacked` blackboard tally subtracts just-landed withdraws from
  the 20-tick-cached base scan so the reserve is never double-taken. Short trips need no
  preparation and get no turn-back rule.
- **Never set out hungry, or without the means.** The journey is not recorded while the bot is
  hungry / thirsty / cold (departure floors 55 / 60, mirroring autonomy's hungry cutoffs — a bot
  the planner wants to feed first never prepares instead), nor while the planner is still
  working the tool chain: `requiredToolChain` gives the lowest adequate tool plus its recipe
  closure (gatherable ingredients are leaves, never expanded — the planner gathers them; only
  craft-only items expand, via the first all-reachable recipe, the planner's own choice) and the
  stations it needs, and the trip waits while `plan.step` targets the chain (withdraw / craft the
  tool or a part, build its station) or `plan.leaves` hold a chain ingredient. Both waits are
  bounded by `prepDeadlineTicks` 1200 from `tr.since`, after which the bot departs bag-only.
  Storage is the bot's own base scan — for hired workers `fillHireSensors` re-anchors it to the
  employer's base — plus the ADR-323/327 `mayTakeFromStorageAt` rule: never another bot's or a
  stranger's storage. No box / box too far / box not permitted → depart bag-only immediately.
  The first version of this slice cancelled the trip at route assignment when the tool was not
  held; that was wrong — the planner backward-chains the tool (a fresh bot has no axe yet and
  ADR-343's tests depart for wood exactly so) — so the cancel was replaced by the wait above,
  and the route is assigned regardless.
- **Turn-back.** A bot that runs out mid-trip turns back toward home (or the trip origin when it
  has no base) instead of pressing on. Full sim (`turnBackNow`): the bag is empty of a kind and
  that need is < 30. Off-screen: provisions drain per tick at the vitals rates, and
  `provisionsExhausted` fires only when a provision the bot was carrying runs out (a kind that
  started at zero was never carried — it does not turn the bot back, so a 0/0 record never
  reroutes a return leg). A long trip that went off-screen with no journey record gets one from
  the current bag, but only when the bag holds provisions; an empty bag travels on ADR-343's
  abstract foraging. The turn-back sets a `return` leg home (no destination ban, no journey
  record on the return leg) and `journeyBlocked` cools down re-launches for
  `journeyRetryCooldownTicks` so the bot does not ping-pong. Foraging en route in full sim is the
  existing gather / eat path; the turn-back is the backstop.
- **needsFloor interaction (decided).** The off-screen floor (50) stays as the survival last
  resort — abstract foraging keeps the bot alive at 50 — but it is not the plan: it does not let
  the bot continue, which is why the turn-back keys off provision points, not vitals. The same
  hook covers explore / poi / trade / relocate / return legs (preparation runs on route
  assignment for any kind; return legs record bag-only, far from storage).

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr344_journey_preparation.test.ts`: 33 passed, 0
failed — estimate sizing (short packs little, long packs proportionally more, mounted packs
less than foot), no-starvation (reserve untouched, never departs hungry), the tool-chain wait
(fresh bot's wood expedition waits for the axe chain, departs once the axe is in hand; the wait
is deadline-bounded), the end-to-end pack-and-leave (withdraws the pack from its own box, keeps
the reserve, departs prepared and walks > 20 tiles), hired workers pack from the employer's
storage only, and the turn-back / forage rules in full sim and off-screen. Neighbours re-run
green: adr343 / adr324 / adr321 / adr323 / adr327 / adr336×2 / adr337×2 / adr338×2 / adr339×2 /
adr340 / adr341 / adr342×2 (17 files, 238 tests) — 271 passed, 0 failed across all 18 files.
Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean. Two regressions caught by
the neighbours in-session and fixed: the first gear design (cancel when the tool is not held)
broke ADR-343's wood expeditions, and the first off-screen fallback (record a 0/0 journey for
an empty bag) turned ADR-343's return leg straight back to base+1. Test-harness notes: the
end-to-end test drives the controller with `commands: false` so `copen` / `cwithdraw` / `cclose`
stay action strings (`survivorController` otherwise moves them into `o.commands` via
`emitAgentCommands`, which is why the first version saw the pack complete but no transfer land);
and the rig's box sits west of the base because a box on the east side wedges the bot against
its south-west corner on the north-east departure (diagonal input into the corner blocks both
axes — pre-existing nav geometry, not preparation).

**Honest cuts.** Rest stops are budgeted time, not simulated stops. Off-screen preparation is
impossible (a bot away from storage cannot pack); such trips get the turn-back rule from current
bag contents instead. A bot that fails to mount still packs at the mounted estimate and may
turn back early (safety net); `willRide` omits mountPolicy's fetch-radius detail. `prepared` is
a record of coverage at departure, not a guarantee (a pantry that cannot cover a very long
detoured route departs short and the turn-back guards it). The tool-chain wait covers the
planner working the chain; a stuck or empty plan departs after the deadline (or immediately if
the plan is empty). Nothing verified on a real phone.

## ADR-345: Water navigation — AI humans swim / ford across where safe, route around where it is not (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Long trips cross rivers and lakes, and the route layer already knew about water
(ADR-329: region costs from sampled water, Infinity for all-water regions; ADR-343's 1200-tile
expedition detours around a lake wall) and mounts could swim (ADR-322). But no layer decided what
an AI human ON FOOT does at the water. A probe (since deleted) showed the gap exactly: with a
straight route across a 40-wide lake, the bot walked straight in at the shore and swam across —
soaked (Wetness 255), alive, at swim speed, with no stamina cost and no danger check. The cause is
in the layering: `walkerWaypoint` (creature_nav) blocks deep water in its A* and falls back to the
closest reachable tile, but `goTo` then steers straight to the goal (`wp?.x ?? tx`) — and the
movement system lets any walker enter a swim tile (swim=true at ground level) — so the A* detour
only ever delays the swim. The region router only avoids all-water regions, so a leg through a
partially-wet region swims straight through too. Meanwhile the exposure system already wets anyone
in water (0.15/s, Task 33) and wet clothing loses half its insulation (Task 31) — the costs of a
crossing existed, but nothing weighed them before entering.

**Decision.** New pure decision leaf `packages/gameplay/src/ai/water_crossing.ts` (data in
`packages/gameplay/data/travel.json` `"water"`; no new art, no binaries), wired in `ai/travel.ts`:

- **Depth sampling** (`regionSampleDepth`, `legWaterProfile`): water depth at a point by the ADR-329
  rule — loaded terrain wins (shovel edits and flowing water included), unloaded terrain from the
  seeded generator, so an unloaded lake is deep in the middle and shallow at its shore exactly as the
  chunk will generate. A leg's profile samples depths every `sampleStepTiles` (2): tile counts of dry
  / shallow / deep, the longest deep run, and the distances to the first deep / first wet sample.
  Shallow is a ford (wadeable by everyone at `wadeSpeedMul`, walk anim, no stamina cost); deep is a
  swim (at `swimSpeedMul`). `regionCost` is unchanged (ADR-329 intact).
- **The decision** (`decideCrossing`): ford (shallow only — always allowed, even cold: wading is
  walking, and the exposure system already charges for it); swim (deep run ≤ `swimMaxDeepTiles` 12
  on foot, when fit); ride (mounted — a swimming mount, moose, the only swimming species in
  `mounts.json`, crosses deep water up to `rideSwimMaxDeepTiles` 24; any mount wades shallows);
  around (a deep run longer than the bot or its mount can swim, or any deep water under a mount
  that cannot swim — the strict rule, used by the bank gate and the off-screen leg-entry check, where
  the local geometry is known); wait (the crossing is structurally fine but the bot is cold — bodyTemp under
  `COLD_BELOW` — hurt, hungry / thirsty under the travel `minHp` / `minNeeds`, or without the
  stamina the deep water costs: deep seconds × `swimStaminaPerSec` 1.2 × `staminaMargin` 1.5, plus a
  `minStamina` 0.25 floor). Speeds for the estimate are the off-screen speeds (the journey.ts
  convention); the margin absorbs a moose, whose walk is slower than the off-screen mount speed.
- **Route time** (`checkRouteWater`, at assignment in `fillTravelSensors` and `offscreenPlan`):
  every leg must be structurally crossable on foot or by the mount the bot will be riding (the
  ADR-321 mountPolicy rule via `willRide` — an own mount + skill + a long route). A leg that is not
  is re-planned around with its regions avoided (`planRegionRoute` / `requestRoute` take an optional
  `avoid` set; the goal region is never avoided). Two re-plans; when no route around exists the
  trip ends like any unreachable goal, and when the plan budget is spent the old route stays — the
  bank / leg-entry gate is the backstop. The condition gate is deliberately NOT checked here: a bot
  far from the water may recover before it arrives. For a mount that cannot swim the planning rule
  is relaxed (`legUncrossableAtPlan`): only a deep run over `nonSwimmerPlanDeepTiles` (12, the
  local nav's detour allowance — water wider than that along the leg is beyond what the local nav
  can skirt within its budget) forces a re-plan; smaller water is left to the bank gate. The first
  version used the strict rule here (any deep water under a non-swimmer) and it ended trips at
  assignment: ADR-331's 400-tile horse trip crosses rivers the local nav skirts in seconds, and
  each re-plan found new rivers further along, so the one-re-plan limit killed it before it started.
  (Region legs are at most ~23 tiles, so the threshold has to sit below the leg length to fire at
  all — a 24 threshold could never have caught the 40-wide lake, whose legs run 14–16 deep.)
- **Bank gate** (`waterGate` in `travelRun`, before `goTo`): the water profiled is the path the bot
  will actually walk — the local-nav waypoint (`walkerWaypoint`, the same call `goTo` makes) when
  the world has structures, so a pond the local nav skirts is not a bank; when the local nav has no
  path (undefined) the straight waypoint is the fallback and the profile crosses the water. (A
  failed local nav returns undefined only once the bot has walked the reachable path — until then it
  returns waypoints along it, so the bot walks to the bank before the gate fires.) When the water is
  at hand — the first wet sample within `bankTiles` (3), backed off by one sample step because the
  first-wet distance is measured to a sample that can sit a step past the first wet tile — a bot in
  bad shape holds at the bank (the behaviour returns false, so eat / drink / warm get the ticks)
  until it recovers or `waitTicks` (1200) pass, when it re-plans around instead of waiting forever.
  A structurally impossible crossing re-plans around this leg at once (`rerouteAroundLeg` — the
  leg's own regions avoided, not the whole route; the planning check already passed the later legs,
  and they get their own gate when reached). The trigger reads the first WET sample, not the first
  deep one: a mount that cannot swim beaches at the deep boundary (it can wade the shallows but
  cannot press on), so the decision has to happen before the bot wades in — the first version
  triggered on first-deep and the horse test beached exactly there. In deep water already the bot
  presses on to the far shore, never waits in the water; in the shallows with a changed world under
  it, a re-plan's new waypoint is on land and the leg back out is shallow / dry, so it walks out.
- **Swimming costs stamina** (`travelRun`): deep water drains `swimStaminaPerSec` per second via the
  existing `spendStamina` (shallow wading costs none). The pre-crossing stamina estimate is the
  guarantee; the drain is the cost.
- **Off-screen** (`offscreenStep`): the leg-entry check re-plans around a leg no crossing can make
  before the bot steps into it (off-screen nothing can recover, so "wait" counts as "around"; when
  the budget is spent the step holds and retries next). The re-plan avoids the leg's own regions
  (`rerouteAroundLeg`): off-screen there is no local nav to skirt small water, so the strict
  decision applies here even though the planning check left small water to the bank gate. Progress is
  costed at the water under the bot's feet, re-sampled every tile — deep at `swimSpeedMul`, shallows at
  `wadeSpeedMul` — never the leg's average speed (a long dry tail after a river must not dilute the swim; the first version
  averaged and a 10-tile river cost ~1.5 s instead of ~5 s). Wetness (the exposure system's
  `WATER_WET_PER_SEC`) and swim stamina are applied from the water the traversed segment actually
  held, so a river crossed mid-step still soaks the bot.
- **Dismount is NOT implemented** (deliberate cut): the task allows dismounting *or* routing around,
  and dismounting into deep water would strand the mount — no riderless-mount recall across water
  exists — so the bot always routes around instead; when no route exists the trip ends like any
  unreachable goal.

**Validation.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr345_water_navigation.test.ts` (19 tests): depth
sampling (loaded shallow / deep / land, unloaded = seeded generator everywhere); leg profiles
(ford / river / lake / dry); the decision table (ford always, swim when fit, wait when cold /
hurt / hungry / thirsty / low on stamina, around when too long, ride for a swimming mount, around
for a non-swimmer in deep water, ride for a non-swimmer in shallows); full sim — a bot crosses a
3-wide ford and arrives wet but alive, a straight route across a 40-wide lake re-plans around
(arrives dry, never enters the water), a cold bot refuses a 10-wide river at the bank for 600
ticks (dry, trip still live) then crosses once warm, a moose rider stays mounted across
swimmable water, a horse rider routes around the lake and stays mounted; route assignment — a
route forced through a lake (lake regions seeded cheap) is re-planned around at assignment, a
horse trip across small seeded rivers is NOT ended at assignment (the ADR-331 regression: the
trip is `sent` with the route still crossing rivers under the planning threshold), a horse trip
is still re-planned around lake-scale water at assignment, and the same seed plans the same
water-aware route on fresh worlds; off-screen — progress across a water leg is slower than dry
speed (the wet leg takes ~14 calls vs ~9 dry), never faster than dry speed, the bot arrives wet
with less stamina, and an off-screen bot re-plans around a lake it cannot cross instead of
swimming it. The full-suite run caught the ADR-331 regression above (1 failed / 1819 passed /
3 skipped — the horse trip ended at assignment); after the fix the neighbours re-run green:
adr345 / adr343 / adr344 / adr324 / adr329 / adr321 / adr323 / adr327 / adr331 / adr336×2 /
adr337×2 / adr338×2 / adr339×2 / adr340 / adr341 / adr342×2 (21 files, 303 tests) — 303 passed,
0 failed; full `packages/gameplay/test` suite: 177 passed / 2 skipped (179 files), 1822 passed /
3 skipped (1825 tests), 0 failed. Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3:
`packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** The bank gate's local-nav branch (`walkerWaypoint` when structures exist) has no
dedicated test — it mirrors `goTo`'s identical call, and the structure-less path (the straight
profile, which is the real path in the open wilderness) is covered; a bot walking past a river
near structures is the untested case. `nonSwimmerPlanDeepTiles` duplicates the local nav's
detour allowance (`NAV.detour` in creature_nav) by convention, not by reference — the decision
leaf stays pure (data JSON only), so if the nav constant ever changes the knob has to be retuned
by hand. Local (non-travel) movement is untouched: a gather trip across a pond still uses
the legacy walk-in — the travel layer is where long crossings are decided. A bot that runs out of
stamina mid-crossing still finishes (movement never requires stamina to swim); the pre-crossing
estimate is what keeps it out of water it cannot survive. Nothing verified on a real phone.

## ADR-346: The ADR-343 route gate applies to resource expeditions only (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-343 gave the travel layer ownership of long-range movement: while any route was
active the local trip scored 0 (and an in-progress trip was ended) and `return_home`'s farFromHome
was pinned to its logistic floor, so neither could hijack an expedition. The full gate caught a
regression in `apps/client/test/adr203_ai_human_autonomy.test.ts` — "an AI human builds a campfire
near home before night" — which passed 3/3 at base 5300607 and failed 1/3 with ADR-343/344/345.
Bisect confirmed the batch as the cause. A probe (seed 11, 4 bots, 15:00 start) showed bots with
unmet needs (stone, dye, wood) launching explore trips to far destinations instead of gathering
locally, and no campfire built; the 5 campfires in the world were pre-existing abandoned-structure
ones. Water profiling ruled out ADR-345's bank gate for the near-home bot (its leg was dry), and
the journey records showed ADR-344's preparation resolving (bag-only departures), so the cause was
ADR-343's arbitration: the local trip is the early-game gather loop — it out-scores travel (~1.0
vs 0.55) and walks 18–36 tiles around home, letting the gather sensor find the flag/fire materials
(dye especially) — and `return_home` is what brings a bot on an explore route home at dusk.

**Decision.** Narrow both gates to resource expeditions (`travel.kind === "resource"`), the only
kind with a destination that matters: `trip` "want" in `packages/gameplay/src/ai/base_behaviors.ts`
and `return_home` farFromHome in `packages/gameplay/src/agents.ts`. Explore / POI / trade / return /
sent / relocate routes restore exact base behaviour — the trip may interrupt them and `return_home`
may fire at dusk. The expedition itself is unchanged: the trip still never starts on a resource
route, an in-progress trip is still ended there, and `return_home` stays floored there.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr346_expedition_only_arbitration.test.ts` (4 tests):
trip scores with an explore route and 0 on a resource route; `return_home` scores > 0.5 at night far
from home on an explore route and < 0.1 on a resource route; an in-progress trip survives an explore
route but is ended by a resource route; full-sim — a bot with unmet needs on an explore route starts
a local trip. 4 passed, 0 failed. The regression test `adr203_ai_human_autonomy` passes 3/3 with
the fix (was 1 failed / 2 passed). ADR-343's own pins still hold (both use resource routes).
Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** The near-home bot in the probe also sat at explore leg 0 for ~4000 ticks on a dry
25-tile loop; with the trip allowed again it gathers instead of walking the loop, and adr203 passes,
so the stall was not pursued further — if a bot is ever seen idling on a short explore leg with no
needs, that is a separate travel-behaviour investigation.

## ADR-347: The hologram places exactly where it shows (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** In building mode, a player moved the hologram to a location, tapped place, and the
piece landed in a completely different location in front of the player a couple tiles away. Two
root causes, both making the piece land somewhere other than the ghost. (1) Touch, portrait — the
reported bug: `apps/client/src/build-hud.ts` `onTouchControl()` hit-tested touch controls using
the landscape anchor with an unclamped scale, while `VirtualControls.place()`
(`packages/input/src/touch.ts`) renders and hit-tests buttons with the portrait anchor when
`w < h` and scale clamped to [1, 1.15]. On a 390×844 portrait phone the ✓ button renders at
(351, 582) but was tested at (359, 675) with a 16.6 px radius — a ~93 px miss. Both the input
layer's `pointerdown` (which fires `Build.PlaceConfirm` via `touch.btn.confirm`) and the build
HUD's canvas `pointerdown` fired for the same tap, and since `blocked()` returned false the HUD
treated the ✓ tap as a world tap: `setTouchPoint(screenToWorld(tap − 48px lift))` moved the ghost
to the world point under the button, then the confirm placed it there. Landscape was unaffected
(anchors coincide); the same leak applied to the ✗/⟳ buttons. (2) Every device: the Place/Move
command carried the raw aim, not the ghost. `placePreviewIntent()` / `moveIntent()` sent
`preview.request` (unsnapped aim point + requested rot) while the renderer draws the ghost at
the snapped `preview.x/y/rot`. Magnet / snap-assist / claim bump / corner auto-fit all move the
ghost off the request, so the server re-snapped the request to a different slot.

**Decision.** (1) `onTouchControl` now resolves the portrait anchor when `w < h` and clamps
scale to [1, 1.15], exactly matching `VirtualControls.place`/`scale`; `LayoutEl.anchor` gained
an optional `portrait` anchor. (2) New exported `previewSlot(p)` in
`packages/gameplay/src/ui/placement.ts` returns the ghost's snapped slot (re-attaching `FINE_ROT`
for fine pieces, since `preview.rot` is the bare 15° step); `placePreviewIntent` and `moveIntent`
now send it, and `BuildMode.place()` re-snaps/re-validates the ghost's slot via `previewSlot(p)`
instead of `p.request`. Re-snapping the slot is idempotent in an unchanged world, and the server
still re-validates it. `BuildMode.rotate()` was deliberately left alone: the fitted rot is passed
into `rawPreview` by `fitCorner`/`magnetizeL`, so `request.rot` already equals the shown rot in
the auto-fit cases.

**Verification.** New `apps/client/test/adr347_hologram_place.test.ts` (8 tests) and
`packages/gameplay/test/adr347_hologram_place.test.ts` (3 tests): portrait `onTouchControl`
blocks ✓/✗/⟳ at their rendered spots (positions derived from `VirtualControls.geometry()`);
portrait ✓ tap never moves the ghost while world taps still do; per-device
(keyboardMouse/gamepad/touch) off-centre-aim and assist-hop confirms send the ghost's slot and
`tryPlace` lands on the ghost; fine rug keeps `FINE_ROT|5` and the 1/16-tile slot; `moveIntent`
sends the move ghost's slot. All 11 new tests failed before the fix and pass after; updated
assertions in `adr268_ghost_confirm.test.ts` and `menus.test.ts` now pin the ghost coords
(ADR-268's contract, now literally true). Neighbour suites 129 tests green. Typecheck with
pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean; client only pre-existing
`src/tutorial/overlay.ts` errors from the sparse-checkout missing `input_glyphs.json`
declaration, in a file untouched by this slice.

**Honest cuts.** No live-phone check of the portrait ✓ tap — the fix is verified by tests
deriving button positions from the same `VirtualControls.geometry()` the renderer uses, but the
user's eyes on the live build are the real check that a portrait tap places exactly on the ghost.

## ADR-348: Safe zones around beds, AI homes and guest arrivals (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The safe spawn radius (20 tiles, ADR-326) covered installed starter points and the
ADR-325 world-wide AI spawn points, but three spawn point kinds had no safe zone. (1) Bed
respawn: a bed can sit anywhere in the world, far from any spawn point. (2) AI home respawn: an
AI human's remembered base can be anywhere. (3) Friend-code guest spawn (ADR-295): a one-shot
arrival point near the host, anywhere in the wilderness. A player respawning at a remote bed, an
AI human returning home, or a guest still loading in could be ambushed on arrival.

**Decision.** Same 20-tile radius and same rules for every kind, through the same
`inSpawnSafeRadius` predicate — no enforcement site changed (`zombies.ts`, `population.ts`
untouched; they already read the predicate). `ExtraSafeSpawnPoints` in
`packages/gameplay/src/spawn_points.ts` gains two ADR-348 mechanisms: keyed live providers via
`addSafeSpawnCentreProvider(world, key, fn)`, re-evaluated at most once per tick (the predicate
runs in hot paths: zombie acquire, animal engage, spawn gates), idempotent by key; and one-shot
centres via `addTemporarySafeSpawnPoint(world, point, durationSeconds)` with a tick expiry,
pruned on read. `setExtraSafeSpawnPoints` now preserves already-registered providers and
temporary centres on re-install. Beds: `installBedRespawn` registers the `"beds"` provider
(`bedSpawnPoints()`: every owned bed's beside-bed respawn point); `bedRespawnPoint` was
refactored onto a shared `bedSpots()` scan with identical behaviour — distance still measured
from the bed footprint, same tie-breaking; unowned beds (abandoned-site furniture) are not
centres. AI homes: `setAiHomeLocator` registers the `"ai-homes"` provider
(`aiHomeSafeCentres()`), mirroring `aiRespawnPoint` (blocked homes excluded; dead bots included,
so the home stays a centre through the respawn wait); the hired/clan exclusion is factored into
`keepsAdr153Rule()` and shared by `aiRespawnPoint` — a hired worker's or clan member's home is
deliberately not a centre, since they keep the ADR-153 rule. On the Node server the home locator
is never set, so no provider fires there (homes only exist in local mode). Guest arrivals: the
server registers the arrival point as a temporary centre for `guestSafeSeconds`, one new knob in
`packages/gameplay/data/pvp.json` (`PvpTuning.guestSafeSeconds: 300`, 5 min); the radius stays the
shared `SAFE_SPAWN_RADIUS = 20` for every kind.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr348_spawn_safe_zones.test.ts` (19 tests) and
`apps/server/test/adr348_guest_safe_zone.test.ts` (1 test): beds — predicate to 20 tiles and not
beyond, unowned bed not a centre, demolished bed stops being one (next tick, per-tick cache
pinned), bed-respawn refactor guard, legacy zombie spawner never spawns inside, zombie does not
acquire, zombie retaliation re-engages after being hit, horde zombie still chases, wolf does not
engage but retaliates when hurt, population gate (bed-covered chunk spawns nothing + control);
homes — predicate, hired worker's home not a centre, moved home relocates the centre, zombie does
not acquire, horde still chases; temporary centres — cover for exactly `guestSafeSeconds` then
lapse, zombie does not acquire, horde still chases, coexist with static centres; guest join —
real guest join near a host at (500.5, 500.5), arrival point a safe centre to 19 tiles (not 21),
lapses after `guestSafeSeconds`, installed starter points stay protected. 20 new tests, all
passing. Neighbour suites green (spawn points, ADR-325/326, animals, population, pvp, hordes,
respawn, friend spawn). Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` and
`apps/server` clean.

**Honest cuts.** Guest-zone expiry is time-only (300 s), not "until the guest leaves": if a
returning player restores a saved position instead, the provisional point keeps an empty
5-minute zone near the host — harmless, and beds cover their own respawn points. A bed
placed/demolished mid-tick is reflected from the next tick (per-tick provider cache); invisible
in live play since checks are per-tick anyway. No visual surface to this slice, so no live check
is needed beyond playtesting a bed respawn in a remote base.

## ADR-349: Fruit trees and crops visible in the world (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Players only saw fiber plants, trees, and berry bushes, even though wild crops and
fruit trees were already spawning. Two reasons the world didn't read as crop-scattered. (1)
Wild plants drew with the small, weedy `wild_*` sprites (44×64, ~420–800 opaque px, little
produce colour) that blend into grass, while the farmed `crop_*` art is bigger and clearly shows
produce (pixel analysis: `crop_corn` 965 opaque px with 260 red + 125 yellow vs `wild_corn` 704
px, 0 red; `crop_tomato` 176 red vs `wild_tomato` 41). (2) Fruit trees were rare: ~3.5 per chunk
(~90 per 25 chunks). Their fruit is already in the idle art — verified numerically, not
visually: apple idle has 156 red px (depleted 0), cherry 114 (0), orange 294 orange px (99), and
the idle frame differs from the bare depleted frame for all five species; gathering already
worked through the existing interact path.

**Decision.** Data-only change, no new art, no binaries. (1) `packages/gameplay/data/resources.json`:
24 wild resources now carry `"sprite": "crop_<key>"` (e.g. `wild_corn` → `crop_corn`,
`flax_patch` → `crop_flax`, `cotton_bush` → `crop_cotton`, `herb_patch` → `crop_herbs`). Wild
nodes keep their key and yields, so ADR-247 (seeds only from gathering each crop's own wild
plant) is untouched; they just draw with the mature farmed art. `wild_garden` keeps its own art
(mixed garden, no single crop counterpart). Fruit-tree sprites unchanged — they already show
fruit. (2) `packages/gameplay/data/worldgen.json`: grass `nodeChance` 0.045 → 0.055, sand 0.025
→ 0.03; every wild crop listed ×2 in the grass band (wheat/hay/lettuce ×3, keeping the ADR-257
≥2 rule); fruit trees ×2 in grass, plus pear/cherry/peach added to the forest band (apple ×2
there), orange/aloe ×2 on sand. All knobs in data JSON. Measured density over 25 chunks per
seed: wild plants 427–476 → 414–694 across 20 seeds (520–592 on the original 4); fruit trees
83–110 → 194–281 (2.2–2.6×; ~8–11/chunk); total nodes +7–12% only. Every wild species and
every fruit tree appears on every seed tested (min per-species count 2 across 20 seeds).
Placement still avoids water (generator skips tiles 1/8, pinned by test); regrown nodes avoid
structures/roads/players via the existing ADR-134 `clearStructures` path. Claims don't exist at
worldgen time (player-placed later), so "not inside claims" holds structurally for new worlds —
same as before, not a regression.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr349_wild_crops.test.ts` (8 tests): per-seed
density minimums (wild ≥380, fruit ≥100 over 25 chunks, 6 seeds) + determinism per seed /
difference across seeds; no wild nodes on water; all 24 wild resources draw as their `crop_*`
art and resolve to real pack sprites; fruit-tree idle ≠ depleted frame for all 5 species;
gathering an apple/pear/cherry/orange/peach tree yields its fruit via the existing gather path;
gathering `wild_corn` yields corn + `corn_seeds` only; `seedSourceIssues` still clean; frost pass
depletes wild corn + apple tree below 40°F while berry bush and ordinary tree survive; farming
end-to-end (till → plant wheat → water → grow → harvest `crop_wheat`, wheat + seeds in
inventory). 8/8 pass. Neighbour suites: gameplay + world 198 files, 1,930 passed / 3 skipped /
0 failed; render + assets 676 passed / 1 failed (known pre-existing `pack.test.ts` KEYS.md,
sparse-checkout only). Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` clean.

**Honest cuts.** Fruit visibility at phone scale: the fruit dots in the existing idle art are
small; a render-side fruit overlay or scale bump for fruit trees could make them more obvious,
but that touches `apps/client/src/view.ts` and was left as a follow-up, not done here. The art
was verified numerically, not visually — the user's eyes on the live build are the real check
that the world reads as scattered with crops. Winter: fruit trees and wild plants still die
below 40°F per the existing Task 28 rule (frost-depleted nodes go invisible until regrown), so
the crop-scattered look is a spring/summer/fall thing, as designed.

## ADR-350: Damage pulse runs on composited DOM layers, not a canvas repaint (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The red pulsing edges when damaged stuttered. There is no DOM/CSS damage pulse —
the only "red pulsing edges" is the canvas vignette in `FxDraw.draw()`. The pulse phase was
already driven per render frame (`fx.step(dtReal)` in `mountFx`'s post-render `draw()`), and the
damage path does zero per-frame DOM/layout work. The stutter is raster cost: while
`hurt`/`lowHp`/`dread` is active the overlay canvas can never idle-skip, so every frame does a
full-screen `clearRect` + a 256px→~1080p `drawImage` upscale of the vignette. Measured with the
real `Fx`/`FxDraw` code against node-canvas (real 2D raster) at phone size (390×844 CSS, DPR 3 →
979×2118 backing store), 600 frames @ 60 Hz: idle 0.005 ms mean; low-HP pulse 0.6 **48.6 ms mean
/ 51.3 ms p95 / 100% of frames over the 16.7 ms budget**; hurt decay after one hit 14.0 ms mean /
29% over budget; low-HP + dread 64.2 ms / 93.6 ms p95 / 100% over budget. The pulse alpha math
itself is smooth (max frame-to-frame Δalpha 0.113 is the intended heartbeat double-thump) — the
frames presenting it were ~3× over budget, so the thump landed in dropped-frame jumps. Caveat:
node-canvas/Cairo is a CPU rasterizer, so absolute ms on a phone GPU will differ, but the op
counts and the before/after ratio are implementation facts.

**Decision.** The three full-screen alpha washes — hurt/low-HP vignette, dread vignette, hit
flash — moved from the per-frame canvas repaint to three dedicated DOM layers
(`#vfx-wash-hurt/dread/flash`, `position:absolute; inset:0; z-index:2; will-change:opacity;
pointer-events:none`, appended after the FX canvas so they sit exactly where the canvas
vignette sat: above the world, below the HUD at z-index 5+). Per frame only `style.opacity`
changes (rounded to 0.001, skipped when unchanged); backgrounds change only when the wash
colour changes (event-time, e.g. a cold hit). The alpha math is the pre-350 canvas math verbatim
— same beat windows, coefficients, caps — only the sink changed. `syncWashes()` runs before the
canvas idle check, so the canvas now idle-skips while the pulse runs; hurt / low-HP / dread /
flash no longer keep the canvas awake. The `source-over` reset before the fog block was
preserved. `shrink()` zeroes the washes; `dispose()` removes them. All tuning knobs live in new
`apps/client/src/fx/damage.json` (normalised defensively to shipped defaults on garbage input).
Visual equivalence: the CSS gradient reproduces the baked 256px vignette exactly — stops
converted from canvas `[r0,r1]` parameterisation to CSS `[centre, edge]` (mid stop 0.55 →
64.89%; core 21.98%; edge 71.09%), using explicit `rgba(r,g,b,0)` never the `transparent`
keyword (which would darken mid-tones through black). Pixel check vs the old baked vignette at
native size: max |Δalpha| = 0.0039 across horizontal/vertical/diagonal radii. The gradient is
evaluated at native resolution, so it is at least as crisp as the old 256px upscale.

**Verification.** Real-raster harness (fixed code, same scenarios): low-HP pulse 48.6 ms →
**0.003 ms mean** (p95 0.014 ms, max 0.050 ms, 0/600 frames over budget, 0 canvas ops); hurt
decay 14.0 ms → 0.001 ms; low-HP + dread 64.2 ms → 0.002 ms. New
`apps/client/test/adr350_damage_pulse.test.ts` (5 tests): 600-frame low-HP pulse asserts zero
canvas `drawImage`/`fillRect` (≤1 first-frame dirty `clearRect`), mean draw < 1 ms, opacity
identical to the pinned pre-350 formula every frame with range 0.132–0.330; hurt-decay peak 0.57
then quiet; flash/dread caps; vignette-off and `shrink()` silence; cold-hit recolours the
background exactly once (0 rewrites over 60 frames); gradient string/geometry assertions;
garbage JSON normalises to defaults. 5/5 pass. Neighbour suites: FX/damage neighbours 30/30;
full `apps/client/test` + `packages/render/test` 1,203 passed, 0 failed (7 files fail at
collection for the pre-existing sparse-checkout gap — `assets/ui/` absent in this checkout).
Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `apps/client` only the 3 pre-existing
`src/tutorial/overlay.ts` errors (missing `input_glyphs.json` declaration), proven pre-existing
by stashing; the new files are clean. Sim/render separation intact: no sim, input, or renderer
code touched; `Fx.step` phase rate, hurt decay, hit-stop, and shake untouched; fog/flicker/rays/
particles still draw on canvas exactly as before.

**Honest cuts.** Flicker/fog/rays stay on the canvas: they're transient horde/nightfall layers
(not the reported damage stutter) with non-uniform shapes (moving fog blobs, beams), not
single-alpha washes — converting them would be scope creep with no measured need. `draw()` still
sizes the overlay canvas before the idle check (pre-350 behaviour); skipping allocation when
only the vignette is active would save ~8 MB one-time but changes `texBytes()` behaviour — left
as-is. No real-phone visual check: the gradient is pixel-equivalent numerically, but the user's
eyes on the live build are the final check that the pulse reads the same.

## ADR-351: Rope leading — lead tamed and wild farm animals home on a rope (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Rope already existed as an item (`rope`, resource, maxStack 30) but did nothing.
Players and AI humans had no way to move a farm animal to their fenced-in area except taming
in place (Task 28) or waiting for it to wander. The ask: rope in the hotbar + equipped lets
the holder attach a rope to a nearby farm animal (tamed or wild), the animal follows, and
arriving at the holder's fenced-in area ends the lead cleanly — with the rope *visible* in the
world between holder and animal, for player-led and AI-human-led animals alike, and with
release on un-equip / death and forgiving break-free rules.

**Decision.** New `RopeLead { holder: u32 }` component on the led animal, appended at the end
of `GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS` and replicated to all (`r(C.RopeLead, "all")`) — the replicated
component *is* the visibility mechanism: no extra net event, no sprite. Tuning lives in new
`packages/gameplay/data/rope.json` (`attachRange 3.25, followDistance 2.2, runDistance 6,
breakDistance 16, stuckSeconds 6, dangerRadius 5, arrivalRadius 2, scanRadius 24,
leadSpeedMul 1`; bots `attachCooldownTicks 40, banTicks 3600, giveUpTicks 1200, leadUtility 0.9,
minHp 0.5, safeTiles 8, scanEveryTicks 40, waitBehind 5`). Leadable farm species are the 10
land animals (`animal_chicken/duck/goose/turkey/cow/goat/sheep/pig/alpaca/rabbit`); **bees are
not leadable** (they fly; honey goes to the Apiary) and pets never are; all rideable mounts are
leadable when not ridden. `checkLead` gates: holder alive, target alive with `Animal`, not a
`Pet`, not already led, rope equipped (strictly the main hand — see below), one lead per holder,
ownership (wild: anyone except an animal standing inside someone else's claim, so rope can't
steal; tamed: the owner entity, or a hired worker whose `Worker.owner` PlayerId matches the
owner's; mounts: `mayUseMount`), within `attachRange`. New reject reasons `not_leadable`,
`no_rope`, `already_led` appended to the server `COMMAND_REJECT_REASONS`.
`ropeSystem` (authority, every tick, after `gameplay.mounts`) walks the animal toward the
holder via `creatureStep` — same nav as pets, so fences contain it and there are no teleports
— walk speed below `runDistance`, `fleeSpeed` above it, stopping at `followDistance * 0.7`.
A zombie within `dangerRadius` of the animal makes it **balk** (stop, lead stays, stuck clock
pauses) — not a break. Break-free is distance > `breakDistance`, or the animal itself not
moving ≥0.25 tiles for `stuckSeconds` while it should be following (fence in the way).
Arrival: `leadDestination` is the holder's claim centre + radius (nearest `PrivilegeZone` of
the holder's tribe), else `BotHome`, else the `Worker` hire anchor; entering the claim, or
reaching the anchor, releases with `Arrived` and resets the animal's `Animal.homeX/homeY` to
where it stands, so it stays. Un-equip, holder death, animal death all release with no
dangling lead. `animalAISystem` skips led animals, otherwise wild animals would flee/wander
against the rope. `ropeEquipped` is strictly `Equipment.mainHandItem === rope`: `equipSystem`
leaves `HotbarSelection` pointing at the rope slot even after the same-slot Equip toggles the
main hand off, so a selection fallback made un-equip never release — caught by test.
AI: `fillRopeSensors` + `lead_animal` (`ai/rope_behaviors.ts`, same shape as the mount
behaviours) — nearest leadable within `scanRadius` via the spatial hash, own tamed strays
outside the home claim score +10 over wild animals; the bot equips the rope (`equip:<slot>`),
walks to the animal, attaches (`rope:<target>`), walks it to the destination, releases on
arrival at a home anchor (inside a claim the system releases on entry), gives up after
`giveUpTicks` and bans the animal for `banTicks`. While leading, the bot **stops and waits**
when the animal lags more than `waitBehind` tiles: the bot walks 2.6 tiles/s, a cow runs at
2.0 and walks at 0.9, so walking on would stretch the rope past `breakDistance` (move
magnitude is normalised away in the bot input frame, so slowing down is not an option —
stopping is). Action strings `"rope:<target>"` / `"rope:0"` map to `RopeLeadCmd` in
`agent_output.ts`, server-validated by `checkLead` like every other bot command.
Client: Interact (E / pad X tap / touch "Use") with rope equipped and a leadable animal in
reach sends `ropeLeadIntent(animal)` — wired in `main.ts` before `mountCtl.update()` so rope
wins over riding when rope is equipped; it never releases on Interact, so gather/ride still
work. Livestock and mount panels get Lead / Release buttons (disabled unless the rope is
equipped, tooltip explains). The rope itself is `apps/client/src/rope-overlay.ts`: a
pointer-events-none 2D canvas at z-index 2, same `CameraLike` pattern as the claim overlay,
drawing one sagging line per live lead (5px dark halo + 2px tan `#D8B06A` stroke + knot dots,
hand lifted 14px, neck 10px, `ROPE_SAG_PX = 8` at the midpoint), with a still-frame signature
skip like the claim overlay; mounted right after `mountClaimOverlay`, hidden when a menu is
open.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr351_rope_lead.test.ts` (15 tests) and
`apps/client/test/adr351_rope_overlay.test.ts` (4 tests): attach + follow to heel distance;
wild + tamed both leadable, bee / someone else's animal / no-rope / already-led rejected;
release on un-equip through the real Equip intent and through the command; arrival inside
the claim ends the lead with `Arrived` and the animal stays; break-free too far; danger balk
(the animal stops, the lead stays, it resumes when the zombie leaves); fence-pen stuck
break-free; holder/animal death cleanup; a led animal does not wander on its own AI; the rope
command is registered with its entity field; a bot equips, attaches, walks a wild cow home
and the lead releases by arrival inside the claim; the rope sensor reports target then live
lead; `"rope:<target>"` / `"rope:0"` parse to the command. 19/19 pass. Neighbour suites:
mounts/taming + pets/farm + inventory/equip 85/85, mounts/saddles + claims 53/53, no
regressions. Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11
workspace projects. Full gate (`vitest run` from the repo root, ~22 min on this VM): **3,942
passed / 2 failed / 3 skipped** (3,947 tests; 604 files passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped). The 2
failures: the known pre-existing sparse-checkout `pack.test.ts` KEYS.md ENOENT, and the
`persist` autosave benchmark (per-tick p95 61.7 ms vs the 50 ms non-PERF ceiling while the
gate itself loaded the VM) — it passes alone in ~1 s, and the slice touches no persist code
(`ropeSystem` early-returns with no leads), so that one is load flakiness. The gate also
caught two stale tail assertions (`apps/server/test/task22_recruitment.test.ts`,
`apps/server/test/adr170_vehicle_controls.test.ts`) that pin the append-only
`GAMEPLAY_NET_COMMANDS` tail; both were extended with `...G.ROPE_COMMANDS` after the mount
commands, the same way Task 25 extended them for dye.

**Honest cuts.** Two real bugs caught by the tests, both fixed in-slice. (1) The stuck
detector first measured the *gap to the holder closing*; a holder walking away steadily keeps
the gap constant while the animal follows at full speed, so the lead broke free after 6s even
though the animal was moving. It now tracks the animal's own position — a lead only breaks
when the animal itself hasn't moved. (2) `ropePoints` computed the sagging midpoint from the
un-lifted ground projections while the endpoints are lifted 14/10px, so the rope hung 20px
below the visible chord instead of 8; the midpoint is now computed from the lifted endpoints.
Deferred: bots do **not** fetch rope from storage — a bot with no rope in its bag simply never
leads. No `RopeEventEvt` net event / toast wiring in `main.ts` (the replicated `RopeLead`
component is the visibility mechanism; `ropeEventText` exists in gameplay for future toast
use). A bot with no claim and no home anchor holds the rope and does other work while the
animal follows it (no destination to walk to). No real-phone / real-controller visual check
of the rope line — the overlay is verified numerically only; the user's eyes on the live build
are the real check for Interact attach (keyboard E, gamepad X, touch Use), panel Lead/Release,
arrival release inside the claim, and break-free feeling forgiving.

## ADR-352: Dung and a longer-lasting fertilizer (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Animals produced eggs, milk, wool, honey and truffles, but nothing for the fields:
the only fertilizer was bone-meal/fiber (`fertilizer`, 600 s at 1.5x), and bones mean killing
things. The ask: all animals produce Dung a couple of times a day; dung is a short-lived pickup
(10 s if unpicked); dung crafts into a different fertilizer that lasts a bit longer.

**Decision.** New `packages/gameplay/data/dung.json`: `perDay 2` (big grazers/mounts —
cow/horse/bison/moose/elk/yak — 3), `jitterFraction 0.25`, `despawnSeconds 10`, `dropRadius 0.8`,
`count 1`, `excluded ["animal_bee"]`. Coverage is every animal archetype in ai.json (kind
"animal") except the bee — farm animals, pets, mounts and wild animals, birds included; the bee
is the only exclusion because it flies and honey is its produce (it goes to the Apiary, never to
the ground). Production is a new persistent-but-not-networked `DungTimer { nextAt: u32 }`
component (appended to `GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS`, after RopeLead) driven by `dungSystem`
(authority, every 20 ticks, after the rope system): a missing timer is seeded with a jittered
first drop, a due timer drops and re-arms. The jitter comes from `world.rngFor("dung.next", e)`
(seeded by world seed + tick + entity), so a herd seeded on the same tick still staggers instead
of dropping in unison, and a restart honours the stored schedule (no backlog). Dead animals
never produce. The drop is a plain ownerless LootBag holding 1 dung at the animal's feet (the
generic dropped-item path: same Container / LootBag / `tagLootSource(Animal)` shape as animal
loot, so pickup, stacking, weight, replication and persistence come for free), with
`despawnAtTick = spawn + 10 s` — the exception to the 3-minute dropped-item rule, applying to
dung bags only; every other bag keeps its own lifetime from `loot_despawn.ts`. The client fades
the bag over its short life through the existing `despawnFadeAlpha` path (`syncLootFade`).
New items `dung` (resource, maxStack 50, 0.1) and `dung_fertilizer` (resource, maxStack 30,
0.3), ids 496/497 from the regenerated lock (append-only), and recipe `dung_fertilizer`
(no station, 2 s: dung 2 + fiber 2 → 2 dung_fertilizer), id 383. The fertilizer lasts
`dungFertilizerSeconds 900` (15 min) in `farming.json` vs 600 s for the old one — 50% longer,
chosen because it is clearly longer without trivialising the bone-meal fertilizer or the
watering cycle — at the **same** `fertilizerMul 1.5`: dung is slower-release, longer not
stronger, so the dose is stored in the existing `Crop.fertilizerUntilTick` with no new Crop
field, no schema migration, and the old fertilizer byte-for-byte untouched. `fertilize()` takes
an optional seconds parameter (default 600 s); `farmUseSystem` and `farmPrompt` accept the
`dung_fertilizer` key alongside `fertilizer`, and the XP source stays "fertilize". No new art:
the dung bag draws the generic LootBag sprite and both items fall back to the category-generic
icon via `resolveIcon` (adding an `icons` entry would fail `pack.test.ts`, which requires every
icons key to exist as a pack sprite; there is no dung sprite). Pickup and fertilizing use the
existing Interact / Use intents, so keyboard, gamepad and touch all work with no new UI.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr352_dung_fertilizer.test.ts` (19 tests): data
(2/day, jitter bounds, cow/horse 3/day, herd stagger, full species coverage incl. mounts and
wild animals, bee excluded, recipe shape); every covered species drops on schedule and the bee
never does; a drop is 1 dung in a LootBag within `dropRadius`; production repeats on the stored
schedule; a dead animal never produces; `DungTimer` is persistent, not networked, not
replicated, and round-trips through the chunk codec on a tamed animal (nextAt intact, Animal
rebuilt by husbandry); a dung bag lives exactly 10 s with an `expired` event while a dropped
wood stack still lives its full 3 minutes; fade alpha is ~1 at spawn and decays through the
10 s (a normal bag is unchanged: full alpha at spawn and 10 s in); picking up dung works and
stacks; dung_fertilizer crafts through the real crafting system; dung fertilizer gives a 900 s
dose vs 600 s for the old one at the same 1.5x growth multiplier; the Use path consumes one and
refuses a second dose while fertilized; the dose drains, expires and can be reapplied. 19/19
pass. Neighbour suites: farming/fertilize + loot/despawn + crafting + pets/farm 74/74;
mounts/saddles + rope + crafting queues 81/81; no regressions. The gate also caught two
source-model tests that enumerate how every item is obtained (`economy.test.ts` "every item has
a gather or craft source" and `balance.test.ts` reachability + raw cost): dung is produced by a
system, not gathered/crafted/looted, so both now list dung as a base source with an ADR-352
comment — the same treatment as the soil/shovel and boil-source precedents already in those
files. Typecheck with pinned
TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects. Full gate (`vitest run` from the repo root, ~22 min on this VM): **3,962 passed / 2 failed / 3 skipped** (3,967 tests; 605 files passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped). The 2 failures: the known pre-existing sparse-checkout `pack.test.ts` KEYS.md ENOENT, and the `persist` autosave benchmark (per-tick p95 64.2 ms vs the 50 ms non-PERF ceiling in round 1 while the gate itself loaded the VM; rounds 2–3 were 1.81 and 4.26 ms) — it passes alone, and the slice touches no persist code, so that one is load flakiness, as in ADR-351's gate.
