Two earlier full gates caught real regressions that were fixed before this commit: gate 1 caught the fade-window change breaking a pinned server ADR-238 test, gate 2 caught the economy/balance source-model tests (dung had no listed obtainable source). A third gate run was killed by a runtime restart before producing output; this is the re-run after it.

**Honest cuts.** Two test bugs of mine, both fixed in-slice. (1) The chunk-codec test first
asserted `Animal` on a decoded *wild* animal — `Animal` was never persistent, so a wild animal
round-trips as a Transform-only stray (pre-existing engine behaviour, not something this slice
introduced) and its orphaned DungTimer is inert (`dungSystem` only reads `Animal` entities).
The test now uses a tamed animal, whose `Animal` husbandry rebuilds after a load — which is
also the case that matters, since tamed animals and mounts are the ones players keep. A wild
animal's timer is still seeded on first sight, so nothing is lost in practice. (2) A dung
bag's fade: a first attempt capped `despawnFadeAlpha`'s window at the bag's own lifetime so a
10 s bag would spawn at full alpha — the full gate caught it (a pinned server ADR-238 test:
a shortened-expiry bag must fade by *remaining* time, and the cap broke that). The change was
reverted in full: dung spawns part-faded (~0.44 alpha) exactly like any other bag 10 s from
expiry and decays to the floor — the existing dropped-item presentation, not a special case. The crop
inspector's fertilizer fraction still divides by the 600 s bone-fertilizer dose, so a
dung-fertilized crop reads "full" for its first 5 minutes and then drains — cosmetic, and
fixing it properly needs a stored fertilizer kind on Crop (a schema change) for a HUD
fraction; left as-is. Dung and dung fertilizer use the generic resource icon until dedicated
art ships. No real-phone check: the 10-second pickup window and the fade are verified
numerically only; the user's eyes on the live build are the real check that dung is noticeable
enough to grab in time without being annoying.

## ADR-353: Animals eat more crops and use the trough (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** A mount tamed on carrots would only ever eat its taming foods, and a farm animal at a
trough would only ever eat hay: the trough held a whole harvest the animals ignored, and a mount had
no hunger at all (it regened unconditionally). The ask: mounts and other animals eat other crops
besides the ones used to tame them, and a hungry animal eats from the animal trough — with taming
untouched, ownership respected, and no faster hunger.

**Decision.** Diets are data, split from taming. Mounts gain a `diet` array per species in
`packages/gameplay/data/mounts.json` (hay/wheat/corn/potato/carrot/apple/lettuce/beetroot/pumpkin/
berries-class lists, 9–10 items each, taming foods included: a horse eats carrots when hungry too)
alongside the unchanged `foods` (love/like/ok) table; `mountDiet()` / `mountEats()` in
`mount_defs.ts` read it, while `foodPref()` — the taming gate — still reads `foods` only, so a
diet-only crop (corn for every species) is refused for taming (`not_food`, item kept) and can never
build taming progress. Farm animals gain a `diet` per kind in `skills.json`
`husbandry.animals` (grazers hay-first, birds grain, pigs potato-first, rabbit carrot-first; the bee
keeps `["hay"]`, exactly what it ate before, so its fed window for honey production is unchanged),
read by `farmAnimalDiet()`; pets gain crops in `pets.json` diets (dogs apple/berries/carrot/corn/
potato/pumpkin, birds lettuce/rice, rabbit beetroot/corn/lettuce, turtle beetroot/corn, squirrel
lettuce/pumpkin — cats, ferret, fox and owl are carnivores and unchanged), which flows through the
existing `petFoodValue()` into hand-feeding, ground eating and trough eating with no pets.ts change.
Wild animals have no diet data of their own (`ai.json` archetypes carry kind/hp/speed/perception/
aggro/flee/wander/attack/loot only, and no wild eating system exists), so a wild animal's diet is
its species diet, which governs it once tamed or as a mount — no dead data was added to ai.json.
Mount hunger is a new persistent-but-not-networked `MountHunger { fedUntil: u32 }` component
(appended to `GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS`, after DungTimer): a clock, not a drain — every meal resets the
same `fedSeconds 600` window (new `mounts.json` tuning knob, same 600 s as farm animals), so the
wider diet never makes a mount hungrier faster. Fresh tames, spawned mounts and legacy mounts are
seeded fed on first sight (the DungTimer no-backlog rule), hand-feeding a tamed mount feeds it, and
while hungry a mount does not regen — it needs food to recover, but never loses hp to hunger
(pets' rule: starvation floors, never kills). Trough eating: `husbandrySystem`'s hay-only block is
now diet-aware — a hungry farm animal at a trough eats one item off its diet (hay first for
grazers, so the old path is the diet's head) and is fed 600 s; `mountSystem` does the same for an
unridden hungry mount at the nearest own trough within `troughRange 10` (same range as farm
animals), healing `feedHeal` like a hand-feed. Pets already walked to their trough; they now find
diet crops there through the unchanged `foodSources` path. Ownership is new for the feeding
trough (the pet trough already had it): `troughOwnerId()` (the piece's `PieceOwner`, set at
placement), `troughTribeId()`, and `mayEatFromTrough()` — owner's, clan-mate's (same tribe) or
unowned troughs only, never a stranger's; a hired worker's animals count as the employer's
(`tamedOwnerId()`, the `mountOwnerIdFor` rule). An empty or wrong-food trough falls back to
grazing/foraging as before (the graze guard is the same ownership + diet check, so a stranger's
trough never blocks grazing), and a fed animal never double-dips: one item per meal, the fed window
blocks re-eating, and the graze loop clears `Grazing` once fed. No new UI, no new art, no input
changes (animals eat autonomously; putting food in a trough is the existing container UI on all
three inputs). Ridden mounts do not trough-eat (the rider steers; they hand-feed), and mounts have
no grazing fallback — there is no wild/mount grazing system to fall back to, so a hungry mount with
no trough food simply stays hungry (no regen) until fed.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr353_animal_diets_trough.test.ts` (21 tests): data
(every mount diet wider than its taming table with a non-taming crop, all diet items resolve, the
taming tables pinned byte-for-byte; every farm kind has a diet, bee hay-only; pet diets resolve,
dog eats carrot, cat refuses it, treats untouched; knobs in data, windows unchanged); farm animals
(hungry cow eats 1 corn for 600 s, hay still feeds, every kind eats a non-hay diet item, empty and
wrong-food troughs fall back to grazing, a stranger's trough is untouched and grazed past instead,
no double-dip — exactly 1 item, fed, no graze, and a second run eats nothing); mounts (every
species eats corn from its owner's trough, a trough meal heals `feedHeal`, hungry mounts do not
regen while fed mounts regen the usual 6 hp/min, stranger's trough untouched vs clan-mate's and
unowned troughs eaten from, ridden mounts do not trough-eat, taming refuses corn and still tames
on carrot, hand-feeding a tamed mount feeds it, `MountHunger` persistent / not networked /
round-trips through the chunk codec); pets (hungry dog eats a carrot from its owner's pet trough,
source 2, fullness +25; hand-feeding a carrot works; a non-food trough is untouched). 21/21 pass.
Neighbour suites: mounts/taming + rope + dung + pets/farm 140/140, farming/crops + seed sources
32/32, foods/vitals/crop bars/economy/balance 47/47; no regressions. Typecheck with pinned
TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects. Full gate (`vitest
run` from the repo root, ~22 min on this VM): **3,983 passed / 2 failed / 3 skipped** (3,988 tests;
606 files passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped). The 2 failures: the known pre-existing sparse-checkout
`pack.test.ts` KEYS.md ENOENT, and the `persist` autosave benchmark (per-tick p95 57.4 ms vs the
50 ms non-PERF ceiling while the gate itself loaded the VM) — it passes alone in ~3 s, and the slice
touches no persist code, so that one is load flakiness, as in ADR-351's and ADR-352's gates.

**Honest cuts.** Three test bugs of mine, all fixed in-slice. (1) Four mount tests set
`fedUntil: 0` at world tick 0 and expected hunger — but `tick > fedUntil` is false at tick 0, so a
fresh world reads a 0-fedUntil mount as fed (the same boundary as `Tamed.fedUntil`); the tests now
step once first, then set `fedUntil: 0`. (2) The pet-trough test ran 200 ticks and expected 1
carrot eaten — the pet correctly ate twice (4 s eat cooldown, fullness 10 → 35 → 60), so it now
runs 60 ticks and pins exactly one meal. (3) The fed-mount regen assertion used precision 6 and
the pet fullness assertion was exact — both are f32/drain noise (mount hp accumulates ~1e-3 over
1200 f32 additions; the pet's fullness drains ~0.2 while walking to the trough), so both use a
proper tolerance now. Deferred: bots do not fetch diet foods for troughs — the AI `feed_trough`
behaviour still deposits hay only, and `fetch_mount_food` still fetches taming foods; a player (or
a future bot change) stocks the trough with crops. Mounts do not seek out a distant trough or
graze: they eat when within 10 tiles of an own trough (the farm-animal pattern), and a hungry
mount with no trough food waits, unharmed, rather than foraging. No real-phone check: trough
eating is verified numerically only; the user's eyes on the live build are the real check that
animals visibly eat from a stocked trough.

## ADR-354: Tameable animals don't attack on sight (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Animals that are going to be tamed (the user's example: the moose) should not
attack on sight. Audit of where aggression is decided (`animalAISystem` in
`packages/gameplay/src/population.ts`, ai.json `aggro.mode`): `hostile` attacks anyone in
range, `territorial` attacks anyone in range near its home, `defensive` only attacks when
hurt, `passive` never attacks. Of the 35 species with a taming path — 9 mount animals
(`mounts.json`: horse, donkey, deer/red_deer/stag, elk, moose, bison, yak), 17 pet species
(`pets.json`), 11 farm kinds (`skills.json` husbandry) — 34 were already calm: passive
(horse, donkey, deer, chicken, duck, turkey, sheep, pig, alpaca, rabbit, fox, squirrel) or
defensive, i.e. retaliation-only (elk, bison, yak, cow, goat, goose, bee, all dogs/cats/
birds/ferret/owl). Exactly one tameable attacked on sight: the **moose, territorial, range
2** — Task 15 had calmed it from range 4 to 2, but anyone walking within 2 tiles of where
it spawned was still charged. The genuinely hostile animals are the wolf (hostile, range
2.5), the bear and the snake (territorial, ranges 5 / 1.6) — none of them tameable, all left
unchanged. Hordes are zombies and untouched.

**Decision.** Two layers, so the rule holds in data *and* in code. (1) Data: the moose's
ai.json aggro mode is `territorial` → `defensive` (range 2, leashRange 12, attack damage
20 all untouched), matching elk/bison/yak — it now only engages when hurt, and the Task 15
pin on its aggro values is updated to the new mode. (2) Code: new data-only module
`packages/gameplay/src/tameable_defs.ts` (same cycle-free pattern as `rope_defs.ts`)
exports `TAMEABLE_ANIMAL_KEYS` — the union of mount animals, pet animals and husbandry
kinds, derived from the same JSON the taming/husbandry systems read — and
`isTameableAnimalKey()`. `animalAISystem`'s `wants` now requires `!isTameableAnimalKey`
for *initiation* (the hostile / territorial / defensive-when-hurt branch); the engaged /
retaliating branch is unchanged, so a tameable still presses its actual attacker within
leashRange and still flees when badly hurt (scared), and each species keeps its own
fleeRange / wander radius / idle behaviour — nothing was made to flee identically.
`isAggressiveSpawnKind` also excludes tameables, so a tameable never counts as an
aggressive spawn kind either. Audited and already correct, no change: turrets/traps
(`isHostileTo` leaves alone anything without a PlayerId, so no animal is ever a turret
target), territory defence (`nearestClaimHostile` scans zombies only), AI-human defence
sensors (`fillDefenceSensors` records only `kind === "zombie"` sightings), pet guarding
(`threatNear` keys off real attackers in aggro memory plus zombies), the safe-spawn
radius (hostile mode only — wolf + zombies), and mount taming (spook/kick read
`mounts.json` tuning and the species' attack, not aggro mode). `botSignals.enemyNear`
still adds a flat 0.2 for *any* animal seen (chickens included) — generic unease, not a
defence trigger, left as-is. No new UI, no art, no input changes; tuning stays in data
JSON (ai.json mode, no new knobs needed).

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr354_tameable_calm.test.ts` (7 tests):
data (tameable set is exactly mounts + pets + husbandry, all 35 keys resolve in
`animalDefs()`, no tameable is hostile/territorial, moose defensive range 2 / leash 12;
wolf + zombies still aggressive, moose not an aggressive spawn kind); no tameable
initiates on a nearby player over 5 s held at 1 tile (all 35 species); the moose
specifically never attacks in 30 s at 1 tile from a player and from an AI human
(second survivor); every tameable with an attack retaliates when hit from outside its
aggro range but inside leashRange (1 damage → Attack state); the wolf still attacks on
sight and a night zombie still hunts (hp drops); a moose at a live arrow turret's feet
draws no fire (`isHostileTo` false, 0 `TurretFired` in 5 s, hp unchanged) while a
zombie in the same spot takes all 3 shots, and `nearestClaimHostile` ignores a moose
inside a claim but finds a zombie there; a moose still tames by feeding (Progress +
Tamed events, owner set). 7/7 pass. Neighbour suites: mounts/taming + rope + dung +
diets + pets/farm + Task 15 + animals + population 99/99; defences + day-calm +
territory + safe spawns + AI defence + hordes + seed safe zone 145/145; pets/guard/
saddles/mount-food/saddle-chain/mount-preference/AI humans 98/98; mount seek/tame +
spook/back-off/give-up 21/21 (ADR-321, spook/back-off/give-up intact). Typecheck with
pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects.
Full gate (`vitest run` from the repo root, ~24 min on this VM): **3,991 passed / 2
failed / 3 skipped** (3,996 tests; 607 files passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped). The 2
failures: the known pre-existing sparse-checkout `pack.test.ts` KEYS.md ENOENT, and the
`persist` autosave benchmark (per-tick p95 58.6 ms vs the 50 ms non-PERF ceiling while
the gate itself loaded the VM) — it passes alone in ~3 s, and the slice touches no
persist code, so that one is load flakiness, as in ADR-351's, ADR-352's and ADR-353's
gates.

**Honest cuts.** The Task 15 moose test pinned `mode: "territorial"` — updated to
`defensive` with an ADR-354 note, since the data change is the point of the slice; its
behaviour assertions (no attack at 3 tiles, retaliation when hit, flee when badly hurt)
pass unchanged. The `enemyNear` 0.2-for-any-animal signal was deliberately left alone:
it is not a threat classification and changing it would alter bot utility for chickens
too. No real-phone check: calm moose behaviour is verified numerically only; the
user's eyes on the live build are the real check that a moose walked up to no longer
charges.

## ADR-355: Resource-specific storage structures (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Players and AI humans had only generic containers (basic_storage_box /
storage_box / large_chest / salt barrels / Apiary), so ores, logs, crops and stone all
landed in the same boxes and had to be hunted through by hand. The storage batch asks
for one buildable piece per resource family that stores only its own kind. Fixed piece
keys, because the art slice (ADR-356) depends on them: `ore_store`, `log_store`,
`stick_store`, `crop_store`, `stone_store`.

**Decision.** (1) Data: five tier-1 furniture pieces in `packages/gameplay/data/pieces.json`
(188 → 193 pieces; ids 189–193 appended to `ids.lock.json` via `lock:ids`), each
`paintable`, free placement, layer 2, hp 120, ground, 12 slots like `basic_storage_box`,
with tier-1 costs from gatherable/craftable materials (ore: planks 6 + stone 4 + nails 2;
log: planks 4 + rope 2; stick: sticks 8 + fiber 4; crop: planks 6 + rope 1 + fiber 2;
stone: stone 8 + planks 2). Each carries a `$comment` noting ADR-355. (2) New optional
PieceDef field `accepts?: string[]` (raw) / `accepts: readonly number[]` (resolved,
`defs.ts`, empty = unrestricted): validated at load — every listed key must be a real
item id (`itemRef`) and a non-empty list is only allowed on a container. Families:
ore_store takes the five raw ores (`copper_ore`, `tin_ore`, `iron_ore`, `lead_ore`,
`chromite_ore`); log_store takes `wood` + `hardwood`; stick_store takes `sticks`;
crop_store takes harvested produce (wheat, lettuce, pepper, beetroot, rice, hay, corn,
potato, carrot, tomato, pumpkin, squash, beans, cabbage, onion, cotton, flax, hemp —
NOT `*_seeds`, which stay in generic storage); stone_store takes `stone`,
`stone_brick`, `clay`, `clay_brick` (clay counts as stone-family here: raw masonry
material, kept with the stone). Ingots are smelted products, not ores, and do not belong
in the ore store — that boundary is pinned by test. (3) Enforcement is server-authoritative
in `containerSystem` (`building/actions.ts`, Deposit branch, before `transferItem`):
depositing an item not in the piece's `accepts` fails with new append-only
`BuildFail.WrongStorage = 34` (`events.ts`; the enum previously ended at
`NoMovePermission = 33`). Withdraw is unaffected — anything already inside can come out
— and pieces without `accepts` behave exactly as before. The client surfaces the reason
via `BUILD_FAIL_TEXT[34] = "Wrong store for this item"` (`apps/client/src/build-hud.ts`).
(4) AI humans: the new stores are base storage automatically (`isBaseStoragePiece`:
any `container > 0` piece that is not a stall/fire/station/turret/trough — verified, not
duplicated). New lookups in `ai/storage_api.ts`: `nearbyStorageFor(world, e, item,
radius)` (nearest accepting store, generic fallback so a bot is never stuck holding
something it cannot store) and `storageHolding(world, e, item, radius)` (nearest store
that actually holds the item, matching first); both are pure lookups, permission stays
with the caller. `storageTargetFor(c, item, holding)` (`ai/base_behaviors.ts`) walks the
candidates matching-first, permission-checks each (deposit: the server's own
`canUseBaseStorage`; fetch: `mayTakeFromStorageAt` with the employer's home for hired
workers, own base otherwise), and falls back to the scanned base box. Wired into the
stash behaviour (each surplus stack goes to the store that accepts it), the planner
`withdraw` step in `base_work`, and the three hired-worker fetch sites in
`hire_behaviors.ts` (hoe, repair material, craft supply). Hired workers fetch ore from
the employer's ore store under the existing permission rules — never another player's:
a foreign claimed store is skipped even when it is the nearest one holding the item.
No new UI (the container UI opens these like any container), no new input, no art in
this slice (ADR-356).

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr355_storage_stores.test.ts` (13 tests):
data (193 pieces, the five keys/ids, 12 slots / tier 1 / furniture / `piece:<key>` gate
tokens with no skill node, accepts lists exactly as specified, ingots excluded from the
ore store, seeds excluded from the crop store, every other container unrestricted, and
`loadDefs` rejecting an unknown accepts key and accepts on a non-container); deposit
enforcement (right-family deposits succeed in all five stores, 10 wrong-family
deposits fail with `WrongStorage = 34` and the items stay in the bag, withdraw still
works, the generic box still takes everything); AI lookup (`nearbyStorageFor` prefers
the matching store, falls back to generic, undefined with no storage at all;
`storageHolding` prefers the matching store that holds the item); AI behaviour (a bot
stashing surplus copper ore deposits it into the ore store, not the generic box; a bot
with no matching store falls back to the generic box; a hired worker withdraws ore
from its employer's ore store while the employer's generic box stays untouched; a hired
worker never fetches from a stranger's claimed ore store even when it is nearest).
13/13 pass. Neighbour suites: containers / building / farming / crafting / defs 112/112;
AI humans / planner / mounts / defence / turret-ammo / bot crafting 142/142; AI life /
claim-build / defence / ruin-base / homestead / saddles 146/146. Typecheck with pinned
TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects (root
`node_modules/@engine/gameplay` symlink moved aside for the run, then restored; re-run
clean after the two cosmetic cleanups below).
Full gate (`vitest run` from the repo root, ~19 min): **4,002 passed / 4 failed /
3 skipped** (4,009 tests; 606 files passed, 4 failed, 2 skipped). The 4 failures: the
known pre-existing sparse-checkout `pack.test.ts` KEYS.md ENOENT; the known flaky
`persist` autosave benchmark (per-tick p95 59.8 ms vs the 50 ms non-PERF ceiling while
the gate itself loaded the VM — it passes alone, and the slice touches no persist
code); the `task25_dye` piece-count pin (188 → 193, flagged 159 → 164 — fixed
in-slice right after the gate by updating the pin with an ADR-355 note, exactly like
ADR-354's Task 15 pin update; the suite passes on re-run); and `adr229_build_icons`,
which lists exactly the five new keys as missing dedicated build icons — that is
ADR-356's art work, not a regression in this slice (see Honest cuts). After the dye-pin
fix the expected re-run tally is 4,003 passed / 3 failed.

**Honest cuts.** `adr229_build_icons` stays red until ADR-356 ships dedicated build
icons for the five stores: the test requires `build_<key>` in both the `items_build`
atlas manifest and the client stylesheet, and asserts both `missing` and `pending` are
empty, so the `sprite_fallbacks.json` art-pending path cannot satisfy it — and
pointing the new pieces at an existing sprite would violate the dedicated-art-only
rule, so no placeholder was faked. `storageTargetFor` falls back to the scanned base box (`bs.storage`)
when no permission-passing candidate exists, rather than to a farther matching store —
the scanned box is the trusted base default, so a bot never walks to a foreign store,
but an own matching store farther than the generic fallback radius is not preferred in
that corner. The defence, travel and mount-food fetch paths were audited and left
alone: defence/travel fetch from `bs.storage` (ammo and journey packs have no matching
store, so the generic fallback already covers them) and mount-food already scans all
stores via `nearbyStorage`. No real-phone check: the stores have no dedicated art yet
(ADR-356) and the WrongStorage message has not been seen on screen.

## ADR-356: Dedicated art for the five resource-specific stores (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-355 shipped the five stores (`ore_store`, `log_store`, `stick_store`, `crop_store`,
`stone_store`) with mechanics only and left `adr229_build_icons` red: the test requires a dedicated
`build_<key>` icon for each piece in both the `items_build` atlas manifest and the client stylesheet, and
the `sprite_fallbacks.json` art-pending path cannot satisfy it. The stores also had no world art at all
(no `dec_*` sprite, no fallback entry), so a placed store drew nothing in the world.

**Decision.** (1) World art, Task 34 precedent: new `apps/client/src/task355-art.ts` reuses the `Px`
rasterizer from `task34-art.ts` (no fork) and paints one 1024×384 atlas per store
(`decor_ore_store`, `decor_log_store`, `decor_stick_store`, `decor_crop_store`, `decor_stone_store`),
8 cols × 3 rows of 128px: row = fill state (0 empty, 1 half, 2 full), cols 0–3 = rotation 0 damage
stages 0–3, cols 4–7 = rotation 1 (narrower side view), `rotationArt: "mirror"`. Declared in the new
`packages/assets/pack/task355/manifest.task355.json` fragment (layout only; its `image`/`ktx2` paths point
at the real `nature_icons` atlas only because the pack test requires existing PNG + KTX2 twins, and are
never fetched — `view.ts` merges `task355AtlasSources()` blob URLs over them before `setRegistry`, exactly
like task34/task256). The fragment is indexed in `MANIFEST_INDEX`, served by the client art mount
(`vite.config.ts` regex gained `task355`, which the ADR-248 server/client parity test requires), and its
sprites are locked append-only in `pack/ids.lock.json` (`dec_*_store` 5458–5462) via `lock:ids:pack`
(`write-lock-pack.ts` gained the fragment). Each store is its own silhouette in the game's palette with
the 1px dark-plum outline, and damage darkens it (`k = 1 - stage * 0.16`, the Apiary rule) with cracks:
ore_store = a stone-lined open bin with wooden corner posts and visible ore chunks (copper orange, iron
blue-grey, tin pale, lead dull, chromite near-black) with bright glints, heaped above the rim when full;
log_store = a log rack of upright posts and a base beam, long horizontals with ringed cut ends, the pile
growing from bare rack to four rows; stick_store = a teepee bundle of leaning sticks tied with rope at
the crown, feet splayed, fattening with fill (a spare rope coil on the ground when empty); crop_store = a
slatted produce crate with side posts and a light rim, lettuce / carrots / pumpkin / tomatoes / corn
peeking then heaped above the rim; stone_store = a dry-stone bin of three grey block courses with offset
seams and a cap course, grey stone + tan clay + red-brown brick heaped when full. (2) Fill states use the
existing `building.states` mechanism, not a new pipeline: the fragment declares
`states: {empty, half, full}` per sprite (same rows as the default `frames`), and `buildPieceVisual`
resolves the numeric state to the row. The level is mirrored server-side by a new postSim system
`gameplay.storeFill` (`STORE_FILL_EVERY = 10`, `packages/gameplay/src/systems/store_fill.ts`) into a new
networked component `StoreFill {level: u8}` (appended to `GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS`, scope `"all"` in
`GAMEPLAY_REPLICATION` — it rides the static channel with `BuildPiece`; NOT persistent, it is derived and
recomputed on load). Buckets by filled-slot fraction: 0 slots = empty, 1–5 of 12 = half, 6–12 = full.
postSim placement matters: client replicas only `simulate` simulation systems, so a replica that cannot
see the viewers-scoped `Container` never clobbers the authority's level (the `stallDisplay` pattern).
`view.ts` `syncPieceState` gained a store branch (same 15-tick stagger as the fired branch) that reads
`StoreFill` from the net world and passes the numeric state to `buildPieceVisual`; the build ghost shows
the default (empty) frames. (3) Build icons: `build_ore_store` … `build_stone_store` declared in
`packages/assets/pack/items/manifest.items.json` at `items_build` frames 297–301 (the last free cells of
the 16×19 grid; max used was 296) with matching `--cz-ipos` rules in `gameplay-panels.css`
(60% / 66.67% / 73.33% / 80% / 86.67% × 100%) and locked ids 5453–5457. The cells are transparent in
the shipped `items_build.png` / `@2x.png` (verified: 0 opaque pixels) and the snapshot push route carries
text only, so the 32px icon pixels themselves await the user's art pass (same as the Apiary's frame 286
in `d163528`): paint a small version of each world sprite into cells 297–301 (1x + @2x) and the existing
manifest + CSS entries will light up with no code change. No `sprite_fallbacks.json` entries were needed:
the stores now have dedicated `dec_*` art, and pointing them at another piece's sprite would violate the
dedicated-art-only rule (the stale `apiary -> salt_barrel` entry was left alone — out of scope).

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr356_store_fill.test.ts` (5 tests, relative imports only):
buckets (0/1–5/6–12 of 12), the system mirroring empty → 0 / 1 slot → 1 / 6 slots → 2 / drained → 0
for all five stores, generic containers never getting `StoreFill`, `syncStoreFill` change-only reporting,
the postSim system in the pinned order, and `StoreFill` replicating scope `"all"`. 5/5 pass. New
`apps/client/test/task355_art.test.ts` (4 tests): five painted atlases, distinct non-empty cells, empty ≠
half ≠ full per store with outline present and full holding more pixels, damage stages and the narrower
rotation differing, the merged registry resolving every `dec_*_store` sprite with `stateNames` in
`StoreFill` order and `buildPieceVisual` frames [0, 8, 16] per level (damage stage 3 → frame 19), and
the build icons at frames 297–301 with matching CSS positions. 4/4 pass. `adr229_build_icons` is GREEN
(2/2) — the red test ADR-355 left behind. Neighbours: pack tests (only the known pre-existing
sparse-checkout `KEYS.md` ENOENT), adr355 / adr242 / adr248 / adr333 / task256 75/75. Typecheck with
pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects (root
`node_modules/@engine/gameplay` symlink moved aside for the run, then restored). Full gate (`vitest run`
from the repo root, ~19 min): **4,016 passed / 2 failed / 3 skipped** (4,021 tests; 610 files passed,
2 failed, 2 skipped). The 2 failures are the known pre-existing ones only: the sparse-checkout
`pack.test.ts` KEYS.md ENOENT, and the flaky `persist` autosave benchmark (per-tick p95 61.7 ms vs the
50 ms non-PERF ceiling while the gate itself loaded the VM — it passes alone, and the slice touches no
persist code).

**Honest cuts.** The build-menu tiles point at transparent atlas cells until the art pass paints frames
297–301 in `items_build.png` + `@2x.png` (1x cell 32px at col = frame % 16, row 18; @2x cell 64px) —
the test is green on the text declarations, but the tile will look blank, not wrong, until then. The
world art is verified numerically only (pixel counts, outline, per-state frame differences), like Task 34:
the user's eyes on the live build are the real check that each store reads as its own thing at a glance.
Fill is by filled-slot fraction, so one stack of 99 ore in a single slot still reads "half" — the bin
looks stocked, not heaped, until six slots are used. No real-phone check.

## ADR-357: Runtime-painted build-menu icons for the five stores (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-356 declared `build_<store>` icons at `items_build` frames 297–301 and expected a
binary art pass to paint those cells, but the parent verified with a pixel read that the cells are fully
transparent in the shipped atlas (0 opaque pixels vs 349 for the Apiary's frame 286) and the snapshot
push route carries text only, so no PNG could ship the pixels from this VM. The storage batch was gated
but held for this fix: the five stores would have shown blank tiles in the build menu while looking
right in the world.

**Decision.** Paint the menu icons at runtime from the world art that already exists, instead of waiting
for a binary art pass. New code in `apps/client/src/task355-art.ts` (same module as the world art, same
`Px` rasterizer — no fork): `paintStoreMenuIconPixels(store)` paints one store's half-full front cell
(fill 1, rot 0, stage 0) at 128×128, pixel-identical to that cell of the store's painted atlas; the
half-full state reads best at 32px (the store plus its contents, not an empty bin or a heap).
`storeMenuIconDataUrl(store)` converts it to a PNG data URL through a document canvas (sync `toDataURL`,
undefined when no canvas exists); `storeMenuIconsCss(urls)` builds one override rule per store —
`[data-icon="build_<store>"]{--cz-icon:url("...");--cz-ipos:center;--cz-isize:contain}` — and
`installStoreMenuIcons(doc?, urls?)` appends (or replaces) `<style id="task355-menu-icons">` in the
document head. The override wins over the generated `items_build` block by document order at equal
specificity (same `[data-icon="..."]` attribute selector), so no change to `gameplay-panels.ts`,
`iconize()`, or the generated CSS was needed — the tiles, the ghost preview, and any other
`build_<store>` surface all pick up the painted icon. `view.ts` calls `installStoreMenuIcons()` once
during init, next to the `task355AtlasSources()` merge. It is a safe no-op without a canvas (returns
false, appends nothing, never throws), so the old blank-tile behaviour is the fallback, never a crash.
The manifest + CSS entries for frames 297–301 stay in place as the documented home for these icons;
runtime-painted icons are the source of truth until a binary art pass paints those cells, at which point
removing the one `installStoreMenuIcons()` call in `view.ts` lights the atlas icons up with no other
code change. The code deliberately does not probe the atlas pixels at startup (that would need an async
fetch + decode for five cells on every load).

**Verification.** New `apps/client/test/adr357_store_menu_icons.test.ts` (5 tests, relative imports only):
each icon is pixel-identical to its store's half-full front world cell, non-blank (> 40 opaque pixels),
carries the 1px dark-plum outline, and is distinct across the five stores (and differs from the empty
and full cells); the override stylesheet carries one centred, contained rule per store; install appends
exactly one style element, replaces it on re-install, and is a safe no-op without a canvas (jsdom has
no 2d context: `storeMenuIconDataUrl` returns undefined, install returns false, nothing appended); the
build menu tiles for the five stores carry `data-icon="build_<store>"` + `data-bicon="1"` in the
furniture category with the installed override matching each tile's icon key; and the manifest + CSS
entries for frames 297–301 remain in place. 5/5 pass. Neighbours: `adr229_build_icons` 2/2,
`task355_art` 4/4. Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11
workspace projects (root `node_modules/@engine/gameplay` symlink moved aside for the run, then
restored). Full gate (`vitest run` from the repo root, ~18 min): **4,021 passed / 2 failed / 3 skipped**
(4,026 tests; 611 files passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped). The 2 failures are the known pre-existing
ones only: the sparse-checkout `pack.test.ts` KEYS.md ENOENT, and the flaky `persist` autosave benchmark
(p95 58.2 ms vs the 50 ms ceiling under gate load — it passes alone, and the slice touches no persist
code).

**Honest cuts.** The icons are verified numerically only (pixel-exact against the world cells) — the
user's eyes on the live build are the real check that each store reads as its own thing at 32px in the
build menu. The 128px PNG data URLs (~5 × a few KB, base64) live only in a runtime `<style>` element,
never in the shipped files. A future binary art pass painting frames 297–301 should remove the
`installStoreMenuIcons()` call so the atlas icons take over; until then the two declarations coexist
and the runtime one wins.

## ADR-358: Animal-drawn vehicles — wagons, carts, carriages and transport chariot (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The wagon/vehicle batch (queued 2026-11-11 12:50 CST, behind the storage batch): realistic-looking,
realistically sized wagons of varying sizes (covered and non-covered), carts, carriages, and a transport chariot
that moves much faster when harnessed to a horse; a Harness item to hook up / detach (ADR-359); players/AI humans
shown riding in the driver's seat (ADR-360); custom artwork, sprites and animations (ADR-361). This slice is the
sim core only: defs, the drawn-movement mechanic, and crafting. The motor-vehicle system (ADR-096) already had
everything else — append-only defs, `Hitch` links, pin-joint trailer posing, `Container` storage, kit crafting —
so the work is extending it to a tow that is not a vehicle at all: a tamed mount.

**Decision.** Nine defs appended to `data/vehicles.json` (ids 31–39, append-only; the first 30 defs are untouched):
`wagon_small` / `wagon_small_covered`, `wagon_medium` / `wagon_medium_covered`, `wagon_large` /
`wagon_large_covered`, `cart`, `carriage`, `chariot`. Four new classes in `VEHICLE_CLASSES`,
`vehicles.schema.json` and `vehicle_storage.json`: `wagon`, `cart`, `carriage`, `chariot`. Covered wagons are the
same footprint, seats and storage as their uncovered twin, differing only in the `covered` flag (new optional
boolean, `true` only on class `wagon`) and a little extra mass for canvas + hoops. `fuel` and `stamina` are null;
`VehicleState` is not added on spawn and engine/headlight toggles refuse with `no_controls`, so drawn vehicles have
no engine bits on the wire. Sizes are grounded in the ADR-319 realism table (1 tile = 1 m, player 1.75 m):

| def | footprint (m) | seats | storage slots / maxWeight | mass (kg) | maxSpeed | pullMul |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wagon_small (± cover) | 2.6 × 1.4 | 2 | 30 / 400 | 350 (380) | 6.0 | 0.70 |
| wagon_medium (± cover) | 3.6 × 1.6 | 2 | 42 / 800 | 550 (590) | 5.5 | 0.62 |
| wagon_large (± cover) | 4.6 × 1.8 | 2 | 54 / 1200 | 800 (850) | 5.0 | 0.55 |
| cart | 1.8 × 1.2 | 2 | 8 / 120 | 180 | 6.5 | 0.90 |
| carriage | 3.2 × 1.6 | 4 | 16 / 250 | 700 | 6.0 | 0.65 |
| chariot | 1.6 × 1.1 | 2 | 2 / 40 | 120 | 11.5 | 1.20 |

(Small wagon ≈ a farm wagon, large ≈ a Conestoga-scale freight wagon, cart ≈ a single-axle farm cart, carriage ≈
an enclosed coach — 4 seats but less cargo than a wagon of the same size — chariot ≈ a light two-wheel war/sport
chariot. Storage slots are base × class scale from `vehicle_storage.json`: wagon 3/72, cart 2/12, carriage 2/24,
chariot 1/4. Seat 0 is the front driver bench on every def; exact per-type seat positions are ADR-360's rendering
concern, but the anchors exist and are sane now.)

**Drawn movement — the hitch design.** The mount is the tow parent and the vehicle its trailer, reusing the
existing `Hitch` component and the trailer pin-joint posing rather than a parallel system. `Hitch` already stores
NetIds, so it needs no schema change: a mount carries `Hitch` (`towNetId` = the drawn vehicle's NetId; added by
`makeMount`/`tameMount`, and lazily by `hitchVehicles` for legacy mounts) and the drawn vehicle's
`Hitch.parentNetId` is the mount's NetId. `vehicleSystem` now treats *any* vehicle with a resolvable parent —
vehicle or mount — as a trailer posed by its parent, and never self-drives a drawn vehicle (an unhitched drawn
vehicle is held at speed 0 even with a driver and drive input). `stepTrailer` and `poseTrailersInHitchFrame`
(client, after interpolation) pin the drawn vehicle's front hitch to the mount's **rear pin** — behind the mount by
half its body length (`mounts.json` `size.lengthM` / 2) plus a 0.3-tile drawbar gap — instead of a vehicle rear
hitch, with the same ±1.75 rad jackknife clamp. A ridden mount is posed from its rider's Transform (the rider
already moved in the input phase; `mountSystem` snaps the mount there later the same tick), so the pin stays exact
rather than lagging a tick; an unridden mount tows from its own Transform. `validateHitch` rejects motor tows of
drawn vehicles and mount tows of motor trailers as `incompatible` (the drawn front hitch's `accepts` list is
empty — mounts are not a vehicle class, so the rule is the drawn class itself, not the allowlist), and the
compatibility check runs before the busy checks so a wrong-kind tow reports `incompatible` even when the tow is
busy. `validateUnhitch`/`unhitchVehicle` resolve the tow by NetId (`entityByNetId`, not `vehicleByNetId`) so a
mount tow clears both sides; a mount counts as parked when its rider's `Riding.speed` is below the parked
threshold (`mountParked`; unridden mounts are parked). No ownership check on hitching in this slice — the
vehicle-hitch command never had one for motor trailers either; the Harness item (ADR-359) owns the hook/detach UX.

**Speed — data, not a constant.** `drawnSpeedCap(def, species, galloping) = min(def.maxSpeed, mountWalkOrGallop ×
def.drawn.pullMul)`, with `pullMul` on the def. The cap is enforced on the mount, not the trailer:
`installVehicleCraft` registers `drawnTowCap` as the `RideTowCap` resource (defined in `systems/movement.ts` so
movement stays free of the vehicle module — no import cycle), and `applyRidingInput` clamps the rider's target
speed to it, so a laden wagon slows its horse instead of being dragged faster than its cap. A chariot (cap 11.5)
does not slow a galloping horse (9.6) at all — the multiplier above 1 means "no drag", not "faster than the horse
can run" — while the same horse pulls a large wagon at 5.0 galloping and 2.97 walking, and a cart at its 6.5 cap.
A mount-towed drawn vehicle reports true tiles/s in `Vehicle.speed` (per-tick displacement / dt); motor tows keep
the legacy per-tick displacement value, untouched. The vehicle guard's powered limit already covers drawn defs
(`maxSpeed × boostMul`); no guard change was needed.

**Crafting.** Kits craft at the **workbench** (wooden vehicles, not garage) from three new parts — `wooden_wheel`
(planks 2 + iron_ingot 1), `canvas_cover` (cloth 4 + rope 1, covered wagons only), `wagon_frame` (planks 6 +
iron_ingot 2 + nails 4) — plus the existing `axle`, `seat`, `hitch_coupler`, `planks`, `iron_ingot`, `rope`,
`cloth`. Nine `vehicle_kit_<id>` items (ids.lock.json 498–509 items, 384–395 recipes, append-only) and
`vehicle_crafting.json` entries (`fuel: "none"`). Repair uses `wooden_wheel` (field 0.1, garage 0.3, `wreckOk` at
a garage, classes wagon/cart/carriage/chariot); `repair_kit` also works (classes empty = all). Kit item sprites
are placeholder keys in the existing `item_vehicle_kit_<id>` pattern — no art ships in this slice; dedicated art
and build-menu icons are ADR-361's. Two neighbour tests narrowed their motor-only rules to match:
`adr125_speeds` (the 2.5–6× sprint band) and `vehicle_craft` (garage station) now exempt drawn defs.

**Render note.** `packages/render/src/vehicles/layout.ts` `isPowered` now excludes the drawn classes (duplicated
`DRAWN_VEHICLE_CLASSES` list — render must not depend on gameplay). Without this, `VehicleView` would have shown
a headlight cone on a moving/occupied wagon: drawn vehicles carry no `VehicleState`, and the view defaults lights
on in that case. Wheel dust still applies (drawn vehicles kick up dust above 1.5 tiles/s); door open/close sounds
on seat changes are left as-is for ADR-361 to revisit with the art.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr358_drawn_vehicles.test.ts` (16 tests, relative imports only):
defs validate (append-only ids 31–39, drawn/fuel/cover rules, bad-def rejections); covered twins share
footprint/seats/storage; storage grows with wagon size and a carriage carries less than a same-size wagon; the
speed-cap table (chariot-with-horse gallop cap 11.5 beats horse walk 5.4 and wagon cap 5.0; donkey chariot 8.28);
mount hitch rules (mount tows drawn, motor tow of drawn and mount tow of motor trailer both `incompatible`,
`too_far`, `tow_busy`, `already_hitched`, moving-mount refusal, unhitch clears both sides); a wagon follows its
mount on the pin joint at gallop (pin gap < 1e-3, ~5.5 tiles/s, mount–wagon separation ~3.9 tiles) and a chariot
outruns it behind the same horse (~9.6 tiles/s, mount unslowed); a walking horse pulls the wagon at ~3.35
tiles/s; a drawn vehicle never self-drives with a driver and drive input; `poseTrailersInHitchFrame` re-pins a
stale drawn vehicle onto its mount (predicted entities untouched); crafting (every drawn kit at the workbench,
`validateVehicleCraft` clean, deploy records the crafter and spawns with no `VehicleState`/fuel, `wooden_wheel`
field + wreck-at-garage repair, engine toggles `no_controls`). Neighbours: `vehicles`, `vehicle_craft`,
`vehicle_net`, `vehicle_state`, `adr125_speeds`, `adr319_mounts`, `adr321_ai_mounts`, `adr323_ai_mount_supplies`,
`adr339_mount_preference/wiring`, `vehicle_keys`, `balance`, `gameplay`, `adr127_move_normalize`,
`adr351_rope_lead`, `adr352_dung_fertilizer`, `adr353_animal_diets_trough`, `adr354_tameable_calm`,
`adr344_journey_preparation`, render `vehicles` — all green (67 + 88 + 76 + 19 across the runs, no failures).
Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects (root
`node_modules/@engine/gameplay` symlink moved aside for the run, then restored). No package-name self-imports in
new test files (grep confirms; the only `@engine/gameplay` mention in the touched files is a pre-existing comment
in render's `layout.ts`). World schema hash with default gameplay installed: **0xde24c45e** (was 0x029aeedf — the
defs salt changed; no component was added, so saves stay compatible). Full gate (`pnpm vitest run` from the repo root,
2026-11-11 ~23:00 CST): **4,037 passed / 2 failed / 3 skipped** (616 files: 612 passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped) — the 2
failures are the known pre-existing ones (pack.test.ts missing `assets/building/KEYS.md` in this checkout; persist
autosave bench timing flake at 61.1 ms p95 vs a 50 ms threshold). New suite 16/16 in the gate.

**Honest cuts.** Not this slice (ADR-359/360/361 own them): the Harness equipment item and hook/detach UX; the
visible seated driver pose and driver-steers-the-mount input routing (note for ADR-360: while a driver sits in
seat 0 of a harnessed wagon, drive input must route to the pulling mount — today the mount's own rider drives and
a wagon driver cannot move anything); dedicated vehicle art and build-menu icons (kit sprites are placeholder
keys). An unridden mount tows from its own Transform, so a wandering mount's wagon lags one tick behind the pin
(the ridden case is exact). Hitching has no ownership check yet (same as motor trailers). A drawn vehicle's
`Vehicle.speed` is true tiles/s while motor-towed trailers keep the legacy per-tick displacement value — the two
conventions now differ by design, and a future cleanup should unify them.

## ADR-359: Harness equipment — hook up / detach for animal-drawn vehicles (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-358 built the drawn vehicles and the pin-joint hitch but left two gaps: hitching had no
ownership check and no harness requirement, and there was no hook/detach UX. This slice closes both: a Harness
equipment item that equips to a mount (not the player), a harness gate on drawn-vehicle hitching, detach via the
existing `vehicleUnhitch`, and AI humans that harness and hitch their own mounts. The visible seated driver pose
and driver-steers-the-mount input routing are ADR-360's; dedicated harness/vehicle art and build-menu icons are
ADR-361's.

**Decision — where harness state lives.** A new `MountHarness {item: u16}` component, appended to
`GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS` after `StoreFill` (networked + persistent, `r(C.MountHarness, "all")` in
`GAMEPLAY_REPLICATION` so every peer sees which mounts are harnessed — the mount panel and riding HUD read it on
the replica). It sits beside the saddle fields on `Mount` rather than inside it: `Mount`'s schema is frozen (the
saddle fields were part of its ADR-319/320 shape), and new tack state follows the `RopeLead`/`MountHunger`
pattern of an appended component on the same entity. No durability: a harness is tack, not armor — it never wears
and is never repaired, so `giveSaddleBack(..., 0)` is correct (`slotsAdd` defaults durability to the item's
`maxDurability ?? 0`).

**Decision — mirror the saddle pattern.** Same command shape (`gameplay.mountHarness {target, slot}` /
`gameplay.mountUnharness {target}`, appended to `MOUNT_COMMANDS` + `MOUNT_ENTITY_FIELDS`, so they flow
automatically into `input.ts` registration and the server's `GAMEPLAY_NET_COMMANDS`), same validation shape
(owner, near, item-is-harness, return-to-inventory on unequip), same event pattern (`MountResult.Harnessed = 15` /
`Unharnessed = 16`, delivered at end of tick), same client panel placement (mount panel, beside the Saddle
section), same AI action-string pattern (`mharness:<mount>:<slot>` / `munharness:<mount>`, in
`COMMAND_ACTIONS`).

**The item.** `harness` in `items.json` (id 510, append-only): name "Harness", category `resource`, maxStack 1,
weight 4, `family: "harness"`. Data-driven: `isHarnessItem` / `harnessItemId` in `mount_defs.ts` read the family,
so a future variant just works. Recipe (id 396): workbench, 6 s, leather 2 + rope 2 + iron_ingot 1 — cheaper
than `saddle_leather` (leather 4 + rope 2 + thread 2, 8 s), because it is tack, not a seat. No skill node:
`hasSkillUnlock` returns true when no node grants `item:harness`, so it is craftable by default.

**Hook up.** `validateHitch`'s drawn branch returns `no_harness` for an unharnessed mount tow (new rejection
reason, alongside `not_harness` for equipping a non-harness item and `hitched` for unequipping while towing).
Gating order in the drawn branch: dead → no_hitch → moving → **no_harness** → too_far → actor_too_far. The
hitch itself reuses ADR-358's `Hitch` + pin joint unchanged; mount + vehicle then move as one unit (proved, not
reimplemented). Detach reuses `vehicleUnhitch` (no new command): the vehicle stays parked at speed 0 and the
mount keeps its harness. Unequip-while-hitched is **rejected** (`hitched` — detach first), mirroring the
unsaddle "empty the bag first" gating. `mountDied` drops the harness into the death loot bag and removes
`MountHarness`, like the saddle.

**Client.** `mountBody` in `gameplay-panels.ts`: a harness line in the status head ("Harness on · towing X /
ready to pull") and a new "Harness" section after Saddle with Put on / Remove harness / Detach / Hook up buttons
(hook-up disabled unless harnessed; remove disabled while towing). Same shell-button list on keyboard, gamepad,
and touch via the Mount menu (U / LB+X / "Mount") — no separate input path. `mountView` gains `harness?`,
`harnesses[]`, `towing?`, `drawn[]` (parked unhitched drawn vehicles within 4 tiles of the mount); `ridingHud`
appends ` · towing <Label>`; `vehicleLabel` humanizes def ids ("wagon_medium" → "Wagon Medium").
`mountRejectText` also covers `gameplay.vehicleHitch` `no_harness`/`incompatible` (main.ts funnels rejections
through it). The harness icon falls back to the category icon automatically via `sprite_fallbacks.json`
`categoryIcons` — no art ships in this slice (ADR-361).

**AI.** `harnessPlan` in `mount_behaviors.ts` (new `HarnessPlan` type, `harnessUp` sensor on a 40-tick scan
cadence, `harness_up` behavior weight 0.6, calm, 100-tick cooldown): equip a harness from the bag, else craft one
at the workbench when unlocked + affordable (station in range or at the base station). Gated on a nearby drawn
vehicle — a bot never crafts a harness speculatively; `fillVehicleSensors` runs before `fillMountSensors` in
`buildAgentView`. `hitch_drawn` / `unhitch_drawn` in `vehicle_behaviors.ts` (reuse the `VEHICLE_CRAFT.bots`
knobs: minIndustriousnessToHitch 0.5, hitchWhenInvFreeBelow 0.2, seekRadius 30, arriveDistance 6): `drawnPair`
picks the bot's own harnessed mount, not towing/busy, plus a parked unhitched drawn vehicle within 10 tiles;
`drawnTowDone` = towing AND (invSpaceFree ≥ hitchWhenInvFreeBelow + 0.3 OR at the drive goal within
arriveDistance). The hitch run rides the mount to a staging point (front hitch + heading × (lengthM/2 + 0.3
drawbar gap)) via an approach point 3 tiles behind staging, so the final leg runs along the vehicle's heading
and the mount arrives facing it — the rear pin trails the facing, not the path. It dismounts as soon as the pin
sits on the front hitch (`pinAligned`, the server's `hitchRange`), and re-approaches after an overshoot or a
stalled final leg instead of circling. A bot without a harness never hitches a drawn vehicle. `SeenMount` gains
`harness` and `towing?`; `MOUNT_SENSOR_KEYS` gains `harnessUp`; `mounts.json` bots gain `harnessScanEveryTicks`
40, `harnessCooldownTicks` 100, `harnessUtility` 0.6.

**Test harness note.** The ADR-359 AI tests pass analog movement (`applyMovementInput(..., {x: o.moveX, y:
o.moveY})`) like a production bot: the bits-only conversion quantises to 8 iso diagonals and cannot ride a mount
onto a 1.5-tile pin. The ADR-358 `horse()` helper now harnesses the horse (the new gate requires it) — an
intentional behavior change, documented in the helper comment.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr359_harness.test.ts` (18 tests, relative imports only): item +
recipe (id 510 / 396, append-only, cheaper than a saddle); equip/unequip/swap/stranger/death/replication
(`MountHarness` replicates + persists); hook-up with harness succeeds for all 9 drawn classes; hook-up without
harness is rejected `no_harness`; detach frees the vehicle (parked, speed 0) and the mount keeps its harness;
unequip-while-hitched is rejected `hitched`; harnessed mount + vehicle move as one unit (pin gap, ~5.5 tiles/s);
mountView/HUD text; event + reject text; AI action strings + registry; AI `harness_up` equips from the bag and
crafts at the workbench; AI `hitch_drawn`/`unhitch_drawn` end-to-end; AI without a harness never hitches.
Neighbours (281 passed, 0 failed across three runs): `vehicles`, `vehicle_net`, `vehicle_craft`,
`vehicle_state`, `adr319_mounts`, `adr320_saddles`, `adr358_drawn_vehicles`, `adr321_ai_mounts`,
`adr323_ai_mount_supplies`, `vehicle_keys` (101); `adr339_mount_preference/wiring`, `adr344_journey_preparation`,
`adr351_rope_lead`, `adr352_dung_fertilizer`, `adr353_animal_diets_trough`, `adr354_tameable_calm`,
`adr127_move_normalize`, `balance`, server `adr170_vehicle_controls`, server `task22_recruitment` (137); client
`gameplay-panels`, `adr319_mount_render`, `adr322_mount_acts`, `vehicle_bandwidth` (43). Typecheck with pinned
TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects (root
`node_modules/@engine/gameplay` symlink moved aside for the run, then restored). No package-name self-imports in
new test files (grep confirms). World schema hash with default gameplay installed: **0xb629eab2** (was
0xde24c45e — the new `MountHarness` component; no mount carried a harness before this slice, so there is no
legacy harness state to migrate). Full gate (`pnpm vitest run` from the repo root, 2026-11-11 ~17:30 CST):
**4,055 passed / 2 failed / 3 skipped** (617 files: 613 passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped) — the 2 failures are the
known pre-existing ones (pack.test.ts missing `assets/building/KEYS.md` in this checkout; persist autosave bench
timing flake — it passes on re-run, p95 1.6–3.2 ms vs the 50 ms threshold). New suite 18/18 in the gate.

**Honest cuts.** Not this slice (ADR-360/361 own them): the visible seated driver pose and driver-steers-the-mount
input routing; dedicated harness/vehicle art and build-menu icons (the harness icon is the category fallback).
The ADR-358 `horse()` helper change means ADR-358's mount-hitch tests now exercise the harnessed path only —
the unharnessed rejection is covered by ADR-359's own tests. A bot that owns a harness but no drawn vehicle
never crafts one speculatively (by design), so the harness only appears once a vehicle exists.

## ADR-360: Driver-seat riding for animal-drawn vehicles (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-358 built the drawn vehicles and the pin-joint hitch, ADR-359 the harness gate — but a wagon
driver in seat 0 could not move anything: the mount's own rider drove, and a seated driver was cargo. This slice
closes that gap: the seat-0 driver steers the pulling mount, the vehicle follows on the pin joint, the driver
renders on the bench, and AI humans drive their hitched wagons. Dedicated vehicle/harness art and build-menu
icons are ADR-361's.

**Decision — input-phase hook, not a sim-phase driver (Design A).** `applyMovementInput`'s Driver branch calls
the `DrawnDrive` resource hook (registered by `installVehicleCraft` alongside the ADR-358 `RideTowCap`), and
`driveDrawnVehicle` in `vehicles.ts` moves the mount with the same `applyRidingMotion` a mounted rider gets —
so the mount moves in the input phase exactly like a ridden mount's rider does, and `mountTowPose` / `stepTrailer`
see the moved mount the same tick. The alternative (a sim-phase `DriveInputs` in `vehicleSystem`, Design B) would
have moved the mount a phase later and split the funnel; Design A keeps one funnel for players (server +
prediction), bots, and tests. `applyRidingInput` is now a thin wrapper over `applyRidingMotion(world, mover,
species, speed, hurt, actions, dt, analog, owner)` — identical motion logic, with the auto-sprint run-up and
`PlayerIntent` writes only when the input owner is the moved entity. The production frame path
(`applyGameplayInput`) calls the hook too (one tick at the fixed rate); the server/client funnel
(`applyDemoInput`) now passes the driver's real buttons + analog instead of `0` (harmless for motor drivers —
the branch ignores them there).

**Decision — precedence: the mount's own rider wins.** If a mount has a live rider AND someone sits in the
wagon's seat 0, the rider's input steers and the wagon driver's is dropped (the rider is on the animal and their
input runs first in the same input phase). The state can arise — `checkRide` blocks the driver from mounting, not
a second player from riding — so it is a rule, not an unreachable case, and it is tested (rider west beats driver
east). `RideTowCap` is re-keyed from the rider to the **mount** for the same reason: a wagon driver steers the
same mount a rider would, and `drawnTowCap` now resolves the tow from the mount's `Hitch.towNetId`.

**Speed, stamina, and state.** Sprint is the gallop (a motor vehicle's boost). Driving never builds an
auto-sprint run-up (ADR-289) and never drains the driver's stamina. The driven speed lives in a sim-local
`DrawnDriveSpeeds` resource (`Map<Entity, number>`, like `DriveInputs`) — never replicated or persisted, so a
reload or rejoin ramps up from 0; it is cleared on exit, unhitch, rider takeover, and a dead mount. The hook sets
the mount's gait anim (Walk/Run by the same `walk + 0.3` threshold as a ridden mount) on authority only, and
skips Hurt/Eat — a laden wagon caps a galloping horse at 5.5, below the run threshold, so it walks; a chariot
horse at 9.6 runs. The animal AI must not fight the driver: `drawnDriven(world, mount)` (seat 0 occupied) makes
`population.ts` skip the mount, like a ridden one — through the existing `isDrawnDriven` helper in movement.ts,
not a direct import (the population ↔ vehicle import cycle). No new component: the world schema hash is unchanged
at **0xb629eab2**.

**Enter / exit coherence.** Exit restores Idle, frees the seat, and places the driver on the vehicle's left side
(the motor rule, `width/2 + 0.6`). Dismounting the mount while it tows leaves the tow intact, and the driver can
then climb into the wagon — with one honest wrinkle: the dismount spot (beside the mount, 0.9 tiles) sits just
outside a medium wagon's enter reach (4.0 vs 3.8), so the player walks up to the bench first (tested as the real
flow, not a teleport). Exiting while hitched leaves the hitch; re-entering ramps the driven speed up from 0.
There is no eject-on-wreck anywhere (motor rule): a wrecked wagon refuses entry (`wrecked`), keeps its driver
seated, and the mount still pulls it, like a motor trailer.

**Client.** `VehicleView.sync` already returned `RiderPlacement[]` (seat anchor, quantized facing, depth-nudged)
for any def with seat anchors — but `syncVehicles` discarded the return value, so motor-vehicle riders rendered
at the vehicle centre, not their seats. This slice applies the placements in `syncVehicles` via the exported pure
helper `applyVehicleRiderPlacements` (net world → view entity by NetId, Transform + PrevTransform so the rider
does not interpolate from the centre), for **all** vehicles — one shared path, no fork, and motor riders move to
their seats too. The placement is world-space, so all four view rotations land the same spot; the `vehicle` anim
chain is forced for any `Driver` (`driverVe`), so the seated pose does not depend on the sim AnimState. The
engine/lights HUD chip (`vehicle-controls.ts`) hides for drawn defs and ignores the engine/lights buttons there
(Interact still exits); `driving` stays true, so the touch driving layout is unchanged.

**AI.** New `drive_drawn` behavior in `vehicle_behaviors.ts` (same knobs as `drive`: bravery 0.25, drive 25 tiles,
arrive within 6; gallops when farther than 18 from the goal): enter the towed wagon's driver seat (`venter:<id>:0`),
steer toward the drive goal through `AgentOutput`, exit when arrived and parked. `pickRide` excludes drawn classes
(motor/bicycle only) and the `drive` behavior returns false for a drawn vehicle it somehow rides, so the two
behaviors never fight; `drive_drawn` sits **after** `vehicle_service` in the array because `vehicle_craft.test.ts`
destructures `[drive, vehicle_service]` by position. `"drive_drawn"` joins `DISMOUNT_NOW` in `mount_behaviors.ts`,
so a riding bot gets off its mount to climb into the wagon. The AI test harness's `apply` gains the
`VehicleEnterCmd` / `VehicleExitCmd` cases the ADR-359 harness lacked.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr360_driver_seat.test.ts` (17 tests, relative imports only):
seat-0 pose per def in all 8 directions (Sit, facing = vehicle heading) + carriage 4-seat passengers; driver
steers the mount (pin gap < 1e-3, wagon_medium gallop 5.5, chariot 9.6, walk 3.35); passenger input moves nothing;
unhitched wagon stays put; rider-vs-driver precedence; population AI does not fight the driver (goal set west,
driver steers east); exit/dismount/re-enter/wreck coherence; `drive_drawn` registry + `pickRide` exclusion +
mount-policy dismount + end-to-end bot drive (enters, hauls to (30, 0), arrives, exits, still hitched); schema

## ADR-361: Dedicated art for wagons, carts, carriages, chariot and harness (SurVivaZ)

Unique runtime-painted art for the nine drawn defs and the harness — no recolors, no reused sprites, no
binaries (the snapshot push route carries text only). Painted with the `Px` rasterizer in
`apps/client/src/task361-art.ts`, in the game's warm palette with the 1px dark-plum outline `[40,30,50]`
(Task 34 / ADR-356 house style); the fragment `packages/assets/pack/task361/manifest.task361.json` carries
layout only, and `view.ts` overrides the registry sources with blob URLs from the painter (same shape as
task34/355). Sixteen atlas keys (`veh_art_<def>` × 9, `veh_art_harness_<art>` × 7) registered in
`packages/assets/pack/ids.lock.json` (+16 keys, 5463–5478) and in `MANIFEST_INDEX` (optional fragment). The
fragment must ALSO be added to the `pack/` mount filter in `apps/client/vite.config.ts` — it hardcodes the
served fragment dirs, and without `task361` the dev server never serves the manifest, so the client never
requests it (caught by the ADR-248 server/client parity test; see the gate note below).

**World sprites.** One atlas per def, 8 directions in Art order (E,SE,S,SW,W,NW,N,NE), one frame per direction
(`idle` frames `[0]`, dirStride 1); medium/large wagons use 4 cols × 2 rows so the atlas stays under the 2048px
mobile cap (262×8 = 2096 and 307×8 = 2456 would exceed it). `resolveVehicleArt` binds by def id at native
scale 1 with facing offset +PI/4; the frame anchor (`py/h`) comes from `drawnVehicleFrame`, which mirrors the
renderer's own `vehicleFrame` projection (45.25 px/tile on diagonals, drawbar tip included). Frames: wagon_small
217×161, wagon_medium 262×184, wagon_large 307×207, cart 180×143, carriage 244×214, chariot 171×124; covered
twins are taller by the canvas arch (e.g. wagon_small_covered 217×194). The bench top sits at `seatZPx`
(32px on wagons/cart/chariot, 37px on the carriage) = `modelZScale × seatZ × 16`, so the ADR-360 driver rests
on the painted bench. Geometry asserted against `vehicles.json` in the tests (footprint, seatX, hitchX, covered).

**Per-vehicle look (eyes on the live build are the final check — this art was verified numerically, not
visually).** Wagon_small: barn-red `[176,64,46]` open bed, wooden cargo rails, crates/barrel/sacks, front bench,
two axles. Wagon_medium: same shape in green `[63,138,74]`, longer bed, more cargo. Wagon_large: blue
`[47,111,176]`, the biggest bed by a clear margin. Covered twins: the same bed in the same paint with a cream
canvas arch `[232,222,196]` over dark hoop arcs behind the bench — no cargo visible. Cart: natural-wood
single-axle bed, twin shafts, small bench. Carriage: near-black `[44,44,52]` enclosed cab with glass windows
`[58,84,104]`, a door seam, gold beltline trim, a roof slab, a driver's box at the front and two brass lamps.
Chariot: crimson `[178,60,44]`, slim two-wheel with the biggest spoked wheels (r 0.8 vs the cart's 0.62), low
rails, a small rear bench — it reads light and fast. Every vehicle has a ground shadow and a drawbar/tongue
running forward from the front hitch 0.38 tiles, bridging the gap toward the mount's rear pin from the vehicle
side (the harness traces end at the mount's rear edge).

**Harness.** `mount_harness_<art>` overlays for all seven mount arts, one 128px cell per direction sized to each
species' body averages (max body 79×95 horse, 76×102 moose). Leather chest + girth bands, a back strap along
the spine, brass buckles, two rope traces running back toward the vehicle. `LAYER_KEY.harness = 0.005`, below
the saddle (0.01) — a harnessed + saddled mount shows both. `view.ts` `syncMounts` adds the layer via `layerOn`
exactly when `isHarnessed(net, m)` (MountHarness present) and destroys it on unequip/mount loss; the layer
copies the mount's VAnim state, so it stays frame-locked to the gait. One cell per direction is shared by every
gait frame (tack has no gait of its own), so the mount bobs ~1–2px under the straps while walking/galloping.

**Build-menu / kit icons (ADR-357 pattern).** Thirteen keys — the nine `item_vehicle_kit_<def>`, `item_wooden_wheel`,
`item_canvas_cover`, `item_wagon_frame`, `harness` — painted at runtime from the world art (each kit icon IS its
def's SE world cell at icon scale, pivot (64,100); the three parts and the harness are dedicated small drawings:
spoked wheel, folded canvas, bare frame, coiled harness) and injected as the `#task361-menu-icons` CSS override
after the stylesheet (`installVehicleMenuIcons`, same call site as `installStoreMenuIcons`). Drawn vehicles have
no build-menu pieces (pieces.json has none — kits craft at the workbench), so the icons surface on crafting
recipe tiles and inventory/hotbar slots, all reading the same `data-icon` keys; `panelIcon` routes a kit tile to
the painted icon once the override is installed and to the fiber category fallback before it (asserted both ways).

**Cuts, stated not faked.** Wheels do not animate: the vehicle body sprite is created with `frameId: 0` and no
VAnim, so the renderer shows one frame per direction and always plays `idle` — spokes are painted 15° off
vertical, a mid-roll pose, instead of faking an animation the game can't show; there are no moving/idle
variants. Damage/wear stages are a cut: Art car sprites carry `intact`/`damaged`/`wrecked` anims and
`atlasManager` builds a `damage[]` table, but it is only consumed by `resolvePiece` (build pieces) — vehicle
bodies never go through it, so no worn/damaged variants were bolted on as a parallel system.

**Tests.** New `apps/client/test/adr361_drawn_vehicle_art.test.ts` (12 tests, node env) + `adr361_vehicle_menu_icons.test.ts`
(2 tests, jsdom) + `adr361_vehicle_menu_icons_fallback.test.ts` (1 test, jsdom): every def's world sprite resolves

2128/2999/4562 where open beds have 0); sizes order wagon_small < wagon_medium < wagon_large by frame and by
painted opaque width; carriage glass 1308 px vs 0 on the wagon; chariot tyre 639 px vs the cart's 383; harness cells
466–1225 opaque / 109–316 outline per direction with leather + rope present; every icon non-blank, outlined and
distinct (kits 2531–4457 opaque, wheel 5353, canvas 4313, frame 2566, harness 3597); fragment layout matches the
painter, atlas image/ktx2 twins exist on disk, no key collides with vehicles/nature/items/task34/task355; the

`task355_art`, `adr357_store_menu_icons`, `adr229_build_icons`, `adr319_mount_render`, `adr322_mount_acts`,

The first gate run (4,098 passed / 4 failed) also failed `adr248_server_manifest_parity` — a real regression

## ADR-362: In-game guide — content + data (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The guide batch (ADR-362 content/data, ADR-363 UI, ADR-364 art) needs a content model the UI
slice can render without changes to its shape, and the guide's numbers must not drift from the game: a guide
that quotes a stale number is worse than no guide. The content must also stay honest about what changed since
earlier tasks — ADR-277 removed direct air-temperature HP damage, so the guide must not repeat the Task 24
"outdoor cold damage 0–10 °F at 2.0 hp/s, blocked by insulation ≥ 10" rule; insulation now only moves felt
temperature, and only the freezing/overheating body-temperature tiers harm.

**Decision — content model.** `packages/gameplay/data/guide.json` holds 15 sections (getting-started,
controls, icons, diseases, temperature, cooking, building, ai-humans, animals, mounts-vehicles, crops-farming,
storage, seasons-weather, combat-defence, multiplayer-clans). Each section has an id, title, an icon reference
(a key only — `item:`, `piece:`, `vehicle:`, `mount:` or `pet:`, resolved to art by ADR-364), an intro, and
body items of three kinds: `{ text }` prose, `{ fact, label, format }` numbers, and `{ keys, label, action? }`
controls rows.

**Decision — no numbers in prose.** Prose (`text`, `intro`, `label`) must contain no digits at all;
`validateGuide` enforces it. Every duration, temperature, damage, cost or stat a player reads is a fact entry
resolved by `packages/gameplay/src/guide.ts` from the same data files and named constants the game reads:
diseases from `data/diseases.json` + `CARE_CURE_SECONDS` / `FLU_AFTER_SECONDS`; season ranges and weather from
`data/environment.json` (shown in °F, converted from the °C ranges the game stores); crop rules from
`data/farming.json` + `FROST_KILL_F` / `LATE_FALL_DAYS`; treats from `data/pets.json`; storage from
`data/pieces.json`; vehicles from `data/vehicles.json` via `drawnSpeedCap` (chariot 11.5, large wagon 5.0
behind a galloping horse); mounts from `data/mounts.json`; the hire pool size from `WANTED_ITEM_KEYS` (35);
the safe radius from `SAFE_SPAWN_RADIUS` (20); fire heat from `FIRE_HEAT_MAX_C` / `FIRE_HEAT_TAU_S`
(+15 °C over 120 s); body-temperature tier boundaries probed from `temperatureTier` (freezing 35 °C,
overheating 39 °C) rather than copied; salt burn from `SALT_CONSUME_TICKS` (3 min). Where a value cannot be
sourced it is left out, not guessed.

**Decision — accessor for ADR-363.** `getGuideSections()` / `guideSection(id)` return the validated sections;
`resolvedGuideSection(id)` returns the same shape with every fact already resolved to a display string
("70–88 °F", "15 min", "10 Pine Log, 10 Stone, 2 Dye"); `resolveGuideFact(path, format)` resolves one fact
and throws on an unknown path, format or value. `validateGuide()` returns every problem (dangling fact path,
unresolvable icon key, digits in prose); `getGuideSections()` throws when the shipped guide is malformed.
Exported from the `@engine/gameplay` index. No UI is built here and no art is resolved (ADR-363/364 own
those); `apps/client/src/game-menus.ts`, `gameplay-panels.ts` and the pause menu are untouched.

**Decision — controls rows.** Each row names the input action(s) it documents and is pinned by the tests to
`packages/input/profiles/keyboardMouse.json` (gameplay cannot import the input package, so the check lives in
the test, not the loader). The one exception is the character-sheet row (K), a client menu hotkey, pinned to
`apps/client/src/game-menus.ts` instead.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr362_guide.test.ts` (10 tests, relative imports only): the
loader validates clean with 15 sections in order; prose carries no digits (232 prose strings checked); every
fact path has an independently recomputed expectation from the raw source JSONs and resolves to it — 130
distinct paths (133 fact entries), so a drift in any source file fails the test; headline numbers pinned
(summer 70–88 °F, heat wave 89–100 °F, winter 0–35 °F, flu 15 min / Honey Tea, care cure 4 min, dung
fertiliser 15 min, chariot 11.5 tiles/s, large wagon 5 tiles/s, claim cost 10 Pine Log + 10 Stone + 2 Dye,
safe radius 20 tiles, 24 inventory slots, 394 recipes, fire +15 °C); every disease in diseases.json has a
duration (when it expires) and a cure fact; every icon key resolves in its own table; every item key a fact
names exists; all 28 controls rows match the default keyboard profile (plus the K menu hotkey); accessors work
and throw on unknown paths/formats. Neighbours: adr355/adr356 storage suites green (28 tests across the 3
files); full gameplay package suite green (191 files passed, 2 skipped; 2005 tests passed, 3 skipped).
Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects (root
`node_modules/@engine/gameplay` symlink moved aside for the run, then restored) — the first run caught 1 real
error in the new test (`bindings` possibly undefined), fixed, re-run clean. No package-name self-imports in new
files (grep confirms).

**Honest cuts.** Not this slice (ADR-363/364 own them): no guide window UI, no menu/pause wiring, no art
resolution — the icon keys are references only. The guide does not surface numbers with no data source to pin
them to (e.g. per-kind zombie HP is in zombies.json but not shown — the combat section sticks to spawn rates,
safe radius and fire). Job names (Gather, Farm, Defend, Craft, Maintain) are prose: they come from the
`WorkerJob` const enum, which is erased at runtime, so no runtime derivation exists and the test does not pin
them. The `diseases.count` fact path exists in the registry for the completeness check but is not referenced
by any section.

## ADR-363: In-game guide — UI, main menu + pause menu (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-362 shipped the guide content model (15 sections, facts resolved from the game's own
data, icon keys only). This slice builds the window players actually open: a Guide entry in the main menu
and in the in-game pause menu, rendering the ADR-362 sections with no new UI language and no new art.

**Decision — one body, two shells.** `apps/client/src/guide-panel.ts` builds the guide body once
(`buildGuidePanel(initialId?)`): a section list above the selected section's detail. The in-game modal
(`GameMenus.guidePanel()`, gm-modal shell) and the main-menu screen (`BootUI`, boot panel) share that body;
only the shell differs. The body renders through `getGuideSections()` / `resolvedGuideSection(id)` — title,
intro, prose items, fact label + resolved value rows, and controls rows with `<kbd>` key chips. Guide text
lives in the ADR-362 data, never hardcoded in the UI.

**Decision — pause flow preserved, not reimplemented.** The pause menu gains a Guide entry (a `GAME_MENUS`
row, so it appears in Pause automatically; no hotkey, not a menu-bar button). Opening it stacks the guide
over the pause menu in the UINav stack; Esc / ✕ / B closes back to pause, and the pause menu stays in the
stack while the guide is open — so the singleplayer pause in `main.ts` (keyed on `nav.isOpenId("pause")`,
audio off, UI live) holds exactly as before. Closing from the main menu returns to the main menu. No other
menu entry's behaviour changes.

**Decision — section navigation, no search.** The 15 sections are a button grid (the quick-jump) with
`[data-tabs=tab]`, so gamepad LB/RB cycles them through the existing `cycleTabs` tab pattern, and the
selected tab follows the chat-channels convention (selected = plain green button, the rest `alt` — that
class is what `cycleTabs` reads to find the current tab). Keyboard arrows / Tab / Enter, touch taps and
D-pad + A all work through the existing modal and boot-screen navigation; focus starts on the first section
(`data-autofocus`) on the main menu. No search box: a text search would invent a new modal pattern for a
list short enough to scan.

**Decision — icons via the existing `[data-icon]` hook, text-only fallback.** `guideIconKey(icon, has)`
resolves a section's icon ref to a `[data-icon]` key only when the shipped stylesheet has art for it:
`item:` via the item's sprite key (`iconForItem`, same fallback the panels use), `piece:` via the
build-menu icon (`buildIconKey`, tiered candidates first), `vehicle:` via the ADR-361 kit key
(`item_vehicle_kit_<key>`). `mount:` / `pet:` have no menu-icon art and resolve to nothing. A section
without a resolvable icon renders its title text-only — no `<img>`, never a broken image. 13 of the 15
sections resolve today (all 8 `item:` keys and all 5 `piece:` keys have shipped CSS rules); the two that
do not are `pet:dog_lab` (animals) and `mount:horse` (mounts-vehicles).

**Verification.** New `apps/client/test/adr363_guide_ui.test.ts` (11 tests): the resolver with permissive,
shipped-CSS and empty `has` sets; all 15 sections render (title, intro, every text / fact / keys item via
the ADR-362 accessors); icons render only where art exists (torch yes, dog_lab / horse no, no `<img>`
anywhere); guide opens from the pause menu and stacks over it (`isOpenId("pause")` still true), ✕ and Esc
close back to pause, LB/RB cycles sections; the main menu gains a Guide button, the guide opens, keyboard
arrows move between sections, Esc / Back returns to the main menu without resolving a choice. Neighbours:
menus/modals, tutorials, pad navigation, store/vehicle menu icons, seed picker, world preview, compass
tutorial, version marker (12 files, 74 tests) green. Full client suite green: 184 files, 872 tests
passed. Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean across all 11 workspace projects
(root `node_modules/@engine/gameplay` symlink moved aside for the run, then restored). No package-name
self-imports in new files (grep confirms).

**Honest cuts.** No search or quick-jump beyond the section grid (see above). No art resolution for
`mount:` / `pet:` icons — that is ADR-364's job; the animals and mounts-vehicles sections show a text-only
title until then. The guide has no hotkey and is not on the menu bar: it opens from the main menu or from
pause only.

## ADR-364: In-game guide — art: section icons + action images (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** ADR-362 shipped the guide content model (15 sections, icon keys only) and ADR-363 the
window, but two section icons had no art (`pet:dog_lab`, `mount:horse`) and the guide showed no pictures
of the actions it describes. This slice wires every section icon through the existing art and adds images
for the six key actions (building placement/hologram, cooking at a fire, taming/feeding, harnessing a
mount, using the trough, claiming a base) — all from the game's own sprites and runtime-painted art, no
new sprites, no recolors, no binary art (the snapshot push route carries text only).

**Decision — the two gaps close with atlas-crop CSS rules, not new painting.** `pet_dog_lab` and
`mount_horse` get hand-written `[data-icon]` rules appended to `apps/client/src/gameplay-panels.css`
(after the generated ICONS block, the ADR-264/265 pattern — the generator only rewrites between the
ICONS markers, so the tail is safe). Each rule crops the SW idle frame (direction 3, the widest profile
view for both animals: dog 51×32, horse 75×82) out of the shipped atlas with `--cz-isize` / `--cz-ipos`
computed from the nature manifest's `dirFrames` (frame-major indexing: `dirFrames[frame * dirs + dir]`).
`guideIconKey` maps `pet:` → `pet_<key>` and `mount:` → `mount_<key>` like the other kinds, gated on
`has()`. All 15 sections now resolve an icon.

**Decision — action images are composed scenes of `[data-icon]` tiles.** guide.json gains a fourth body
item kind, `{ image, caption }` (validated in `guide.ts`: kebab-case registry id, non-empty digit-free
