`guide_book.png` (so `iconImg`/`iconUrl` serve it like the embedded ic_ icons) and installs
a `[data-icon="guide_book"]` override rule; idempotent, safe no-op without a canvas, with a
`urls` test seam like the other installers. Installed at startup in `IsoView.create` (next
to `installVehicleMenuIcons`) and lazily in `buildGuidePanel` — the boot menu can show the
Guide before the view exists. Used by: the `GAME_MENUS` guide entry (was `"📖"`, now
`guide_book.png` — the entry has no menu-bar button, so the def was dead text until now);
the pause menu's Guide button and "Play the guide again" button (the `panel()` button tuple
gains an optional icon element); the Settings "Play the guide again" button (was `"📖 Play
the guide again"`); the in-game Guide panel header (`guidePanel()` prepends the icon to the
h2); the boot-menu Guide screen header (`menu.ts`, `<img src="iconUrl(...)">` in the header
string). The main-menu Guide BUTTON stays text-only (it never had an emoji; the boot menu's
branding-icon path covers Singleplayer/Multiplayer/Settings only). The tutorial's "Broken
leg 🦴" step is untouched — the tutorial is not the Guide.

No sprint with a broken leg (`packages/gameplay/src/systems/movement.ts:244`): the sprint
computation in the shared `applyMovementInput` (server authority + client prediction alike)
gains `&& !hasDisease(world, e, "broken_leg")`. While the leg is broken, sprint stays 0 —
speed is walk x the disease moveMul 0.5 — and `vitalsSystem` never sees a sprint to drain
stamina for, because it reads `PlayerIntent.sprint`. The `AutoSprint` latch is untouched, so
sprint resumes the moment the leg heals (cure or expiry) with no new warm-up. Other diseases
do not block sprint (only `broken_leg`). Riding gallop (`applyRidingMotion`) and driving
boost are deliberately NOT gated: the mount's speed is not the rider's leg. Client
reflection: on foot there is no sprint button on any device — sprint is the ADR-289
auto-sprint after 4 s straight, and the Shift key / touch Boost button do nothing on foot
today (Boost lives only in the driving layout, where it gallops the mount). So there is
nothing to disable on foot; the enforcement is the sim, the HUD already shows the broken-leg
chip, and the tutorial "Run" step cannot complete while the leg is broken (its probe reads
`PlayerIntent.sprint`). Note for the record: the Guide's Controls row still says Sprint is
Shift — Shift is the Sprint action bit, used for gallop and by AI; on foot it is a no-op
today. That wording predates this ADR and is left alone.

Gaps (no icon invented): the treats rows for cat_tabby, fox and owl derive `pet:<species>`
but only `pet_dog_lab` has a CSS rule — cat_tabby has a shipped atlas
(`pets_cat_tabby.png`) and needs one crop rule in the ADR-364 pattern; fox and owl have no
`pets_fox`/`pets_owl` atlas files at all (their in-world sprites live in the nature atlas as
`animal_fox`/`animal_owl`), so their pet rules need an art decision first. Spring has no HUD
season icon (`SEASON_ICON` covers summer/fall/winter only), so the spring row stays bare.
The 69 icon-less rows are listed in the ADR-387 report. Tests: new
`packages/gameplay/test/adr387_guide_icons.test.ts` (derivation pinned row by row, every
returned guide key resolves in its defs table, coverage 133/64 pinned) and
`adr387_broken_leg_sprint.test.ts` (blocked while broken, walk x 0.5, no stamina drain,
other disease sprints, cure/expiry resume, AI human blocked, tutorial contract), plus
`apps/client/test/adr387_guide_icons.test.ts` (book pixels, install seam, panel rendering
per row, quick-jump icons, entry buttons and headers, no 📖 anywhere in the Guide UI).
Updated: ADR-362 (resolved fact items now carry `icon`), ADR-363/ADR-364 (fact-row `<img>`
icons are allowed, scoped to fact rows / action-image figures respectively).


## ADR-388: Quieter crouching, and the render path is ready for dedicated crouch frames (SurVivaZ)

Context: ADR-244 already toggles crouch (walk ×0.6, noise ×0.4, zombie sight ×0.55) and ADR-241 already
asks the doll for `crouch_idle` → `idle` / `crouch_walk` → `crouch_idle` → `walk` → `idle`. The live v1
customization pack (and every wear layer) has no dedicated crouch clips; only the excluded v2 sample does.
Gather / build / attack / door / structureHit already went through `makeNoise` (so the crouch multiplier
applied), but walking produced no `NoiseLevel` at all, so "quieter when crouched" was almost meaningless
for sneaking past zombies. AI humans already sneak-crouch in the 4..10 tile band (ADR-252). Art & Assets
will author the missing clips; this ADR must not paint, reuse, or recolor walk frames as crouch.

Decision: keep the ADR-241 key lookup and v1 fallback (no fake art). Add `walk` (12), `sprint` (18) and
`swim` (7) to `zombies.json` `noise`. `applyMovementInput` emits that amount through `makeNoise` when a
`Survival` entity actually changes position (authority only, same as every other source), so crouch still
multiplies it to 0.4×. Swimming uses the swim amount (water muffles). A crouched body cannot sprint, so
it stays on walk ×0.4. Client footstep SFX (not zombie hearing) use `Anim.Crouch` at `CROUCH_STEP_GAIN`
0.45. AI humans share this funnel, so their sneak-crouch is quieter too. Tests cover every noise table
entry, standing vs crouched walk / swim, no noise when still, determinism, crouched AI walk, and the
anim chain keys.

Art landed in `5eb3c037` (`docs/ART_KEYS_CROUCH.md`): dedicated `crouch_idle` (2 frames @ 4 fps) and
`crouch_walk` (4 frames @ 8 fps), 8 facings, on every live v1 doll layer (body, wear, hair, hat, face,
eyes, hands, accessories). Pages `cz_crouch_<slot>_<n>` stream like the ride pages; the ADR-241 chain
still falls back while a page is paging in, or if a layer is missing the clip: `crouch_walk` falls back to the resident `walk` (the doll keeps stepping instead of sliding on idle) and `crouch_idle` to `idle`. Crouch pages are never boot-prefetched or cache-warmed (`collectWarmupPrefetchUrls` now skips every lazy doll page, not only ride pages), and page-ins stay inside the existing 2-uploads-per-frame budget, so a first crouch costs a few frames of fallback, not a stalled frame. The
renderer reads frame counts, rects and anchors from the manifest (it does not hardcode them). AI
humans share this rig; no separate bot sheets.

## ADR-389: Waterfall tile classification and Art's lip / sheet / pool frames (SurVivaZ)

Context: ADR-386 already detects a water face that drops ≥ 2 levels (`WATERFALL_MIN_DROP`) and draws
it as a mesh face with downward procedural streaks (flags 6..9), suppressing the gt skirt on that face.
Art & Assets shipped dedicated waterfall tiles in `e8c03108`, polished in `097c8a71`
(`docs/ART_KEYS_WATERFALL.md`): page `gt_waterfall` (resident with the other gt_ ground pages, 1x and
@2x PNG + KTX2; `097c8a71` packs 256×352 / 512×704), unique packed keys
`gt_waterfall_{lip,sheet_1,sheet_2,pool}_{px,nx}`, 6 frames @ 8 fps looping on `animations.idle`.
The anchor is the diamond centre, the same world point as `gt_water`. Trim rects (and therefore
dirFrames fractions) may change as Art polishes the page — the renderer reads them with
`AssetRegistry.dirFrame()` and does not hardcode them. py and ny are not packed — draw the px or nx
key with `FrameRef.flipX` (instance mask bit 8). Every key's placeholder is `gt_water`.
`gt_waterfall_pool_*` is an impact overlay (foam, splash ring, mist), not a full-diamond refill.

Decision: a classifier (`classifyWaterfallFaces` / `classifyWaterfallAt` in
`packages/render/src/waterfallTiles.ts`) tags, in world space with dirs px/py/nx/ny:

- **lip** on the source of a ≥ 2 drop (the breach / tiles[0] drop edge);
- **fall** on the source of that drop (sheet_2 for a 2-level face; drop > 2 stacks sheet_2 then
  sheet_1, never stretched) and on 1-level water-to-water cascade steps after the fall (sheet_1);
- **pool** on the lower neighbour at each fall's destination, in the same flow direction as the sheet.

An ordinary 1-level stream ledge, a land cliff, and a missing / unloaded neighbour are not falls.
A 1-level cascade is only a sheet when the source sits downhill of a ≥ 2 waterfall (walk uphill at
most 8 water steps). `planWaterfallArt` resolves Art's packed keys via `AssetRegistry.dirFrame()`
and returns instance descriptors. `TileTerrain` still emits the destination's `gt_water` instance;
the pool (and the lip) is a mode-4 overlay drawn on top of that water in a blended pass on chunks
that have a fall (one extra instanced draw; blend stays off for every other ground tile). Sheets
stay in the opaque pass so the foam at the foot of the sheet stacks with the pool. Art mode 3 draws
a sheet as a full frame with no diamond/skirt discard. Camera-facing faces only (view-quarter mask);
far faces keep the mesh silhouette. When the page is resident, 1-level cascade skirts are suppressed
so sheet_1 shows, and `uWaterfallArt` turns off the ADR-386 procedural streaks — the mesh face is a
quiet under-layer. Canvas2D draws the same planned instances after ground art (pools, then lips,
then sheets), with `scale(-1,1)` around the pivot when `flipX` is set, and is a no-op when the page
is missing (residency is cached per registry). Until the sprites are in the registry,
`planWaterfallArt` returns [] and streaks stay.

Keys (no seasonal twins; falls do not ice): `gt_waterfall_lip_px` / `_nx`, `gt_waterfall_sheet_1_px`
/ `_nx` (1-level, 16 px), `gt_waterfall_sheet_2_px` / `_nx` (2-level, 32 px), `gt_waterfall_pool_px`
/ `_nx`. Paint box 64×64 at 1x (32 px diamond + 32 px skirt for a 2-level face).

## ADR-390: Storage container windows show the container's display name (SurVivaZ)

Context: the inventory panel always titled the window "Inventory" and the container pane "Storage · N
slots", so a player searching a crate, a log store, a death bag or a saddlebag could not see which
container was open. Phone portrait has a narrow header; a long name must not cut off.

Decision: `containerDisplayName(world, entity, player?)` resolves, in order: a `Mount` → "Saddlebag";
a `Vehicle` → title-cased def id (`wagon_medium` → "Wagon Medium"); a `LootBag` → "Your Bag" / "Death
Bag" / "Zombie Loot" / "Supply Crate" / "Loot Bag" (same sources as ADR-161 labels, title-cased for a
window); a `BuildPiece` on the entity or `pieceOf` the storage attachment → title-cased piece key
(`log_store` → "Log Store", `large_chest` → "Large Chest", `campfire` → "Campfire", ruins and
crafting-station storage included). Fallback "Storage". `containerView` carries `name`;
`inventoryPanelTitle` is that name when a container is in reach, else "Inventory". The inventory
modal's h2 and aria-label use it on open and on refresh; the container section heading and aria-label
use it too. Header CSS: `min-width:0` on the header, `flex:1; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis;
white-space:nowrap` on the h2, `flex-shrink:0` on the close button, so portrait does not cut off.
No new controls (keyboard, gamepad and touch already open this panel).

## ADR-391: Lossless oxipng pass over every shipped PNG, pinned and cached by file hash (SurVivaZ)

Context: the built dist was 963.8 MB, 539.8 MB of it 2,725 PNGs written by Art's tools with default zlib
settings. The git pack is already 5.55 GiB, so re-encoding the PNGs in the repo (a second copy of every
image in history) is not an option. The phone downloads and caches all of this on first play.

Decision: `vite build` runs `optimizeDistPngs` (scripts/oxipng.mjs) at the end of the art copy step,
over the whole dist (art/ and Vite's assets/). Each PNG is looked up by sha256(tool tag + source bytes)
in `.cache/oxipng/png/`; misses are recompressed with oxipng 9.1.5 `-o 2` (no `--strip`, no `--alpha`)
and stored; a cached result replaces the dist file only when smaller; entries this build did not use are
pruned. The binary is pinned: on linux-x64 the 9.1.5 musl release tarball is downloaded once into
`.cache/oxipng/tools/` and its sha256 checked (`571e69fc…a472e2`); elsewhere an `oxipng 9.1.5` on PATH or
`OXIPNG_BIN` is used. `SURVIVAZ_OXIPNG=off` copies PNGs verbatim; the default warns and skips when the
binary is unavailable; CI and Pages set `required`, so a deploy never silently ships unoptimized PNGs.
Both workflows restore `.cache/oxipng` with actions/cache (key: tool version + hash of the PNG sources).

oxipng only changes the zlib stream, filters and colour type (RGBA → palette / grey where exact):
decoded RGBA, fully transparent texels' RGB and every ancillary chunk are unchanged. Verified on the full
dist: 2,725 / 2,725 PNGs decode to identical RGBA with identical chunk sets; no 16-bit or interlaced
files. `apps/client/test/adr391_oxipng.test.ts` pins mode off, decode identity (palette reduction with
transparent coloured texels) and cache hit / prune behaviour when the pinned binary is present.

Result: PNG 539,795,816 → 407,407,325 B (−132,388,491). Cold run 2 m 25 s on 8 cores (about 5 min on
a 4-vCPU runner), cached rebuilds re-run only changed PNGs. Rejected: `-o 4` (+0.8 %, 4× time), Zopfli
(+1.1 %, 26× time).

## ADR-392: Ship only the art the client resolves; resident atlases lose their unread KTX2 twins (SurVivaZ)

Context: the art copy shipped every file that matched the MOUNTS regexes. The size audit replayed the
client's real resolution (merged manifest → `sourcesFromManifest` → `AtlasManager.rebuild` pools) and
found files nothing can request: the 15 stalls / pvp_clan atlases that lose the first-wins merge to the
pack's copies, `@2x` tint / sway / emissive mask PNGs (only 1x masks load, `fitToPage` scales them),
emissive KTX2 (the emissive layer is PNG only), atlas layout JSON (frames live in the manifests), the KTX2
twins of atlases that are resident on every device path (resident atlases always load PNG pages; KTX2 is
read only by the lazy wear / veh / bld / body / stream pools), Art's engine-pack copies under
`ui/{input,hooks}/atlas/engine/`, branding mocks, the flat menu backgrounds (parallax ships), the
`ui/kit/css/` frames (Vite bundles them from the CSS) and the 26 legacy `.ogg` files ADR-334 left
behind (read only by `pack/audio/manifest.json`, which no client code loads).

Decision: `vite build` plans dist/art with `planArt` (apps/client/art-build.ts) instead of copying every
mounted file. The planner replays the client at build time: `servedManifestIndex` →
`loadMergedManifestWith` (fragments, v2 shards, ids.lock) → `sourcesFromManifest(..., {probeSiblings:
false})` exactly as view.ts does, plus prefetch-art.ts's `collectPrefetchUrls` /
`collectWarmupPrefetchUrls`. A file under an atlas directory (`pack/**/atlases/`, `stalls/atlases/`,
`pvp_clan/atlases/`) ships when a resolved source names it (url, emissive, every mask candidate, ktx2,
masksKtx2, every page and its KTX2 twins), when it is a `*.hands.json`, or when its file name appears
literally in client / package source or in a shipped non-manifest JSON (name tags, gather fx, CSS).
`AtlasManager.rebuild`'s pool sorting moved into the pure `atlasPoolSets` (rebuild calls it; no behaviour
change) so the build uses the same code: `ktx2UnreadAtlases` is the set that is in no lazy pool with
every streaming flag on and low-budget residency (budget < 128 MB streams pets / critters / ground), and
those atlases' `ktx2` / `masksKtx2` / `pages[].ktx2` / `pages[].masksKtx2` fields are deleted from the
shipped manifest JSON (shards included); their files then drop under the same rule. The 74 pets /
critters / ground atlases that stream on low-memory devices keep their KTX2. The legacy `.ogg` names
left the MOUNTS regex. The dev server is unchanged and serves every mounted file.

Pixel and sound identity: `apps/client/test/adr392_art_plan.test.ts` replays the client against the
planned output and pins that (1) every resolved file that exists in the mounts ships, (2) the resolved
sources equal the unplanned ones except the stripped KTX2 fields, (3) every stripped atlas is resident
under all 64 combinations of the six streaming flags, (4) the low-memory streamed pets / critters /
ground keep KTX2, (5) drops are only atlas-dir files nothing resolves or names, resident KTX2 twins and
the listed UI copies, and no `.ogg` ships. So the A16's ASTC / ETC2 KTX2 pools, desktop's lossless pools,
`gl=safe` / `?ktx2=0` PNG pools and Canvas2D's 1x PNGs request the same bytes as before.

Result (source bytes): 470 unreferenced atlas-dir files (32.4 MB), 173 KTX2 twins of 103 resident atlases
(21.4 MB), 87 UI files (10.8 MB), 26 ogg (0.46 MB).

## ADR-393: No art ships twice: shared byte-identical tint masks, runtime art URLs for CSS / tutorial art (SurVivaZ)

Context: after ADR-392 two kinds of duplicate bytes were left. (1) Art's customization gear families
(bone / bronze / iron / steel / composite cuirass, gauntlets, boots, greaves …) reuse one tint mask
shape: 35 `*.tintmask.png` / `*.tintmask@2x.png` / `*.tintmask.ktx2` files are byte-identical to another
file of the family. The colour pages are all different and stay unique. (2) Pack atlases named by source
path in `gameplay-panels.css` (`url("../../../packages/assets/pack/...")`, icons / build / skills / mount
art) and the tutorial's `new URL(".../input_glyphs.png", import.meta.url)` were bundled by Vite into
`assets/` as a second copy of files `art/` already ships.

Decision: (1) `planArt` groups served `pack/customization/atlases/*.tintmask(@2x).(png|ktx2)` by sha256;
the first name of each group (sorted) is canonical, every manifest path naming another member (masks,
masksKtx2, pages[].masksKtx2; customization fragment and shards) is rewritten to the canonical file name
in the same directory, and the duplicates are not copied. Sharing a URL is safe: page-ins fetch and decode
per call (`defaultImageLoader`, `loadKtx2Rgba`), `AssetManager` reference-counts by URL, Canvas2D caches
by URL, and the bytes are identical. (2) A pre plugin (`rewritePackCssUrls`) points those CSS urls at
`<base>art/pack/<path>` when the file is served and larger than `assetsInlineLimit` (4 KiB); smaller ones
stay for Vite to inline as data URIs, so no request is added. Vite's "didn't resolve at build time"
notice for these runtime urls is filtered from the log. The tutorial glyph atlas loads
`${BASE_URL}art/ui/input/atlas/input_glyphs.png`. The Cozy Camp `ui/kit/css/` frames stay Vite-bundled
from the CSS (ADR-392 stopped copying them to art/), so they too ship once.

Validation: `apps/client/test/adr393_dedupe.test.ts` pins that aliases are byte-identical tint masks in one
directory onto a shipped canonical, that no shipped manifest names a dropped duplicate, that CSS urls
above the inline limit are rewritten (and their files ship) while small ones are not, and the glyph url;
`adr392_art_plan` replays the client and checks the resolved sources equal the unplanned ones with only
the alias substitution and the KTX2 strip.

Result: 35 tint masks (1,291,815 B before oxipng); Vite assets/ PNGs 50 → 10 (−3.1 MB). Honest cut:
gather-fx.ts keeps its `new URL()` imports; nine of its ten files are under 4 KiB and inlined into the JS
(no request at boot); only `nature_adr128_fx@2x.png` (6.9 KB) still ships twice.

## ADR-394: Merged-manifest JSON ships gzipped; decoded once, then cached plain (SurVivaZ)

Context: the 26 JSON files the client fetches through `loadMergedManifestWith` (15 fragments, the v2
customization / nature shards, `pack/ids.lock.json`) are 40.9 MB minified, mostly `dirFrames` that are all
used. They gzip 17× (2.4 MB). GitHub Pages does not compress responses this large on the fly, so a phone's
first boot downloaded all 40.9 MB before the world could build.

Decision: `planArt` marks exactly the files the client replay fetched; the build writes them as
`<name>.json.gz` only (zlib level 9, deterministic) and `manifests.index.json` (still plain) gains
`"gz": true`. view.ts and prefetch-art.ts read those through `assetJsonGz(url)` (asset-fetch.ts): a Cache
Storage hit under the plain `url` returns the cached JSON text; a miss fetches `url + ".gz"`, decodes it once
(`gunzipText`: `DecompressionStream("gzip")`, or the pure-TS `inflate.ts` on browsers without it, i.e. Safari
< 16.4; a body without the 1f 8b magic is taken as already decoded, in case a host sends Content-Encoding),
stores the decoded text in this deploy's cache under `url`, and parses. Concurrent readers (prefetch-art and
view) share one in-flight decode; each gets its own parsed copy. The dev server and `vite preview` keep
serving plain JSON (no `gz` in their index).

Boot cost, measured in headless Chrome 156 on this box with the real `assetFetch` / `assetJsonGz` code and
`loadMergedManifestWith` (fetch + decode + parse + merge of all 26 files; median; old = plain JSON dist,
new = this dist; cold = empty Cache Storage and HTTP cache, warm = second boot of the same deploy):

| profile | cold old → new | warm old → new |
|---|---|---|
| desktop CPU, localhost | 680 → 601 ms | 430 → 373 ms |
| 4× CPU throttle (phone estimate), localhost | 2,527 → 2,421 ms | 1,591 → 1,449 ms |
| 6× CPU throttle, localhost | 3,918 → 3,646 ms | 2,253 → 2,221 ms |
| 4× CPU, 20 Mbit/s 40 ms RTT | 18,396 → 3,668 ms | 1,529 → 1,446 ms |

No profile is slower. Rejected: decompressing on every boot (cache the `.gz` bytes): warm boot +373 ms at
4× CPU (DecompressionStream of 40.9 MB is not free); the plain-text cache makes a repeat boot the same work
as before this change. The inflate fallback costs about +15 % over DecompressionStream at 4× CPU and only
runs where DecompressionStream is missing.

Validation: `packages/render/test/adr394_gzip_json.test.ts` checks inflate against zlib (stored, fixed,
dynamic, Huffman-only, RLE, long matches, a real manifest), truncated / non-gzip rejection,
DecompressionStream and fallback agreement, plain bodies, and `assetJsonGz` (one `.gz` fetch shared by
concurrent readers, the plain text cached under `url`, a warm boot served from the cache with no network,
missing optional fragments). A headless-Chrome boot of the built dist (desktop, Android A16 user agent with
its KTX2 pools, `gl=safe`, `ktx2=0`, `renderer=canvas`) made no art request that 404s and logged no page
errors; requested art matched the pre-change dist apart from randomly dressed NPCs.

Result: 40,948,947 → 2,403,582 B (−38,545,365).

## ADR-395: Dist size guard and built-dist replay in CI and Pages (SurVivaZ)

Context: ADR-391–394 took the built client from 963.8 MB to 732.6 MB. Each cut can regress without any
existing test noticing: a new art drop with stray files, an `.ogg` back in the MOUNTS regex, a manifest
shipped plain, an unoptimized PNG set when the oxipng download fails, or pack art bundled into `assets/`
again by a new `new URL()` / CSS `url()`.

Decision: `scripts/check-dist-size.mjs [distDir]` runs after the build in both workflows. It fails when
the dist is over `DIST_BUDGET` (800,000,000 B, about 67 MB of headroom for new art before someone has
to look), when any `.ogg` ships, when `manifests.index.json` lacks `gz: true`, a fragment ships plain or
its `.json.gz` / `ids.lock.json.gz` is missing, when large pack art reappears in `assets/`, or (with
`SURVIVAZ_OXIPNG=required`) when the oxipng run's stats do not cover every dist PNG. It prints bytes per
file type. `apps/client/test/adr395_dist.test.ts` runs in the same step with `SURVIVAZ_DIST` set (skipped
in `pnpm check`, which runs before the build). It replays the client over the built files, decoding each
`.json.gz` with both zlib and the ADR-394 inflate fallback. It pins that the shipped art set is exactly
the plan, that every resolved file is present, that the resolved sources equal the plan's, and that every
non-PNG file (KTX2, m4a, fonts, JSON) is byte- or parse-identical to its source.

Result: on the final build the guard reports 5,081 files, 732,608,668 B (PNG 372.4 MB / 2,299, KTX2
330.8 MB / 1,960, m4a 20.5 MB / 706, JS 4.3 MB, `.json.gz` 2.4 MB / 26). The pre-change dist fails it
on budget, ogg, plain manifests and duplicated pack art.

## ADR-396: HUD icons resolve through `iconUrl`; every icon path the client requests must exist (SurVivaZ)

Context: the live site requested `icons/ic_sun.png` and got a 404, both before and after the ADR-391–395 size
cuts. Task 25 moved the custom 32×32 HUD icons into embedded data URIs (`apps/client/src/game-icons-data.ts`,
`ICON_DATA`, read through `iconUrl(file)`), and `apps/client/public/icons` keeps only the app icons
(`icon_180/192/512.png`). `hud.ts` still built `${BASE_URL}icons/<file>` by hand in three places: the season
chip (`ic_sun.png` / `ic_leaf.png` / `ic_snowflake.png`), the thermometer fallback (`ic_temp.png`) and the
vitals fallback when a `vital_*` UI frame is missing. Those files were never shipped, so each request 404'd.
The sun icon itself exists and is dedicated art: `ICON_DATA["ic_sun.png"]` (the same icon the guide and the
touch overlay's Wake button already draw through `iconUrl`).

Decision: the three HUD call sites use `iconUrl`, so they draw the embedded data URIs and make no network
request. No icon was swapped or reused: each slot draws the same dedicated file it named before.
`apps/client/test/adr396_icon_paths.test.ts` fails when client or gameplay source builds an `icons/…` URL
outside `iconUrl`, or names an `ic_*.png` / `icon_*.png` that is in neither `ICON_DATA` nor `public/icons`.
Its dist block, run with `SURVIVAZ_DIST` in the CI and Pages dist step next to `adr395_dist`, checks that
every `icons/…` path in the built `index.html` and every non-embedded icon name exists in the dist.
`adr239_hud_temp` now expects the season chip's `src` to be the embedded data URI.

Gap for Art: there is no dedicated spring icon. `SEASON_LABEL` has four seasons, but `SEASON_ICON` has three
entries, so spring falls back to `ic_sun.png`, which was already the behaviour. A dedicated `ic_spring.png`
(or `ic_sprout.png`) is needed to fix that properly.

## ADR-397: Continuous roofs, engine side of Art's rfx scheme: region picks, band lift, overlays, preview, material hook (SurVivaZ)

Context: Tracey's screenshot of a placed log cabin roof shows repeated stripes and hard edges between cells. She wants
more roof variety, roofs that blend across neighbours, and no larger files or lower quality. The engine audit (the
real `building_t1` frames composited at the iso placement, plus a read of the render path) and Art & Assets' audit
(their `docs/ART_KEYS_ROOFS.md` §1) agree:
- Each `roof_gable` tile is its own mini ridge.
- Every tile is a closed slab with its own outline and side face.
- `roof_flat` sits at 4–7 px while slopes rise to about 27 px.
- Every tile is an identical repeat.
- Selection used only piece key, tier and rot (`buildPieceVisual`), with no neighbour context. ADR-311 picks pieces
  per site; player-placed roofs (the screenshot) get exactly what was placed.

The engine adds no seam of its own, so padding, snapping, overlap and lighting needed no change:
- Every roof frame keeps at least 8 px of transparent margin inside its 84×96 cell, so neighbouring cells cannot
  bleed (still 2 px at quarter resolution).
- Piece pivots are device-pixel snapped (`snapPivot`).
- Tiles meet exactly on the 64×32 diamond, and the 67 px silhouette overlaps its neighbour by about 1.5 px.
- Pieces get no per-tile shade or tint jitter: the per-part seed only feeds season flags, which `bld_roof_*` does not get.
- Roofs share one draw bias.

Decision: implement Art's proposal §4 exactly (keys `rfx_<form>_<seg>_<shape>[c][_v<n>]_t<0..4>`).
- `@engine/assets` `roofRfx.ts` (rules as data in `roofRfx.json`): one level's roof tiles go in, one pick per tile
  comes out.
  - Regions: 8-connected members of one membership group. The legacy keys form one group; `roof_cottage`,
    `roof_gambrel` and `roof_shed` each form their own.
  - Form: legacy groups are `hip` if they have any slope, corner or hip piece, `gab` if any gable, `flt` otherwise;
    chimney-only is `hip`.
  - Bands:
    - `hip` / `cot`: Chebyshev BFS over the bbox + 1, `clamp(cheb − 1, 0, 3)`.
    - `gab` / `gam`: ridge axis from the majority rot, else the long axis; `clamp(min(runA, runB), 0, 5)`.
    - `shd`: members downhill along the majority rot, clamped to 0–3.
    - `flt`: 0.
  - Lower mask (gab/gam: perpendicular bits only; flt: non-membership only) → the exact 16-entry shape/row table, plus
    the gab n = 0 `up_r` and shd `lotop` / `lo` / `top` / `up` exceptions.
  - Crest on `e` / `o`, for forms that have crest keys.
  - Interior variant from `hashU32(0x52F00396, tx, ty, level) & 3` (0–1 → v0, 2 → v1, 3 → v2), only on
    `lo_e` / `up_e` / `f` and never with a crest.
  - Lift: Σ rise per band (hip/gab 14; cot 10, 16…; gam 22, 8…; shd 9; flt 0).
  - Overlays: gab/gam verges and gable-wall strips (`wall_lo` / `wall_up` for gam), shd verges, side walls and
    high-side walls, and the `rfx_chimney` stack at the tile surface height.
  - `rfxSpriteKeys` tries skin, then the variant dropped, then the crest dropped (all Art keys) before giving up.
- Material hook: `materials.rules` maps a region's wall material (majority of its tiles' `roofWallMaterial` = wall
  tier key or `tier:variant`, read from the walls one level down) to an Art skin (`skinKey` template). It is empty
  until Art ships the split-log shake skin and its rule.
- Client `RoofTiler` (`apps/client/src/roof-tiler.ts`):
  - Tracks roof tiles per level. A place or remove bumps that level's version (the cache key: `StructureIndex` has no
    single version, only `chunkVersions`). The next frame re-picks only that level.
  - A steady frame does no roof work.
  - The placement ghost runs the same selection with itself as a member, memoised on the level version.
- Render: a new `SpriteBindings.pieceRoofFx`.
  - Once the rfx sprite's streamed page is resident, the piece draws it at its row, raised by the lift, with overlay
    parts right after it (`ROOF_OVERLAY_BIAS` per step, `PIECE_PARTS_MAX` = 16 parts per piece in the static cache
    key).
  - Until then, and on Canvas2D, `BuildPiece.visualId` is still the legacy roof and draws exactly as before.
  - An overlay whose page is not resident is skipped, never replaced by a streaming stand-in.
  - Cutaway still works: rfx sprites carry a `roof…` building piece.

Result: no visual change until Art's `rfx_*` pages land. With no keys present, no binding is made and every roof
draws its current sprite (pinned by test). Size impact today is zero; Art estimates ≈ 2.8 MB for the full set
(hard ceiling 5 MB), against 732.6 MB of the 800 MB guard. Perf: the selection runs once per level change;
`pieceRoofFx` is one map lookup per roof piece per frame, and the overlay parts are cached static instances.

Validation:
- `packages/assets/test/adr397_roof_rfx.test.ts` covers the full shape table and inner-corner rows, form rules,
  hip 2×2 / 3×3 / 4×4 / 11×11, a concave L and a hole, gable E–W and N–S with verges and walls, crest, gambrel
  rises and strips, flat parapet / field, shed segs, verges and walls, group separation, the chimney stack,
  variants, key fallback order and the material rule.
- `apps/client/test/adr397_roof_tiler.test.ts` covers `hashU32` parity with `abandoned.ts`, no bindings without
  art, resolution with tier, lift and overlays, the level version, zero work on a steady frame, and the preview.
- `apps/client/test/adr397_roof_draw.test.ts` covers the SpriteBatch path: legacy unchanged, resident rfx raised
  14 px with its overlays in order, and the legacy fallback while the page streams.

Questions back to Art, as read from §4:
- A hip / cot outer corner's crest test ("(r+1)%4 or (r+2)%4 is a member with equal band") fires on every perimeter
  corner of a ≥ 3-wide hip, because the corner's edge neighbours are band 0 too. That is implemented exactly as
  written; if only the 2×2 case was meant, the rule needs "both".
- Overlay depth is a fixed bias after the tile; a headless check with real overlay art is still to do.

## ADR-398: Cottage, gambrel and shed roof pieces; abandoned-site forms; one build-menu entry per roof form (SurVivaZ)

Context: Art & Assets' continuous-roof proposal adds three forms with new gameplay pieces. The owner decided:
- Add `roof_cottage`, `roof_gambrel` and `roof_shed`.
- Abandoned barns, mills and stables get gambrel roofs; sheds and hunter shacks get shed roofs; cottages and
  farmhouses get cottage roofs.
- The build menu collapses to one roof entry per form, and placement picks slope, corner and hip shapes
  automatically (ADR-397). It must stay gamepad, keyboard and touch navigable.

Decision:
- Pieces: `pieces.json` appends the three as tiered cell roofs (cottage / gambrel minTier 1, shed from twig;
  costScale 1.3 / 1.3 / 1.1). They are appended, so every older piece id is unchanged; the id lock only gains 194–196.
  The world schema hash moves with the id-lock salt (no new component).
- Abandoned sites: `RoofStyle` gains Gambrel (ridge along the long side), Shed (one pitch, eave across the long side)
  and Cottage. Their pieces go in place of the ADR-311 tiles, with the same count and order. The ADR-311 style is
  still drawn from the roof stream exactly as before, so layouts, loot and chimney rolls do not move.
  `data/roof_forms.json` maps kind → piece and is `live: false`: the new pieces have no legacy art, so a site roofed
  with them would draw nothing until Art's `rfx_cot` / `rfx_gam` / `rfx_shd` pages ship. Flip it in the art commit.
- Build menu (`apps/client/src/roof-menu.ts`, `GameplaySource.roofForms`):
  - Once `rfx_hip_*` art is in the registry, `roof_corner` and `roof_hip` leave the tile list and `roof_slope` reads
    "hip roof".
  - `roof_gable` and `roof_flat` read "gable roof" and "flat roof" once their forms ship.
  - Each new form appears once its own `rfx_` art ships.
  - Only the tile list changes; the grid, focus order and pad / keyboard / touch handling are the existing build
    window's.

Validation: `packages/gameplay/test/adr398_roof_forms.test.ts` covers the appended pieces, no form while not live, the
kind mapping when live, and that a forced form roofs the whole top story with the rest of the plan unchanged.
`apps/client/test/adr398_roof_menu.test.ts` covers the list before art, hip art collapsing corner / hip, new forms
appearing per form, labels, and forms read from the registry's `rfx_` keys.
`adr229_build_icons` skips the three gated pieces only while `live: false`, and asserts that the menu hides them.
Once live flips, it requires Art's `build_roof_{cottage,gambrel,shed}_tN` icons; the gameplay and schema counts move from 193 to 196 pieces.

Alias stems (amends ADR-397): Art's work-in-progress manifest packs some names differently from §4 of its doc.
`roofRfx` therefore resolves each tile and overlay as `[stem, ...alts]`, so either naming works:
- verges `rfx_<form>_<lo|up>_v{el,er,r}`, plus `up_vf` on a plateau;
- the flat field `rfx_flt_lo_f`;
- the gable / gambrel plateau `up_f`.

The first name the registry has wins, and none is invented. Missing names resolve to nothing and the legacy piece draws.

## ADR-399: Whole-roof snow for continuous roofs (SurVivaZ)

Context: the per-sprite `SEASON_SNOWCAP` pass whitens each sprite's top alpha edge. On continuous roofs that would
draw a snow line on every tile, bringing the stripes back, which is why Art kept `rfx_` outside the `/^roof/` season
rule. The owner chose an engine pass with no new art.

Decision: a new instance flag `SEASON_ROOFSNOW` (16384) is set on the rfx roof surface part only (not verges, gable
walls or the chimney, and not cutaway or ghosts). The sprite shader's `roofSnow` takes its coverage from world-space
noise on the drawn iso position (`vScr`), which is continuous across neighbouring tiles like the roof itself, and
weighted towards brighter, sky-facing faces. It scales with the existing snow cover `uSeason.z`. Legacy roofs keep
their `_winter` twins or SNOWCAP as before. Canvas2D draws legacy roofs only, so it needs no mirror.

Validation: `adr397_roof_draw.test.ts` pins the GLSL entry point and that the flag bit is disjoint from the other
season and crisp bits. The headless WebGL2 boot of the built dist compiles the shader.

## ADR-400: Art's rfx roof art is live: every requested key resolves, aliases removed, forms on, roof pages stream (SurVivaZ)

Context: Art shipped the rfx base set (4a5ac969, 7d72fa87), the crown rule and the spring icon (5f1ccfa1) and the
split-log shake skin (5793d0e9, 4ff07a07). The engine had to stop guessing names and use exactly what is packed.

Decision:
- Keys: `adr400_roof_art.test.ts` enumerates every stem and overlay the ADR-397 selection can name (all forms, bands,
  masks, variants, crests, tiers, the shake skin) and requires each to resolve to a packed sprite with no fallback
  except Art's documented ones (crest / variant dropped, shk → base where §8 has no shake art). Art's final names match
  §4, so the ADR-398 alias stems (`RfxPick.alts`, `RfxOverlay.alts`) are removed.
- Crown rule (Art 5f1ccfa1): the flat crown replaces the peak / ridge only on a region clamped at `kmax`; an unclamped
  hip keeps its peak, so no pit opens in the middle of a small roof. Shed `kmax` is 12 (a 12-deep shed corner carries
  3 × 12 + 3 overlays, so `PIECE_PARTS_MAX` is 48).
- `roof_forms.json` is `live: true`; abandoned barns / mills / stables, sheds / hunter shacks and cottages / farmhouses
  get their forms. An rfx-only piece (cottage / gambrel / shed) standing alone draws `rfxStandIn`: the rfx sprite the
  selection picks for it as a one-tile region, at its tier, so it has a view entity, a ghost and a Canvas2D picture
  before its neighbours arrive.
- Streaming: `isStreamedBuildingAtlas` covers `rfx_t<N>_<a|b>` and `rfx_shk_t<N>` (`/^rfx_(?:[a-z]+_)?t\d+(?:_[a-z])?$/`),
  in their own `bld` group (6 slots desktop, 4 low-memory) sized to the 2016 px roof pages, so they never take a tier
  page's slot. `items_build_rfx` is a UI sheet (the build window's CSS), not streamed.
- Build menu: the hip / gable / flat tiles show Art's form icons (`build_rfx_hip|gab|flt_tN`) once that form draws
  continuously. The guide's spring row uses `ic_blossom`.

Validation: `adr400_roof_art.test.ts`, `adr397_roof_rfx.test.ts`, `adr311_abandoned_roofs.test.ts`,
`adr398_roof_forms.test.ts`, `adr387_guide_icons.test.ts` (65 rows with icons); headless WebGL2 / Canvas2D composites.

## ADR-401: Seamless rfx joints in WebGL2; Canvas2D draws continuous roofs (SurVivaZ)

Context: the headless composites showed a dark line on every rfx tile joint. Straight-alpha pages sampled bilinearly
mix the transparent (0,0,0,0) texels into the edge colour, and SRC_ALPHA blending darkens that band again.

Decision: instance flag `RFX_EDGE` (32768) on rfx roof parts (surface and overlays). For those the sprite FS discards
below a = 0.5, divides the filtered colour by the filtered alpha (the alpha-weighted average of the art's own opaque
texels) and draws opaque. Neighbours overlap by about 1.5 px, so the joint closes without a hairline of the wall below.
0.2 / 0.35 drew the edge texels' course lines over the neighbour as a dotted seam; above 0.5 the joints reopened. Other
sprites are untouched. Canvas2D reads the same `pieceRoofFx` binding once a page image is loaded (tile lifted by its band,
overlays after it), else the legacy art, as WebGL2 does; it has no shader, so its joints are the art's own edges.

Validation: `adr397_roof_draw.test.ts` (flag bit, shader text, Canvas2D binding / lift / overlays / fallback); the
composites in both renderers.

## ADR-402: Split-log shakes: Art's §8 vote, one compact rule, wall variant names (SurVivaZ)

Context: Art replaced the ADR-397 material pick with a vote (5793d0e9) and then made wood walls log walls too, an owner
decision (4ff07a07). The engine was asked to keep the log-wall tier set one data entry and to let the clan palisade
count once the wall exposes its variant name.

Review of Art's rule (`pickRegion`): every roof tile with a supporting wall votes for the skin its wall maps to, or
for base (""). The largest count wins and a tie goes to base. With one skin this is the strict majority §8 describes
(shk needs more votes than base). With two or more skins it would be a plurality with a tie for first going to base;
that is noted, not changed, since only `shk` exists. Interior tiles (no wall one level down) do not vote. A region mixing
a log cabin and a stone annex follows the majority of its walls. Only hip / gab / shd / cot take the skin; flt and gam,
and every t2+ tile, fall back to base keys through `rfxSpriteKeys`. That is correct: there is no art for them.

Decision:
- `materials.rules` is one rule: `{ skin: "shk", forms: [hip, gab, shd, cot], wallTiers: ["twig", "wood"],
  wallVariants: ["clan_palisade"], sites: ["cabin", "hunter_shack", "fisher_hut"] }`. `rfxRuleMatches` matches exactly
  what Art's nine entries did: `wallTiers` only for the plain look (bare `<tier>`), `wallVariants` at any tier,
  `sites` against `site:<kind>`. The log-wall tier set is the single `wallTiers` entry.
- `wall` gains `variantNames: ["plain", "clan_wood", "clan_stone", "clan_palisade"]`. Variant 0 still reports the bare
  tier. The art is unchanged: there are no `wall@<name>` sprites, so the name lookup falls through to the tier sprite as
  the index did, placed pieces keep their numeric `VPiece.variant` for the clan variant groups, and ghosts already
  used variant 0. The build menu's variant picker now reads the names instead of "Variant 2..4".
- Cabin ruins: abandoned cabins, hunter shacks and fisher huts are stamped with wood (plank) walls, so with Art's
  twig + wood rule their roofs take shakes with no extra wiring. The `site:<kind>` entries stay in the rule for a client
  that reports them; none does (a networked per-wall site tag would cost a world-schema change and a replication mask
  bit for no visible difference now).
- `RoofTiler.refreshWalls` re-reads the wall material under up to 64 roof tiles per frame, round robin (4 edge lookups
  each), and re-picks a level only when a material changed. A wall placed, upgraded or demolished after the roof above
  it now reaches the roof; before, the material was read once when the roof tile arrived.

Validation: `apps/client/test/adr402_shake_walls.test.ts` covers the rule shape, the match table, vote / tie / unlisted
forms, every shake key resolving to `*_shk_t<N>` where §8 has art (base elsewhere), palisade and plain walls through
`roofWallMaterial`, the three cabin-ruin kinds picking shk, and refreshWalls. Art's `roofs_rfx.test.ts` and
`adr397_roof_rfx.test.ts` also pass.

## ADR-403: Withdrawn: networked per-wall site tag for cabin-ruin shakes

A `PieceSite` component that tags walls stamped inside abandoned cabin / hunter shack / fisher hut sites, so that they
vote `site:<kind>`, was built and then reverted before it was pushed. Art's twig + wood rule (4ff07a07) already gives
those ruins shakes through their wood walls (ADR-402), and the tag would have cost a world-schema hash change and a
replication byte. The number is kept so the log stays contiguous.

## ADR-404: Roofs sit on the wall tops (per-form seat, wall clip under roofs, rfx depth bias, eave art request)

Context: owner feedback on the ADR-400 composites. The roof looked sunk inside the walls: a strip of wall caps and posts
showed along the far edges, and the front wall posts poked up through the front eave. There were three causes:

1. Height. Every rfx part was drawn with its base on the level floor (48 px above the walls' floor). The wall art is
   taller than one level: its cap reaches 60-62 px above the pivot on every tier (twig, wood, stone, metal, bld t1-t4).
2. Overhang. The rfx art stops 1-3 px past the tile diamond. The wall cap is about 6 px thick on screen, half inside
   the diamond and half outside it, and posts reach about 7 px past the tile corners. Raising the roof covers the far
   caps but opens the near ones, so no single offset covers both.
3. Order (WebGL2 only). Eave pixels sit below the tile pivot and get no height term in the depth key, so near wall caps
   and posts out-ranked the roof. Canvas2D paints level by level, so a level-1 roof already came after level-0 walls.

Decision. Engine only, offsets and occlusion only: no art is scaled, duplicated or recoloured.

- Seat. `roofRfx.json` `forms.<f>.seatPx` (hip 9, cottage 7, gable 7, gambrel 7, shed 7, flat 5). `RoofTiler.resolve`
  adds `rfxSeat(form)` to every part's `liftPx`: the tile, its overlays, and the gable/gambrel/shed end strips, so a
  strip still meets its tile. Art's `zoffPx` (band height, §4) is unchanged. Each value is measured per form, because
  each form's eave sits at a different depth in its tile.
- Wall clip under roofs (both renderers). `RoofTiler.planeOver(x, y, level)` (binding `pieceRoofPlane`) returns the
  seated roof-plane height (levelPx + seat) when an upright's pivot touches a tile with an rfx roof one level up: the
  two tiles beside an edge, the four around a vertex post, or the tile under a centre pivot. The renderer then drops
  the upright's pixels above that plane along its edge (`roofClipLine`: view-u edges slope down-right, view-v edges
  down-left). A vertex post reads the roofed view cells around it: at a roof's far corner the line is a V (both eaves
  fall away from it), on a far edge it follows that edge, and anywhere else it is level. Centre pivots are level.
  An edge wall whose end is a roof's far corner bends its line down past that end (min of its own line and that
  corner's V), so its end post never peeks above the far eave.
  - WebGL2: instance flag `ROOF_CLIP` (65536). aF.xy carries the line (build pieces never use the wet / cold inputs),
    the vertex shader passes the height over the plane and the screen px as linear varyings, and the fragment shader
    discards above the line (k x px, or -0.5 |px| for the V), after the derivatives. The static piece cache signs the
    line (PIECE_SIG_N 35), so a roof change re-signs the walls.
  - Canvas2D: the same line as the piece's clip polygon.
  
  This is occlusion: the wall top is where the roof rests, and nothing is recoloured. Where the roof art has no
  overhang, the cut shows background instead of a wall strip.
- Order. `RFX_SEAT_BIAS = 1.1` is added to every rfx part's WebGL2 depth key, so the roof beats the caps and posts of
  the walls under it. Trade-off: an upright standing right against a front wall can have its head drawn under the eave.
  The local player keeps the focus silhouette.

Validation: `apps/client/test/adr404_roof_seat.test.ts` decodes the building and main-pack atlases. For every form (hip,
gab, cot, gam, shd, flt) on every plain wall tier (wall_twig, wall, wall_stone, wall_metal, bld_wall_t1..t4) it lays a
7x5 house, draws the clipped walls and then the seated roof, and checks that at least 90% of each facing's wall columns
meet roof art directly above their visible top (no strip above the roof, no background gap under it). The E facing of
the gable/gambrel/shed/flat houses is the end-strip side and is left to the composites. The test also checks that the
old unseated, unclipped roof fails, the clip-line slopes, the seat range, and the depth bias. Composites (WebGL2 and
Canvas2D, every form) are in /workspace/share/roofs_adr400/.

What the engine cannot do, and what Art must paint: true eaves, meaning a visible overhang past the walls rather than a
flush edge. The request for Art (`rfx_<form>_*` eave and corner tiles, every form, tier and skin, including shk):

- extend the roof surface 6 px (1x) past the tile diamond on the outer side of every eave edge;
- extend 8 px at the outer corner shapes, so the corner posts are covered;
- add a 3-4 px fascia/drip edge under the S and E (camera-facing) eaves;
- for the gable, gambrel and shed end strips (`rfx_*_wall*`), extend the strip bottom 3 px, so it overlaps the wall top
  at every seat;
- keep the 72x68 frame and anchor 0.647, or grow the frame symmetrically and update the anchor in the manifest.

Once that art lands, re-measure the seats with the test (expect about 13, the wall-top height). Raise its threshold to
100% with the 7 px corner-post span included, and drop the clip if the eaves cover the caps on their own.

## ADR-405: A poisoned manifest cache entry heals instead of bricking every boot; real manifest failures name their cause (SurVivaZ)

Context: after ADR-394 the live game (c203cbec) failed on Tracey's phone with "3D renderer unavailable —
showing debug view [E-1AC6]. manifest shard missing: manifest.customization.hat.json", deterministically on
every reload. The same failure puts the game in the debug view (flat tile grid, no terrain height, no custom
water tiles, no indoor zoom) — exactly the Xbox Series X symptoms 1, 3 and 4 reported the same morning. The
live `.json.gz` files are all valid (gunzipped + parsed with zlib; the pure-TS inflate fallback agrees
byte-for-byte on all 10 customization shards), and a clean desktop-Chrome boot of the live build loads fine,
with and without DecompressionStream. The failure reproduces exactly in Chrome when Cache Storage holds one
garbage entry under the hat shard's plain URL: the overlay text, the E-1AC6 code, the debug renderer, and the
persistence across a reload are byte-identical to the phone report. The mechanism is in `gzText`
(asset-fetch.ts): it trusted a Cache Storage hit blindly — `hit.text()` straight into `JSON.parse` — and
`assetJsonGz` + view.ts swallowed every failure into `undefined`, so a single bad write (a 200 with an error
body, a deploy-window flap, a carrier middlebox) failed every boot forever with no cause. Which write poisoned
Tracey's phone cannot be proven from here (the live files are valid now); the fix does not depend on it.

Decision: `assetJsonGz` now distinguishes missing from failed. `gzText` returns undefined ONLY for a 404 on
every attempt — including one cache-bypassing `reload` fetch, so a stale cached 404 cannot fake a missing
file. A non-404 HTTP status, a network error on both attempts, or a gunzip failure throws with the URL and
status. `assetJsonGz` parses the text; on a parse failure it evicts the cache entry (`dropAssetCacheEntry`)
and retries once from the network bypassing both caches, so one bad write heals on the next load (usually
within the same boot) instead of bricking the deploy; if the retry also fails to parse it throws
`manifest JSON parse failed: <url>` with the cause. A fetch/gunzip failure is retried once the same way,
then the real error surfaces. view.ts no longer `.catch(() => undefined)`s the gz loader: a real failure
fails the boot (and the safe-retry reload) loudly with its cause, while a genuinely missing optional fragment
still skips silently. Prefetch keeps its best-effort catch. Two latent unhandled rejections fixed along the
way: the in-flight dedupe used `void p.finally(cleanup)`, whose derived promise re-rejects — now
`.then(cleanup, cleanup)` in both `assetFetch` and `readGzText`. Pushing a new build also heals a poisoned
phone by itself (the cache is keyed by BUILD_HASH and old caches are dropped), but the retry is the durable
protection: it heals a poisoned entry in the CURRENT build without a new deploy.

Xbox memory thread (separate, not proven to be this bug): the console ultra tier budgets 448 MB of atlases
against the ~512 MB the browser GPU process is assumed to get, and the 4K render targets (~116 MB) sit on top
of it — `vram.withinBudget` counts atlas bytes only. The arithmetic in the old comments was wrong (448 is
87% of 512, not "~half"); the comments now state the real accounting and that the ~512 MB assumption is
unverified on real hardware. No budget is changed without evidence, and no graphics quality is lowered.
Canvas2DRenderer's decoded-image cache was unbounded (every atlas ever touched stayed decoded); it is now an
LRU capped at 256 loaded images (the resident set is ~237 pages), with in-flight loads never evicted. That
bounds a proven leak; it is NOT claimed to be the Xbox memory cause, which was not reproduced. Stale comments
that listed SraKmd among the basic/software adapters are corrected (it is the Xbox console adapter).

Validation: `packages/render/test/adr405_manifest_cache_recovery.test.ts` (8 tests: poisoned entry heals and
the cache holds valid JSON, poison + 404 -> undefined, poison + garbage -> throws with the URL, fetch
failures retried once via `reload`, 503 on every attempt throws, stale cached 404 heals via `reload`,
genuine 404 stays undefined, `dropAssetCacheEntry` removes one entry) and
`packages/render/test/adr405_canvas2d_images_lru.test.ts` (3 tests: 256-image cap with oldest-first
eviction, hit refreshes recency, in-flight placeholders never evicted). All 11 fail against the pre-change
code (reverted in a scratch copy, exports stubbed). `packages/assets/test/manifest_shards.test.ts` gains one
test: a loader failure propagates with its cause, not as "missing". The phone failure was reproduced in the
probe before the fix (configs D/E/F: clean boot loads, no-DecompressionStream boot loads, poisoned cache
reproduces the exact [E-1AC6] overlay on load #1 and again after reload); the fix is proven at the code
level by the recovery tests — a live re-probe after the push is still the confirmation that a poisoned
phone heals in the real browser.

Result: one bad cache write can no longer brick a deploy; the next manifest failure will name its cause
(HTTP status, gunzip, or parse) in the overlay and the error log instead of "manifest shard missing".

## ADR-406: A stale 404 for a manifest shard must not brick a boot; required shards throw with the cause (SurVivaZ)

Context: after ADR-405 shipped (76e4b165), Tracey's phone still shows "3D renderer unavailable — showing
debug view", now with a different shard and code: "[E-5B80] / manifest shard missing:
manifest.customization.top.json". The hat shard no longer errors. The failure is deterministic across reloads
("it's still happening") and happens on both Wi-Fi and mobile data. Error codes are per-message hashes
(error-log.ts), so E-5B80 vs E-1AC6 just means a different file, not a different failure type. Ruled out with
evidence: deploy propagation (the Pages run for 76e4b165 completed 09:09:08 CST, a full 11 minutes before the
09:20 failing screenshot; CI completed 09:18:38 CST, both success); the file itself (top.json.gz → 200,
590,702 B, valid gzip, decodes to 9,188,794 B, parses as JSON; the customization index is a v2 index listing
10 shards and the live manifests.index.json says "gz": true); a service worker (none exists anywhere); an old
poisoned Cache Storage entry (the cache bucket is build-hash-keyed and old buckets are dropped, and the only
two `cache.put` sites cannot write a 404 page under the plain URL). The mechanism is in ADR-405's `gzText`
(asset-fetch.ts): it makes three back-to-back attempts against the SAME cache key in the same millisecond
window (`force-cache`, default, `reload`). A 404 stuck in the browser HTTP cache and/or the nearby CDN edge
defeats all three identically: Pages 404s carry an ETag and no Cache-Control and are cached heuristically
(verified live: a 404 is served `X-Cache: HIT` with `Age` in the hundreds of seconds), so a `reload` fetch
revalidates into a 304 and serves the stale 404 again. The 404 was most likely first cached during the deploy
window (09:06–09:09, when the new file did not yet exist at that cache) or an earlier flap — Pages had already
been observed flapping 503/404 on large manifest URLs, and the top shard is the largest (590 KB gz / 9.2 MB
decoded). A user reload repeats the identical sequence against the identical stuck entries, which is why the
failure is deterministic; switching networks does not help because the browser HTTP cache is on the device and
both networks can reach the same nearby edge. Which layer holds the stale 404 (browser cache, edge, or both
reinforcing each other) cannot be distinguished from the VM and is stated as the one honest unknown — the fix
defeats a stuck cache at every layer, so the distinction changes nothing.

Decision: `gzText` keeps ADR-405's three instant attempts unchanged (healthy path identical), then adds
delayed retries that run only while the file is still 404ing: after 600 ms a plain `cache: "no-store"` fetch
(no validators, no cache read or write), and after a further 1,800 ms a `cache: "no-store"` fetch against a
cache-busting URL (`<url>.gz?v=<unique-token>`, `cacheBustUrl()` — a URL never requested before has no entry
in any cache, so it must be served from origin; verified live, `top.json.gz?v=…` → 200, 590,702 B, because
GitHub Pages ignores the query string for static files). The decoded text is cached in Cache Storage under
the plain URL, so the next boot reads it from there. Worst case for a genuinely missing file: 5 attempts over
~2.4 s, then undefined (optional) or a throw (required). A fetch that throws never overwrites an earlier
response's evidence: the retry loop only reassigns the response when one actually arrived. `assetJsonGz`
gains `opts.required`: for index-listed shards (and required fragments) a 404 on every attempt now throws
`manifest load failed: <url>: HTTP 404 on every fetch attempt (instant, delayed, and cache-busting retries
included)` instead of returning undefined, so a genuinely missing file reads as a 404 after a cache-busting
retry, never as "manifest shard missing"; undefined stays reserved for genuinely optional fragments.
`loadMergedManifestWith` takes an optional `io.getRequired` (required fragments and every shard of a v2 index
load through it; without it — the dedicated server's file-based loader — `io.get` is used and behaviour is
unchanged). view.ts passes `getRequired: (u) => assetJsonGz(u, { required: true })` when the index says gz,
and gives the `manifests.index.json` load one cache-busting retry before falling back to MANIFEST_INDEX (the
index is a single point of failure: if it 404s, the loader falls back to plain-JSON fragment loads and every
gz-only fragment 404s). Deliberately not done: no boot-level retry of the whole manifest phase (the
loader-level schedule already covers the transient window, including a full cache-key change); no `no-store`
on the first attempts (the HTTP-cache fast path is kept for the healthy case); no graphics-quality or budget
change. The user is not asked to clear site data (that could wipe her save) — the fix heals the stuck cache
inside the boot itself. The ADR-405 poison-heal behaviour is unchanged.

Validation: new `packages/render/test/adr406_manifest_stale_404.test.ts` (8 tests: healthy path unchanged,
stale 404 clearing after the instant attempts heals via the delayed retry, stale 404 that never clears for
the plain key heals via the cache-busting retry with the healed text cached under the plain URL, genuinely
missing shard throws with cause for a required load with all 5 attempts run, genuinely missing shard still
undefined for an optional load, poisoned cache entry still heals, 503 on every attempt still throws,
`cacheBustUrl` appends a fresh `?v=` key and is unique per call) and
`packages/assets/test/adr406_required_manifest_load.test.ts` (4 tests: required shard load throws with the
cause, missing shard without `getRequired` still throws "manifest shard missing", optional fragment still
skipped, required fragment uses `getRequired`). The new tests were written first and run against the
pre-change code: 6 failed / 6 passed (the 6 passes are behaviour guards that already held); all 12 pass
with the fix. One ADR-405 test's expectation was updated to the new 5-attempt fetch sequence
(`["force-cache", undefined, "reload", "no-store", "no-store"]`); no ADR-405 behaviour changed. Full
suites, serialized: total 4,545 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed — the 1 failure is the known persist autosave
bench flake (re-run standalone with `PERF=1`: 1/1 passed). Typecheck EXIT 0, all 11 projects (TS 5.9.3).
Canaries 34/34 (adr203 3/3, adr252 18/18, adr331 8/8, adr385 5/5). The fix is proven at the code level by
the mock-fetch repro and the new tests; browser-level proof needs the pushed build and Tracey's reload, plus
a live re-probe of the poison config against the pushed build.

Result: a transient or stuck 404 can no longer brick a boot — the loader waits, then changes the cache key,
and heals inside the boot; a file genuinely missing from the deploy now names itself (URL, HTTP 404, the
retries that ran) in the overlay and the error log instead of "manifest shard missing".

Non-blocking observations: the customization index's `bytes`/`sha` per shard describe the on-disk
(pretty-printed) source files (verified: on-disk `top.json` is 18,776,681 B, sha `832ab784…`, exactly as the
index says), while the deployed `.gz` contains the minified form (9,188,794 B, sha `c95229d6…`). Nothing in
the loader verifies `sha`/`bytes`, so this is harmless — but any future shard-integrity check must account
for the minification. The delayed retries run only for 404s, not for network errors (a network error still
throws immediately and is retried once by `assetJsonGz`'s bypass-cache retry, the ADR-405 behaviour).

## ADR-407: Consoles run at the high tier, not ultra — the Xbox boot must fit the 1 GB UWP app cap (SurVivaZ)

Context: Tracey, on a browser on Xbox Series X, reports "Error code: SBOX_FATAL_MEMORY_EXCEEDED happens
when starting to load the game assets on console browsers". SBOX_FATAL_MEMORY_EXCEEDED is the Chromium
sandbox error for a tab/renderer process that asked for more memory than its sandbox allows; on desktop the
limits scale with physical memory (4–16 GB) and exceeding them usually means a leak, but on Xbox the browser
runs as a UWP app and Microsoft caps foreground UWP apps at 1 GB (games get 5 GB; Microsoft Learn, "System
resources for UWP apps and games on Xbox One", which states the cap applies to Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S
and that exceeding it causes memory allocation failures). Edge on Xbox is a UWP app, so the whole tab — JS
heap + GPU set + Edge's own overhead — must fit ~1 GB. The code's old frame ("the ~512 MB the browser GPU
process is assumed to get", capabilities.ts) was the wrong frame and is corrected here: the cap is per app,
not per GPU process, and the ~512 MB figure was unverified. No "SBOX" string exists anywhere in the tree;
there is no handling of it. The error cannot be reproduced without a real Xbox sandbox — everything below
is proven at code level + emulation, and the live re-probe + Tracey's real-Xbox retest after the push are
the real check.

Mechanism (measured, not guessed). Consoles were locked to ultra: `classifyDevice` returned start 3,
ceiling 3 for the SraKmd adapter / Xbox UA, so a console got a 448 MB atlas budget and 4K render targets
(~116 MB: scene + emissive RGBA8, DEPTH_COMPONENT24 depth, half-res lightmap, two half-res bloom targets —
see `renderTargetBytes`) ≈ 564 MB GPU-side before the JS heap. ADR-212 already budgets the console JS heap
at 384 MB soft (desktop 1024, mobile 256); the live manifest set decodes to ~39 MB of JSON text whose parsed
object graph retains ~91 MB of JS heap (measured in Node V8 on the real live files: heap 97.5 MB after the
parallel parse of the 10 customization shards alone, 34.9 MB of shard text). Emulation (Hatch Chromium over
CDP, live build, SraKmd renderer stub + Xbox UA + 8 cores / 8 GB, probe `xbox407-probe.mjs`): console ultra
boots to vram total 341.3 MB (budget 448, resident 128, reserved 213.3) with JS heap 326 MB at spawn and
344 MB after 30 s, Chrome RSS 2,383 MB (SwiftShader-inflated, not Xbox-comparable). At 4K output the GPU set
is ~457 MB (341.3 atlas + ~116 targets); 457 + 344 ≈ 800 MB before Edge's own overhead — against a 1 GB app
cap, that is why the tab dies exactly when assets start loading. The JS heap has no distinct parse spike
above its plateau (polled every 500 ms through boot: monotonic rise to ~344 MB); the cost is retained, not
transient. A second measured fact matters: fitBudget already cannot fit the resident set + pool reserves in
448 MB, so console ultra renders its resident art at 0.25x downscale — ultra was never delivering full-res
art on Xbox in the first place.

Decision: consoles start at high (start 2, ceiling 2) — 256 MB atlas budget, <=1080p targets (~29 MB), a
~285 MB GPU set at 4K output. The same emulation at the high tier (`?gl=high`, which exercises the exact
code path this makes default): vram total 193.3 MB (budget 256, resident 80, reserved 113.3), JS heap
349 MB at spawn, at the SAME 0.25x atlas downscale — the art is no blurrier, and the building pools are
even at a higher scale (1 vs 0.5 at ultra, because the smaller reserve leaves more room for resident art).
Total: ~222 MB GPU + ~344 MB heap ≈ 566 MB, inside the 1 GB cap with ~450 MB for Edge's overhead. Two
guard rails make the tier stick. (1) The device ceiling binds: a console that once remembered ultra is
clamped back to high by `startLevel`, and the frame-time bench can demote a console but never promote it
(`benchAdjust` only promotes desktop-unknown/desktop-dgpu). (2) The default Full preset can no longer
re-open native-res targets on a console: `QualityController.fullResolution` is false when the detected
device class is console. This second hole mattered: Full is the default preset on every device (Task 26),
and without it Full would have bypassed the 1080p pixel cap and rebuilt 4K targets (~141 MB with the
ultra tier's full-res lightmap) on a fresh-install Xbox. Desktop and mobile are untouched: their tiers,
budgets and Full-preset behaviour are asserted unchanged in the new tests, and the Full bypass still works
on desktop (ceiling 3). `renderTargetBytes(w, h, lightDownscale = 2)` is a new pure helper in
capabilities.ts (14 B/px at the high tier) so the budget invariant is testable: console atlas budget +
targets at maxPixels must fit the 512 MB design budget (256 + ~29 = ~285 MB), leaving the rest of the
1 GB cap for the heap and Edge.

Honest costs, stated plainly. Xbox renders at <=1080p instead of 4K, and character paper-doll pools use
the KTX2 compressed tail at 256 MB instead of lossless PNG (`losslessCharPools(256)` is false; ADR-220
measured ~10% of a paper-doll sheet's texels >32 off, which read as smeared, blotchy clothes/faces). The
probe's close-ups show no visible smearing at play zoom (both configs render the player cleanly), but the
real-Xbox severity needs Tracey's eyes — a game that runs at 1080p beats a game that crashes at boot.
What is NOT claimed: no real-Xbox fix is proven here; the sandbox limit itself is unverifiable from the VM
(the documented 1 GB UWP app cap is the best public figure, and the retail Edge tab's effective limit may
differ — the fix's ~450 MB of headroom is the margin against that unknown). The ~91 MB retained manifest
graph is a quantified follow-up, not part of this ADR: dropping it after the registry builds would buy
further headroom, but it needs its own change and gate. ADR-405/406 loader behaviour is unchanged
(the delayed no-store + cache-busting retries still apply to the same shard fetches).

Verification: new tests `adr407_console_memory_budget.test.ts` (7 tests) written first — 5 failed / 1 passed
on pre-change code in the repro run, 6 failed / 1 passed in the scratch-worktree revert check (the 7th is
the budget invariant, which fails pre-change because `renderTargetBytes` does not exist there); all 7 pass
with the fix. Existing expectations updated (not weakened): `device_tier.test.ts` Xbox Edge ultra→high,
`sceneTarget.test.ts` console Ultra→High (the `?gl=high` recovery half is unchanged — it is now the
default, so the recovery path is a no-op for consoles), one comment in `frametable_rows.test.ts`. Typecheck
EXIT 0 all 11 (TS 5.9.3); full suites serialized total 4,552 passed, 9 skipped, 1 known persist autosave
bench flake (p95 59.9989 vs 50, re-run PERF=1 1/1 passed); canaries 34/34.

## ADR-408: Auto is the default graphics preset again (SurVivaZ)

Context: Task 26 made Full the default preset on every device, reversing the Task 1 decision that kept Auto as the safe default. Full pins the Ultra tier AND bypasses the soft DPR / pixel-budget caps in IsoRenderer.resize(), so every fresh install renders at the device's native DPR — including low-end phones, which run hotter/slower for it. Tracey asked (2026-11-14) for the default back to Auto so the game adapts per device via the frame-time governor instead of pinning Full everywhere.

Decision: `DEFAULT_QUALITY_PRESET` in `packages/render/src/quality.ts` changes from `"full"` to `"auto"`. Everything else follows that one constant: `loadPreset()` falls back to Auto when nothing is stored, `QualityController`'s constructor default is Auto, the Settings save fallback (`game-menus.ts`) and the renderer init (`IsoRenderer.ts`) both read the same constant, so no other code change was needed there — verified by grep, not assumed. The header comment records the reversal (Task 26 → ADR-408). The stale "Full stays the default" claims are corrected in the warm-up module header (`warmup.ts`) and the README renderer bullet. The two historical "Full stays the default" sentences inside the ADR-380/ADR-381 entries are left untouched — they were true when those ADRs landed. Deliberately not changed: tier definitions, governor tuning, atlas page scale (`atlasPageScaleForPreset` still gives @2x to Ultra/Full, 1x to Auto), the Full preset itself, and the ADR-407 console guard (present in this tree: `fullResolution` is false on consoles, and Auto on a console runs the governor under the console ceiling). No stored choice is migrated, reset, or rewritten: a player who chose Full keeps Full, and a stored "nonsense" value still falls back to the default (now Auto).

Validation: the "Task 26: Full is the default preset" tests in `packages/render/test/full_resolution_preset.test.ts` are updated to ADR-408: the default is Auto, a fresh install loads Auto, a bare `new QualityController()` is Auto and not full-resolution, every stored choice is still kept verbatim, and an unparseable stored value falls back to Auto. The updated tests were run against the pre-change code: 2 failed / 11 passed (exactly the two updated default tests fail behaviourally, `expected 'full' to be 'auto'`); all 13 pass with the fix. Full suites, serialized, on the rebased tree (base 3f6c13e7, ADR-407 in the tree): total 4,552 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed — the 1 failure is the known persist autosave bench flake (p95 66.24 vs 50; re-run standalone with `PERF=1`: 1/1 passed). The pre-rebase run on 6ca7c2f7 gave 4,545 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed (same flake, p95 56.02); the +7 is ADR-407's console-budget tests, which pass alongside the ADR-408 default tests (targeted run: 20/20). Typecheck EXIT 0, all 11 projects (TS 5.9.3), re-run on the rebased tree. Canaries 34/34 (adr252 18/18 + 3/3, adr331 8/8, adr385 5/5, in the full-suite logs).

Result: fresh installs start on Auto and the governor adapts the tier to the device; nothing changes for anyone who already picked a preset. No speedup is claimed and no phone ms is claimed — the governor's behaviour is unchanged, only the starting preset for players with no stored choice.

## ADR-411: Varied terrain heights + dig/raise 300 (SurVivaZ)

Context: two gaps in the terrain model. (1) Worldgen never reached its own maximum: sampling `heightAt` over ±512 (step 2) for 5 seeds gave min 0 but max 20 on every seed — 21 and 22 never occur. The formula's real ceiling was plateau 3 × relief 6 + detail 2 = 20 (the "detail 0..3" comment was wrong; `floor(field*2) + floor(biome*2)` tops out at 2). (2) Tracey clarified (2026-11-17) that players can dig 300 tiles down and raise the ground 300 tiles up from a tile's generated ground. The old absolute bounds (-60..75, ADR-297) and every byte-wide store behind them could not hold that: `terrainDigAt` is levels relative to generated ground (0..22), while LEVEL_MIN/LEVEL_MAX are absolute levels, so the absolute bounds must cover generated ground ± 300.

Decision — worldgen: `HEIGHT_MAX` 22 → 26 and wilderness relief 2..6 → 2..8 (`relief = 2 + 6*blend`), so plateau 3 × 8 + detail 2 = 26 is actually reached. 1 level stays 16 px and 1 floor stays 3 levels. Near spawn nothing changes: within 160 tiles `blend` is 0, relief is still 2, and the height formula is byte-identical to before — spawn patches keep faces ≤ 3 and the same gentle cap (max 7). Farther out the world gets real mountains and valleys (measured faces up to 24 levels in the wilderness survey).

Decision — dig/raise 300: `TERRAIN.minLevel/maxLevel` are now -300 / `HEIGHT_MAX + 300` = 326 (`TERRAIN_EDIT_RANGE = 300` in `terrain_depth.ts`); the shovel flow (`TerrainFail.Limit` + the `setTerrainDig` clamp) follows the same constants, so no other gameplay code changes. Everything that assumed the byte range widens: `Chunk.height` Int8 → Int16 and the chunk codec v1 → v2 (heights 1024 × i16; v1 blobs still decode — u8 heights sign-extended, legacy flow bytes decoded as before); the flow-water encoding gains a v2 code `raw = level + 1000` (700..1326) while the ADR-297 legacy branches are kept and checked after it; `TerrainEdit.dig` i8 → i16; world-preview heights Int8 → Int16 (a flow-encoded lake surface is 1000+); TileSync full-chunk height runs switch from `v & 0xff` bytes to zigzag varints (server and client ship together, so the wire change needs no versioning). Render, camera, `standHeightAt`, climb/fall rules and underground rules need no change: they all read decoded levels, and the 3-level climb cap / fall-damage formula already handle arbitrary drops.

Compatibility: old saves load. A v1 chunk decodes through the v1 branch, and a v1 chunk holding a `TerrainEdit` entity migrates: `migrate.ts` gains a `widened` migration kind (old field type → new type, signed values sign-extended — a dug -5 stays -5 instead of becoming 251), with `TERRAIN_EDIT_WIDEN_MIGRATION` in `DEFAULT_MIGRATIONS`; `migrateChunkBytes` now returns early for v2 rows, whose 2-byte height section the v1 layout walk would misparse. Without the migration, decode rejects the old schema hash (verified in the new persist test). The graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands), and the ground-shape model / tilesets are ADR-409/410's slices, not this one — slopes derived from height deltas now see larger deltas in the wilderness (up to ~24 levels), which is the intended cliff face, not a regression.

Validation: new tests `adr411_varied_heights.test.ts` (world), `adr411_dig_raise_300.test.ts` (gameplay), `adr411_terrain_edit_widen.test.ts` (persist), plus a TileSync heights case in `net/test/tiles.test.ts`. Measured before/after on the same 5 seeds (±512, step 2): min 0 / max 20 → min 0 / max 26 = HEIGHT_MAX on every seed. Real shovel loops reach -300 and 326 from generated ground 0 and 26, with `Limit` exactly at the bounds; a -300 pit floods and keeps level -300 through flow/render; `TerrainEdit` dig ±300 round-trips the codec; 60°F holds at 300 levels down in winter. Existing bounds assertions updated (not weakened): task36 terrain tests, ADR-273 preview (`HEIGHT_MAX` 26, wilderness max ≥ 25), ADR-296/297 codec round-trip over -300..326, ADR-386 preview levels ≤ `HEIGHT_MAX`, empty-chunk size bound (2075 bytes with i16 heights), persist chunk `format` 2. Two knock-ons, both measured, not assumed: the world schema hash moves `0x35deea19` → `0x92e6f70a` (TerrainEdit.dig i8 → i16, no new component — the ADR-360/371 pins are updated), and the ADR-384 single-level-ruin flat share drops ~0.41 → ~0.35 (taller wilderness relief leaves fewer perfectly flat footprints; the realised ruin density stays inside its 0.08–0.13 band, so only the flat-share band widens to 0.30–0.47). Typecheck clean with pinned TS 5.9.3; neighbour suites (worldgen, terrain, farming, building/placement, water, render, net, persist) re-run with no regressions.

## ADR-410: Tilesets for the sloped ground shapes (SurVivaZ)

Context: ADR-409 gives every ground tile a shape (flat/ramp/wedge/valley/peak/stepped) and the renderer already swaps the base layer to a slope key when it resolves — but no slope art existed, so every sloped tile fell back to the flat base tilted geometrically. Valley/peak/stepped keep a flat top + cliffs and need no new art.

Decision: runtime-painted slope tilesets, following the ADR-356/357/361 pattern (no binaries in the snapshot push route). One atlas per season (`gt_slope_summer/fall/winter/spring`), 15 cols × 4 rows of 68×52 cells, anchor (34,18): frame = material index (GROUND_PRIORITY order: rock, sand, dirt, mud, forest, grass, snow) × 8 + shape (0–3 ramp downhill +u/+v/−u/−v, 4–7 wedge low corner (u−,v−)/(u+,v−)/(u+,v+)/(u−,v+)); 224 sprites, ids 6100–6323, keys `gt_<mat>_slope_ramp_<d>` / `gt_<mat>_slope_wedge_<c>` with the same season suffixes as flat ground. The painter (`apps/client/src/task410-art.ts`) transcribes the shipped ground palettes faithfully from `ground_mats.py` (note: Python calls the material "stone", the engine "rock") and reuses the flat tiles' art language — tone-field islands, value-noise specks, and the same per-material decorations (tufts, flowers, pebbles, leaves, cracks, slabs, puddles, frost, snow patches). The tone field is cached per (material, season) and shared by all 8 shapes; only the light model differs per shape, so each tile is genuinely drawn for its shape: 5 quantized cel bands (1.14/1.07/1.00/0.93/0.86) with narrow blends, a downhill crease (×0.84 at the edge) and an uphill rim (×1.06); a wedge shades its two triangles on the fold diagonal, each by its own downhill axis. The vertex shader does the geometric foreshortening, so the texture is painted flat-on-the-ground. 2x is the master (2040×416 per season); 1x is box-downsampled and snapped to the block's own palette colours, mirroring the shipped pipeline. Install follows ADR-357: `task410AtlasSources()` is idempotent and a safe no-op without canvas; `view.ts` merges the blob URLs over the manifest sources and excludes the four atlases from load-progress counting. Flat tiles are untouched — the renderer only swaps when the slope key resolves.

Validation: new tests `apps/client/test/adr410_slope_art.test.ts` (5 tests) and `packages/render/test/adr410_slope_art.test.ts` (2 tests), 7/7 passing: every one of the 224 keys resolves through the merged registry; every painted cell is non-blank by pixel check (2x cells ~4,557 opaque px, 1x >1,000), in-palette with cel-bounded colour counts (2x < 320 distinct, 1x < 210); all 8 shapes of a tile differ; ramp downhill thirds are darker than uphill thirds (ratio < 0.93) in all 4 directions and wedge low corners darker than the opposite corner, for every material; flat keys still resolve to the flat atlases; the end-to-end TileTerrain test with the real registry shows a ramp tile uploading the slope sprite id (not the flat base) in all 4 view rotations, a wedge uploading its low-corner key, and a flat tile keeping the flat base. Neighbours: render + world slope suites 577 passed / 0 failed; assets pack test 47 passed / 1 failed — the known pre-existing `assets/building/KEYS.md` ENOENT (the `assets/` drop is absent from this checkout; unrelated). Client painter neighbours (task355/357/361) 70 passed. Typecheck with pinned TS 5.9.3: apps/client, packages/assets, packages/render all clean except two pre-existing errors from `scripts/oxipng.mjs` being skip-worktree in this checkout (untouched files).

Result: 7 materials × 4 seasons × 8 shapes = 224 slope tiles shipped as runtime paint, 0 download bytes. Cost is a one-time ~0.53 s paint at boot and ~0.6 MB of in-memory PNG blobs (measured in the VM with a filter-0 zlib-6 encoder: 43–44 KB per 1x atlas, 105–108 KB per 2x atlas; browser toBlob output will differ slightly).
