No quality reduction: the same palettes, decorations, and cel shading as the flat ground, with per-shape light so the tilt reads. The graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands). The user's eyes are still the final check that slopes read correctly on the phone.

## ADR-409: Sloped ground shapes (SurVivaZ)

Context: terrain transitions were blocky stepped levels — every 1-level height step drew as a vertical cliff
face (mesh cliff + textured skirt + gt_side face + drop-edge relief), so gentle hills read as stacked slabs.
The game already had the heightfield (seeded worldgen, 1 level = 16 px); what it lacked was a shape model
that turns neighbour heights into ramps and wedges.

Decision — model (`packages/world/src/slope.ts`, pure, no imports): `classifyGroundShape({h, edge, diag})`
is a deterministic function of one tile's render height and its 8 neighbours' render heights, so the mesh
(`tilemap.ts`, world axes) and the textured instances (`terrainTiles.ts`, view-space axes) always agree, in
all 4 view rotations. Corner rule: a top-face corner drops exactly 1 level iff the lowest tile touching
that vertex is exactly 1 level below this tile. The vertex minimum is the same whoever asks, so adjacent
top faces share their edge heights exactly — no slits, no holes. Water neighbours carry the 0.25 surface
inset, so their heights are fractional and can never equal h-1: shores stay ledges, never slopes. Void
neighbours (<= -90, the renderer's existing void convention) are ignored. Kinds from the 4 edge drops:
`flat`, `ramp` (one edge 1 lower — one sloping plane), `wedge` (two adjacent edges 1 lower — the top folds
down toward the low corner), `valley` (two opposite), `peak` (all four), `stepped` (any edge 2+ lower).
Guard: valley, peak and 3-edge wedges would need all four corners down, which would drop the whole top to
the low height and erase the tile (a lone peak would read as flat ground while the player stands 1 level
above it), so they keep a flat top and their 1-level cliff faces — they render exactly as before ADR-409
and need a centre vertex to slope. A `slopeSide` is an edge with a 1-level drop whose two corners both
dropped: only there is the cliff face suppressed. Any other 1-level edge keeps its cliff face, which closes
the strip between the descending top edge and the low neighbour. Diagonal-only lows dimple the shared
corner (kind stays `flat`).

Decision — rendering: the mesh top face uses `h - cornerDrops[i]` per corner, drops the dark ledge lip on
sloped corners, and emits no cliff quad on slope sides (tilemap stamp now covers the 4 diagonal chunks too,
since diagonals feed the corner drops). The textured instance carries the corner drops in its skirt-mask
bits 16/32/64/128 (corners (u-,v-),(u+,v-),(u+,v+),(u-,v+)); the vertex shader bilinearly interpolates
them over the diamond so the art tilts with the mesh (flat tiles are bit-identical to before), and the
build clears the downhill skirt bit, zeroes the drop-edge relief, and skips the gt_side face on slope sides.
A wedge's textured diamond is a bilinear interpolation of the mesh's two triangles — it can sit up to 0.25
level off the mesh at the diamond centre, inside the existing +0.004 depth bias, so no z-fighting is
expected; the mesh underneath is the same material colour if it ever shows. 2+-level steps are unchanged
(cliffs, skirts, side faces, relief all as before). Canvas2D keeps flat diamonds (fallback renderer only).

Decision — gameplay truth unchanged: stand height, movement, pathing, building placement and farming all
still read the flat tile height h; nothing in gameplay was touched. Flat buildable areas place exactly as
before (no placement rule changed). Rendering never writes chunk heights (asserted in the new render test).

Decision — ADR-410 contract: `groundSlopeArt(shape)` (world/slope.ts) returns the art selector for a
sloped tile, and `groundSlopeKey(mat, season, kind, dir)` (render/groundArt.ts) builds the sprite key:
`gt_<mat>_slope_ramp_<d>` (d = downhill axis, view-space: 0=+u, 1=+v, 2=-u, 3=-v) and
`gt_<mat>_slope_wedge_<c>` (c = low corner: 0=(u-,v-), 1=(u+,v-), 2=(u+,v+), 3=(u-,v+)), same 68x52 cell
and anchor (34,18) as the flat `gt_<mat>` bases, same season suffixes. The renderer swaps the base layer
to the slope key only when `GroundArt.id()` resolves it, and the slope keys are pinned in `pageSprites`
once they ship; until ADR-410 paints them the flat base is kept and tilted geometrically, so nothing is
ever invisible. The graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands); the height range and edit
bounds are ADR-411's slice, not this one.

Validation: new tests `adr409_ground_shape.test.ts` (world, 8 tests: flat/void, ramps × 4 directions,
wedges × 4 corners, valley/peak/3-edge guard, stepped + ramp-next-to-cliff, diagonal dimple, water
inset, cornerMask) and `adr409_slopes.test.ts` (render, 7 tests: ramp/wedge instance bits in all 4 view
quarters, 2-level step keeps skirt + relief, gt side-face counts 1 vs 3, slope-art fallback vs shipped
key, mesh corner heights + cliff suppression, render never writes heights). Typecheck clean with pinned
TS 5.9.3 (world + render). Neighbour suites re-run with no regressions (worldgen, render, terrain,
building/placement, pathing, farming). Not verified on a real phone: the tilt is geometric, but whether
ramps read as slopes (rather than smeared diamonds) at play zoom needs Tracey's eyes on the live build.

## ADR-413: AI humans wear paths into roads on routes they travel often (SurVivaZ)

Context: AI humans walked the same home <-> destination / home <-> favourite spot / home <-> resource routes
for hundreds of trips and the world never showed it — no visible trace of use, and no reason for a bot to
prefer the way it already knows. The user asked for paths/roads to emerge from repeated travel.

Decision — counting (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/worn_paths.ts`, new): a route is an unordered pair of
tile endpoints (the travel layer's trip origin and goal, so home <-> destination, home <-> favourite spot and
home <-> resource node are all the same mechanism, either direction). Every completed trip (arrived) on a
route counts once, in the bot's AiMemory (`wornRoutes`, new field on AiMemory in `ai/planner.ts`, persisted
through game.agents like the rest of AiMemory — flushAiMemory JSON). Failed / timed-out trips do not count,
and neither do hops under 6 tiles. A route needs WORN_PATH_TRIPS = 3 completed trips before it wears a path;
endpoints within 4 tiles of a remembered route count as the same route (a bot rarely departs from the exact
tile it left from last time).

Decision — forming: at route assignment (`fillTravelSensors`, and the off-screen counterpart `offscreenPlan`
in `ai/travel.ts`), a route worn enough lays Dirt Path road tiles (RoadSurface.Path, owner 0 = worn, not
player-built) along the Bresenham line between the endpoints via roads.ts `spawnRoad` — so a worn path is a
first-class ADR-119 road: it renders through the existing road autotile art (`road_path_m<mask>`, canvas2d
flat decals, seasonal dusting — no new art, no new rendering path), it gives the ADR-119 movement bonus
(roadSpeedMul, 1.1x on dirt path), and it persists / replicates through the core chunk codec (Road is
networked + persistent, like Crop) with no new component, no schema change and no persist migration. Tiles
are skipped when already road, in water, or inside someone else's privilege zone (hasPrivilege) — a worn
path never paves a lake or a stranger's claim. Forming again lays nothing once the path exists.

Decision — use: at the same route-assignment point, when >= 60% of the straight line's tiles are already
road (and road reaches both ends), the route waypoints are replaced by the road tiles, compressed to
direction changes (a straight 100-tile path is 2 waypoints, not 100), so the bot walks the path instead of
its region-centre route. The water check (checkRouteWater) still runs afterwards on the new route, so a worn
path never strands a bot at a river it cannot cross; a re-plan around water replaces the worn route as
before. Off-screen bots follow the same rule (offscreenStep walks tr.route, whatever it is).

Decision — cost bounds: counting happens only on trip completion; forming and the preference check happen
only at route assignment (a <= 128-tile Bresenham scan each) — no per-tick work, no full-world scans. Caps:
at most 8 routes remembered per bot (least-travelled evicted first), at most 128 tiles laid per formation,
at most 4096 worn-path tiles per world (a formation past it lays nothing). The graphics preset default is
untouched (ADR-408 stands).

Validation: new tests `adr413_worn_paths.test.ts` (gameplay, 5 tests: 3 trips form an owner-0 Path road
along the line, 2 trips / failed trips / short hops do not, a later trip is routed along the road tiles and
the bot walks them to the goal, counts + path survive an AiMemory JSON round-trip with the Road
networked+persistent contract asserted, per-bot route cap with eviction). Typecheck clean with pinned
TS 5.9.3 (gameplay). Neighbour suites re-run with no regressions (adr324, adr343, adr344, adr345, adr326,
adr336, roads_signs_hordes — 134 passed total including the 5 new). Not verified on a real phone: the path
is the existing dirt-path art, but whether a worn path reads as a track (rather than a player road) at play
zoom needs Tracey's eyes on the live build.

## ADR-412: Abandoned-structure corners and walls sit on their own ground tile (SurVivaZ)

Context: generated abandoned structures bumped up against raised ground looked unnatural — their corner pieces and walls elevated off the ground, floating over a visible gap. Repro (cottage 5x5 at origin (8,8), flat footprint at level 2, neighbours at level 5 from x/y 13): the south wall, east wall and the NE / SE / SW corners all rendered at level 5 while the foundations and north/west walls sat at level 2.

Root cause: no terrain height lives in generation or placement at all — every stamped piece carries story level only (`Transform.z` = level * levelHeight, 0 for ground floor), and the lift is entirely the renderer's (`view.ts` `groundZ`, which reads the single tile under `floor(x), floor(y)`). But walls and `wall_corner_outer` L pieces anchor exactly on the footprint boundary lines: south walls at y = y0+h, east walls at x = x0+w, corners at the four vertices (x0/y0, x0+w/y0, x0+w/y0+h, x0/y0+h). For those anchors `floor()` lands on the neighbour tile OUTSIDE the structure, so a raised neighbour lifted the piece by the full height difference. ADR-384's single-level gate only checks footprint tiles, so a flat-footprint site next to raised ground stamps fine and then floats — generation was never the defect, and the gate must not change (skipping such sites would thin ruins near hills for no reason).

Decision — render-side grounding (`apps/client/src/view.ts`): new `pieceBoundaryGroundZ(tiles, x, y, z, lh)` grounds a build piece on the lowest terrain height among the tiles touching its anchor (2 tiles for an edge, 4 for a vertex, across chunk edges via a direct `getChunk` read that leaves groundZ's one-entry cache alone). The structure's own tile is always one of the touched tiles, so a raised neighbour can no longer lift the piece; a lower neighbour only sinks the base behind the higher ground, which reads as a foundation down the slope, never a floating gap. Off-boundary anchors touch exactly one tile, so it is identical to `pieceGroundZ` for foundations, furniture and interior pieces, and story lift / decor offsets are unchanged. It is used for placed build pieces (the render loop's `GPiece` branch; walkers keep `pieceGroundZ`) and for the placement ghost preview, so a wall ghosted against raised ground sits on the structure's tile too. Deliberately NOT a placement-time nudge: nudging stored Transforms would desync them from the slot derived from the position (`slotFromPos` / `structureIndexSystem`) and would leave already-stamped ruins floating. Because the fix is in render, old ruins in already-generated/saved worlds are fixed in place — no regeneration, no persist/schema change, no generation or placement change, and the graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands).

Validation: new tests `apps/client/test/adr412_ruin_ground.test.ts` (7 tests) and `packages/gameplay/test/adr412_ruin_ground.test.ts` (3 tests), 10/10 passing. The client tests pin the repro (single-tile read = 5 on the south/east walls and three corners) and the fix (all four corners and all four walls = 2, upper-story boundary pieces keep their story on top of the structure's ground, off-boundary anchors identical to `pieceGroundZ`, chunk-edge anchors read both chunks, lower neighbour sinks the base only). The gameplay tests pin the anchor geometry (corners on the four vertices, south/east walls on the boundary lines), that a flat footprint next to raised ground still stamps, and that stamped pieces carry story level only — so the render fix covers pre-ADR-412 ruins. Neighbour suites re-run with no regressions (adr142 ghost ground, adr300/301/311/340/373/384 abandoned, modular_building — 70 passed). Typecheck clean with pinned TS 5.9.3 (gameplay clean; apps/client clean except the two pre-existing `scripts/oxipng.mjs` errors in untouched files). Not verified on a real phone: the gap is gone by construction in the headless harness, but whether the grounded walls read correctly at play zoom needs Tracey's eyes on the live build.

## ADR-414: Terrain height visible on the console browser's Canvas2D fallback (SurVivaZ)

Context: on Edge on Xbox Series X the ground reads flat — slopes, raised/lowered ground and the ADR-409/411 shapes are not visible — while the same build looks right on the phone. There is no Xbox in the VM, so the root cause was traced through the render decision code, not observed on the console.

Root cause: the console browser lands on the Canvas2D fallback renderer, not the WebGL2 path. `chooseRenderer` (`packages/render/src/canvas2d.ts:42`) probes a fresh canvas for WebGL2 first, and the client (`apps/client/src/view.ts`) falls back to `Canvas2DRenderer` when that probe fails or `new IsoRenderer` throws; the canvas2d header itself names "console browsers after a GPU reset" as a fallback case, the IsoRenderer constructor notes Xbox Edge ANGLE/D3D11 adapters refusing `high-performance` after a GPU reset, and ADR-407 documents the 1 GB UWP cap tripping GPU resets. The WebGL2 path is height-complete at every quality tier (the tilemap mesh tilts top faces by `classifyGroundShape` corner drops and draws cliff faces; TileTerrain tilts/skirts/side-faces — no tier gates any of it, and the console high tier changes only resolution, atlas budget and effects), so the tier is not the cause. The gap is entirely in Canvas2D: `flatTiles` and the render-loop flat fallback drew every ground tile as a flat diamond at `worldToScreen(x, y, 0)` and `gtBlock` baked every gt cell at a fixed `dy`, never reading tile heights. `packages/world/src/slope.ts` documents it outright ("Canvas2D keeps flat diamonds (fallback renderer only) — not wired to this model yet"). Sprites already used their Transform z on this path, so only the ground was flat.

Decision — shared height geometry in a new module (`packages/render/src/canvasGroundHeight.ts`), wired into both Canvas2D ground paths: `c2dTileHeight` / `c2dNeighbourLow` (the `tilemap.ts` height + 0.25 water-inset reads, undefined instead of NO_TILE_HEIGHT for missing tiles) and `c2dGroundGeometry(z, low)`, which feeds view-space neighbours into `classifyGroundShape` and returns the tilted top quad (per-corner drops, exactly the mesh top face) plus cliff-face polygons on lower sides that are not slope sides — far faces (-u/-v) drawn before the top so the top paints over their overlap as the mesh depth test does, near faces (+u/+v) after it, shaded 0.62 / 0.8 / 0.28 as `tilemap.ts cliffShade`. The flat path draws the quad + faces in diagonal painter order (row-major would let a later low tile paint over an earlier high tile's face). The gt-block path offsets each cell vertically by its height (`dy - z * 16`), grows the baked canvas by the block's height range (`c2dGtPads`, z = 0 stays exactly where the flat block put it), and fills cliff faces the art skirt does not cover: full far faces, and near faces below the skirt (`c2dGtFaceBelowSkirt`, 1-level drops need no fill — the 16 px skirt covers them). Block heights are clamped to +/-32 levels (`C2D_GT_Z_CLAMP`) so the canvas stays bounded: worldgen relief (<= ~26 levels) is never clamped; shovel extremes compress monotonically but stay visibly high/low, and faces still meet neighbour tops exactly. Void neighbours draw no face (a deliberate deviation: the mesh draws a cliff down to -99 at the load edge). Water is unchanged (flat surface at z = 0 on both paths). No package.json change; the graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands).

Status — DONE (follow-up wiring, 2026-11-17): the shared module is now wired into `packages/render/src/canvas2d.ts` on top of the landed ADR-415/417 file — `flatTiles` draws the tilted top quad + cliff faces in diagonal painter order via `drawC2DGroundCell`, the render-loop flat fallback calls `flatTiles` in view space, `gtBlock` offsets each cell by its clamped height, grows the baked canvas by `c2dGtPads`, and fills far faces plus near faces below the skirt (water cells keep their ADR-415 `gt_water` art at z = 0), `drawGroundArt` culls/draws with the block's `topPad`, and a `cliffColor` sits next to `groundColor`. The `Canvas2DRenderer.render()` end-to-end test in §7 below is green. One adaptation from the integration spec: the ADR-415 test's gt-block filter (`height === 276`) now accepts `height >= 276`, because shore cells carry a -0.25 water-inset low so lake blocks bake 280 px tall — verified a real regression first (7/7 at HEAD, 5/7 with the wiring, 7/7 again after the filter fix).

Validation: new tests `packages/render/test/adr414_canvas2d_terrain_height.test.ts` (14 tests, 14/14 passing): heights read (water = 0 surface, missing/empty = undefined), water inset -0.25, flat top = the old diamond lifted by its height, 1-level step tilts into a ramp with no cliff on the slope side, plateau draws a flat top with a cliff face on every lower side, 2-level drop keeps a flat top + full face, water neighbour draws a 4 px face, void neighbour draws none, shades match the mesh, gt clamp/pads, below-skirt face, and a harness driving the shared flat-cell drawing over a TileMap (a 3-level plateau draws 48 px above the low ground with a cliff face closing the drop; flat ground draws exactly the old diamonds), plus the render-level end-to-end tests driving `Canvas2DRenderer.render()` on the console path (no registry → flat fallback) with a recording 2D context: a 3-level plateau's top fills 48 px above the flat ground's with its -u cliff face (`rgb(31,24,16)`, spanning y -64 to 0) closing the drop, and a second render of an all-flat map produces exactly the 25 old diamonds. Typecheck clean with pinned TS 5.9.3 (render package, symlink-removed CI simulation, exit 0). Full `packages/render` suite: 602 passed / 2 skipped, 0 failed (93 files passed, 2 skipped). The gt path is exercised end-to-end by ADR-415's `renderLake` (real `gtBlock` bakes through `render()`: water + grass draws verified, including into the taller 280 px lake blocks). Not verified on a real Xbox: the console path is the fallback the codebase documents, but whether the height reads at play zoom on the TV needs Tracey's eyes on the Xbox. Honest cuts: gt cells are offset flat, not tilted like the WebGL2 slope art (the flat path tilts); heights beyond +/-32 levels in one gt block compress; no per-vertex lip darkening on flat tops (the mesh's ledge lip) — cliff faces + tilts carry the readability instead.

## ADR-416: Auto-zoom on entering an abandoned structure, console browser (SurVivaZ)

Context: on Edge on Xbox Series X, entering an abandoned structure does NOT automatically zoom in on the player, while the same build zooms correctly on the phone. There is no Xbox in the VM, so the root cause was traced through the zoom-trigger code, not observed on the console.

Root cause: the console browser lands on the Canvas2D fallback renderer, not WebGL2 (`chooseRenderer` picks it whenever WebGL2 cannot be created; the canvas2d header names "console browsers after a GPU reset", and ADR-407 documents the 1 GB UWP cap behind the context losses). The indoor-zoom chain is `main.ts:410` → `camZoom?.setIndoor(iso.renderer.indoor, dt)` → ADR-206 `setIndoor` in `apps/client/src/camera-zoom.ts` (180 ms debounce, 280 ms easing, no input/viewport/capability gate — nothing console-specific blocks it). On WebGL2 the signal exists (`IsoRenderer.ts:257`, `get indoor()` returns `sprites.cutawayActive`, "last frame had a roof/upper-floor cutaway around the focus entity"). At base `11f30930`, `Canvas2DRenderer` had NO `indoor` getter at all (zero `indoor`/`cutawayActive` references in `packages/render/src/canvas2d.ts`), so the per-frame read returned `undefined`, `setIndoor` never flipped its `want` flag, and the indoor factor stayed 1 — the zoom could never engage on that path, whatever the player did. The `view.ts:396` cast (`new Canvas2DRenderer(canvas) as unknown as IsoRenderer`) hid the missing member at compile time, so nothing flagged it.

Decision — the signal now exists on the Canvas2D path, from the same cutaway the WebGL2 path runs: ADR-417's `Canvas2DRenderer.indoor` (`get indoor()` returns `cutawayActive`), computed in `updateCutaway` from last frame's piece cover (`PieceCoverIndex.region` around the focus tile/level — cover above the player's level, or a roof on its level), with one frame of lag exactly like `IsoRenderer`. ADR-416's own contribution is the proof that this signal drives the zoom on the console path: no change to `camera-zoom.ts` (debounce/easing behaviour for the working platforms is unchanged), no change to `main.ts` (the `iso.renderer.indoor` read was already correct), no package.json change, and the graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands). Note on attribution: the `indoor` getter and cutaway machinery in `canvas2d.ts` are ADR-417's uncommitted work, labelled as such in the code — this ADR depends on that commit landing (with or before this one); without it these tests fail at `r.indoor` being `undefined`.

Validation: new tests `packages/render/test/adr416_canvas2d_indoor.test.ts` (6 tests, 6/6 passing) and `apps/client/test/adr416_canvas2d_indoor_zoom.test.ts` (1 test, 1/1 passing). The render tests pin the signal on the Canvas2D path (false before any frame and while roof art is still loading, true once the player stands in a roofed 4x4 ruin with art loaded and cover built — one frame of lag, like IsoRenderer — false outdoors even with the ruin's cover built, false in an unroofed ruin, cleared on stepping out, cleared with no focus entity). The client test drives the real `Canvas2DRenderer` through frames inside a roofed ruin and feeds its `indoor` into the real `attachZoom` exactly like `main.ts:410` does (signal read before the frame renders), then asserts the camera zoom rises to `DESKTOP_ZOOM * INDOOR_GAIN` (×1.55) at a 1920x1080 viewport. Neighbour suites re-run: `adr417_canvas2d_cutaway.test.ts` green; `adr415_console_water.test.ts` has 2 failures in the sibling's still-in-progress water work (not this slice). Typecheck clean with pinned TS 5.9.3 (gameplay symlink aside, CI simulation): render package clean, zero errors; client package shows only the 2 known pre-existing `scripts/oxipng.mjs` errors in untouched files (`adr391_oxipng.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts` — the script is absent from this sparse checkout), none in ADR-416 files. Not verified on a real Xbox: the signal and the zoom are proven in the headless harness under the console's exact render path (Canvas2D fallback, 1920x1080), but whether the zoom feels right at play zoom on the TV needs Tracey's eyes on the Xbox. Honest cuts: none in this slice — the fix is the signal itself; the one-frame lag matches WebGL2 by design.

## ADR-415: Water tiles show on the console browser's Canvas2D fallback (SurVivaZ)

Context: on Edge on Xbox Series X water tiles do not show their tiles — water renders blank/wrong — while the same build looks right on the phone. There is no Xbox in the VM, so the root cause was traced through the render decision code, not observed on the console.

Root cause: the console browser lands on the Canvas2D fallback renderer, not the WebGL2 path. `chooseRenderer` (`packages/render/src/canvas2d.ts:42`) probes a fresh canvas for WebGL2 first, and the client (`apps/client/src/view.ts`) falls back to `Canvas2DRenderer` when that probe fails or `new IsoRenderer` throws; the canvas2d header itself names "console browsers after a GPU reset" as a fallback case, the IsoRenderer constructor notes Xbox Edge refusing `high-performance` after a GPU reset, and ADR-407 documents the 1 GB UWP cap tripping GPU resets. The WebGL2 water builders are correct (verified at builder level: gt mode emits `gt_water` instances with shore corner tints, legacy mode emits `tile_water`, and the tilemap mesh carries flag-1 water-top verts at z = -0.25), so the defect is not in WebGL2. The gap is entirely in Canvas2D: `drawWater` draws only the flat ADR-184 gradient image (1 px/tile, shore→deep), and `gtBlock` explicitly skipped every `GroundLayerKind.Water` layer, so `gt_water` / `gt_water_shallow` never drew even when resident. The old comment's rationale ("grey detail art needs the GPU tint") is true for legacy `tile_water` but not for `gt_water`, which carries its full baked colour (ADR-251). Winter ice and leaves were not skipped — only Water.

Decision — `gtBlock` (`packages/render/src/canvas2d.ts`) no longer skips Water layers: they are pushed to the bake ops like every other layer, with brightness `0.80 + 0.26 * waterShoreTint(x, y)` — the same deep→shallow ramp the WebGL2 shader applies (`terrainTiles` FS `mix(0.80, 1.06, k)`), applied via `g.filter = brightness(...)` per op and reset to `"none"` after the loop so non-water ops are untouched. The flat `drawWater` gradient stays as the under-layer (it already ran under the blocks). No package.json change; the graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands).

Validation: new tests `packages/render/test/adr415_console_water.test.ts` (7 tests, 7/7 passing): WebGL2 control pins (gt-mode water instances, legacy `tile_water` instances, mesh flag-1 verts) plus the Canvas2D console path end-to-end — `chooseRenderer` picks `canvas2d` when the webgl2 probe returns null; deep + shallow water draw their gt tile art into the baked ground blocks; brightness follows the 0.80 deep / 1.06 shore ramp (all in [0.79, 1.07]); the gradient under-layer still runs and the baked blocks reach the screen. Before/after: with the fix reverted, exactly the two water-tile tests fail while the gradient-under-layer test still passes (the gradient alone was all the water had). Not verified on a real Xbox: which step puts the console on Canvas2D (probe failure vs IsoRenderer throw vs post-reset state — the console's own `[view] gl...` / `[view] WebGL2 unavailable` / `[view] IsoRenderer failed` log lines would confirm it), and whether the tiles read at play zoom on the TV needs Tracey's eyes. Honest cuts: brightness is a per-op canvas filter, not the shader's per-vertex tint, so the ramp is per-tile rather than per-corner; gt blocks still bake progressively (one newly-loading image per frame on first load — pre-existing behaviour, not introduced here); no visual check on real hardware.

## ADR-417: Ceilings and building parts don't block the indoor view on the console browser (SurVivaZ)

Context: on Edge on Xbox Series X, ceilings and other base building parts block the view of the player inside an abandoned structure or other structure, while the same build is fine on the phone. There is no Xbox in the VM, so the root cause was traced through the occlusion code and the conditions the console browser produces, not observed on the console.

Root cause: the console browser lands on the Canvas2D fallback renderer, not the WebGL2 path. `chooseRenderer` (`packages/render/src/canvas2d.ts:42`) probes a fresh canvas for WebGL2 first, and the client (`apps/client/src/view.ts`) falls back to `Canvas2DRenderer` when that probe fails or `new IsoRenderer` throws; the canvas2d header itself names "console browsers after a GPU reset" as a fallback case, the IsoRenderer constructor notes Xbox Edge ANGLE/D3D11 adapters refusing `high-performance` after a GPU reset (`packages/render/src/IsoRenderer.ts:295`), and ADR-407 documents the 1 GB UWP cap tripping GPU resets. The WebGL2 path is occlusion-complete at every quality tier (no tier gates `style.occlusion` or the cutaway — the only occlusion switch is the demo's `?occ=off`): `SpriteBatch.prepare` computes the cutaway region around the focus from the gridless `PieceCoverIndex` (the client never calls `setBuildingGrid`, so the grid path never runs), hides other-level pieces in the region outright (`pieceHiddenByStory`), fades same-level roofs / front enclosure walls to `cutawayAlpha` 0.10 (`pieceShouldCutaway`), and fades tall sprites in front of the player toward their `Occluder.fade` (0.35) or the style alpha. The gap is entirely in Canvas2D: `gatherPieces` painted every piece at alpha 1 with no cover index and no cutaway, the sprite loop had no Occluder fade at all, and `render()` ended with `void this.focus` — the focus entity was never even read, so `renderer.indoor` (which the indoor zoom reads) was `undefined` on this path too.

Decision — the indoor occlusion pass, ported to Canvas2D (`packages/render/src/canvas2d.ts`, WebGL2 untouched): `updateCutaway` computes the cutaway region from last frame's `PieceCoverIndex` cover, cached on focus tile/level + view quarter + cover fingerprint like ADR-381 (one frame of lag, as on WebGL2), and exposes it as `cutawayActive` / `indoor` (parity with `IsoRenderer.indoor`); `gatherPieces` fills `coverNext` per resolved piece and swaps it at the end, hides other-level pieces in the region, fades same-level roofs / front enclosure walls to `cutawayAlpha` 0.10 via the shared `pieceShouldCutaway` / `pieceHiddenByStory` / `isEnclosurePieceKey`, and fades other tall pieces in front of the focus whose art rect overlaps it through the shared `occluderFade` math (explicit `Occluder.fade` wins, else the style alpha 0.35, smoothed at `fadeSpeed` 8/s); the sprite loop applies the same `occAlpha` (explicit Occluder, auto-occlusion for tall static props, actors never auto-occlude and reset the reused entity-index slot, `SpriteFlag.Footprint` excluded) and hides other-story sprites in the region (`hideOtherStory`). Dither mode falls back to the same fade (Canvas2D has no dither pattern; the player stays visible either way). `diagReport` now reports `indoor` so `?diag=1` on the console shows whether the cutaway is active. A `groundZAt` helper (the `tileHeight` read, inlined so the file stays GL-free) supplies the player's level. No package.json change; the graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands).

Validation: new tests `packages/render/test/adr417_canvas2d_cutaway.test.ts` (6 tests, 6/6 passing): frame 1 has no cutaway yet (cover lag) but the roof already fades to 0.35 through piece occlusion, frame 2 hides the level-1 roofs outright, fades the same-level roof to 0.10, and leaves the far roof and floors opaque with `indoor` true; front walls at q=0 fade to 0.35 while walls behind stay opaque; at q=2 the wall now in front cuts away to 0.10; walking outside clears the cutaway and the roofs come back opaque, and no focus means nothing fades; a full `render()` drive pins tall sprites in front of the player fading (auto → 0.35, explicit `Occluder{fade: 0.5}` → 0.5) with the player and behind-sprites opaque, and an upstairs sprite inside the region not drawn while the player and an outside sprite are. Typecheck clean with pinned TS 5.9.3 (render package, symlink-removed simulation). Full render suite on the combined tree (incl. sibling ADR-414/415/416 files): 95 files passed / 2 skipped, 604 tests passed / 2 skipped, 0 failed. Not verified on a real Xbox: which step puts the console on Canvas2D (same open question as ADR-415 — the console's `[view] gl...` log lines would confirm it), and whether ceilings/walls actually clear at play zoom on the TV needs Tracey's eyes. Honest cuts: `InteriorPart` camper interiors are untouched (vehicles only, not structures); a doll character with an explicit Occluder is not faded (actors never auto-occlude and view specs never put Occluders on characters); L-corner arms / rfx overlays step the shared per-entity smoothing once per part instead of once per piece (same steady state, one frame faster to it); piece occlusion uses the drawn art rect where WebGL uses the footprint-projected rect (same hit in practice — wall/tree art fills its footprint).

## ADR-418: Terrain slope seam gaps and floating pieces (SurVivaZ)

Context: the user reported (2026-11-17 17:41 CST, phone screenshot) that the new ADR-409 slope shapes cause visual glitches — blue gaps showing through and pieces floating in the air, plus textures overlapping / not fitting together where regular flat tiles meet the new shapes. The screenshot shows terraced dirt stepping down on two axes at once. No GL exists in the VM, so both causes were proven in the headless harness with repro tests that transcribe the shipped geometry, and the fixes are verified the same way plus against the real mesh builder.

Root cause 1 — blue gaps (the sky clear colour, not water): a flat-bottomed cliff quad does not reach a tilted neighbour's low endpoint. `packages/world/src/slope.ts:86-91` drops a corner only when the vertex minimum is exactly h-1, so if a third tile touching a shared vertex is 2+ below, the high tile's corner does NOT drop while the 1-below neighbour's corner DOES drop to that third tile's height. The cliff quad (`packages/render/src/tilemap.ts:235,240`) was a flat rectangle from the tile's height to the neighbour's FLAT height, emitted whenever the edge was not a slope side. Concrete case: tile T h=5, +x neighbour N=4, +y neighbour=3 — T's +x edge endpoints are 4 and 5, N's shared edge endpoints are 4 and 3, so the triangle (1,0,4)-(1,1,4)-(1,1,3) in the plane x=1 had no face on either side: a 1-level (16 px) hole. A sweep over the four tiles touching a shared edge found 56/81 height combos unsealed. The blue is the sky clear colour (`IsoRenderer.ts:610` clears with day.sky; `timeOfDay.ts:51` daytime sky is [0.35, 0.55, 0.78]); water renders only on water tiles far below these terraces.

Root cause 2 — floating pieces / texture overlap: the textured instance did not tilt the way its shader comment claimed. The VS (`terrainTiles.ts` TERRAIN_TILES_VS) said "the diamond tilts by bilinear interpolation over the frame", but `sdrop` was computed only at the four frame-quad vertices and the GPU then linearly interpolated `gl_Position` across the two TRIANGLE_STRIP triangles, whose fold is the frame diagonal v1-v2 (top-right to bottom-left). The vertex-colour mesh top face (`tilemap.ts:226-229`) is two triangles folded on the N-S diamond diagonal (corners 0-2). Different fold + frame corners not on the mesh plane = the instance's diamond corners sat at the wrong heights vs the mesh: up to +0.83 levels (13 px) high and -0.55 levels (9 px) low (ramp +u N -0.27 / E +0.35 / W -0.36 at 1x; wedge low S N -0.49; diagonal dimple W +0.71 at 1x / +0.83 at 2x), while flat tiles agreed exactly (0.00). Adjacent instances disagreed at shared vertices (ramp low corner 4.35 vs flat neighbour 4.0). The ADR-410 slope art itself is correct (same cell/anchor as flat bases; dirs match) — no art was repainted.

Disproved (left alone): the all-four-corners guard (`slope.ts:92-94`) — when it fires the neighbour's shared corners cannot drop, so the cliff bottom meets the neighbour's flat edge exactly; slope-side suppression — a slope side forces the vertex minima to h-1 = the neighbour's height; chunk boundaries — defects reproduce inside a single chunk; ADR-410 art anchor/direction.

Decision — fix 1, cliff quads follow both top faces: new `cliffEdgeSpan` in `packages/world/src/slope.ts` (with `NEIGHBOUR_EDGE_CORNERS`, the neighbour's corner indices at the shared vertices in `GROUND_SHAPE_SIDE_CORNERS` order: +x [0,3], -x [1,2], +y [1,0], -y [3,2]) returns the trapezoid for one edge — top = this tile's edge heights, bottom = the neighbour's edge heights at the same two vertices — and whether it is emitted (neighbour lower and not a slope side). `packages/render/src/tilemap.ts` emits that trapezoid (the neighbour shape is classified lazily, only on an edge that actually emits a cliff; water / void neighbours stay flat) instead of the flat rectangle, and the top edge now follows the tile's own corners too, so no fin pokes above a tilted top. Flat tiles render exactly as before (flat top and bottom when no corner drops). Decision — fix 2, the instance fold is now the mesh fold: new `packages/render/src/terrainTileTriangulation.ts` (the single source of truth shared by the shader and the tests) triangulates the instance as 30 vertices / 10 triangles drawn as TRIANGLES — the diamond is exactly the mesh's (N,E,S),(N,S,W), so the instance surface inside the diamond IS the mesh top face, exact at every point, and the ring between diamond and frame is triangulated with the frame corners (one triangle against each diamond edge plus one in each frame corner; 0 gaps / 0 overlaps over both shipped frames, verified numerically). Frame corners keep the old bilinear drop so the skirt hangs as before; diamond corners take their own corner's drop (screen-position-aware, so E/W swap under flipX while the mesh never mirrors). Solving for frame-vertex drops that hit the mesh corners exactly was rejected: the system is near-singular (determinant 0.006 at the 2x frame) and the solution swings to +/-22 levels, which would throw the skirt hundreds of px off — the fold itself had to change. Flat tiles are unaffected (all drops zero). The draw calls changed from `TRIANGLE_STRIP, 0, 4` to `TRIANGLES, 0, 30` (opaque + waterfall overlays); waterfall/side-face instances carry no corner bits, so they stay flat as before, and flipX bit 8 is never set together with corner bits, so the mirror-aware drop selection only ever matters at sc=0. Decision — Canvas2D fallback too: `packages/render/src/canvasGroundHeight.ts` `c2dGroundGeometry` had the same flat-cliff assumption in 2D paint (flat face bottom = gap under the face; flat face top = a cliff-coloured triangle overpainted on the tilted top by near faces, which draw after the top), so its faces now use the same `cliffEdgeSpan` (neighbour shape classified from the same `low()` lookup; a water neighbour — fractional height from the 0.25 inset — is flat by definition and never classified) and `low` is the lowest bottom corner so the gt-block below-skirt fill and canvas pads cover the deepest drop. No package.json change; the graphics preset default is untouched (ADR-408 stands); no slope-shape design change (ramps/wedges/valleys/peaks as classified by slope.ts — only their seams are exact).

Validation: full gate (`vitest run` from the repo root, 26 min on this VM): 4,657 passed / 2 failed / 6 skipped (4,665 tests; 691 files passed / 9 failed / 4 skipped) — the only failures are the known pre-existing ones (7 suites fail to load on the absent `scripts/oxipng.mjs`, `packages/assets/test/pack.test.ts` on the absent `assets/building/KEYS.md`, and the `packages/persist/test/bench.test.ts` timing flake at 60.1 ms vs the 50 ms ceiling under full-suite load). Base gate at 63da69bf was 4,632 passed / 2 failed / 6 skipped. New/updated tests: `packages/world/test/adr418_slope_seams.test.ts` (9 tests — the repro tests now call the real `cliffEdgeSpan`: the two hole cases pin the trapezoid spans, a top-edge fin test, the 81-combo sweep plus a 324-case sweep over all four edges, a per-edge neighbour-mapping unit test, a 4-rotation consistency test, and the two disproof controls); `packages/render/test/adr418_instance_mesh_seam.test.ts` (11 tests — the repro tests now evaluate the real triangulation table: corners + interior points exact in both frame scales, all four view rotations, the adjacent-instances meeting point, the flat control, plus real-mesh cliff quads driven through `TilemapRenderer.build` pinning the trapezoid z-values [4,5,3,4] and the unchanged flat step [5,5,3,3]); `packages/render/test/adr418_canvas2d_seams.test.ts` (5 tests — terraced face, below-skirt fill, flat step, water neighbour, slope side). Neighbour suites re-run with no regressions (adr409/adr410/adr411, adr246/adr251/adr253/adr267/adr276, adr386/adr389, adr414/adr415/adr417, canvas2d — 14 files, 97 tests, all passing). Typecheck clean with pinned TS 5.9.3 (gameplay symlink aside, restored after): core, assets, world, gameplay, render, net, testkit, persist, input and server all clean; apps/client shows only the 2 known pre-existing `scripts/oxipng.mjs` TS2307 errors in untouched files (`adr391_oxipng.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts`). Not verified on a real phone: there is no GL in the VM, so the shader change itself is verified only through the shared table (the GLSL embeds the same data the tests evaluate) and the real mesh builder — whether the blue gaps are gone and the slope art sits flush at play zoom needs Tracey's eyes on the live build, ideally on the same terraced dirt from the screenshot. Honest cuts: the gt_side textured faces keep flat bottoms (their bottom can sit up to 1 level above the tilted neighbour edge), but the fixed mesh cliff behind them now covers that triangle with vertex-colour cliff, so it reads as a shade difference, not a hole; the instance skirt still hangs from bilinear frame-corner drops (bounded in [0,1]), so its bottom edge is approximate where the frame corners extrapolate — the diamond, which is what meets the neighbours, is exact; the 30-vertex draw is 7.5x the vertex-shader work per ground instance (trivial against fragment cost, and chunk-cached).

## ADR-419: Ramp tool — grade a ±1 staircase for players and AI humans (SurVivaZ)

Context: ADR-409's slopes are render-only — gameplay still reads flat tile heights, and a 2+-level step is a cliff face players and AI humans cannot walk up. Players asked for a ramp tool that slopes land with the new terrain pieces: pick a start tile, a direction, and a target height change, and get a walkable grade instead of digging tile-by-tile with a shovel.

Decision — (b), one new command, `gameplay.terrainRamp` (`{x: i32, y: i32, dx: i8, dy: i8, delta: i8}`: foot tile, axis direction, signed height change). New `packages/gameplay/src/ramp.ts`: `planRamp()` plans the ramp (graded tiles are foot+dir·i for i = 1..|delta|, target foot height + sign·i, so consecutive tiles differ by exactly 1 along the graded axis), `gradeRamp()` validates every step with `editTerrain(dryRun)` and applies the edits round-robin (level 1 of every tile, then level 2, …), so every intermediate state — including a partial ramp left by an aborted apply — is itself a ±1 staircase, never a cliff. Caps: |delta| ≤ 16, ≤ 96 edits per ramp. The alternative (a) — a client loop over `TerrainCmd` — was rejected: each tile would re-check shovel reach (a ramp longer than ~3 tiles extends past `TERRAIN.reach`), re-charge the 2/s fallback rate per tile, and strand a half-graded cliff if the client stopped mid-loop. The ramp command therefore checks reach only for the foot tile; every graded tile is still checked for privilege, occupancy and soil exactly like a single shovel edit. Rate: 2/s (`COMMAND_RATES`), one charge per ramp. Registered append-only last in `registerGameplayCommands` and bridged last in `GAMEPLAY_NET_COMMANDS` (after `ROPE_COMMANDS`); no `COMMAND_ENTITY_FIELDS` entry (no NetId fields). `editTerrain` gained a 6th `skipReach` parameter, used only by the ramp path.

Soil economy: 1 soil per level per tile — an up-ramp of +3 on flat costs 1+2+3 = 6 soil (checked in total up front; a per-edit dry run would see the same unspent bag every time). A down-ramp cuts into the plateau and yields soil instead. A water tile costs one extra edit to fill first (editTerrain fills water at its bed level before rising, ADR-263); digging water is refused (BadTile), so a down-ramp stops at the shore and an up-ramp over water builds a causeway. A downhill ramp near shore floods only its lowest dug tile on the flow step — flowed water's surface is its own bed, so water does not climb the ramp.

AI: the trigger is a frequent route (≥ 3 trips, the ADR-413 worn-path threshold) whose straight Bresenham line crosses a ≥ 2-level step — `findRampOnRoute()` in `ai/terrain_base.ts` finds the first such step, `fillPlanSensors` stores one live `RampPlan` in `AiMemory.ramp`, and a new `ramp` goal in the planner ladder (after earthworks) grades it in one `ramp:x:y:dx:dy:delta` action after the bot walks to the stand (a `TooFar` dry run means "not there yet", like `nextTerrainWork`). Soil: the pad/pit quarry cap (12 soil) cannot fund a ramp, so ramp work gets a ramp-sized quarry — dug beside the foot tile, max 3 deep, until the ramp's own `soilNeeded` (≤ 96) is funded. Also fixed the stale `height < -27 || height > 44` bound in `planTerrainBase` to the ADR-411 `LEVEL_MIN/LEVEL_MAX` (−300/326).

Client: ramp mode extends the existing shovel UI in `world-tools.ts` (same right-hand column, nothing new overlaps the HUD) — "Ramp" button toggles the mode (click again cycles length 2/3/4/6), T / LT+Y toggles, Esc exits; then ⬆/⬇ (Y/H, LT+D-pad) grades up/down from the marked foot tile in the facing/aimed direction, with the foot + graded line previewed as diamonds. New `Terrain.Ramp` action: keyboard `KeyT`, gamepad LT+Y, touch via the HUD button. Movement physics unchanged (1-level steps were already walkable, MAX_UNAIDED_CLIMB 3); `classifyGroundShape`'s corner rule untouched (ADR-418 guard is load-bearing).

Validation: 15 new tests in `packages/gameplay/test/adr419_ramp.test.ts` (planning, grading, reach, soil, water fill/refusal, shore flooding, command handler + rejection, AI find/plan/quarry/planner, bindings); extensions to `task36_terrain` (soil conservation), `adr409` (broad ramp profiles classify `ramp`), `adr418` (ramp profile through the 81-combo sweep, 0 violations), `adr170`/`task22_recruitment` tail pins. Typecheck clean with pinned TS 5.9.3 (gameplay symlink aside/restored; client shows only the 2 known pre-existing `scripts/oxipng.mjs` errors). Full `apps/server/test/`: 154 passed / 1 failed — `spawn_world` "one in-game day" timed out at 180 s under full-suite load and passes alone (~100 s), a load flake. Not verified on a real phone/Xbox: no GL in the VM, so whether the ramp reads as a smooth slope at play zoom needs the user's eyes. Honest cuts: a 1-wide ramp on flat ground does not classify every tile as `ramp` — its sides are cliffs by design (only the graded axis is a ±1 staircase); the ramp top ends in a ledge onto whatever ground lies beyond; ramp length is fixed to 2/3/4/6 in the UI; a bot only grades ramps on routes it already travels often.

## ADR-420: Dock (tier 1) + Shipyard (tier 2) boatbuilding stations, placed in deep water

New `PieceDef.requiresWater` (`"deep"`/`"any"`; free placement, ground true): `validatePlacement` inverts the water rule at the Terrain position — every footprint tile must be deep water (`waterDepthAt`), else new `BuildFail.NeedsDeepWater` (35); `slot.z` is pinned to `WATER_SURFACE_HEIGHT` (0); without terrain installed the check fails closed. Water pieces are claim-exempt (`needsClaim` false) and public — water has no Claim Flag. Stations `dock:6`, `shipyard:7` (`StationKind.Dock/Shipyard`); Dock crafts raft/canoe/rowboat kits, Shipyard crafts Motorboat/pontoon/Speedboat kits (recipes bind in later boat slices). Tier 1/2 is structure progression, not `tiers.json` material tiers; the Shipyard is standalone (no dock required) and gated by its iron/steel material chain (furnace + anvil). Skill nodes dock_craft (requires workbench_craft) and shipyard_craft (requires anvil_craft) were added in ADR-426 — ADR-221 requires every station piece to have exactly one unlock node, and the planner's `locked` hold + skill_pick x4 unlock boost already teach bots those nodes. Planner: `STATION_KEYS` + ladder goals after the anvil + `STATION_SLOTS` water probes; there is no water search yet, so a base with no deep water in the probe directions never builds one. Runtime-painted art in `apps/client/src/task420-art.ts` (atlases `decor_dock`/`decor_shipyard` + menu icons); the `pack/task420` fragment and `view.ts` hook land with the boat slice (ADR-421). Guide facts added for both stations (costs resolve from `pieces.json` via the ADR-362 registry).

## ADR-423: Triple the map size without changing streaming cost

- **Definition.** The map is the guaranteed-feature region: `REGION_SIZE` 512 → **1536** tiles (`packages/world/src/generator.ts`, exported). `REGION_FEATURE_SCALE` = 3. `WATER_FEATURE_RADIUS` stays 120 (starter window); `SCALED_WATER_FEATURE_RADIUS` = 360.
- **Region zero is preserved exactly.** It uses feature scale 1, so the same seed puts the same lake/river/pond/elevated lake at the same coordinates as before ADR-423 (pinned by `adr423_map_size.test.ts`). Non-zero regions use scale 3: lake dist 48–83 → 144–249, pond 36–75 → 108–225, lake r 12–17 → 36–51, pond r 3–4 → 9–12, river halfLen 70–99 → 210–297 (amp/period/offset ×3; width 1.15–1.7 unchanged), elevated lake dist 84–104 → 252–312, r 6–10 → 18–30, rim 4 → 12, level 4–7 unchanged. Spillway window 255 → 767; target range / max length 64 (region zero) / 192 (scaled regions).
- **Preview** 512×512 stride 4 → 1536×1536 stride 12: same 16,384 samples, same SVG path count and menu-render cost, 3× coarser per pixel. Menu note updated to 1536 × 1536.
- **Deliberately unscaled:** `NODE_GUARANTEE_RADIUS` 160, spawn radius 96, `climateScale` 512, relief blend 160/224, `HEIGHT_MAX`, chunk size, `loadRadius` 2, region-memo cap 16, travel `regionTiles` 16, `worldgen.json` bands/chances — region zero is preserved, so scaling them would move the starter experience away from the unchanged starter features.
- **No perf loss argument.** Chunk streaming is unchanged (cost is per loaded chunk, load radius unchanged). Steady-state chunk-gen cost is unchanged (interleaved base/after probe: origin and span grids identical). First-visit region cost regressed (median ~3.5 → ~9.5 ms, mean ~10 → ~18 ms, max ~75 ms, n=24×2) from the scaled siting scan, but it is paid once per memoised region and regions are 3× wider, so per-distance cost falls. `pnpm bench` ms under load are not comparable (the unmodified base tree fails identically under load; re-run in a quiet window).
- **World compat.** Old saves: region zero (±768 tiles) generates byte-identically; newly generated chunks outside region zero will differ from pre-423 (different region derivation). Already-persisted chunks are untouched. `CHUNK_VERSION` unchanged (no format change).
- **Honest cuts.** Guaranteed-feature density outside region zero drops 9× per tile (one feature set per 1536² region). Preview first open sites up to 4 neighbouring regions (rotated footprint reaches ±1086 tiles). Boot-drain over-2 ms % not re-measured.

## ADR-421: Tier-1 paddle boats — raft, canoe, rowboat (SurVivaZ)

New vehicle class `boat` (defs 40–42, append-only): raft (2 seats, 2.2 tiles/s, 24 slots / 600 kg, stamina 0.6/s), canoe (2 seats, 4.2 tiles/s, 8 slots / 120 kg, stamina 1.0/s), rowboat (4 seats, 3.2 tiles/s, 16 slots / 300 kg, stamina 1.2/s). Paddling, not fuel: `fuel: null` + `stamina` (bicycle-style drain, 35% throttle when exhausted); `validateVehicleDefs` carves boats out of the motor-fuel rule and rejects a boat with fuel or without stamina. No hitches: nothing tows a boat, no boat tows anything.

Water movement: boats move ONLY on water (`boatWaterMul`: deep 1.0, shallow 0.55, land 0; never the road bonus). `boatPoseBlocked` requires every footprint point of the destination pose to be water, plus the usual terrain/edge/solid blockers with swim tiles passable — a boat driven at the shore beaches and stops, never clips onto land. Boat kits deploy on water only (`validateDeploy` returns `not_water` on land; shallow counts) and craft at the dock (ADR-420): raft 45s, canoe 60s, rowboat 90s. No `VehicleState` (no engine/lights; `validateVehicleToggle` returns `no_controls`); render excludes boats from headlights and cabin crop; the client HUD hides the engine/lights chip for boats. Dismount reuses the ADR-371 safe-tile search, which prefers land/shallow over deep water. No sinking in this slice; a boat at rest on water stays afloat.

AI: `fillVehicleSensors` sees boats and `pickRide` offers one through the generic `drive` behaviour. `decideCrossing` gains a sixth decision, `"boat"` (optional `{ boatAvailable }`): a fit on-foot bot takes the boat over a deep run of any length instead of swimming; the fitness floors still apply, and mounted or cold bots never take it. Default calls keep the old five-way decision exactly.

Art: runtime-painted in `apps/client/src/task421-art.ts` + `pack/task421` (one `veh_art_<id>` atlas per boat, 4 cols x 6 rows, 2 rows per paddle phase; idle = mid-stroke frame 8, `row` cycles [0, 8, 16]); kit icons painted at runtime. The ADR-420 dock/shipyard art wiring (pack/task420 fragment + view.ts hook) landed in this slice too. Guide facts added for the three boats (count, canoe speed, raft storage slots scaled via `storageCapacity`, rowboat seats) in the Mounts and vehicles section.

Validation: 18 new tests (`adr421_boats_tier1`, `adr421_boats_art`, `adr421_boats_registry`); related suites green (154 gameplay + 22 render/assets). Typecheck clean with pinned TS 5.9.3 (client shows only the 2 known pre-existing oxipng TS2307 errors). Schema hash moved to `0xd75236d9` (new defs change `VEHICLE_DEFS_HASH`; old clients/servers refuse to connect — same-deploy only). Not verified on a real phone/Xbox: art is verified numerically, not visually. Honest cuts: the `row` phase cycle is declared but the renderer still shows one frame per direction (no VAnim on vehicle bodies); `travel.ts` does not yet pass `boatAvailable` to the crossing decision, so a travelling bot won't seek out a boat; a boat nosed at the shore cannot slide parallel to it (reverse out instead).

## ADR-425: Map size display in the map-generation window

Context: The "New world" screen showed a seeded terrain preview with only a hardcoded "1536 × 1536 tiles" note, so players could not tell how big the pictured region was compared to the world they spawn into, or whether 1536 tiles was a map border.

Decision: The `.preview-note` under the preview is built from the same constants worldgen uses, never hardcoded prose numbers: `PREVIEW.width × PREVIEW.stride` tiles across (128 × 12 = 1536, exactly one `REGION_SIZE` starter region) and a human-readable walk-across time of `REGION_SIZE / movement.walkSpeed` (1536 tiles at 2.9 tiles/s ≈ 9 minutes). The note states the preview is one region and the world streams on beyond it with no fixed edge, so the number is not misread as a map border. It is seed-independent by construction (the extent cannot vary per seed).

No metres-per-tile conversion is shown: no such constant exists anywhere in the game (the only related numbers are render-scale figures — `PX_PER_M` and "45.25 px per tile" — which are not a world truth), so inventing a distance in metres would have been false precision. If a real tile-size constant is ever defined, the walk time can be joined/replaced by it.

Consequences: A drift test (`apps/client/test/adr425_map_size_display.test.ts`) imports `PREVIEW` / `REGION_SIZE` / `defaultDefs()` and fails if the note and worldgen ever disagree; it also guards the debounced preview draw path. Menu strings stay literals (locale files hold no menu strings). Honest cut: the note is longer than the old one (~150 chars vs ~100) and will wrap to more lines on a narrow phone panel — kept in the single existing `.preview-note` element with no layout change.

## ADR-424: Very large lakes with islands, seeded (scaled regions only)

Each non-zero region gets one great lake (radius 55–80, distance 190–270 from the region centre, max extent 350) on a diagonal, with ≥1 island guaranteed inside it (main island r 6–12, plus 0–2 islets r 5–8) and ≥4 tiles of water ringing every island, so no island is a peninsula. Island ground is sand beach (tile 2, height 1) around grass (tile 3, height 2): buildable land, reachable by boat (shallow band hugs the shore, deep water 3 tiles out). Precedence: elevatedLake > island > greatLake > lake > pond > river. Diagonal placement is load-bearing: the fourth cardinal collides with ADR-386 elevated-lake siting relocation (a relocated disc swallows islands, and rejecting those candidates cut far-region siting from ~92% to ~72%); at 45° the discs are geometrically disjoint (~166 tiles closest approach vs 122 radii+rim), so siting is untouched. Region zero has no great lake — the ADR-255/423 starter layout and spawn are byte-identical. Survey gains `greatLakes`/`islands` counts and `forced.greatLake`. Guide text added (prose only — lake/island sizes are seeded ranges, not single constants). Honest cuts: the menu preview covers region zero only, so a player cannot see a great lake in the map-gen window (extending the preview to neighbouring regions is a follow-up); no AI crossing/island-waypoint integration (`water_crossing.ts`/`travel.ts` untouched — AI humans cannot yet path to islands); island look verified numerically only, no GL in the VM.

## ADR-422: Tier-2 motorboats — motorboat, pontoon, speedboat (SurVivaZ)

Three fuelled boats (defs 43–45, class `boat`): motorboat 7.5 tiles/s, 4 seats, 12 slots/200 kg, gasoline 40 L @ 0.12 L/s; pontoon 5.0 tiles/s, 8 seats, 36 slots/1500 kg (boat class max), diesel 90 L @ 0.10 L/s; speedboat 11.0 tiles/s, 2 seats, 4 slots/60 kg, gasoline 45 L @ 0.28 L/s. A boat is exactly one of motor (fuel, no stamina) or paddle (stamina, no fuel). Motorboats get `VehicleState` (engine + headlights, key required), burn fuel in the existing `stepPowered` path (1.3× on boost), and deploy at 10% fuel on water only. Kits craft at the shipyard with smithing gates (motorboat 180 s/smithing 2, pontoon 300 s/smithing 3, speedboat 240 s/smithing 3), each consuming an engine part. No shallow-water stall — same deep 1× / shallow 0.55× / land 0× water path; an empty tank cuts thrust and the boat coasts to a stop. `engine_small/medium/large/diesel` repair items list `boat` (garage revival of wrecks); `repair_kit` still covers the field. Bots see real fuel fractions, `pickRide` offers fueled motorboats, `vehicle_service` refuels below 0.25. Art: same runtime painter as ADR-421 (`task421-art.ts` + `pack/task422`), throttle phases with `wake` cycle, outboard + prop wash, twin-hull pontoon with canopy. World schema hash `0xd75236d9` → `0x1e514b1a` (defs only, no new component). Guide facts added for the three motorboats (speeds, pontoon storage via `storageCapacity`, motorboat fuel capacity). Honest cuts: art verified numerically only — no GL in the VM, so the user is the final visual check, especially the pontoon canopy and the speedboat at game scale; no sinking, no persistent wakes, no engine sound; motorboat headlight cones render but were not visually checked. The `vehicle_craft.test.ts` cost-scaling check still passes but only just — a future cheap size-m or expensive size-l kit could trip it.

## ADR-426: Full-gate fix-ups for ADR-419–425 (SurVivaZ)

The slice gates ran only their own suites; the first full gate (4,760 passed / 8 failed / 6 skipped) caught six regressions the slices missed. Two failures were the known pre-existing ones (pack.test.ts KEYS.md absent from the sparse checkout; persist bench wall-clock flake). The other six are fixed here, with no slice behaviour changed except the dock/shipyard skill gate, which the codebase's own ADR-221 rule requires:

- **adr125 (boats vs the motor-vehicle speed rule).** The test looped every non-bicycle, non-trailer, non-drawn vehicle and required 2.5–6× sprint; a raft is 0.47× sprint and even the speedboat (11.0 tiles/s) is only ~2.4×. Boats are watercraft, not land motor vehicles: the loop now excludes class `boat`, and a new pin requires every boat to beat swim speed instead.
- **adr221 (dock/shipyard unlock nodes).** Dock and Shipyard are station pieces, so ADR-221 requires exactly one unlock node each. Added `dock_craft` (crafting branch, tier 4, x 920 y 440, cost 1, requires `workbench_craft`, icon `skill_tinkerer`) and `shipyard_craft` (tier 5, x 920 y 550, cost 2, requires `anvil_craft`, icon `skill_grease_monkey`) to `skills.json` (140 → 142 nodes; the skill audit's node-count pin moves 140 → 142 with it). No planner change: a locked piece goal already holds on the planner's `locked` field until `skill_pick` learns it, and unlock nodes already get the ×4 `pickSkillNode` boost. Fresh players now get `BuildFail.SkillLocked` placing a dock/shipyard until they learn the node (pinned in `adr426_gate_fixups.test.ts`); `spawnLearned` test players are unaffected. The ADR-420 DECISIONS entry and test, which had claimed "no dedicated skill node", are corrected.
- **adr398 (roof-tail pin).** The "last 3 pieces are the roof trio" pin went stale when dock/shipyard appended after them; it now checks `slice(-5, -2)`.
- **station_crafting / ADR-136 (station tags).** The known-station list was a hardcoded `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`; dock (6) and shipyard (7) were untagged. The list is now derived from `STATION_NAMES`, so a future station cannot go untagged.
- **adr229 (build-window icons).** Dock/shipyard had no atlas + stylesheet build icons. Static entries were added pointing at `items_build` frames 302/303 — the last two free cells of the 16×19 sheet (302 used, 2 free) — with CSS `--cz-ipos` 93.33% 100% / 100% 100%, mirroring the Apiary (286) and store (297–301) pattern. The runtime painter `installTask420MenuIcons` already overrides those keys with painted data URLs, so the tiles render from the painted art, not the blank binary cells.
- **adr387 (guide-icon pin).** The panel count pin (65) missed the two new dock/shipyard cost rows, which carry icons; now 67.
- **Second gate (4,766 passed / 6 failed): three more pins the first gate's slice fixes moved.** `decor.test.ts` counts `"icon":` occurrences in skills.json (159 → 161 for the two new nodes; both reuse existing icons, so the existence check still passes). `pack.test.ts` "lock is up to date" failed because the two new manifest sprites need the assets pack lock regenerated (`write-lock-pack.ts` — appends `build_dock: 6324`, `build_shipyard: 6325` and nothing else). The world schema hash moved `0x1e514b1a` → `0x2ec1a43d`, pinned in `adr360_driver_seat` + `adr371_vehicle_passengers`: the delta is the `gameplay.skills` salt only (skills.json is the sole hash input ADR-426 changed — no component, def, or vehicle changed). It is save-safe: disk saves migrate per component, `Progression.nodes` is an unchanged `u32[8]` bitfield, and the two nodes append at the end, so old saves' node bits keep their meaning; the world-hash check only gates the net snapshot path, where client and server always run the same version.

## ADR-427: Serve the new boat/dock art fragments to the client (SurVivaZ)

CI failed on the ramps/boats batch push (run 44301248441, `pnpm check`): `adr248_server_manifest_parity` failed because the server's merged manifest had fragments `task420`, `task421`, `task422` that the client's served manifest index did not. Root cause: ADR-420/421/422 added the fragments to `packages/assets/src/manifest-index.ts` (so the server merges them) but never added them to the art-serving allowlist in `apps/client/vite.config.ts` (MOUNTS `pack/` regex), which lists every task fragment explicitly (`task34|task256|task355|task361|task410`). The client therefore never served or fetched the new fragment manifests — the parity test caught it, and without the fix the built site would also have shipped without the Dock/Shipyard and boat art fragments (`planArt` uses the same mounts). Fix: add `task420|task421|task422` to the regex. Verified locally with the parity test itself (restored `scripts/oxipng.mjs` from origin/main, content-identical, to let it load): it fails without the fix with exactly the CI diff and passes with it. Why the local gate missed it: the test imports `vite.config.js`, which imports the missing `scripts/oxipng.mjs`, so the file was one of the 7 sparse-checkout load failures locally and never ran.

## ADR-428: Wild crops and fruit trees spawn on the production server (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Players only ever saw berry bushes and one other plant model, even though ADR-349 had
put wild crops and fruit trees into `worldgen.json` and proved it with tests. Two independent
blocks, both in the production path only. (1) `createGameServer` built `new ProceduralGenerator({
seed })` with no `bands`, so the generator fell back to `DEFAULT_BANDS` — the 7 fossil kinds
(fallen_branches, fiber_grass, berry_bush, loose_rocks, tree, boulder, iron_vein). All 40 crops'
wild plants (ids 17–20, 68–94) and all fruit trees (ids 29–62) could never spawn. (2) The chunk
`onLoad` handler dropped any kind outside a 7-entry `NODE_RESOURCES` allowlist — a second block
even if the generator had placed them. The correct wiring already existed and was used only by
tests: `worldgenBands(defs)` + the `defs.resources.has` passthrough in `spawnChunkNodes`. ADR-349
changed only data JSON the production server never read, and its test built the generator the
test-only way — that is why it passed while live stayed broken. This is the live path for both
the client's embedded server (`local.ts` → `createGameServer`) and the dedicated server.

**Decision.** `apps/server/src/game.ts`: the generator is now `new ProceduralGenerator({ seed,
bands: worldgenBands(gameplayDefs(world)) })`, and the `onLoad` handler spawns every node kind
the defs know (`defs.resources.has(n.kind)`), deleting `NODE_RESOURCES`. `stampAbandonedChunk` on
chunk load is preserved in the same handler. `worldgenBands` (`packages/gameplay/src/world.ts`)
now also forwards `temp` / `humidity`: the generator's snow rule reads `baseClimate`, which
defaults a missing band temp to 15°C, so dropping them warmed the rock band 8°C → 15°C and
flipped cold-peak snow tiles (6) back to bare rock (5) — measured 5 flipped tiles in a 47×47
sample grid on seed 1234 before the forward, 0 after. With the forward, the banded generator is
tile/sample/chunk-tile identical to the old default-bands generator (seeds 1234/77/11/99), so
the only live-world change is node kinds. No worldgen.json / band / density change, no region
or lake change, no farming or seed-economy (ADR-247) change.

**Spawn points move (algorithm unchanged).** `computeSpawnPoints` requires a node-free 5×5 patch,
so points shift on every seed tested (same quadrants, still on grass, still clear — pinned by
the new test through the server). `spawn_world.test.ts` now builds its expectation from the
production bands; the old default-bands expectation encoded the pre-428 wiring. `NODE_GUARANTEE_RADIUS`
stays 160; the guarantee now covers the real ~70 kinds instead of 7. Node counts over 25 chunks:
seed 1234: 1279 → 1731 (+35%); seed 21: 750 → 1197 (+60%).

**Other `new ProceduralGenerator({ seed })` sites — no change.** `apps/client/src/main.ts:308`
(menu spawn-point preview) and `packages/gameplay/src/ai/travel.ts:104` (water/depth sampling
via `tileAt` only) and `packages/world/src/preview.ts:18` (map-gen preview, tiles/heights only)
never spawn nodes, and tiles are identical either way, so they need no bands. Two follow-ups
noted, not done: the menu preview in `main.ts:308` still computes spawn points with the
default-bands generator, so it now shows stale points vs the live server; and the comment on
`travel.ts`'s `seededGenerator` ("the same generator the server builds its chunks from") is
now literally true only for tiles. The map-gen preview never showed crops (tiles only), so
there is no crop mismatch there.

**Verification.** New `apps/server/test/adr428_wild_crops_server.test.ts` (2 tests): through
`createGameServer` only — never constructs a generator, with or without bands — counts the
`ResourceNode` entities the server spawns over the 5×5 chunks around the origin on seeds 1234 /
11 / 99 (wild > 0, fruit > 0, distinct kinds > 7, `wild_wheat` / `wild_corn` / `apple_tree`
each present) and pins spawn points one-per-quadrant on grass with a node-free patch. The
density test failed before the fix (`seed 1234 wild plants: expected 0 to be greater than 0`)
and passes after. Neighbours: `spawn_world` 3/3, adr349 8/8, adr247 8/8, adr257 5/5,
`task35_water_resources` 3/3 (27/27); gameplay + world suites 2,386 passed / 3 skipped /
0 failed (242 files passed, 2 skipped); server suite 151 passed / 6 failed — all 6 are
5 s-default-timeout flakes on the loaded VM (adr348, agents/clan/day-clock/world-rules
persist, spawn_world day-length): 4 of the 6 time out on the base commit too, and the other
two pass on re-run in isolation. Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `apps/server` clean;
`packages/gameplay` clean (re-run after the parallel ADR-429/430 slices committed).

**Honest cuts.** Existing (stored) chunks keep their old nodes — ADR-429's top-up covers those;
this slice fixes only newly generated chunks. The live look is still the user's eyes on the
build: art was verified numerically before (ADR-349), not visually.

## ADR-429: Wild-crop top-up for already-generated chunks (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The production server built `new ProceduralGenerator({ seed })` with no bands, so only the 7 fossil resource kinds ever spawned. ADR-428 fixes new chunks by passing `worldgenBands(defs)` — but stored chunks keep their own nodes (`regenerateNodes` returns false when a chunk already contains any `ResourceNode` / `NodeRegrow`, ADR-134) and regrowth is same-kind only, so chunks the player already explored near spawn would stay crop-less forever. The user playtests their existing world, so without this slice they would walk around spawn and still see nothing.

**Decision.** A deterministic, idempotent top-up, one node per missing kind per chunk. `computeWildCropTopUp(world, chunk, stored, desired)` (`packages/gameplay/src/wildCropTopUp.ts`, pure — it spawns nothing): the desired set is what the chunk WOULD have under the correct bands (`generator.nodesInChunk`, same seed); a wild-crop / fruit-tree kind (the ADR-349 set: every `wild_*` species + `flax_patch` / `cotton_bush` / `herb_patch`, and the five fruit trees) missing from the chunk's stored nodes gets its first desired placement that passes — a tile with no stored node / stump, whose STORED tile is land (void / water / shallows skipped: stored terrain may have been edited since generation, and the top-up never changes terrain), clear of the ADR-134 protections (no structures within `clearStructures`, no roads within `clearRoads`, no living players within `clearPlayers`, same radii as regrowth; node clearance is the same-tile rule, matching the generator), and outside every claim — both the core `ClaimRegistry` claim and a Claim Flag privilege zone (`zonesNear`, ADR-315). A kind counts as present when any stored `ResourceNode` / `NodeRegrow` of that kind is in the chunk, including a depleted stump (it regrows that kind itself). Other kinds the old bands lacked (clay, salt, veins, …) stay missing — a deliberate limit of this slice, not an oversight. `WorldPersistence` gains a `topUpNodes(world, chunk, entities)` option, called in `fromRecord` only for stored chunks whose nodes are NOT regenerated; the returned placements flow through the existing `onLoad` spawn path and persist exactly like generated nodes. The hook also marks the chunk dirty when it returns placements: top-up nodes spawn in `onLoad` (postSim, after `persist.track`), so their change bits are cleared before `track()` ever sees them, and without the dirty mark the first top-up would never be saved. Fresh and regenerated chunks never call the hook. Measured: mean **16.1 nodes added per chunk** over 48 chunks (6 seeds × 8 chunks, min 1, max 24; cap 30 = one per top-up kind). No worldgen.json / band / density change, no region or lake change, no farming or seed-economy change.

**Wiring (for the coordinator — one small commit in `apps/server/src/game.ts`, NOT in this slice).** In the `WorldPersistence` constructor options, next to `regenerateNodes`, add `topUpNodes: (w, chunk, ents) => computeWildCropTopUp(w, chunk, ents, generator.nodesInChunk(chunk.cx, chunk.cy))` (import `computeWildCropTopUp` from `@engine/gameplay`; `generator` is the `ProceduralGenerator` already constructed in `createGameServer`, which ADR-428 gives the correct bands). Precondition: ADR-428's `chunks.onLoad` handler must spawn every kind in `defs.resources`, not just the 7 `NODE_RESOURCES` entries — otherwise the top-up placements (like all new-band kinds) are skipped at spawn. The server already streams chunks before `persist.track`, so the spawned nodes also join membership in the same tick; the dirty mark above is belt-and-braces for any other ordering.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr429_wild_crop_topup.test.ts` (5 tests) + `packages/persist/test/adr429_wild_crop_topup.test.ts` (1 test, full path: old-band world saves a chunk → post-fix world loads it and gains wild crops through `onLoad` → re-save → reload adds nothing; a never-saved chunk takes the generator path and the hook is never called for it). All 6 pass; the unit tests failed before the implementation (missing module). Neighbour suites: gameplay + world + persist per the slice report. Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` and `packages/persist` clean.

**Honest cuts.** The top-up only sees loaded chunks: a structure in an unloaded neighbouring chunk (within 6 tiles of the border) is invisible to the clearance check — the same limitation `findRegrowSpot` already has, not a regression. ADR-348 temporary safe-spawn points are not checked (they are transient spawn protection, not territory); claims and privilege zones are. Art verified numerically, not visually — no GL in the VM; the user's eyes on the live build are the real check that crops now appear around spawn.

## ADR-430: AI humans harvest wild plants; wild plants and fruit trees render-pinned (SurVivaZ)

ADR-428 (parallel slice) fixes the spawn side — the production server never passed `worldgenBands` to the generator, so wild crops / fruit trees never spawned at all. Once they spawn, two things also had to hold; this slice covers both.

**AI — one real gap, fixed.** General gather already worked generically: `autonomy.ts` picks remembered `kind: "node"` items with `ResourceNode.amount > 0` and matches `def.yields` against needs, and `ai/travel.ts` scans `ResourceNode` entities — pinned here, not changed (a hired Gather worker needing wheat picks the `wild_wheat` node over closer non-wheat nodes, and an unhired bot picks a wild food plant it can see). The farm-job path did not: `computeFarmSensor` (`ai/hire_behaviors.ts`) only harvested nodes whose key is in `FARMING.plantables.map(p => p.becomes)` (farmed `crop_*` / bush / tree nodes), so hired farm workers — and unhired gardeners, who share the sensor — walked past every wild plant even after the spawn fix. Fix: the harvestable set is now `becomes` ∪ every plantable's `wild` nodes. Yields are unchanged (ADR-247: a wild node still drops only its own species' seed and produce; farm-harvesting `wild_wheat` yields wheat + `wheat_seeds` only, pinned); the farm path just stops skipping them. `wild_garden` is deliberately NOT a farm target — it belongs to no plantable's `wild` list (a mixed garden, no single species' seed), so general gather stays its path (pinned). No farming-rule change: no till / plant / water behaviour touches wild nodes, and the ADR-385 reachability pick + ban-awareness apply to wild harvests exactly as to farmed ones (same candidate list).

**Render — verified, no behaviour change.** WebGL2 and Canvas2D share one classification (`IsoView.classify` → `defs.resources.get(n.kind)?.spriteKey` → `this.rs(key)` = `resolveSprite` with `has = registry.ids.sprites.tryId(k) !== undefined`). New `apps/client/test/adr430_wild_render.test.ts` replays that exact path headlessly on the real merged registry (`loadMergedPackManifest`, the same MANIFEST_INDEX the client boots from): every wild-plant kind (each plantable's `wild` nodes, `wild_garden`, every `becomes` bush/tree) resolves through `resolveSprite` to a real sprite id — no kind failed, so no resolution fix was needed and no art was invented. The 24 ADR-349 wild plants draw with their farmed `crop_*` art on the `stream`-residency `nature_crops` atlas (placeholder `placeholder_sprout`); the registry contains the atlas and `sourcesFromManifest` (the exact boot call) includes it. That streamed page-in is the one gap this test can only pin, not prove: WebGL2 shows `placeholder_sprout` until the page loads and Canvas2D shows nothing, so the user's eyes on the live build are the check that a wild plant actually appears. Fruit trees resolve on resident `nature_trees` (no page-in gap), classify `tall` (key ends `_tree` → tall scale + occluder + sway, on both renderers), and their idle frame differs from the depleted frame (fruit is in the idle art). No fruit overlay / scale bump is added here — that is the ADR-349 follow-up, still out of scope.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr430_wild_harvest.test.ts` (7 tests) + `apps/client/test/adr430_wild_render.test.ts` (3 tests). The three farm tests failed before the fix (wild node skipped) and pass after; the general-gather tests passed before and after. Neighbour suites: gameplay farm / AI / seed suites (adr349, adr385, adr259, task28 hay + relocation, adr247, adr257) 64/64; full gameplay gate 2,226 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed (217 files passed, 2 skipped — the `skipIf(!PERF)` benches); render + assets 874 passed / 1 failed (the known pre-existing `pack.test.ts` KEYS.md failure, sparse-checkout only) / 2 skipped; client view/render neighbours (adr430, adr421 registry, task355, adr319, adr410, view_daylight) 22/22 + `adr248_server_manifest_parity` 1/1. Typecheck with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` and `apps/client` clean (the client needed `scripts/oxipng.mjs` + its companion `scripts/oxipng.d.mts` restored from origin/main, content-identical, to load — both match origin, so neither appears in the diff; the files were deleted mid-gate by another worker sharing the tree and restored again before the parity run).

## ADR-431: Bots can claim bases and find berries in a crop-scattered world (SurVivaZ)

ADR-428's spawn fix exposed latent couplings to the old 7-kind world, found by the coordinator's own gate: the full suite went 4,800 passed / 7 failed, and the 5 non-known failures (ADR-252 base/bed/sleep x3, ADR-203 campfire x1, ADR-385 re-target x1) all passed on base `508dfb81` and all failed with ADR-428 alone - bisected slice by slice (ADR-430 alone: ADR-252 8/8). Five mechanisms, fixed in turn; every fix below was probed live (seed 11, ADR-252/ADR-203 fixtures) before it was kept.

**Berries - the dye / Claim Flag chain starved.** A bot builds nothing before planting a Claim Flag, and the flag costs 10 wood + 10 stone + 2 dye; dye is crafted 3 berries -> 1 dye, and the *only* berries source is `berry_bush`.
