Under `DEFAULT_BANDS` the grass band was 3 kinds at 0.03/tile, so berry bushes were 1-in-3 grass nodes (0.01/tile) and a bot always had one in perception range. ADR-349's band has 70 grass kinds at 0.055/tile with `berry_bush` x1, so it diluted to 1-in-70 (0.00079/tile, ~13x sparser). Probed live: the bot's plan sat at `goal=campfire, leaves=[berries]` for the whole 5,200-tick run, wandering between non-berry nodes, never building a single piece. Fix (data only, the sanctioned tuning knob): `berry_bush` is listed 14 times in the grass band - the same duplicate-weight pattern ADR-349 already uses (starters x3, most crops x2) - restoring density to ~0.0093/tile, the pre-ADR-428 level. No recipe, seed-economy, or farming change: dye still costs 3 berries, the flag still costs 2 dye, and the other fruit bushes still yield only their own fruit (they never yielded `berries`).

**Base sites - the node-free-yard veto.** `pickBaseSite` rejected any candidate with a `ResourceNode` anywhere in its 9x8 yard rect. At 0.055 nodes/tile that rect is node-free ~2% of the time, and the 24 deterministic candidates share one salt, so a bot could never claim a site at all (ADR-385's bot never got a home to travel from). But nodes block neither placement (`validatePlacement` has no node check) nor movement (`movementBlocked` checks terrain / edges / solid pieces only), and placing a piece never removes a node - the veto was stricter than the player path for no mechanical reason. Fix: a node vetoes only the 2x2 foundation footprint (`queryRect(bx, by, bx + 2, by + 2)`); `BuildPiece` still vetoes the whole yard. The hut itself never sits on a plant; the yard may hold crops the bot can harvest.

**Stone - the flag's 10 stone, diluted the same way.** Sand `loose_rocks` fell from 100% of sand nodes (0.01/tile) to 1-in-14 (0.002/tile), and rock boulder/rubble from 1-in-2 to 2-in-14 / 1-in-14, so bots expeditioned 100-300 tiles for stone instead of gathering it near home (measured: zero stone nodes within 61x61 of one spawn, 1-6 at the others, and the nearest stone node 100+ tiles out). Fix (data only, same pattern): `loose_rocks` x8 in the sand band (~0.011/tile, the base level), `boulder` x6 + `rubble_pile` x3 in the rock band (~0.022/tile on rock, the base level). Ore veins (copper/tin/iron/coal) are diluted the same way by the 14-kind rock band and are NOT re-weighted here - a follow-up, since no gate test needs them yet.

**Garden outranking gather.** The unhired-gardener `garden` behaviour scored 0.98 against gather's 0.75, so a bot stood on its farm target forever instead of gathering the berries its plan needed. Its comment said it "never outranks the ladder" and "only fills idle gaps", but `noteTripWanted` only sets `tripWanted` for an *unknown* wanted node - a known wanted berry bush did not suppress it. Fix: the garden `plot` consideration also requires `!c.world.gatherNode?.wanted`.

**Farm target shadowed by a nearer tool-locked node.** `farmRun` pushed a bare `"gather"` action, which the server resolves to the *nearest* node in 2.25 tiles regardless of the bot's target. An `animal_carcass` (knife tier 1) 0.41 tiles away shadowed the herb patch 1.07 tiles away: WrongTool 4,579 times in one probe run, zero successful gathers, and the carcass never depletes so it shadowed forever. Fix: `farmRun` harvests with a targeted `GatherCmd` on `o.commands` (the only path that reaches the server for bots; action strings never do), throttled to one per 20 ticks, plus a 240-tick ban escape mirroring `gatherRun`.

**Craft-queue jam on a full pack, and the pack guard.** Gathering filled all 16 pack slots with one stack of each wild species; the dye output then had nowhere to go, the craft-queue head paused on `outputFits`, and `instantChores` re-pushed the same dye job every 100 ticks until all 4 queue slots held identical dye jobs (`queue_full`, 24 berries consumed). Two fixes: (a) `instantChores` never queues a second job for the same craft while a `craftPend` for that output is pending (retry allowed after it expires); (b) the gather sensor counts *every* yield that would take a new pack slot - a willow yields wood (already carried) plus a new sapling and bark, two new slots per tree - and scores such a node worse (5 tiles per new slot, so the bot prefers a tree whose yields stack), skipping it outright only when the pack is literally full *and* nothing it yields stacks (a stone node whose secondary flint is new still gives the stacking stone). A hard reserve was tried first and reverted: it blocked the very rubble_pile the bot needed for stone, and a strict "no opportunistic species while the plan is unmet" rule broke ADR-252 by removing the local-gather fallback (bots expeditioned 200 tiles for berries). The seed-drop escape in the junk rule frees a slot when the pack is full and the plan is blocked: it drops one seed (it regrows; `plan.keep` is never dropped), and it also fires when the plan's craft step output itself is unheld - the torch's inputs were all held, so no leaf was unmet, yet the torch output had nowhere to go.

**Earthworks blocked by a plant on the tile.** `editTerrain` refuses a tile with a `ResourceNode` (`TerrainFail.Occupied`), so a wild plant on a quarry or pad cell abandoned the whole earthworks (probed: an `orange_tree` - a fruit tree that only spawns since ADR-428 - plus a `dry_shrub` on the pad's quarry cells left 6 soil against 8 needed, and the plan abandoned). Fix: a new `clear` plan step - `nextTerrainWork` returns it for the blocking node, the planner passes it through, and `base_work` walks to the node and harvests it with a targeted `GatherCmd` (the right tool is equipped via `view.equipSlot`, the same path `instantChores` uses), with a 240-tick ban escape that abandons the earthworks instead of stalling. The node regrows in place, so the dig follows at once; the same step covers the pit and hired-worker earthworks.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr431_bot_base_in_crop_world.test.ts` (3 tests): berry-bush share of spawned nodes over 10x10 chunks on three seeds is >= 5% (fails at x1, ~1-2%); stone nodes within 30 tiles of the four ADR-203 starter spawns total >= 10 (seed 11); `pickBaseSite` finds a site in a yard scattered with nodes where the old yard-wide rule rejects every candidate, and the found site's 2x2 footprint is node-free. Integration proof is the three previously failing suites, each run alone by the coordinator: `adr252_ai_humans_live` 8/8, `adr203_ai_human_autonomy` 3/3, `adr385_unreachable_retarget` 5/5. Full gate re-run by the coordinator: 4,790 passed / 4 failed / 6 skipped (4,800 tests, 722 files, 1,882.97 s). The 4 failures are the known pre-existing/flaky ones only - `pack.test.ts` (KEYS.md absent from the sparse checkout), persist `bench.test.ts`, `agents_persist.test.ts`, and `spawn_world.test.ts` (all three timeout/bench flakes pass alone: bench 1/1, agents_persist 1/1, spawn_world 3/3). ADR-349 passes in the gate at the 340 floor, and ADR-252/203/385 have no regressions.

**ADR-349 wild floor rebalanced (same ADR, follow-up).** The berry x14 fix necessarily diluted the other wild plants: the grass band went 70 -> 83 entries, wild share 66% -> 55%, and ADR-349's seed-7 wild count fell 419 -> 353, below its 380 floor. Three ways to restore it were tried and all rejected on evidence: (a) raising grass `nodeChance` 0.055 -> 0.06 or 0.065 passed ADR-349 but broke ADR-252 (3/8 at 0.065, and 7/8 at 0.06 - the base test); (b) bumping 12 wild crops x2 -> x3 in the grass band also broke ADR-252 (3/8, twice in a row) - more wild plants mean more opportunistic gathering and the bots miss the 5,200-tick ladder budget; (c) adding `orange_tree` x2 to the forest band (to cover seed 4242's zero) broke ADR-203's campfire test (2/3, twice) - the forest band going 27 -> 29 entries was enough to push the bot past the night deadline. All three were reverted; the worldgen data is exactly as committed above. The resolution is a calibration change, not a spawn change: ADR-349's wild floor is 380 -> 340, with a comment in the test recording why (berry x14 trades ~7% of the other wild plants' count for berry density; worst seed 353, every kind still appears, and 340 still catches a wild-crop spawn break). The lesson for future band tuning: the bot suites are sensitive to *total node density*, not just composition - any density increase, by nodeChance or by entry count, has to be re-proven against ADR-252 and ADR-203, which have tight tick budgets.

## ADR-435: Harden the abandoned-structure terrain gate — resumed stamps and AI rebuilds (SurVivaZ)

ADR-384 requires abandoned-structure footprints to sit on tiles of a SINGLE level (`siteTerrainOk`, `packages/gameplay/src/building/abandoned.ts:754-756`) and skips a straddling site — never relocates, never levels terrain. Two loopholes still let a straddling structure be created, both closed here. ADR-384's skip-not-relocate rule is unchanged, as are `SITE_CHANCE` (0.25), the terrain edit bounds (TERRAIN minLevel −300 / maxLevel +326), worldgen relief, and the seed economy; near-spawn terrain stays byte-identical.

**Loophole 1 — resumed partial stamps bypassed the gate.** `stampAbandonedSite` gated only fresh stamps (`if (!resumed && !siteTerrainOk(...))`). A stamp cut off mid-way by a restart resumed in place as "grandfathered" and completed even if the terrain under it had changed since — the only way terrain changes under a standing partial stamp is a post-stamp shovel dig/raise, plus partial stamps left over from the ADR-382→384 window, when a 1–2 level spread was still allowed. Probed before the fix: a Manor stamped flat, pumped 20 pieces, queue forgotten (restart), terrain tilted one level under the footprint (x ≥ 10), re-stamp — it completed with a marker, a straddling structure. Why the bypass existed, and why removing it is safe: the bypass's stated fear was tearing down a site that was already standing — but a COMPLETE grandfathered site never reaches the resume at all, because `siteExistsAt` returns first (pinned by the ADR-384 test "chunk reload does not add a second site": a complete site under tilted ground re-stamps skipped, pieces untouched). Only a marker-less partial stamp reaches the resume, and for that the least-breaking close is to re-check the gate on resume and skip the REMAINDER, leaving the already-placed pieces standing unmarked — the same outcome as the existing contested-footprint abort (foreign/owned piece in the footprint). Nothing is torn down, no marker is created, no queue entry is left, and the chunk-load path just re-checks cheaply on each reload. Fix: the gate in `stampAbandonedSite` is now unconditional (`if (!siteTerrainOk(...)) return skipped`, resumed or not).

**Loophole 2 — AI claim-rebuild replayed the plan with no gate.** `planClaimRuin` (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/claim_build.ts`) rebuilds missing pieces from the replayed plan (`ruinLayout` → `planAbandonedSite` over all 4 rotations) with no terrain check, so a bot rebuilt a straddling ruin crooked. Probed before the fix: a claimed, reclaimed Cottage with one roof piece demolished was offered a rebuild `build` step after the terrain under it was tilted — and the same for the unrecoverable-layout fallback, which rebuilds a 2x2 hut from `BASE_SLOTS` on the same footprint. Fix: the rebuild stage is gated with `siteTerrainOk(world, ox, oy, w, h)` — when the footprint straddles and pieces are missing, the plan returns stage `rebuild` with no step and `blocked: ["terrain-straddle"]`. Only the rebuild is gated, deliberately: flag / reclaim / repair place no new pieces, so a standing grandfathered ruin can still be claimed and kept up on straddling ground — the ruin stays a ruin, unrebuilt. Returning blocked (not done) keeps the bot's claim target, and the check re-runs each sense tick, so a later shovel levelling of the footprint re-opens the rebuild. The gate reads live terrain, so the 20-tick `ruinLayout` cache cannot stale it.

**Other callers checked.** Every production caller of `planAbandonedSite` / `stampAbandonedSite` was searched: `stampAbandonedSite` is reached only via `stampAbandonedChunk` (chunk load, `apps/server/src/game.ts` `onLoad`) and directly in tests — both funnel through the now-unconditional gate. `planAbandonedSite` is called in production only by `stampAbandonedSite` (gated) and by `computeRuinLayout` in `claim_build.ts`, which only MATCHES live pieces (read-only); its one placement consumer is `planClaimRuin`'s rebuild stage, now gated. No other ungated replay exists. Player placement keeps its own maxSlope tolerance (`building/place.ts`) — only abandoned sites are strict, as in ADR-384.

**Out of scope, noted.** Post-stamp shovel digs under a STANDING, complete building can still create a straddle (a player action after generation); that is covered by the render-side wall/roof-gap fix (ADR-433 slice, `apps/client/src/view.ts`), not here — generation stamping is this slice's scope only.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr435_straddle_gate_hardening.test.ts` (5 tests): the 3 loophole tests failed before the fix (resumed stamp completed the straddling Manor; rebuild and fallback-hut both emitted a `build` step on tilted ground) and all 5 pass after, with the 2 flat-ground controls (resume completes identically; level footprint rebuilds normally) passing before and after — no density regression, `SITE_CHANCE` untouched at 0.25 and the ADR-384 density test still green. Neighbour suites: abandoned/claim/roof/stairs 17 files 165/165 (`adr300`, `adr301`, `adr310`, `adr311`, `adr315`, `adr337`, `adr337_claim_wiring`, `adr340`, `adr341`, `adr372`, `adr373`, `adr382`, `adr384`, `adr385`, `adr398`, `adr412`, `stall_claims`); adr203 canary (`apps/client/test/adr203_ai_human_autonomy.test.ts`) 3/3, also green inside the full client run. Typecheck clean with pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 (`packages/gameplay`, `tsc -p tsconfig.json`). Full gate, run in slices (a single `vitest run` was SIGTERM'd twice — once by a VM restart, once at ~18 min): gameplay 220 files, 2,236 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed; world + persist + net + core + input + testkit + render + assets + server 291 files, 1,533 passed / 2 skipped / 7 failed; client 213 files, 1,041 passed / 1 skipped / 2 failed — 4,810 passed / 6 skipped / 9 failed over 724 files. All 9 failures are pre-existing, not this slice: `pack.test.ts` (KEYS.md absent from the sparse checkout, known since ADR-430/431), persist `bench.test.ts` (autosave timing, known), and 7 wall-clock timeouts (5s, plus `spawn_world` 180s) in server SQLite / client IndexedDB persistence and Xbox-budget tests (`agents_persist` x2, `day_clock_persist`, `world_rules_roads`, `adr348_guest_safe_zone`, `spawn_world`, `adr214_vfx`) — the 5 server files and the 2 client files were each re-run on the stashed base (no ADR-435 code) and fail identically, so the timeouts are the slow shared VM, not this change. The 7 client files that failed to LOAD (`adr248`, `adr332`, `adr333`, `adr391`, `adr392`, `adr393`, `adr395`) only needed `scripts/oxipng.mjs` + `scripts/oxipng.d.mts` restored from origin/main (content-identical, no diff); on re-run 6 pass — including `adr248_server_manifest_parity` — and `adr395_dist` skips (needs a dist build).

**Honest cuts.** A skipped resumed stamp leaves a permanent half-ruin: the placed pieces stand forever with no marker, so the site can never complete, be claimed, or be repaired — each chunk reload re-checks and skips again (cheap: match + gate, ~0.1 ms). That is the price of never completing a straddling structure, and it matches the pre-existing contested-footprint abort; only a shovel levelling of the footprint plus a manual re-stamp could ever revive it, and no such revive path exists today. The rebuild gate likewise leaves a claimed straddling ruin permanently unrebuilt (repaired, but never completed) until the player levels the ground. Art verified numerically, not visually — no GL in the VM; the user's eyes on the live build are the real check.

## ADR-432: Wall/roof gap — failing reproduction tests (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause (established by two independent investigations + coordinator spot-check; this slice encodes it, it does not re-litigate it).** In `apps/client/src/view.ts`, `pieceBoundaryGroundZ` (lines 162-175) grounds boundary-anchored pieces (edge walls, corner vertices) on the MINIMUM height of all tiles touching the anchor — including the tile OUTSIDE the building. Cell-anchored pieces (roof / floor deck tiles) use `pieceGroundZ` (lines 132-135), a single-tile read of their own tile. So on a flat footprint whose outside neighbour drops one level, the perimeter wall sinks one level while the roof above it does not: the wall top ends 1 level (16 px) below the roof seat — a see-through gap. ADR-412's comment (view.ts:149-156) claims "a lower neighbour only sinks the base … never a floating gap" — true at the bottom, false at the top: the base sinking IS the gap, because the roof does not sink with it. The placement ghost uses the same lift (view.ts:543-546), so it shows the gap faithfully. Constants: levelHeight = 3 (`packages/gameplay/data/tiers.json:13`); 1 terrain level = 16 px; 1 floor = 3 levels = 48 px; `floorToTerrainZ(floor, baseZ) = baseZ + floor*3` (`packages/world/src/iso.ts:14`); walls are 48 px tall; roof / floor sim z = 3 (level 1). The numbers in the screenshot case: flat 5x5 footprint at height 3, outside south row (y=9) and east column (x=9) at height 2 — south-wall top `floorToTerrainZ(0, 2) + 3 = 5` vs roof draw z `floorToTerrainZ(1, 3) = 6`.

**The failing test (tests only — no src change in this slice).** New `apps/client/test/adr432_wall_roof_gap.test.ts` (same one-chunk TileMap harness as the ADR-412 test) asserts the wall-top/roof PAIR, not just grounding values: south wall (6.5, 9) top vs roof over (6.5, 8.5), east wall (9, 6.5) top vs roof over (8.5, 6.5), SE corner vertex (9, 9) top vs roof over (8.5, 8.5) — all three fail today with wall top 5 vs roof 6. Control: the north wall (outside also level 3) has no gap and passes. A straddle variant pins current behaviour (3x3 footprint, west column level 2, east columns level 3, outside matching its column): wall tops meet the roof on both sides and the roof steps 16 px mid-footprint — those pass today and must keep passing, since the fix is about the outside neighbour, not re-levelling a split footprint. The one place a single grounding cannot meet both roofs is the vertex on the step line (5, 7): it meets the west roof (5) and sits 1 level below the east roof (6); that arithmetic is pinned explicitly for the fix slice (ADR-433) to consciously revisit. ADR-412 regression pins are replicated in the same file (raised outside neighbour, level 5, must not lift the wall base; wall top already meets the roof in that geometry) so the fix cannot trade one defect for the other. New `packages/gameplay/test/adr432_wall_roof_gap.test.ts` proves the gap is buildable by players: on the same heights, `tryPlace` of a 5-wide foundation row, a wall along the south edge (Transform (6.5, 9, 0)) and a `roof_flat` at level 1 (Transform (6.5, 8.5, 3)) all return ok — no `BuildFail.Terrain` — and the same gap arithmetic from `TerrainRes.heightAt` differs by exactly 1 level.

**Verification.** `apps/client/test/adr432_wall_roof_gap.test.ts` + `packages/gameplay/test/adr432_wall_roof_gap.test.ts`: 3 failed / 8 passed (11 tests) — the 3 failures are exactly the south wall, east wall and SE vertex, each `expected 5 to be 6`; the other 8 (north control, straddle x2, ADR-412 pins x3, gameplay placement + gap arithmetic x2) pass on base. Both ADR-412 files still pass (10/10). Typecheck with lockfile-pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `packages/gameplay` and `apps/client` clean (the client needed `scripts/oxipng.mjs` + `scripts/oxipng.d.mts` restored from origin/main, content-identical, to load — both match origin, so neither appears in the diff).

**Honest cuts.** The gameplay test pins the gap in sim terms (`heightAt` min vs own tile); it cannot see the renderer, so it will still pass after the render fix lands — the client tests are the ones that flip. The step-line vertex pin may need updating by the fix slice if their grounding choice resolves the vertex the other way (it can meet one roof or the other, never both). No visual check is possible in the VM — the user's eyes on the live build are the real check, as with ADR-412.

## ADR-433: Deck-aware boundary grounding — the wall/roof gap fix (SurVivaZ)

**The defect (ADR-432).** On a flat footprint next to a one-level drop outside, the perimeter wall sank one level while the roof above it did not: wall top 5 vs roof seat 6, a 1-level (16 px) see-through gap. Root cause: `pieceBoundaryGroundZ` (`apps/client/src/view.ts`) grounded boundary-anchored pieces on the MINIMUM of all touching tiles (including the outside tile) while cell-anchored roof/floor deck tiles read their own tile only. ADR-412's comment claimed a lower neighbour "only sinks the base … never a floating gap" — true at the bottom, false at the top, because the base sinking IS the gap when a deck sits above.

**Mechanism chosen: deck-aware grounding.** `pieceBoundaryGroundZ` takes an optional sixth argument, a set of deck-tile keys (`deckTileKey(tx, ty, level)`, built by the render loop from the deck pieces it already iterates — see below). Among the tiles touching a boundary anchor, in order: (1) a tile carrying a deck at level+1 — the deck the wall top must meet, roof or floor above — wins, max height among those tiles; (2) else a tile carrying a deck at the wall's own level — the deck it stands on, e.g. walls placed before their roof — wins, max height among those; (3) else the ADR-412 min over all touching tiles. With no `decks` argument the behaviour is exactly ADR-412's min, so every bare call is unchanged. Deck families are `foundation` / `floor` / `roof` (`family` in pieces.json — foundations, floors, all roof forms, including ramp / stilt / triangle variants); walls, doors, furniture, stations and decor never contribute (`deckKeyFor`, pure and unit-pinned). The render loop builds the set in the existing per-frame GPiece pass that already collects shaft-hatch tiles — no extra query, one numeric `Set.add` per deck piece, into a reused `Set` cleared each frame — and `groundBoundaryPiece` passes it, so the fix is derived per frame from live pieces and live tile heights: shovel edits after placement stay correct, nothing is persisted, and generation / placement / worldgen / terrain bounds / the seed economy are untouched. The placement ghost passes the same set (previous frame's — `syncGhost` runs before `render` in main.ts, so a deck placed this frame reaches the ghost next frame; the first frame has an empty set and falls back to min), so the preview shows no gap either. The Canvas2D fallback reads the same lifted `Transform.z` (`packages/render/src/canvas2d.ts` gatherPieces), so this one lift covers WebGL2, Canvas2D/Xbox and the ghost — no second, Canvas2D-only fix was added, and the shared-lift coverage was verified by reading gatherPieces, not assumed.

**Rejected alternative 1 — wall facing / rotation.** Disproved empirically, not just argued: stamped straight walls all carry rot 0 (`packages/gameplay/src/building/abandoned.ts` walls() pushes `rot: 0` for every side), and `slotTransform` (`packages/gameplay/src/building/structure.ts`) maps an Edge slot to facing 0/PI for a North edge and PI/2 for a West edge — so facing encodes only edge orientation, and a house's north and south walls share side North and facing 0 with the inside on opposite sides. Facing cannot identify the inside tile for stamped walls, in any rotation. `PieceSlot` knows the edge side but is sim-local and never replicated, so the client cannot use it either.

**Rejected alternative 2 — max over touching tiles.** Satisfies the roof pair but re-opens ADR-412: a raised outside neighbour (5) would lift the wall base to 5. Pinned against by the ADR-412 replica tests (raised south/east/corners still 2).

**Rejected alternative 3 — min, kept as-is.** Satisfies ADR-412 but is the defect itself (ADR-432's 3 failures).

**The two properties, pinned together.** (a) Raised outside neighbour never lifts a wall base: the decked inside tile wins (ADR-412 replica: raised south/east/SE/NE/SW all still 2, wall tops still meet the roof at 5). (b) Lowered outside neighbour never drops a wall top below the roof above it: the decked inside tile wins (ADR-432 south/east/SE vertex tops now 6 == roof 6). The pin that separates them is the sunk north wall in the ADR-432 file: the SAME anchor and heights give base 0 bare (freestanding, no deck — ADR-412 min, unchanged) and base 2 with the deck set (roofed — stands on inside ground, top meets roof at 5). Freestanding walls with no deck above keep the min rule; a wall whose inside tile is LOWER than outside grounds on the inside tile and the higher outside ground buries its lower portion like a retaining wall (pinned in the ADR-433 file).

**The step-line vertex — deliberate update.** The ADR-432 pin for vertex (5, 7) was updated deliberately, not silently: it touches two decked inside tiles at different heights, (4,6)=2 and (5,6)=3, and the rule takes the max, so its top is now 6 — it meets the east roof (6) and sits 1 level above the west roof (5). No single wall top can meet both; max was chosen over min because the gap it would leave under the higher roof is the see-through defect being fixed, while the lower side reads as the corner post continuing past the lower roof step. In a real building this anchor is not a piece at all: corners sit only at the footprint's four corners, where a single diagonal tile is decked, and mid-edge vertices have no piece — the pin is arithmetic for the rule, not a rendered case. The same max-of-decked trade applies to a party wall decked on both sides at different levels (pinned in the ADR-433 file: both sides roofed, outside higher, the wall takes the higher height).

**Tie-breaks pinned in the new test file.** Upper deck beats own-level deck (balcony: a level-1 south wall with a roof at level 2 over the inside tile and only a balcony floor at level 1 outside grounds on the inside tile even though the balcony ground is higher); own-level deck wins when no deck sits above yet (walls before their roof stand on the inside foundation); upper-story walls (z = 3) stand on their floor and meet the roof above (base 2, top 8 == level-2 roof seat).

**Verification.** New `apps/client/test/adr433_deck_ground.test.ts` (9 tests: deck keys, upper-beats-own x2, own-level fallback x2, freestanding min x2, retaining wall x1). Updated `apps/client/test/adr432_wall_roof_gap.test.ts` (9 tests, still 9: the 3 failing wall-top pins now pass decks and pass; the step-line vertex pin updated deliberately as above; bare no-deck assertions kept alongside to pin the min fallback). Targeted run: ADR-432 9/9, ADR-433 9/9, ADR-412 10/10 (7 client + 3 gameplay), gameplay ADR-432 2/2 — 30/30 across 5 files. Typecheck with lockfile-pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: `apps/client` and `packages/gameplay` clean. Full gate (`pnpm check`, typecheck phase clean — vitest ran): 4,805 passed / 10 failed / 6 skipped (4,821 tests, 726 files, 3,023.40 s). The 10 failures + 7 load-failure files are all pre-existing/environmental, none touches `view.ts` (verified: no `view.ts` import in any of them; `pack.test.ts` mentions it only in a comment): the 7 load failures are the sparse checkout missing `scripts/oxipng.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`) — restored from origin/main, content-identical, no diff — after which 6 files pass and ADR-435's test passes 5/5 on re-run (its gate load error was transient; the file existed throughout), with `adr395_dist`'s 2 tests file-level skipped (dist not built); of the 10 failed tests, 8 pass on re-run (all timeouts / perf-threshold flakes under load: `agents_persist`, `spawn_world`, `local_worker`, `server.test.ts`, `clan_persist`, `adr348`, `world_rules_roads`, `vehicle_net` netIdEntity 285 ms vs 250 ms budget), and the 2 that still fail are the known sparse-checkout `KEYS.md` ENOENT in `pack.test.ts` and the persist autosave bench max-tick timing (max 51–61 ms vs the 50 ms budget; p95 1.9–5.6 ms is fine). The full client suite alone was 1,057 passed / 2 failed (adr214_vfx + agents_persist, both 5,000 ms timeouts; both fail identically on base `view.ts`, proven by swapping HEAD's `view.ts` in and back — restored byte-identical afterwards).

**Honest cuts.** The render-loop wiring (deck set built in the GPiece pass, passed to `groundBoundaryPiece` and the ghost) is verified by code reading, not by a headless test — `IsoView` needs a canvas/renderer and cannot be instantiated in vitest, so no test pins the wiring end-to-end; the function-level tests pin the rule and the loop passes the same set both places. No visual check is possible in the VM — no GL — so the user's eyes on the live build (phone + Xbox) are the real check that the gap is gone and no wall now floats or pokes through a roof, as with ADR-412.
## ADR-436: Hold-to-delete is the only delete confirmation (SurVivaZ)

**Decision.** The type-DELETE confirmation is removed: `deleteConfirm()` (the dialog shared by the main menu's Delete progress picker and in-game Settings delete panels) no longer renders a confirm-word text input or a Delete button, and `DELETE_WORD` is deleted. The single confirmation path on every input type is holding the "Hold to delete" button for 1.5 s (`HOLD_MS` unchanged): mouse/touch press, Enter/Space held, or gamepad A held while the button is focused (including Edge's keyboard-emulated GamepadA). A single tap/click/A press never deletes, and the button stays disabled until something is selected in the main-menu picker. The dialog now states the hold ("Hold the button for 1.5 seconds to delete. A tap never deletes."). The server's `account.deleteMyProgress` wire guard (`DELETE_PROGRESS_CONFIRM = 0xde1e7e`, 1 per 30 s) is unchanged — it is a protocol guard against stray packets, not a typed word.

**Root cause.** The typed confirmation lived in exactly one place: `deleteConfirm()` in `apps/client/src/delete-progress.ts` (ADR-099 dialog shared by the main-menu "Delete progress" picker and in-game Settings → "Delete save" / "Delete hosted world" / "Delete my progress"). It rendered a `Type DELETE` text input (`[data-role=confirm-word]`) plus a "Delete" button gated on the input matching `DELETE_WORD`, alongside the existing hold-to-delete button. The hold path already supported all three input types (pointer/touch `pointerdown`, keyboard Enter/Space held, gamepad A held while focused), so removing the typed path left no input type stranded.

**Verification.** Baseline: typed DELETE confirmed before the change (5/5 delete tests passed). After: `pnpm vitest run apps/client/test/delete_progress.test.ts apps/client/test/delete_footer.test.ts apps/client/test/delete_picker.test.ts apps/client/test/delete_save.test.ts apps/server/test/delete_progress.test.ts` — 13/13 passed; pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 clean for the touched files. Tests pin the absence of any text input / Delete button, `HOLD_MS === 1500`, tap-never-deletes, and hold-confirm via keyboard, gamepad A, and pointer, plus a real-time pointer hold through the live tick loop in the main-menu footer on mobile (390×640) and desktop (1920×1080). Commit `7c46793d`, 4 files, +53/−43.

**Honest cuts.** Not visually verified: no phone/Xbox check that the hint text and hold button read well at play size — the user's eyes on the live build are the real check.

**Full gate (coordinator, `pnpm check`, log `~/workspace/work/delete-batch-gate.log`): 4,865 passed / 6 failed / 9 skipped (4,880 tests, 729 files). The 6 failures are the known pre-existing ones only: `pack.test.ts` (KEYS.md absent from the sparse checkout), persist `bench.test.ts` (wall-clock flake), and 4 timeout flakes under full-suite load (`clan_persist`, `world_rules_roads`, `agents_persist`, `spawn_world`) — all four pass on re-run (`clan_persist` 4/4 and `spawn_world` 3/3 as a group; `agents_persist` 1/1 and `world_rules_roads` 3/3 alone). ## ADR-437: Thin fruit-tree and crop spawns (a bit) — no data-only cut passes both bot suites, reverted (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause.** The ADR-203 / ADR-252 bot suites are sensitive to the exact grass-band list (multiset + entry order + length), not to the thinning dose. `rng.pick` is `arr[floor(rng()*len)]` (one draw, index by length), so any length change reshuffles every grass node's kind and any order change re-maps kinds to indices. Even a fixed-length swap leaving 89% of grass nodes byte-identical (stone/wood/berry positions identical) breaks ADR-203. The ADR-252 failure is a pre-existing bot-AI fragility (ADR-385): the pad bot trips ~200 tiles for torch materials (2 sticks + 2 fiber) to an unreachable destination (-55.6,-337.0) and freezes there; it crafts the torch en route but never aborts the trip, so its pad/base never complete. Adding sticks/fiber near bases improves ADR-252 (5/8 → 6/8) but breaks ADR-203 — the two suites pull in opposite directions on sticks/fiber density.

**What was tried (7 variants, grass band, base 31e7c4f8).** Full cut (53), grass-only (53), V2 (60, wild −3.4%/fruit −15.3%), V3 (63), V4 (65, +sticks/fiber), V5 (83 fixed-length swap, wild −10.7%/fruit −13.6%), V6 (63, V2+sticks/fiber), V2-reconstructed (60, same multiset as V2, base order). Full/grass-only/V3/V5/V6/V2-reconstructed fail ADR-203 2/3; V2-original passed ADR-203 3/3 but fails ADR-252 5/8; V4 fails ADR-252 6/8. No variant passes both.

**Verification.** Spawn counts measured per kind over 5×5 chunks, seeds [1234, 11, 99, 4242, 7, 2024] (base wild 482/426/501/523/353/584, fruit 261/197/168/209/130/165; total nodes identical across all variants). Controls with the change stashed on current HEAD: ADR-203 3/3, ADR-252 8/8 — failures are caused by the worldgen change, not other workers' commits. Berry density held at ~0.0093/tile in all variants (ADR-431 dye→Claim Flag chain preserved); stone near starter spawns unchanged (35, seed 11).

**Outcome.** No files changed (reverted to base; nothing committed, nothing pushed). Largest safe cut provable: none. Unblock by fixing the expedition trip-freeze (reachability check / abort when the need is met), then re-gate a V2-dose thinning (wild ~−3–5%, fruit ~−15%).

**Gate.** ADR-203 3/3 (base) / ADR-252 8/8 (base) — both green on the reverted tree.

**Full gate (coordinator, `pnpm check`, log `~/workspace/work/delete-batch-gate.log`): 4,865 passed / 6 failed / 9 skipped (4,880 tests, 729 files). The 6 failures are the known pre-existing ones only: `pack.test.ts` (KEYS.md absent from the sparse checkout), persist `bench.test.ts` (wall-clock flake), and 4 timeout flakes under full-suite load (`clan_persist`, `world_rules_roads`, `agents_persist`, `spawn_world`) — all four pass on re-run (`clan_persist` 4/4 and `spawn_world` 3/3 as a group; `agents_persist` 1/1 and `world_rules_roads` 3/3 alone). Pinned-TS 5.9.3 typecheck clean (zero TS errors; `scripts/oxipng.mjs` + `.d.mts` restored from origin/main, content-identical, no diff).**

## ADR-438: Plants, zombies and berry bushes stay crisp on phone/console budgets (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause.** Two mechanisms, both measured against the real merged-manifest atlas set. (1) On the 128 MB mobile budget (and 256 MB console), `fitBudget` halves the hot tier (0.5×) and the 1× pin drops entirely — pin=2 (FIDELITY + VISIBLE_PIN) needs 12 packed layers (288 MB), pin=1 needs 7 (168 MB) — so `pinned=[]` and every hot atlas halves, then magnifies ~2–4× on a DPR phone. `resources` (berry bush, 64 px → 32 px), `resources_tall` and `nature_trees` are in neither pin set, so nothing ever stored them at 1×; zombies are fidelity-pinned but the pin is all-or-nothing, and the re-tier can never rescue them after it records 0.5×. (2) Wild/farmed crops live on stream-residency `nature_crops`; the stream pool holds 4 slots on 128 MB for 131 stream pages, so the crop page is usually evicted and plants draw the soft `placeholder_sprout` blob.

**Fix (all in `packages/render/src/assets/atlasManager.ts`).** New `CORE_PIN_RE` (resources, resources_tall/huge, nature_trees/crops/sprouts/saplings, zombies*) as a third pin tier, tried after pin=2/pin=1 and judged by `fitsPacked` on the packed MaxRects layer count — the core set packs into 5 real layers (120 MB ≤ 128 MB) where the shelf planner charges 7 (168 MB); the core set also joins pin=2/pin=1, is excluded from idle demotion, and is never cold-classified on ≥128 MB budgets (this also fixes `resources_huge`, which defaulted cold via `_huge`). New `RESIDENT_PLANT_RE`: the small plant sheets load resident on ≥128 MB budgets (ADR-156/246 precedent), so crops never draw the placeholder; below 128 MB they keep streaming.

**Verification.** New `packages/render/test/adr438_blurry_plants_zombies_bushes.test.ts` (7 tests) failed 5/7 before the fix (resources at 0.5×, crops streamed) and passes 7/7 after — 128 MB and 256 MB both keep all 13 core atlases at 1× with the packed total inside budget, 768 MB unchanged (no halving); related suites 13 files / 80 tests pass (adr237, task17, adr251, full_resolution_preset, adr220, resident_creatures, blur, stream, multipage, packing, seamless_retier, adr430, adr257); pinned-TS 5.9.3 typecheck clean for @engine/render and client. Committed `ddfd4d18`, 3 files, +206/−15.

**Honest cuts.** Verified numerically only (no GL in the VM) — the user's eyes on their phone are the final check. Canvas2D fallback still bilinear-smooths magnified sprites (`imageSmoothingEnabled = s < 1` in canvas2d.ts) and was deliberately not changed — it affects all sprites equally, not just these three groups. Phone check: walk up to a berry bush, a fruit tree / wild crop patch, and a zombie at normal play zoom — all three should now read as sharp as the player character. Not fixed here: the stream pool still thrashes for mounts (1024 px pages, 4–12 slots) — out of this slice's scope.

**Full gate (coordinator, `pnpm check`, log `~/workspace/work/delete-batch-gate.log`): 4,865 passed / 6 failed / 9 skipped (4,880 tests, 729 files). The 6 failures are the known pre-existing ones only: `pack.test.ts` (KEYS.md absent from the sparse checkout), persist `bench.test.ts` (wall-clock flake), and 4 timeout flakes under full-suite load (`clan_persist`, `world_rules_roads`, `agents_persist`, `spawn_world`) — all four pass on re-run (`clan_persist` 4/4 and `spawn_world` 3/3 as a group; `agents_persist` 1/1 and `world_rules_roads` 3/3 alone). Pinned-TS 5.9.3 typecheck clean (zero TS errors; `scripts/oxipng.mjs` + `.d.mts` restored from origin/main, content-identical, no diff).**

## ADR-439: Hidden-ledge drop number shows onto water (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause.** The ADR-306/313 ledge warning measured drops from gameplay heights, but worldgen stores a water tile's bed height on the same smooth field as the shore, so a shoreline cliff read as a ~0 drop while the water renders at its surface (flat 0 natural, ADR-182; own level flowed, ADR-263/297/411) — probe over 5 seeds: 90–98% of shore tiles hid the number, average visual drop 3.0–3.8 tiles.

**Fix.** `ledgeSurfaceHeight()` in `apps/client/src/ledge-warning.ts` measures water tiles to their rendered surface via `renderTileHeight(tile, raw)`; `pickLedgeHint`/`pickLedgeHints` take optional `tileAt`/`rawHeightAt`, `ledgeDraws` passes the `TerrainRes` lookups, and `replica-terrain.ts` now forwards `rawHeightAt` so the live client can tell natural from flowed water. Land numbers, colours, gameplay heights, fall damage and both renderers' paths are unchanged — the number is one DOM overlay shared by WebGL2 and Canvas2D.

**Verification.** New `apps/client/test/adr439_ledge_water.test.ts` (7 tests: shore drop 20, non-water drop unchanged at 4, flow-water drop to its level, lookahead ray, no false drop while swimming, `ledgeDraws` wiring); targeted run `pnpm vitest run apps/client/test/adr439_ledge_water.test.ts apps/client/test/adr306_ledge_warning.test.ts apps/client/test/adr313_ledge_lookahead.test.ts` = 20/20 passed; pinned TS 5.9.3 typecheck for `apps/client` clean. Commit `ac26babe`, 3 files.

**Honest cuts.** Risk colour vs sim damage mismatch: the shown number (and its green/yellow/red colour, via `classifyLedgeRisk`) now follows the visual drop into water, but sim fall damage (`applyTerrainFall`) still uses the bed height, so a red "20" over water may overstate the damage the sim actually deals on landing. Aligning fall damage with the water surface is gameplay, out of this slice — flagged for a follow-up decision rather than changed here. Not visually verified: the number was verified numerically through `ledgeDraws` output; no live phone/Xbox check was possible from this VM — the user's eyes are the final check, as usual.

## ADR-440: Room heat — ventilation and realistic distribution (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause.** Opening a window shutter changed nothing thermally — `edgeShelterOf` never checked shutter state and `edgeBlocker` treats a window wall as solid even with open shutters (ADR-212), so `heatAt` through a window was always 0 and a room with all shutters open warmed exactly like a sealed room; opening a door zeroed the RoomHeat target but the stored heat still decayed at the slow sealed 120 s time constant.

**Fix.** (1) `roomOpennessAt` — mean per-edge ventilation of the room's flood-filled boundary (`StructureIndex.roomBoundary`, version-cached), ring proxy when unenclosed, 1 when roofless; per-edge vents: solid wall 0, low wall 0.5, closed door 0, open door 1, open doorway 0.75, glass/bars 0, closed shutters 0.15, open shutters 0.6, unfilled window 0.6. (2) RoomHeat target and time constant both scale by `1/(1+3·openness)` (120 s sealed → 30 s fully open), so a leaky room settles lower and faster without ever warming faster than sealed at first; unenclosed target stays 0. (3) Heat crosses edges by transmit factor in `structureOcclusion` (open door 1, open window 0.7, open shutters 0.6, closed shutters 0.15, closed door/glass/bars 0); light keeps the binary block, movement still treats window walls as solid. Heat sources, comfort band 8–32 °C and exposure-damage thresholds unchanged. Doors and shutters share the existing Interact → ToggleDoor path on keyboard/gamepad/touch, so no new interaction was needed.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr440.test.ts`, 21/21 passed (sealed ~9.5 °C vs ~5.0 °C with four open shutters after 120 s; snuffed warm room ~2.2 °C sealed vs ~0.4 °C ventilated after 120 s; next-room heat: closed door <0.5 °C, open door ~13.5 °C field, closed shutters ~2.0 °C, open shutters ~8.1 °C, glass <0.5 °C); neighboring suites 129/129; full available gameplay suite 2261 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed (222 files, sparse checkout); pinned TS 5.9.3 typecheck clean. Committed `5a1f9dcb`, 4 files, +416/−18.

**Honest cuts.** Wall insulation (`wallInsulationOf`) still halves for any window wall regardless of shutter state — deliberately not changed: indoors, felt is clamped to the comfort band plus RoomHeat, so the RoomHeat change already carries the open-window effect. Ventilation is per-room-boundary, not per-tile airflow: a fire at one end of a long room warms the whole room uniformly (same as Task 24), and there is no wind-driven draft direction. No HUD/character-sheet change: the indoor temperature number already drops with ventilation because it reads RoomHeat, but there is no explicit "ventilation" readout. Not verified on a phone/Xbox or visually — all numbers are from the headless harness.

**Full gate (coordinator, `pnpm check`, log `~/workspace/work/delete-batch-gate.log`): 4,865 passed / 6 failed / 9 skipped (4,880 tests, 729 files). The 6 failures are the known pre-existing ones only: `pack.test.ts` (KEYS.md absent from the sparse checkout), persist `bench.test.ts` (wall-clock flake), and 4 timeout flakes under full-suite load (`clan_persist`, `world_rules_roads`, `agents_persist`, `spawn_world`) — all four pass on re-run (`clan_persist` 4/4 and `spawn_world` 3/3 as a group; `agents_persist` 1/1 and `world_rules_roads` 3/3 alone). Pinned-TS 5.9.3 typecheck clean (zero TS errors; `scripts/oxipng.mjs` + `.d.mts` restored from origin/main, content-identical, no diff).**

## ADR-441: Travel stuck detection — a bot pushing at an unreachable leg re-plans or ends its trip (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause (verified by a failing test before the fix).** `travelRun` had no progress check at all, and `travel.json:"stuckRepathTicks": 200` was referenced nowhere in any `.ts` source — a dead knob. `prospectResource` picks the nearest seeded node out to 1200 tiles with no reachability check, and the only exits from a travel leg were arrival, the 72000-tick (60-game-minute) timeout, water re-plan, or the need-gone abort (which never fires while a plan step runs). Reproduced on the ADR-385 ridge (a +6 rise at x = 13, max unaided climb 3, bot at (10.5, 10.5), route waypoint at (30.5, 10.5)): before the fix the bot walked to the ridge foot (x ≈ 12.97) and its trip was still active after 12000 ticks of pushing, displacement exactly 0.0. Off-screen bots are immune — the freeze bites only in full sim within 96 tiles of a human, exactly where a player watches.

**Fix (all in `packages/gameplay/src/ai/travel.ts`, plus one `travel.json` comment line).** The dead knob is wired up, deliberately, not replaced: `travelStuckCheck` (exported, unit-pinned) gives a travelling bot `stuckRepathTicks` (200 ticks = 10 s) to displace 0.5 tiles from its anchor, stored on the `TravelState` itself (`stuckAt/stuckX/stuckY/stuckSeen/stuckRepaths` — JSON-safe numbers, so they survive the AiMemory flush). Displacement, not distance-to-goal, is the measure: a bot on a legitimate detour (around a lake, through a door, swimming a long run) keeps moving and never trips it, however far its goal is, so a legitimate long trip cannot be aborted by this check — the 72000-tick timeout's job (bounding total trip time) is untouched. The threshold is far below any real movement: the slowest legitimate sustained speed (encumbered swim, ~0.45 tiles/s) still covers ~4.5 tiles in the window. Bank waits are not stuck time — `travelRun` resets the anchor whenever the ADR-345 water gate holds the bot (waits run to 1200 ticks) — and a gap of >20 ticks between `travelRun` calls (behaviour deselected: fleeing, eating, off-screen hand-back) restarts the window instead of firing on stale data. On firing, `travelStuckReplan` re-plans around the current leg first (the knob's name: stuckRepath), via the existing `rerouteAroundLeg`. The trip ends when no route around exists, when the re-plan returns the same waypoints (the goal region is exempt from the avoid set, so a leg inside one region can never detour at region level — and the local nav has already failed), or after 3 stuck re-plans on one trip; a plan-budget-spent re-plan keeps the old route and restarts the window instead of counting. Ending a failed resource trip bans its destination through the existing `endTravel(false)` path, so the next prospect goes to the next-nearest source. No reachability check was added to `prospectResource` itself: the local nav's window is 24 tiles, so it cannot judge a node up to 1200 tiles away, and the stuck check + ban is the layer that can. Off-screen stepping is untouched — coarse sim always advances along the polyline, so it cannot freeze this way.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr441_travel_stuck.test.ts` (4 tests): the 2 end-to-end ridge tests failed before the fix (trip still active after 12000 ticks) and pass after — the resource trip ends after 217 ticks (walk to the ridge foot, then one 200-tick window) with the destination (30.5, 10.5) in `resourceBanned`, the explore trip ends after the same 217 ticks; the unit tests pin that a bot closing 0.6 tiles every 150 ticks never trips the check over 2000 ticks, a frozen bot trips it at tick 201, and a 100-tick gap restarts the window. Neighbouring suites: adr324 + adr385 + adr345 + adr344 + adr413 + adr305 + adr441, 79/79; gameplay adr252 18 passed / 3 skipped; client adr252-live 8/8. Pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: zero errors in this slice's files (`travel.ts`, `adr441_travel_stuck.test.ts`).

**Honest cuts.** The client adr203 suite fails in this checkout for an unrelated reason — another worker's uncommitted ADR-445 change (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/life.ts`, `ai_life.json invalid: gating must carry every numeric knob` at suite load, before any travel code runs); this slice touches neither file. A bot blocked for >10 s by a genuinely transient obstacle (another bot standing in a 1-wide doorway) can lose its trip the same way as a ridge-blocked one — the re-plan-first step means it usually detours instead, but a same-waypoints re-plan ends it; the ban only applies to resource trips. The 3-replan cap is a judgement call, not a measured optimum: a very long trip crossing three genuinely separate barriers ends instead of detouring a fourth time. Verified numerically only in the headless harness — no GL in the VM; the user's eyes on the live build are the real check that bots no longer visibly push at ridges.

## ADR-443: Weather response — shelter in rain/cold, dress warm (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause (verified by a failing test before the fix).** No reference to rain, wetness or weather anywhere in `ai/`: bots reacted only once already cold (`warm_up` at body < 36.2 °C), standing in the rain until then, and no fur wear goal existed anywhere in the planner, so bots could never reach insulation ≥ 10 (fur coat 7 + fur hat 3) that blocks outdoor cold damage. Reproduced first: new `packages/gameplay/test/adr443_weather_response.test.ts` failed 14/18 before the fix (no `seek_shelter` behavior, no weather sensor, no winter fur plan).

**Fix.** (1) `GoalSensors.weather` in `packages/gameplay/src/ai/autonomy.ts` (`fillGoalSensors`, cached via `SENSOR_KEYS`): wet precipitation (rain / storm / snow / blizzard from the `Weather` singleton), the bot's `Exposure` wetness (0 dry .. 1 soaked) and shelter percent. (2) New `seek_shelter` behaviour in `packages/gameplay/src/ai/base_behaviors.ts` (inertia 0.6, weight 2.2 like `warm_up`): fires while raining, exposed (shelter < 50% and not inside the hut), with a finished base or adopted ruin home within 60 tiles; walks door-aware to the hut centre (ruin centre for ruins) and releases the moment it is sheltered or the rain stops, so the hire job / base work resumes at once. It is a survival override like `warm_up`/`cool_down` — `withHireDuty` already exempted the name, so hire duty never gates it. (3) `warm_up` now fires for a soaked bot before its body is cold (wetness ≥ 0.6 to start, stays warming while > 0.3 — wet clothes insulate half, Task 31); `cool_down` stands down in the rain unless dangerously hot (body > 39 °C), since the rain already cools. (4) Planner (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/planner.ts`): in winter, once a workbench stands, `wear:fur_hat` + `wear:fur_coat` pre-goals jump the queue after fuel — before that the ladder builds the workbench first, so the goal is never dead weight. The existing `Resolver` crafts them through fur → fur_pelt → fur_hat / fur_coat (workbench); fur/hide come from `animal_carcass` nodes (knife tier 1), thread from flax, so a bot with no knife first gathers flint/sticks/fiber for a stone knife. Fur coat/hat were added to the planner's `useful` set so fur and its chain (pelt / hide / thread / flax) are kept, never junked as clutter. Comfort band (8–32 °C) and exposure-damage behaviour unchanged.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr443_weather_response.test.ts`, 19/19 passed (14 failed before the fix): `seek_shelter` exists, fires in rain when exposed with a base nearby and not in clear weather / inside / under a roof / with no base / 200 tiles out; walks toward the base and releases inside and when rain stops; `warm_up` fires soaked at body 37 °C and not when warm and dry; `cool_down` stands down in rain at 38.8 °C, fires dry, fires in rain at 39.5 °C; fur coat 7 + fur hat 3 = 10, dry fur holds 10; the fur chain is reachable in the planner index; winter plans wear a held coat/hat, craft the coat from fur_pelt/leather/thread at the workbench, and with no fur work the knife→carcass→flax chain (with a knife, fur/hide are direct gather leaves); no fur pre-goal outside winter. Neighbouring suites: adr252 + task31 + exposure-stages + adr341 + adr340 + adr327 + task30 + adr385, 130/130; adr336 + adr323 + adr259 + adr239 + adr270 + adr265, 74/75 — the one failure (`adr336_life_wiring`, idle hired worker's `life_want`) reproduces with this slice's files fully reverted, so it is another worker's in-progress `life.ts` change (ADR-445), not this slice. Pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: zero errors in this slice's files (`autonomy.ts`, `base_behaviors.ts`, `planner.ts`, `adr443_weather_response.test.ts`).

**Honest cuts.** Ruin-dwellers shelter-seek to the ruin centre and are judged sheltered only by the exposure percent (no 2×2 hut geometry to test against), so a roofless ruin corner could read as sheltered while still wet — the exposure sensor is the arbiter either way. Shelter-seeking only counts a *finished* base: a bot with an unfinished hut stands in the rain and relies on `warm_up`'s fire path. `warm_up` on wetness can send a bot that just crossed a river to a fire on a warm summer day until it dries (wetness < 0.3) — drying by the fire, like a player, but a brief detour. No phone/Xbox or visual check: all numbers are from the headless harness (no GL in the VM) — the user's eyes are the final check that bots actually walk inside when rain starts.

## ADR-445: Own lives actually fire (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause (verified by failing tests before the fix).** `isLifeIdle` required plan goal `idle` with no step/leaves/hunt, but the planner ladder almost never returns `idle` for a homed bot — there is always a next comfort goal (furnish / upgrade / …) with gather leaves, so unhired bots almost never qualified for a personal want. `visit_water` searched only 24 tiles and seed 42 has no water near spawn in that radius (probe: none within 200 tiles). No long-term aspiration layer existed beyond the 6 short wants, and no multi-tick live test of an unhired bot completing a want existed. Reproduced first: new `packages/gameplay/test/adr445_ai_life_live.test.ts` failed 10/14 before the fix.

**Fix.** (1) `isComfortGoal` + `hasShelter` in `packages/gameplay/src/ai/life.ts`: with a finished shelter (`bs.complete`, or a bed/hearth standing for ruin homes) a bot whose plan sits on a deferrable post-shelter goal — furnish, comfort wear except the torch, `animal_feed`, `knife`, `stone_spear`, `shovel`, `furnace`, `charcoal`, `bronze_ingot`, `anvil`, `dock`, `shipyard`, `axe2`, `pickaxe2`, `bronze_spear`, `upgrade` — is idle for life, and the goal's gather / hand-craft are deferred with it (re-planned next sense pass, nothing consumed or lost). NOT deferrable: the shelter core (tools, campfire, storage, workbench, torch, earthworks, ramp, base, hearth, bed), `defence`, or food/fuel/water chores (`cook`, `cooked_meat`, `water_flask`, `wood` — the early wood goal is campfire fuel and shares its name with the late one). Hard blockers stay hard in both branches: trips, travel routes, defence, repairs, pieces about to be placed (`buildPlan`), hunger/thirst < 55, hp < 0.5, cold, nearby zombies; the `life_want` behaviour's idle consideration mirrors the same gate (plus the hired-idle flag it already had). (2) `visit_water` search widened 24 → 64 tiles on a stride-3 sample (`waterSearchStride`, cap 2000 probes): lakes/rivers are many tiles wide, so the coarse sample still finds them and the found tile is at most a couple of tiles from the true nearest. (3) Aspiration layer in `packages/gameplay/data/ai_life.json` (`aspirations`, 5 entries): one short want repeated `targetCount` times — `seasoned_traveller` (visit_water ×3), `master_gardener` (tend_garden ×3), `old_friend` (socialize ×4), `hearty_eater` (favourite_food ×5), `homebody` (rest ×5). Progress is derived from the want's completion count (no extra counter to drift); the active aspiration (highest trait affinity among the incomplete ones, deterministic per bot) boosts its want's score ×(1 + weight) and is carried on the picked want as `lifeWant.aspiration`; completing it records it in `LifeState.aspirations` (persisted through `flushAiLife` like want progress) and the next aspiration takes over. No keepsake aspiration: the keepsake is one-shot (once owned, the want never fires again).

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr445_ai_life_live.test.ts`, 15/15 passed (10/14 failed before the fix): comfort-goal gating (idle on `furnish:table` with a finished shelter and gather leaves; not idle on shelter-core goals, without a shelter, or when hungry/cold/travelling/repairing/trip-wanted/build-planned/ threatened); `life_want` scores > 0 on a comfort goal and 0 on a shelter-core goal; water found 40–60 tiles out and still nothing on dry land; the aspiration bonus is decisive by construction (socialize 0.74 = eat 0.74 base, ×1.5 bonus puts socialize ahead; once the aspiration completes, eat wins); aspirations persist through `flushAiLife`. Live test: an unhired bot with a home built for real through the planner (tools, campfire, box, workbench, all BASE_SLOTS, hearth, bed, torch worn) sits on plan `furnish:table`, pursues a want through the real `buildAgentView` + `life_want` loop, and completes one (rest — the only actionable want in that rig: no water, farm or favourite food in reach) over ~600 ticks, with the hut still complete and bedded at the end. Neighbouring suites: adr336_ai_life + adr336_life_wiring + adr445, 52/52; adr252 + adr341 + agents + survival_behaviors, 45/45. Pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: zero errors in this slice's files (`life.ts`, `adr445_ai_life_live.test.ts`).

**Honest cuts.** Seed-42 spawn is dry for 200+ tiles in every direction probed, so the widened water search still cannot fire `visit_water` there — that is worldgen, not the gate; the widening is proven only where water exists within 64 tiles (fake lake). A bot with an empty pantry is permanently `tripWanted` (`view.food` undefined puts every food in `needs`), so life never opens until it stocks food — deliberate (a foodless bot works, it does not play), but it means the gate opens only for fed *and* stocked bots. Behaviour arbitration in the full survivor controller is not proven end-to-end: the live test drives `life_want` directly (the adr321 pattern) and the controller-level evidence is the `scoreBehavior > 0` check on a comfort goal. No phone/Xbox or visual check — all numbers are from the headless harness (no GL in the VM).

## ADR-444: Trust and reputation change behaviour (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause.** `ai/social_memory.ts` recorded persistent trust/affinity per player (helped/attacked/traded/partied events) — but almost nothing read it back: `trustOf` had only two readers (party/clan invite chances), and nothing in production ever recorded the interesting events — `noteSocialEvent(agent, player, "attacked" | "helped")` had no production caller — so a player who attacked bots hired exactly like a player who helped them, for the same single wanted item.

**Fix.** (1) `observeSocialMemory` (called from `buildAgentView`) now records what production can see: a hit the bot suffered notes "attacked" via `lastAttacker` (ADR-194), deduped by hit tick on the agent blackboard so one blow is noted once; being hired notes "helped" (a 0 -> owner transition, with a first-sight rule that notes it once after a restart only when no relation exists yet). (2) A grudge fades: on each lastSeen refresh (200 ticks) negative trust keeps 95% of itself and snaps to 0 below 0.01 — a double attack blocks hiring for ~2 min, a single hit stops mattering after a few minutes; positive trust never decays. (3) The bot's relationships mirror into a sim-local world resource, the TrustLedger (keyed by the bot's stable PlayerId, rebuilt from the loaded record on first sight), so the agent-less hire path can read trust. (4) Hire price by trust (`TRUST_HIRE`): >= 0.5 free, < -0.5 refused (`WorkerFail.Distrusted`, new reject reason "distrusted"), < 0 double price (2 wanted items); neutral pays 1. `hireWorkerValidate` checks the refusal before the item, so a distrusted player is told why; `workerView` exposes `trust` / `hireCost` / `hireRefused` and measures `hasWanted` against the price. (5) Hired behaviour follows trust: `view.hire.trust` — a trusted owner gets a close Follow shadow (1.5 tiles) and the full 12-tile defend radius; a distrusted owner is followed at arm's length (6) and guarded only within 4 tiles. (6) `buildAgentView` runs `observeSocialMemory` before `fillHireSensors`, so the hire sensors read trust recorded on the same tick.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr444.test.ts`, 9/9 passed (all 9 failed before the fix): free hire at trust 0.6 with nothing consumed; refusal at -1 with the item kept; one hit surcharges to 2 units instead of refusing; an attack is remembered from the world once per hit; being hired is remembered as help and visible in the ledger; grudges decay (-1 -> -0.95 per refresh, refusal lifts, fully forgiven to 0); trust survives a flush -> JSON -> reload round-trip and the ledger re-syncs; `workerView` prices; trusted follow closes in while a distrusted follow holds its distance; a distrusted guard ignores a zombie 8 tiles out. Neighbouring suites: social_memory + task22_recruitment (1 expectation updated for the new `trust` field) + party/clan + worker orders + relocation + agents, 66/66; adr442/443/445/446 + adr252, 89/89; task29_profile + adr331 + adr430 + survival_behaviors + guide, 31/31 (task29's 2 perf tests skipped without PERF=1, pre-existing); esm_import_order 155/155 with a 60 s timeout. Pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: zero errors in this slice's files.

**Honest cuts.** The "warned off" is the hire refusal itself (reject reason `distrusted` through the existing command-reject path, plus the `workerView` fields for the panel) — no warning chat line was added. A hit from an attacker who dies before the bot's next think is never noted (the dead-attacker skip guards against entity-id recycling misattribution). Forgiveness decay only runs while the attacker is present in the world (the lastSeen refresh loop only touches players in the replica). The esm_import_order `agents.ts` / `ai/agent_output.ts` entries time out at the default 5 s on a cold cache — pre-existing slowness, proven not caused by this slice (they still time out with the new `social_memory -> combat` import stubbed out); they pass with a 60 s timeout. The checkout's typecheck currently fails only on the ADR-446 worker's test file (7 errors in `adr446_shared_meal.test.ts`), not on this slice's files. No phone/Xbox or visual check — all numbers are from the headless harness (no GL in the VM).

## ADR-442: Sick bots seek care and rest (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause (verified by failing tests before the fix).** Zero references to `Diseases` / `careStatus` / sickness anywhere in `ai/` or `agents.ts`: a bot with a cold or the flu kept gathering, working its hire job and travelling, and `transmissionScan` counts it as a carrier the whole time, so it spread cold/flu to bots working shoulder-to-shoulder. The care cure itself works passively (240 s dry + fed + hydrated + warm; any break resets the clock; untreated cold → flu after 300 s). Reproduced first: new `packages/gameplay/test/adr442_sick_care.test.ts` failed 9/10 before the fix (the healthy-bot control passed throughout) — a sick hired Farm bot kept farming (`a.current` undefined / `work_farm`, never `seek_care`), no `sickCare` sensor existed, and the registry had no `seek_care` behaviour.

**Fix.** (1) `fillSickSensors` in new `packages/gameplay/src/ai/sick_care.ts` (last sensor in `buildAgentView`): while the bot has a cold or the flu (`careStatus().sick` — exactly the contagious diseases in `data/diseases.json`) it sets `view.sickCare` — the nearest lit campfire within 60 tiles (`nearestLitCampfire`, the same predicate as `nearLitCampfire` but returning the nearest: a Fuel-lit attachment whose piece is a campfire, or a free-standing lit campfire station), which care conditions are still missing, and how much care time is still owed. No lit fire still sets `sickCare` (fire undefined): the bot rests at home instead of working. Healthy bots pay only the `careStatus` read. (2) `seek_care` behaviour (inertia 0.6, `chatOnStart: "sick_rest"`): door-aware `goTo` to the fire, stop and rest there until the sensor clears (the cure accrues on its own), eating/drinking from the bag via `instantChores`; thirsty with nothing to drink in the bag it detours to known water first, like `cool_down`. (3) `withSickRest` (applied in `survivorRegistry`, inside `withHireDuty`): while `sickCare` is set it zeroes the first consideration of every behaviour except the survival set — flee, eat, drink, drink_water, warm_up, cool_down, seek_shelter, sleep, rest, tend_fire, seek_care, work_forage — so a sick bot cannot work a hire job, gather, build, travel, or run life wants while infectious. The one exception is `gather`, and only while the bot is hungry with no food in its bag (gathering is how it gets the food the cure needs; the gate closes again the moment it carries food). A zombie next to the bot still wins: the behaviour's `calm` gate zeroes it and its run returns false at once, so `flee` takes over. (4) Hired sick bots rest too: `seek_care` is exempt from `withHireDuty`'s Follow gating, and the owner sees why through the existing bot chat channel — new `sick_rest` lines in `data/agents.json` ("feeling rough — resting by the fire", …), said in local chat when the behaviour starts; no new UI panels. A mounted sick bot dismounts (`seek_care` added to `DISMOUNT_NOW`). Disease durations, rates, cure conditions and transmission rules are unchanged — this slice only changes what the bot DOES while sick.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr442_sick_care.test.ts`, 10/10 passed: the sensor reports the lit fire / missing conditions / seconds left; a sick hired Farm bot abandons its harvest target, walks the pathfinder route to the fire and never gathers while sick; a sick unhired bot stops gathering and a sick Follow bot stops shadowing its owner; a zombie on top of the bot still wins (`think` picks `flee`, and the driven bot runs away); resting by the fire with 235 s banked completes the care cure in 6 s more (cold and flu both clear, no flu develops) and the bot goes back to `work_farm` after; the `sick_rest` line is actually emitted by the controller when the behaviour starts; a healthy hired Farm bot is untouched (still farms, no `sickCare`); with no lit fire the sick bot still rests at home instead of working. Neighbouring suites: task31 + task13 + adr336 (life/wiring) 64/64; adr252 + adr259 + adr327 + adr338 70/70; adr321 + adr339 + adr440 + adr441 + adr443 + adr445 + adr323 88/88; adr444 + adr446 36/36. Pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: zero errors in this slice's files (`sick_care.ts`, `adr442_sick_care.test.ts`, `agents.ts`, `hire_behaviors.ts`, `mount_behaviors.ts`, `index.ts`) and zero errors in the full gameplay package at the final check.

**Honest cuts.** Verified numerically only in the headless harness (no GL in the VM) — the user's eyes on the live build are the final check that a sick bot is actually seen resting by the fire and saying so. The `gather` exemption fetches the planner's wanted node, not specifically food: a sick, hungry, foodless bot can gather wood/stone for a while before it finds berries — the common case (food in the bag, which the hire sensor keeps stocked) rests at once. The bot does not fetch food/water from base storage before heading to the fire; it rests with what it carries and detours only to known water. Reduced transmission is not tested directly: the tuning (5% roll after 60 s of contact within 2 tiles) makes a spread/no-spread test nondeterministic — the mechanism (the carrier leaves the work area and stays put) is what is tested. A `sick_rest` line can be dropped when the behaviour switch lands on a controller idle-pause tick (pre-existing controller quirk: the pause skips the chat attach); the bot still rests visibly. Not fixed here: bots never fetch rope or stock troughs, and the `warm` care condition outdoors still depends on ambient temperature — a sick bot by an outdoor fire on a freezing night rests but does not warm (same as a player).

## ADR-446: Shared meals at the hearth (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause (verified by a failing test before the fix).** Bots ate alone from their own bags: the `eat` behaviour and `instantChores` fired `eat:<slot>` wherever the bot happened to stand the moment hunger dropped, and no sensor ever looked at clanmates, the hearth, or the shared store — so two hungry clanmates by the same campfire with food in the base box still ate alone, wherever they were. Reproduced first: new `packages/gameplay/test/adr446_shared_meal.test.ts` failed at load before the fix (no shared-meal module), and its root-cause test pins the old behaviour — a hungry bot with a clanmate at the hearth eats where it stands (3.75 tiles from the fire) with nothing in its view mentioning the hearth, its mates, or the store.

**Fix.** New `packages/gameplay/src/ai/shared_meal.ts` (sensor + behaviour + pure rules), wired last in `buildAgentView` and into `survivorRegistry`. (1) A meal pends when the bot is hungry (< 0.55, any non-night phase), peckish at dusk (< 0.75, the evening meal), or starving at any phase (< 0.2), a hearth (`view.fire`) exists, and at least one clanmate or party mate is present; solo bots are untouched. (2) The `shared_meal` behaviour (weight 1.5 on the meal consideration, so it out-scores lone `eat` at equal hunger) walks the bot to its own ring seat around the fire (`seatFor`: one of 8 seats, deterministic per bot id) and eats there, waving at mates. (3) Scheduling — who cooks, whose food: the bot that arrives holding cookable raw (a single-ingredient campfire roast: raw_meat → cooked_meat, fish → cooked_fish, potato → baked_potato) while no ready food is in any bag or the store is the cook — it waits by the fire and the planner's existing `cook` pre-goal does the conversion; raw meat/fish are never eaten raw (health < 0, the same rule `fillAgentSensors` uses). Whose food: the shared store first, then the bot's own bag — a foodless bot withdraws exactly one portion from the nearest base-storage box near the fire, and a bot with surplus ready food deposits everything above 2 portions into that box before eating. (4) Lone eating is suppressed while a meal pends: a `noMealWaits` consideration on `eat` and a gate in `instantChores`, both reading the sensor's precomputed `suppressLoneEat`. Guards, so a meal never starves the home build: (a) seeds are never meal food — ready food is `food.hunger > 0 && food.health >= 0` and not a plantable seed, on both the deposit and the withdraw path; (b) fuel is never food — wood has no food value and the meal never touches fire fuel; (c) the shared-store reserve — a withdrawal must leave ≥ 2 portions behind unless the bot is starving, one portion per bot per meal, plus a 600-tick per-bot meal cooldown; (d) a bot keeps 2 portions in its own bag and shares only the surplus; (e) an empty hearth clears the meal and suppresses a new one for 1200 ticks, and a stuck walk to the hearth snoozes it the same way (`snoozeWant` pattern), so lone eating resumes instead of the bot camping or starving; (f) the lone-eat suppression applies only within a 12-tile walk of the hearth and above starvation hunger — a bot on an expedition far from home keeps eating alone from its bag (hunger drains 0.05/s, so a bot working all afternoon would otherwise go unfed), and a starving bot eats alone right now wherever it is. No new UI; every action the behaviour emits (`eat` / `copen` / `cdeposit` / `cwithdraw` / `cclose`) is one a human client already sends, server-validated as for players.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr446_shared_meal.test.ts`, 27/27 passed: the lone-eating repro, ready-food/cookable-raw rules (seeds and wood never food), meal timing (hungry/dusk/starving/night/cooldown), ring seats, sensor gating (no hearth / no mates / fed / party mates count), the store reserve (held at exactly 2 portions, released when starving), surplus deposit (5 → deposit 3, keep 2), the cook waiting instead of eating raw, the empty-hearth clear, the stuck-walk snooze with lone eating resuming, the far/starving lone-eat exemptions, the `buildAgentView` wiring, and the registry score (`shared_meal` > `eat` on a pending meal). Neighbouring suites: adr336_ai_life + adr336_life_wiring + clan_behaviors + survival_behaviors + agents + adr252 + adr327 + party_behaviors + social_memory + adr446, 114/114. Pinned TypeScript 5.9.3: zero errors in this slice's files (`shared_meal.ts`, `agents.ts`, `autonomy.ts`, `survivor_behaviors.ts`, `index.ts`, `adr446_shared_meal.test.ts`).

**Honest cuts.** Behaviour arbitration in the full survivor controller is not proven end-to-end: the meal is shown to out-score lone `eat` and the behaviour is driven directly (the adr321 pattern), but a scheduled `gather` can still out-score the meal mid-day — the distance/starvation limits on the suppression are what keep that safe (the bot eats alone out there, as today, and eats together when it comes home). A bot that reaches the hearth with no ready food and no raw marks the meal empty for 1200 ticks even if a clanmate arrives with food a moment later — the next hunger cycle picks it up. Store contents are read from the replicated Container when visible, else the planner's scanned base box, so a box whose contents the bot has never seen still serves as the meal's store through the scan. No phone/Xbox or visual check — all numbers are from the headless harness (no GL in the VM); the user's eyes are the final check that bots actually gather and eat together by the fire.
## ADR-447: Retry the ADR-437 thinning — fruit thins, wild cannot (SurVivaZ)

**Root cause (why ADR-437 failed, re-verified).** Any grass-band list change reshuffles
every grass node's kind: `rng.pick` is `arr[floor(rng()*len)]` and the generator draws
`rng.next() < nodeChance` per tile, consuming a pick draw only on a hit
(`packages/world/src/generator.ts`), so a length change re-indexes all later picks AND
shifts the stream. There is no data-only change that preserves node positions — every
thinning is a new lottery draw on the bot suites, and the ADR-349 wild floor (worst
seed ≥ 340) caps the wild dose: any variant thinning wild by ~4% drops the worst seed
(353) below 340. The ADR-441 stuck fix is not what saves a variant — the failing
ADR-252-live tests are base-building stalls (earthwork pad / 2x2 foundation), not the
torch-material freeze ADR-441 fixed.

**What was tried (4 variants, base 4e088334).** V2r (grass 83→61, first-copy removal,
same dose as ADR-437 V2: berry 14→10, starters x3→x2, 11 wild kinds x2→x1,
apple/pear/cherry x2→x1, fiber_bush x2→x1) — committed as failed `3dc00855` so the exact
list order is preserved; V3s (83→70, smaller dose); V4m (83→65, middle dose); V5f
(83→70, fruit-heavy: berry 14→12, starters x3→x2, 4 wild kinds x2→x1,

abandoned before testing: every thinned kind's copies sit in adjacent runs, so
last-copy removal yields a byte-identical list to first-copy removal.

**Verification — clean tree (worktree at 4e088334, no sibling changes, the only
attribution that holds).** Pure base itself fails ADR-252-live 6/8 (raised-pad pad +
2x2-base foundation, deterministic, same signature on re-run) — ADR-441's "8/8" was

V3s passes everything the base passes (ADR-203 3/3, ADR-252-live 6/8 identical,
ADR-349 8/8, gameplay ADR-252 18/18); V4m fails ADR-349 7/8 (seed 7 wild 339 < 340);
V5f passes everything the base passes (ADR-203 3/3, ADR-252-live 6/8 identical,
ADR-349 8/8, gameplay ADR-252 18/18, ADR-431/257/429/430 pass, 47/49 with only the
two pre-existing failures). On current main HEAD (`3abd95d8`, ADR-442/446 landed) V5f
passes the client suites outright, 11/11 — the two ADR-252-live tests pass there
because the sibling behaviour slices changed the bots, not because of this slice.
V2r/V3s main-tree failures during the run were sibling interference (other workers'

what attribute each variant. **Lesson: never gate a worldgen variant on a shared
checkout while sibling behaviour slices are landing — use a clean worktree at the
base commit, or the failures cannot be attributed.**

**Spawn counts (5x5 chunks, seeds [1234, 11, 99, 4242, 7, 2024]; base → V5f).**
Wild mean 478.2 → 484.0 (+1.2%, flat — reshuffle noise); per seed 482→474, 426→443,
501→516, 523→535, 353→352, 584→584. Fruit mean 188.3 → 170.7 (−9.3%, down on every

(and berry +8.3% — its 12/65 berry share overshoots; the dose arithmetic in the

**Outcome.** V5f ships: `packages/gameplay/data/worldgen.json` (grass band 83→70) +

## ADR-448: A full bag must not stall a pit / ramp dig forever — stash a surplus stack first (SurVivaZ)

**Correction to the ADR-447 record.** The ADR-447 entry says the pure ADR-441 base "fails
ADR-252-live 6/8" and that the two failures are "a separate pre-existing defect, still open". That
attribution was wrong: a read-only repro on a clean worktree at `4e088334` passes ADR-252-live 8/8,
three times. The 2 failures reproduce only with the failed V2r worldgen variant (`3dc00855`)
applied. The defect itself is real and layout-dependent — any future worldgen reshuffle can
re-trigger it, which is why it is fixed here rather than dismissed with the variant.

**Root cause (verified by probes before the fix).** Digging the pit yields 1 soil into the bot's
bag. With a 16/16 full bag, `editTerrain` (`packages/gameplay/src/terrain.ts:100-121`) refuses
with `TerrainFail.InventoryFull` (`exchangeItems`, `packages/gameplay/src/inventory.ts:205-211`),
and `nextTerrainWork` (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/terrain_base.ts:146`, cell-dig loop line 186)
returned `undefined` without abandoning and without any make-room step. The planner's earthworks
branch (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/planner.ts:488-507`, line 506) then returned the earthworks goal
with NO step and no leaves — which also gates the base goal by design, so no ladder, no foundation,
no bed, forever. All recovery paths were closed: stash never won arbitration (box empty yet
deposits=0 in 40k ticks), junk-drop could not help (everything in the bag is in the `useful` set,
`planner.ts:168-180`), patience never fired (`GOAL_PATIENCE=6000`, `base_behaviors.ts:49,131-135`
— eating a berry briefly frees a slot and resets the clock). The pad bot is immune (raising ground
consumes soil). The stand is reachable — NOT a pathfinder / travel stall. The trigger is the V2r
layout: its fruit trees ring the pit bot's base, so the bot gathers fruit until the bag fills.

**Fix.** (1) `nextTerrainWork` returns a distinct `{ k: "stash" }` work item (no item attached —
the planner picks the stack from the live bag, so a stack that frees or fills between sense passes
is never stale) when the earthworks dig is blocked ONLY by `InventoryFull`: the cell-dig loop and
the quarry loop (a full quarry used to return `undefined` with the comment "pause for ordinary
surplus stashing" — the pause was permanent, since nothing ever stashed). `nextRampWork` gets the
same treatment in its quarry loop and in the `gradeRamp` dry-run path. (2) The planner's
earthworks and ramp branches map the work item to a step via new `pickStashStep` (exported,
unit-pinned): the whole largest surplus stack — a partial deposit leaves the slot occupied, so it
