frees nothing — never a kept item (`plan.keep` + soil), a tool / weapon / worn item, and non-food
first (food is only stashed when the bag holds nothing else expendable, and it lands in the base
box, not on the ground, so the bot can withdraw it again); deterministic, ties break on the lowest
item id; `undefined` when nothing is expendable, in which case the goal stays stepless exactly as
before. (3) `base_work` executes the stash step like the `withdraw` step next to it: door-aware
`goTo` to the nearest accepting store (`storageTargetFor`, deposit variant), then `containerSeq`
with `storageDepositActions`. Deliberately NOT changed: `editTerrain` still refuses a full bag
rather than dropping dug soil (the "a full bag never loses dug soil" invariant, `terrain.ts:116`);
the planner's line-506 gate (never build foundations before earthworks completes) — the fix
produces a step, it does not bypass the gate; ADR-433 deck-aware grounding, ADR-435 terrain gate,
ADR-412 boundary grounding, ADR-382 route-around-structures (none implicated, untouched);
ADR-441 stuck detection; `exchangeItems` preview semantics.

**Verification.** New `packages/gameplay/test/adr448_full_bag_stash.test.ts` (4 tests): the pit dig
on a full bag returns `{ k: "stash" }` (not `undefined`, plan not abandoned) and the planner maps it
to a stash step that never names soil or the shovel; `pickStashStep` prefers the largest non-food
stack, never a kept / tool / worn item, deterministic tie-break; the ramp grade on a full bag
returns `{ k: "stash" }` too (the bot must stand at the foot first — `gradeRamp` checks reach
before capacity, same walk-then-grade order `base_work` follows); end-to-end drive through
stash → dig completes the pit (earth done, 12 digs, all four cells at target height and
underground, ladder placed, pit campfire lit, 12 soil kept in the bag, the stashed wood in the box
minus exactly what the ladder / campfire / fuel withdrew back out). Three ADR-265 tests updated
for the intended behaviour change (a capacity-blocked plan now yields a stash step instead of a
stepless goal; the junk sensor still identifies the dye, so a bot with no storage box keeps its old
drop-junk escape). Neighbouring suites: adr252-live 8/8 (stock worldgen) + adr203 3/3 + gameplay
adr252 / adr431 / adr382 / adr385 / adr343 / adr344 / adr345 / adr336 (life + wiring) / agents /
survival_behaviors / task36_terrain / inventory / adr204 / adr349 / adr447, 190/190 across 18
files. Pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 typecheck clean (gameplay package).

**Honest cuts.** Stashing the whole wood stack when the entrance ladder still needs wood costs one
withdraw round-trip per piece (ladder 4, campfire 5, fuel 4 — the drive test exercises all three);
the bot recovers on its own, but a stash that spared the next piece's materials would skip the
trips. With no storage box standing at all, the stash step has no target and the earthworks stays
gated on the `workFail` cooldown exactly as before — the box goal precedes earthworks in the
ladder, so this needs a base with no box only when the box was demolished or never built. A full
box AND a full bag still stalls (the deposit moves what fits, then the step re-issues) — same dead
end as before, now with a step instead of silence. Verified numerically only in the headless
harness (no GL in the VM) — the user's eyes on the live build are the final check that a bot
whose bag fills on a fruit run still finishes its pit base.

**Coordinator batch gate (2026-11-19, HEAD `ea3dfb0e`).** Full `pnpm -r typecheck` clean
(11/11 projects, pinned TypeScript 5.9.3); re-run in three slices: gameplay 2,348 passed / 0
failed / 3 skipped (229 files passed, 2 skipped); apps (client+server) 1,223 passed / 1 failed /
4 skipped (263 files) — the 1 failure is the known pre-existing `agents_persist.test.ts` timeout
flake under full-suite load (5,000 ms timeout; passes alone); remaining packages 1,388 passed /
2 failed / 2 skipped (243 files) — the 2 failures are the known pre-existing ones only
(`pack.test.ts` KEYS.md absent from the sparse checkout, ENOENT; persist `bench.test.ts`
wall-clock flake, 50.53 vs the 50 threshold, passes alone). Totals: 4,959 passed / 3 failed (all
known pre-existing, each confirmed) / 9 skipped across 737 files. No test file failed to load.
Coordinator re-ran the new tests: 4/4 (`adr448_full_bag_stash.test.ts`), plus the updated
ADR-265 suite. V2r one-off verification: `adr252_ai_humans_live.test.ts` 8/8 with the failed V2r
worldgen (`3dc00855`) applied in a scratch worktree at this commit — the layout trigger is closed.

## ADR-449: Mud after rain — wet ground slows walking off-path, worn dirt paths stay fast (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Rain wets the ground (ChunkSurface wetness, per chunk, 0..1) but walking speed ignored it: a
soaked field was as fast as a dry one, and the worn dirt paths ADR-413 lays had no reason to be
preferred in the wet. The cost rule for this batch forbids new per-tick scans; the fix must piggyback
a multiplier that already runs.

**Decision.** One multiplier in the existing `speedMultiplier` (`packages/gameplay/src/systems/movement.ts`,
after the `roadSpeedMul` step): when the mover is off any road surface (`roadSurfaceAt(...) ===
RoadSurface.None`) and the chunk wetness at the mover (`chunkWetnessAt`, O(1) map lookup) is at or
above `mudWetnessThreshold`, multiply speed by `mudSlowMul`. Tuning in `packages/gameplay/data/movement.json`:
`"mudSlowMul": 0.85, "mudWetnessThreshold": 0.5`. Dirt paths keep their 1.1x (the road check runs
first, so a path on wet ground is fast, not muddy). The ChunkSurface producer is included: before
this ADR `chunkSurfaceSystem` iterated an empty store — no producer ever spawned a surface. `world.ts`
now owns `ChunkSurfaces` (a `Map<ChunkKey, Entity>` resource), `ensureChunkSurface` (idempotent),
`despawnChunkSurface`, and `chunkWetnessAt`, wired into `attachWorldStreaming` onLoad (authority,
next to `spawnChunkNodes`) and onUnload. Wetness is transient: rain re-wets a reloaded chunk.

**Consequences.** Wet off-path ground costs 15% speed; paths stay the fast way through the wet. No new
scan, no new per-frame work (the multiplier is inside the existing movement pass). Rain rate is
0.01/s (`environment.json` `surface.rainPerSec`), so ~60 s of rain crosses the 0.5 threshold.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr449_mud.test.ts` 9/9: dry 1.0; wet 255 -> 0.85; threshold
boundary 127/255 -> 1, 128/255 -> 0.85; dirt path on wet ground -> 1.1 (no mud); rain via
`chunkSurfaceSystem` 60x1 s -> wetness >= 0.5 -> 0.85; producer idempotence; despawn; no surface -> 0.

## ADR-450: Winter ice — still water freezes below 32 F, walkable, thaws in spring (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Winter changed the look (snow cover, ice visuals) but never the water: lakes stayed liquid
and uncrossable all winter. The freeze must flip on the temperature change that already drives
seasons, with no slip physics and no new per-tick scan.

**Decision.** Frozen = the blended season mean temperature is below 0 C (weights x meanTemp; summer
26.1, fall 11.4, winter -8.05, spring 12.2 C) — the mean, not the instantaneous temperature, so lakes
don't flicker open on mild winter afternoons; freezing happens over the 0.75-day season blends and
thaws in spring; seasons off = never frozen. New module `packages/gameplay/src/frozen.ts` (the
cycle-free home: `environment.ts` already imports `movement.ts` for `inWater`, so the predicate could
not live there): `FREEZING_C = 0` moved there (environment.ts re-exports it — guide.ts and spoilage.ts
import it from environment.js unchanged), `isWaterFrozen(world)` cached once per world tick in a
WeakMap keyed on (tick, Season offsetDays/lengthDays/blendDays), `isFrozenWaterAt(world, tx, ty)` =
water tile + not flow water (`isFlowWater` via `Terrain.rawHeightAt`, fallback to `heightAt`; rivers,
dug channels and waterfalls never freeze) + frozen. One choke point each: `waterDepth()` returns None
on frozen still water (no swim speed, no swim anim, no wetness gain standing on ice); `inWater()`
returns false; `movementBlocked` and `terrainBlocksWalker` exempt frozen still water (animals and
zombies cross the ice); `animSettleSystem` exempts frozen water from the Swim switch. `worn_paths.ts`:
the "never pave a lake" check changed from `inWater` to a raw `isWaterId(terrain.tileAt(...))` check
(`inWater` now reads frozen lakes as land — otherwise bots would lay dirt paths across frozen lakes).
Walk speed on ice is 1.0x, no slip physics.

**Consequences / open collisions (reported, not solved here).** Boats on a frozen lake cannot move
(`boatWaterMul` -> 0, `boatPoseBlocked` -> true — they freeze in, no crash); fishing and drinking
through ice are disabled (`inWater` false). Bot long-distance travel planning across UNLOADED terrain
still uses raw `waterDepthAt` (conservative — routes around a frozen lake until the chunk loads). A
winter heat wave does NOT thaw the ice in v1 (the predicate ignores weather).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr450_winter_ice.test.ts` 7/7: frozen predicate across seasons
(summer/fall false, winter true, spring false — all at the same tick, exercising the cache key);
`isFrozenWaterAt` (still deep + shallow true in winter, land false, flow false, summer false);
movementBlocked deep in/out of winter + shallow always wadeable; terrainBlocksWalker; waterDepth /
inWater / swimSpeedMulAt (Deep/true/swim mul in summer -> None/false/1 in winter); animSettle (Walk
stays Walk on frozen lake, becomes Swim in summer); flow water still blocks in winter. Test note:
TileMap land must be real `GRASS_TILE`, not tile 0 — `waterDepthAt` never counts tile 0 as land.

## ADR-451: Lightning in storms — one roll per storm, only near players, scorches a tree or starts a small fire (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Storms had thunder and lightning bolts in the sky (`onLightning` existed) but no gameplay
effect: no strike ever landed. `WeatherChanged` and `onLightning` both had zero consumers.

**Decision.** Roll server-side once per storm on `WeatherChanged`. Tuning in `packages/gameplay/data/fire.json`:
`"lightning": { "strikesPerStorm": 1, "radius": 15, "minDistance": 5 }`. New component `LightningFire`
(`{ struckTick: "u32" }`, networked + persistent) appended to `components.ts` + the append-only
`GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS` list. `installLightning(world)` subscribes to `WeatherChanged` (once per world;
one `world.rngFor("lightning")` stream per storm, sequential draws); `resolveLightningStrike(world, rng)`:
pick a random survivor, strike point 5–15 tiles away at a random angle; nearest tree (axe-node
`ResourceNode`, `requiredTool === ToolKind.Axe`, not oneShot) within radius -> `depleteNode` (the tree
dies, leaves a stump for `stumpSeconds` 45 s, regrows after `respawnSeconds` 300 s); else nearest
flammable piece (`flammableTiers` [0,1]) -> `igniteLightning` (ignite + the marker); else no strike;
never strikes a person. `burningSystem` skips `rainQuench` for entities with `LightningFire` (a fresh
lightning fire would otherwise die in ~3 checks: quench 40 vs grow 16) — lightning fires are exempt
from storm quench. `extinguish()` also removes the marker. Wired in `install.ts` next to
`installDiseases`. `FireTuning` in `packages/gameplay/src/combat/pvp_pieces.ts` gained the `lightning`
block.

**Consequences.** At most one strike per storm, always 5–15 tiles from a survivor, never on a person.
A scorched tree regrows; a lightning fire can catch in a storm (and must be fought or left to burn).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr451_lightning.test.ts` 7/7: stub rng puts the strike exactly
5 tiles east of the anchor; tree at (5,0) depletes with a `NodeRegrow` marker (stump + respawn at tick +
300x20); no-tree case ignites a wooden wall with `Burning` + `LightningFire`; `WeatherChanged` emit ->
exactly 1 tree dies from a ring of 8; no survivors -> no strike; ordinary fire dies in a storm over
7 burning checks (140 ticks) while the lightning fire grows past 128; `extinguish` removes the marker.
Note: `emit` is deferred — tests step once after emitting before asserting.

## ADR-452: Rain fills open water — waterskins and containers left outside gain water (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Rain wet the player and the ground but never filled a container: an empty waterskin stayed
empty in a downpour. The precipitation tick already exists; the fill must hook it, not add a scan.

**Decision.** Hook in `exposureSystem` (`packages/gameplay/src/systems/environment.ts`, every 4 ticks,
`sh.rain` already computed): if raining and `sh.rain > 0` and the entity has an Inventory, one
deterministic roll `world.rngFor("rainfill", e).next() < dt / env.rainFillSecondsPerSip`, then fill the
first carried liquid container with room via `fillContainer(world, e, slot, 1)` (+1 sip per
`rainFillSecondsPerSip`). Tuning in `environment.json`: `"rainFillSecondsPerSip": 45`.
Rain water is untreated, so a boiled container reverts to its raw variant on refill (existing
`fillContainer` behaviour). Held/carried containers only — ground and storage containers are out of
scope. Bots fill too (same code path).

**Consequences.** An empty waterskin fills to 3 sips in ~135 s of unsheltered rain (300 s in the test
covers the roll variance). Roofed players stay dry and unfilled. No new scan, no new per-frame work.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr452_rain_fill.test.ts` 6/6: empty waterskin fills to 3 sips
in 300 s rain; Clear -> no fill; roofed room (task24 room builder) -> no fill; boiled_waterskin
reverts to raw on refill; full container stays 3. Test note: `weatherSystem` forbids rain on day 0, so
tests use `setTimeOfDay(w, 12, 1)` (day 1) + the adr312 `run` pattern (drive `exposureSystem(w, 0.2)`
directly with `w.tick += 4` per call; `makeWorld` pins weather via `endsAtTick = 0xffffffff`).

## ADR-453: Smoke columns — campfires show a thin smoke column from far off (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** A lit campfire was invisible until you were close enough to see the fire itself: no
way to spot a distant camp. The map already renders `visibleMarkers` pins generically; a marker is
the cheapest far-off signal.

**Decision.** Map-marker variant only — the in-world tall column is NOT built in this batch. In
`packages/gameplay/src/map_markers.ts`: `spawnMarker` refactored to delegate to new
`spawnMarkerOwned(w, owner, clientId, x, y, visibility, label, party, clan)` (same behaviour);
`SMOKE_MARKER_LABEL = "Smoke"`, `SMOKE_HEARTH_KEYS = ["campfire", "fireplace"]`; `smokeTargetFor(world, fire)`
resolves a Fuel entity to its piece via `pieceOf` (builder = `PieceOwner`, mirroring `builtBy`) or a
free-standing `Campfire` station (owner 0); `placeSmokeMarker` (idempotent, one per fire),
`removeSmokeMarker` (in-memory `WeakMap<World, Map>` index, fallback to a position+label scan within
1.5 tiles for the post-restart case), `removeSmokeMarkerForPiece` (index only — the piece is gone);
`installSmokeMarkers(world)` subscribes to `FireToggled` (place on lit, remove on unlit) and
`PieceDestroyed` (cleanup); wired in `install.ts`. No client change (the client map already renders
`visibleMarkers` pins generically; a "Smoke" marker appears as a pin + label). Visibility private (0)
— only the owner sees their smoke.

**Consequences / open items.** Party/clan sharing is an open follow-up (private-only for now). The
owner's clientId is looked up from the live `[PlayerId]` entity's `Owner` component (0 when offline —
the marker still exists, it just cannot replicate until they are back). Destroy-while-lit smoke
markers rely on the `PieceDestroyed` cleanup; a marker whose fire is destroyed while the world is
down is cleaned by the position+label scan on the next unlit event.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr453_smoke_columns.test.ts` 7/7: place campfire, add coal,
`ToggleFire` intent -> marker appears (label "Smoke", visibility 0, owner 7, at the fire's position);
snuff -> removed; re-light -> still 1; fireplace qualifies; Furnace station lit -> no marker;
`PieceDestroyed` emit -> removed; another player (id 8) sees nothing. Note: `G.Transform` is NOT
exported from the gameplay index — tests import `Transform` from `@engine/core`.

## ADR-454: Bees pollinate — crops within a few tiles of an Apiary yield a bit more (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Apiaries existed (bees, honey) but did nothing for nearby crops: no pollination. The
harvest already computes yields; the bonus must be checked once at harvest only, not per tick.

**Decision.** `apiaryWithin(world, x, y, radius)` exported from `packages/gameplay/src/skills/husbandry.ts`
(reuses the StructureIndex-versioned station cache; attachments have Transforms).
`packages/gameplay/src/systems/gathering.ts`: pollinated flag = `def.key.startsWith("crop_") &&
world.has(node, GrownPlant) && apiaryWithin(...)`; +1 on first yield only, after skill scaling.
Tuning in `packages/gameplay/data/farming.json`: `"pollination": { "radius": 5, "bonus": 1 }` (also
added `"compostFertilizerSeconds": 600` there for ADR-460). Planted-vs-wild discriminator is the
`GrownPlant` component (mature planted crops get it in `farming.ts` cropGrowthSystem; wild nodes
don't). No stacking across apiaries (one bonus, however many apiaries are in range).

**Consequences.** A planted crop within 5 tiles of an Apiary yields +1 on its first yield only. Wild
crops are unaffected. No new scan (the check runs inside the existing harvest path).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr454_bees_pollinate.test.ts` 5/5: paired worlds with identical
entity creation order (two apiaries always placed, positions vary) so the gather RNG stream matches
and base vs base+1 is exact. No import cycle (`apiaryWithin` exported via `src/index.ts` `export *`).

## ADR-455: Footprints in snow and mud (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Walking left no trace: snow and mud showed no sign of passage. The SCOPE found no
transient per-tile overlay state anywhere (worn paths are permanent roads; ChunkSurface wetness is
per-chunk; snow cover is a global season uniform) and the feature as specified breaks the cost rule
in three ways (new state, per-step stamping, new art). Tracey authorized the transient overlay store
(the one place this batch adds new per-step state) and new runtime-painted art for footprints.

**Decision.** CLIENT-SIDE ONLY transient decals (SCOPE option ii). The net client never steps the
gameplay sim (`packages/net/src/client.ts` is a snapshot/interpolation client), so a sim-side
footprint store would live only on the server and never reach any screen; sharing footprints as
world state would need per-step entity replication, which the cost rule forbids. So each client
stamps its own footprints from the replicated state it already has (mover Transforms, per-chunk
wetness via the networked ChunkSurface, season snow cover) and draws them as one-frame VFX overlays
(the StallLayer pattern: replaced before each render, sharing the lit, depth-sorted sprite batch).
No sim state, no replication, no persistence — a footprint is gone on reload, which is correct for
something that fades in 60 s. `apps/client/src/footprints.ts`: `FootprintStore` (stamps
`Map<tileKey, {x, y, untilTick, facing, variant}>`, `version`, `lastSampleTick`, `lastPos`);
`sampleFootprints` runs at most once per `sampleTicks` (5 ticks = 0.25 s), sampling movers (players +
bots via `Survival`, animals via `Animal`, zombies via `Zombie` — all networked) near the local player
(Chebyshev `nearPlayerTiles`); a mover stamps its tile only when it ENTERED a new tile since the last
sample and the surface qualifies (ground snow cover >= `snowCover`, or the chunk wetness >=
`wetness`); standing still stamps nothing and never refreshes a print. Facing is the travel direction
(derived from the sampled position delta — animals/zombies don't update `Transform.facing` per tick);
variant alternates left/right foot (a lateral offset perpendicular to the heading, +-0.18 tiles).
Prints fade linearly over `fadeSeconds` and are pruned on the next sample after expiry; the store is
capped at `maxFootprints` (oldest evicted first). Tuning in `environment.json` `footprints`:
`{ fadeSeconds: 60, snowCover: 0.5, wetness: 0.5, nearPlayerTiles: 40, sampleTicks: 5,
maxFootprints: 512 }` (also added to `EnvironmentTuning` in `defs.ts`). `collectFootprintOverlays`
builds the VFX spawns (alpha from remaining life, `flat: true`, facing from the stamp). Art:
`apps/client/src/footprints-art.ts` paints the footprint at runtime (Px canvas): a single boot print
(sole + toe ball + heel pad, dark semi-transparent, pre-sheared for the iso ground plane — the Flat
flag only fixes the depth key, the art itself must already be an iso-aligned oval, like the road
decals), 8 directional frames in a 512x64 atlas (frame f points along `TASK34_DIR_VEC[f]`, the bee's
convention); fragment `packages/assets/pack/task455/manifest.task455.json` (layout only, `dirStride:
1`, anchor centre) registered in `MANIFEST_INDEX`; `footprintAtlasSources()` merged in `view.ts`
next to the task34/256/355 sources. The fragment ALSO has to be served: `apps/client/vite.config.ts` MOUNTS allow-list (the `task34|…|task422` alternation) — without `task455` there the dev server never serves `pack/task455/manifest.task455.json`, the client manifest omits the fragment (ADR-248 parity fails), and the atlas key never reaches the registry, so footprints would never render on the live build. Caught by the ADR-248 parity test in the full suite; fixed by adding `task455` to the allow-list. Lesson: a new pack fragment needs THREE registrations — `MANIFEST_INDEX`, the fragment file on disk, and the vite MOUNTS allow-list. Render: `flat?: boolean` added to `VfxSpawn`/`VfxInstance`
(`packages/render/src/vfx.ts`) and honored in the WebGL2 VFX push (`packages/render/src/sprites.ts`,
`SpriteFlag.Flat` OR'd in). Wired in `View.render()`: sample from the net world (replicated
Transforms), snow cover from the view world (its season is set there), sprite id cached after the
first resolve, overlay assigned to `r.vfx.overlay` before `r.render(v, alpha)`.

**Consequences / open gaps.** Canvas2D has no main VFX layer (`r.vfx` undefined — ADR-242), so
footprints render on WebGL2 only; the Canvas2D fallback does not draw them. Footprints are
per-client: you see your own and nearby movers' prints, but a print is not shared world state (a
player on another client does not see the same print unless their own client stamped it from the
same replicated movement). The facing convention (frame f = heading f*45 deg in world atan2 terms)
follows the engine's geographic facing; if the atlas's directional frame order is offset, all prints
rotate together (a consistent cosmetic offset, not a per-print error).

**Verification.** `apps/client/test/adr455_footprints.test.ts` 13/13: tuning values; walking in snow
stamps one footprint per tile (facing east = 0, variant alternates); dry summer grass stamps nothing;
soaked chunk in summer stamps (mud); standing still stamps nothing and never refreshes; a mover far
from the player stamps nothing (near-player gate) while the same rabbit near the player stamps;
prints fade after 60 s (pruned on the next sample); the store caps at 512 (oldest evicted first,
tested with a long fade so expiry cannot interfere — a 600-tile walk at 5 ticks/sample takes 150 s,
past the 60 s fade, and with the real fade the store holds 240); the overlay is flat VFX spawns with
alpha from remaining life (1.0 fresh, ~0.5 halfway, empty past expiry); `quantizeDir8` (east 0, south
2, west 4, north 6); the painted atlas is 512x64 with 8 non-empty frames and opposite facings differ;
the fragment declares the atlas + sprite (`dirStride: 1`); `footprintAtlasSources()` is a no-op map in
a canvas-less environment (no crash).

## ADR-456: Smoke in a sealed room — a roaring fire in a sealed room builds smoke and hurts if ignored (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** A roaring fire in a sealed room was cozy and harmless: the room warmed (ADR-440) but the
smoke had nowhere to go and no cost. Opening a window or door vents a room (ADR-440's openness
number); the smoke must use that same number, on the slow tick, with no accumulator.

**Decision.** Stateless v1 (Tracey's decision): instant proportional harm in `exposureSystem`
(`packages/gameplay/src/systems/environment.ts`, the existing per-occupant pass every 4 ticks). The
room openness is hoisted into a local (`roomOpennessAt` once per occupant per pass — shared by the
room-heat vent factor and the smoke check, not called twice). When the fire's heat at the occupant is
at or above `smoke.heatC` (close to a lit campfire at 18 or fireplace at 22; a torch at 4 never
counts) and the openness is at or below `smoke.openness`, a `HealthRegen` Add modifier (the sick-food
pattern, `vitals.ts:114`) of `-smoke.hpPerSec * (1 - openness)` is refreshed, lapsing on its own ~9
ticks after a door/shutter is opened or the fire goes out. No accumulator, no new component. Tuning
in `environment.json` `smoke`: `{ heatC: 12, openness: 0.1, hpPerSec: 1 }` (also added to
`EnvironmentTuning` in `defs.ts`). At fully sealed (openness 0) the Add is -1.0 hp/s against the
0.25 hp/s well-fed base regen — a net drain of 0.75 hp/s (1.0 hp/s when not well-fed), ~100–133 s to
die from smoke alone if ignored. Threshold 0.1, NOT the SCOPE's suggested 0.25: ADR-440 pins one open
door at 0.25 and one open shutter at 0.15, so 0.25 would still smoke with the door open; 0.1 sits
between one closed-shutter window (0.0375, still smokes at 0.96x) and one open shutter (0.15, vents).
Bots share the pass, so a bot in a sealed room with a roaring fire is hurt the same way. A real bug
found while testing this ADR: the ADR-450 refactor's `export { FREEZING_C } from "../frozen.js"` in
`environment.ts` did not create a local binding, so `snowAllowed` threw `ReferenceError:
FREEZING_C is not defined` whenever the weather system considered snow — fixed by importing it at
the top of the file and re-exporting (`export { FREEZING_C };`), so guide.ts and spoilage.ts keep
importing it from this module.

**Consequences.** A sealed room + roaring fire drains hp until a door/shutter is opened or the fire
goes out; opening a vent stops the harm within ~0.5 s and regen resumes. The harm only applies when
no other damage is occurring (the vitalsSystem regen branch is skipped while `dmg > 0` — the same
property as the sick-food pattern).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr456_sealed_smoke.test.ts` 7/7: tuning values; sealed room +
roaring fire hurts (hp drops ~45 in 60 s, modifier -1.0 hp/s, heatAt >= 12, openness 0); opening the
door vents it (hp stops dropping, modifier lapses to 0, openness 0.25); unlit fire does not smoke (hp
100); open doorway vents it (hp 100, openness 0.1875); one open shutter vents it (hp 100, openness
0.15); one closed-shutter window still smokes, weaker (modifier -0.9625, hp drops). The test reuses
the adr440 hut/litRoom builders (foundation + 4 walls + roof_flat, lit campfire piece).

## ADR-457: Wet firewood — wood gathered in rain burns shorter; dry stored wood burns full (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Wood gathered in a downpour burned as long as wood gathered dry: rain had no effect on
fuel. The SCOPE's redesign (accepted): a separate `wet_wood` item gathered INSTEAD of wood when it is
raining at gather time, with its own fuelSeconds — never a second roll, never a status on stored wood.

**Decision.** Data: `wet_wood` added to `packages/gameplay/data/items.json` right after `wood`
(`{"key": "wet_wood", "name": "Wet Pine Log", "category": "resource", "maxStack": 50, "weight": 0.5,
"fuelSeconds": 10}` — no `"sprite"` field, so `spriteKey` defaults to `"wet_wood"`; wood is 20 s).
Drying recipe `dry_wet_wood` in `recipes.json` (`wet_wood` 1 -> `wood` 1, station none, 30 s).
`ids.lock.json` regenerated (`pnpm --filter @engine/gameplay lock:ids`): wet_wood item id 521,
dry_wet_wood recipe id 407 (the regen also supplied the ADR-459 keys, whose earlier regen had not
persisted: cured_poultry 517, cured_prime_cut 518, cured_venison 519, smoked_fish 520; recipes 403–406).
Gathering: in `packages/gameplay/src/systems/gathering.ts`, hoisted `const raining =
isRaining(world.env(Weather).kind)` before the yields loop; per yield, the item handed over is
`wet_wood` when `y.item` is wood's numeric id and it is raining (`addItem` + `ItemGathered` +
`InventoryOverflow` all use the substituted item; the skill roll and counts stay on "wood"). Yields
store numeric item ids (resolved at loadDefs), not string keys — the first version compared
`y.item === "wood"` (always false) and the probe proved it (tree yields `[{item: 1, ...}]`, wood id 1).
Applies to players and bots (shared path); hardwood is NOT substituted (no wet_hardwood). Rain = Rain
+ Storm kinds. Art (authorized new art): `apps/client/src/wetwood-art.ts` — runtime-painted wet-log
icon (128x128, Px canvas, ADR-387 book pattern): dark wet bark, wet sheen, bark ridges, pale sawn end
with growth rings, rain droplets with white highlights, one drip, ground shadow; registered in
`ICON_DATA` as `wet_wood.png` + a `[data-icon="wet_wood"]` override style, wired in `view.ts` next to
`installGuideMenuIcon()`. Dropped items are loot bags (the item sprite never renders in the world)
and dry wood/hardwood/planks/sticks/coal/charcoal have NO manifest sprite entries at all (their UI
icons come from the CSS `[data-icon]` sheet over `items.png`), so the ICON_DATA + CSS-override icon
is the only surface wet wood appears on; if Art later ships a real wet_wood pack sprite under the
same key, it takes over.

**Consequences.** Wood gathered in rain or storm is wet_wood (10 s fuel, half of wood's 20 s); wood
gathered dry and wood already stored are untouched. Wet wood dries to wood in 30 s with no station.
The substitution is by numeric id, so any future item-key rename that keeps the id is safe.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr457_wet_firewood.test.ts` 6/6 (data: wet_wood def + 10 s
fuel; fuel: `fuelSecondsLeft` 10 vs 20 on unlit campfires; drying recipe def + full craft through,
600 ticks; rain -> wet_wood, dry weather -> wood, storm -> wet_wood, snow -> dry wood, oak in rain ->
hardwood not substituted) + `apps/client/test/adr457_wet_wood_icon.test.ts` 2/2 (pixel assertions +
install seam). Test gotchas: the axe lands in inventory slot 0, so `mainHandSlot` must be 0 (slot 1
was empty -> bare-hands yield 1); `weatherSystem` forbids rain on day 0, so tests use day 1.

## ADR-458: Hot meals warm you — a cooked meal by the fire gives a short warmth buff (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Eating a hot stew by the fire felt the same as eating it in a blizzard: no warmth from a
hot meal. The buff must be event-driven on eating (not a per-tick check) and reuse fire proximity.

**Decision.** Tuning in `packages/gameplay/data/vitals.json`: `"hotMeals": { "items": [...14 keys...],
"insulation": 5, "seconds": 120 }`; `VitalsTuning` in `defs.ts` gained the matching `hotMeals` field.
`consumeSystem` in `packages/gameplay/src/systems/vitals.ts` (after the successful-eat point): if the
eaten item is in the list and `heatAt(world, x, y) > 0`, adds Insulation +5 modifier expiring in 120 s
(via `addModifier`/`secondsToTicks`, the same pattern as the sick-food debuffs); `heatAt` imported
from `./environment.js` (no cycle: neither environment.ts nor movement.ts imports vitals.ts). Hot-meal
list: cooked_meat, cooked_fish, cooked_venison, cooked_poultry, cooked_small_game, cooked_prime_cut,
stew_bowl, fish_stew, vegetable_stew, truffle_stew, potato_soup, meat_pie, berry_pie, pumpkin_pie.
EXCLUDED: canned_stew (eaten from the can), stewed_* berries (snacks, not meals), baked potato, bread.
Insulation only shifts felt temperature toward the comfort band, so it warms in the cold and never
overheats in summer.

**Consequences.** A cooked meal eaten where a fire's heat reaches gives +5 Insulation for 120 s.
Baked potato and bread do not count. No new scan (event-driven on eating).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr458_hot_meals.test.ts` 7/7: cooked meat by a lit fire -> +5;
unlit fire -> 0; baked potato / bread by a lit fire -> 0; far from fire -> 0; stew counts and the
buff expires after 120 s; tuning in vitals.json. Test note: `evaluate` is imported from
`@engine/core`, NOT from the gameplay index (`G.evaluate` does not exist); lit campfire via
`G.spawnStation(w, Campfire, ...)` + steps (the emitter index picks it up).

## ADR-459: Salt curing and smoking meat — cured meat spoils much slower (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Fresh meat spoiled fast and the only preservation was jerky (and salted fish): no cured
or smoked variants for the meats players actually hunt. The work is mostly data-only recipes on
freshness numbers.

**Decision.** JSON-only. New items in `packages/gameplay/data/items.json` (inserted after jerky /
salted_fish): cured_venison (hunger 30, health 4), cured_poultry (20, 3), cured_prime_cut (40, 6)
with `"sprite": "jerky"`; smoked_fish (hunger 22, thirst -6, health 2) with `"sprite": "salted_fish"`;
all spoilSeconds 14400, maxStack 20. New recipes in `packages/gameplay/data/recipes.json` (jerky
pattern: 2 raw + 1 salt -> 2, campfire, 4 s): cured_venison, cured_poultry, cured_prime_cut;
smoked_fish is the distinct smoking line (fish 2 + salt 1 + wood 1 -> 2, campfire, 4 s).
`ids.lock.json` regenerated (`pnpm --filter @engine/gameplay lock:ids`): new item ids 517–520, new
recipe ids 403–406 (the ADR-457 regen later supplied them to the working tree — the ADR-459 regen had
not persisted). Correction recorded: jerky spoils in 14,400 s, not 1,800 s (an earlier background pass
quoted 1,800 s, wrong).

**Consequences.** Four new preserved foods (three cured meats + smoked fish), all spoiling in 4 hours
instead of the raw meats' fast spoil. No code change, no new sprites (existing sprites reused via
`"sprite"` — the one place in this batch where reuse is the rule, not new art).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr459_curing_smoking.test.ts` 4/4: item defs (spoil 14400,
sprite reuse), recipe defs (ingredients, campfire station, 4 s), full craft-through of cured_venison
and smoked_fish. Test note: `ItemDef` extends Visual — sprite is `it.spriteKey` directly, not
`it.visual.spriteKey`; recipe `station` is the `StationKind` enum, not a string.

## ADR-460: Compost — rotten food on tilled soil fertilises it, like dung (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Rotten food was only trash: it could be eaten (sick) or thrown away, never used. Dung
already fertilises tilled soil; rotten food should take the same path, with no crafted compost item.

**Decision.** `FarmingData` in `packages/gameplay/src/farming.ts` gained `compostFertilizerSeconds:
number` (600, same as bone fertilizer; dung is 900; tuning in `data/farming.json`). `farmUseSystem`:
`rot` added to the fertilizer branch (fertilize with compostFertilizerSeconds, consumes 1 rot on
success, `NothingToTend` + rot kept on bare soil); XpActivity source `"fertilize"` includes rot.
`fertilize()` requires `kind > 0` (planted crops only) — unchanged. Planted crops only (no bare-soil
change), raw `rot` directly (no crafted compost item).

**Consequences.** Rotten food applied to a planted crop fertilises it for 600 s, like dung (900 s) and
bone (600 s). Bare soil is unaffected; the rot is kept when there is nothing to tend.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr460_compost.test.ts` 3/3: rot fertilises a planted crop
(growthMul check needs `G.water()` first — a dry crop returns 0); bare soil keeps the rot; dung
fertilizer still passes (adr352 suite 19/19). Test reuses the adr352 farm setup pattern (TileMap,
`spawnCrop`, `holderWith`, `useHeld` via `G.farmUseSystem`).

## ADR-461: Moon phases — full-moon nights brighter, zombies bolder; new-moon darker (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** The moon had no gameplay effect: zombies hunted the same under a full moon and a new moon.
Brightness already ships (the moon's light is in the renderer); the remaining lever is boldness.

**Decision.** Boldness only (brightness already ships) — the sight-range lever (+25% at full moon), do
not weaken light avoidance. `moonIllumination(day)` + `LUNAR_DAYS = 29.53` duplicated in
`packages/gameplay/src/combat/zombies.ts` (gameplay must not import render);
`moonSightFactor(world)` = 1 + `ai.moonSightMul` x illumination; applied in `acquire()` to the sight
check. `AiTuning` in `packages/gameplay/src/defs.ts` gained `readonly moonSightMul: number`;
`packages/gameplay/data/zombies.json` ai gained `"moonSightMul": 0.25`. No other AiTuning literals
exist, so the required field is safe. Survivors list in `zombieAISystem` is unfiltered (no radius
issue; max moon sight 18x1.25 = 22.5).

**Consequences.** At full moon a zombie sees 25% farther (sight 10 -> 12.5); at new moon, unchanged.
Light avoidance is untouched (zombies still avoid light the same way).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr461_moon_boldness.test.ts` 5/5: walker sight 10, player at
11 tiles — unseen on new-moon night (day 0), seen on full-moon night (day 15, illumination ~0.999),
still unseen at 14 tiles on full moon; adr194 still passes 6/6.

## ADR-462: Wild animals drink and seek shade (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Wild animals never drank and never reacted to heat or rain: they wandered the same in a
heat wave and a storm. Their think tick already runs; the behaviour must hook it, near players only,
with no thirst stat and no directed shade search.

**Decision.** Drink + linger-in-shade only — no directed shade search, no thirst stat, cosmetic only.
`packages/gameplay/src/population.ts`: `AnimalState` gained `Drink = 5`; `animalDrinkTuning()` (ai.json
`tuning.animalDrink`: chance 0.2, radius 12, nearPlayerTiles 40, drinkSeconds [3, 6]; `AiData.tuning`
in `packages/gameplay/src/ai/population.ts` extended); `findDrinkShore(world, x, y, radius)` —
expanding square rings step 1 (1-wide streams are never stepped over; a step-3 grid was first tried
and misses them), first hit wins, goal always land adjacent to water; `shadeLingerAt(world, x, y)` —
raining/Heat + already under cover (`shelterAt` point query: rain < 1 in rain, sun < 1 in heat). Think
branch (in `animalAISystem`, on a separate `"animal.drink"` rng stream so existing wander rolls are
untouched): if near a survivor (THREATS list already built this pass, spatial-index fallback when the
list is capped) and not tame — shade first (linger: Idle, goal = current pos, thinkAt +2–4 s), else
drink roll: adjacent water (`nearWater` from `systems/vitals.ts`) -> Drink in place 3–6 s; else walk
to the nearest shore within radius. Arrival (movement section, `d < 0.1`): a Wander arriving beside
water near a player drinks deterministically (one drink per trip; the next think resumes normal
behaviour) — added after a probe showed drink trips happened but the post-arrival 20% roll usually
failed (the rabbit walked to shore at ticks 768/1152/2522 but never drank in 3000 ticks; after the
fix the probe showed Drink state for 402 ticks). Drink animals don't move
(`state !== Idle && state !== Drink`); anim maps Drink -> `Anim.Drink`. Tame/ridden/led animals were
already skipped above the think branch. Test setup: `animalAISystem` is NOT installed by `makeWorld`/
`installGameplay` — tests add it manually (`w.addSystem("simulation", "gameplay.animalAI",
G.animalAISystem)`); `installPopulation` registers it on the server only.

**Consequences.** Wild animals near a player (within 40 tiles) drink at water and linger under cover
in rain or heat. No thirst stat, no directed shade search, no behaviour change far from players.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr462_animals_drink_shade.test.ts` 7/7: `findDrinkShore`
(11.5, 0.5), too-far radius -> undefined, no water -> undefined, no terrain -> undefined; rabbit
drinks on land (Drink state + `Anim.Drink`, tile != 1) within 6000 ticks; no player -> never drinks;
player at 100 tiles -> never drinks; `shadeLingerAt` (roof+rain true, open+rain false, roof+clear
false, roof+heat true); roofed rabbit lingers in rain (max distance < 1 tile over 60 s; lone roof =
foundation + `roof_flat` level 1, adr312 hut pattern with builder `0 as Entity`) while an open rabbit
wanders > 2 tiles. Test terrain: `new TileMap()` + `w.setResource(G.TerrainRes,
G.terrainFromTileMap(map))` + `map.setTile(x, y, 1)` (tile 1 = water). Rabbit: flee range 7, wander
radius 6 — the player must be 7–40 tiles away (test uses player (0,0), rabbit home (10,0), water
(12,0)).

## ADR-463: Carrion birds — crows circle a fresh kill for a while (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** A fresh kill lay bare: nothing marked it, no scavenger came. Crows exist (crow art, crow
speed 3.2); the death event already fires. The birds must hook the death event, circle on the ground,
and leave when the kill is gone — no flight logic.

**Decision.** Ground-circling only, no flight logic. New component `Carrion` (`{bag: "u32", untilTick:
"u32", angle: "u8"}`, persistent only, server-only) appended to `components.ts` + the append-only
`GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS` list. `AiData.tuning` gained `carrion`; `ai.json` tuning.carrion =
`{crowsPerKill: 2, circleRadius: 2.5, maxSeconds: 120, nearPlayerTiles: 40}`. In `population.ts`:
`carrionTuning()` (defaults 2 / 2.5 / 120 / 40); `installCarrion(world)` subscribes to `Died` —
animal/zombie kills only (not players, not tame pets — `Pet` excluded), near-player gate 40 tiles via
the spatial index; spawns 2 crows (`spawnAnimal(world, "animal_crow", ...)` 1–3 tiles from the death),
sets each crow's `Animal.homeX/homeY` to the death position (circle the kill, not the spawn spot),
adopts the kill's loot bag at spawn if already present (the dead sweep in `animalAISystem` runs after
`gameplay.death` in the same tick, before deferred `Died` delivery — verified from
`GAMEPLAY_SYSTEM_ORDER` in `install.ts`). Think branch in `animalAISystem`: carrion check runs FIRST
(before drink/shade) — expiry checked on the crow's own think ticks only, never by a global scan:
destroy if `tick >= untilTick` or the adopted bag is no longer alive; else adopt a `LootBag` within 4
tiles of home if none adopted; else set the next circle goal (angle +43/256 ≈ 60 deg per think, radius
2.5 around the bag or the death spot). Arrival-drink excluded for carrion crows (`!world.has(e,
Carrion)` in the arrival branch). Wired in `install.ts` next to `installLightning` /
`installSmokeMarkers`. Rabbit loot is guaranteed (raw_meat chance 1 in ai.json), so the bag test is
deterministic.

**Consequences.** A fresh animal/zombie kill near a player draws 2 crows that circle it on the ground
for up to 120 s, leaving when the bag is taken/destroyed or the time expires. No flight, no new scan
(expiry is checked on the crow's own think ticks only).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr463_carrion_birds.test.ts` 7/7: tuning defaults; kill near
player -> 2 crows, bag adopted, home = death pos; crows circle 60 s (moved > 2 tiles, stayed < 6 from
the kill, still alive); cap expiry (gone by 150 s); bag destroyed -> crows leave at next think (<= 200
ticks); far kill (100 tiles) -> no crows (and the rabbit really died); player death -> no crows
(player really died).

## ADR-465: Wind that does things — smoke drifts, fire fans downwind, boats catch a tailwind, wind dries clothes (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Wind state already shipped (core `Weather` carries `windDir`/`windSpeed`; Windy rolls in
fall/spring) but did almost nothing gameplay-visible: it dried ground (ADR-449) and chilled bodies
(ADR-312), and the renderer swayed sprites with it — but smoke ignored it, fire spread isotropically,
boats were wind-blind, and wet clothes dried at the same rate in a gale as in calm air. The sailboat
is a separate vehicle (ADR-479); this ADR is the wind itself.

**Decision.** Four hooks, all riding systems that already run. (1) Smoke drift (render): `BurningFx`
and `HearthFx` take an optional world-space wind vector; smoke particles gain `wind * 0.6` tiles/s
(wind already scaled by `windSpeed/refSpeed` by the caller); embers keep their radial spread.
`IsoRenderer` passes the vector from `readWind` (style-default fallback, same as the sway wind).
Canvas2D keeps radial smoke — its `hearthParticles` path is separate, WebGL2 only in v1. (2) Fire
fanning (sim): new pure `windSpreadFactor(windDir, windSpeed, from, to)` in `pvp_pieces.ts` —
`spreadChance * (1 + mul * cos(angle - windDir))`, clamped `[minMul, maxMul]`, factor 1 below
`windFan.minSpeed`; knobs in `data/fire.json` (`windFan: {minSpeed: 2, mul: 1, minMul: 0.1, maxMul:
2}`). `burningSystem` multiplies its spread roll by it. ADR-468 reuses the same helper. (3) Boats:
new pure `boatWindBonus(windDir, windSpeed, heading, isMotor)` in `vehicles.ts` — a following wind
(within 45° of heading) adds up to +25% to maxSpeed at windSpeed 12 (motorboats half, +12.5%), any
wind adds a leeward drift of `windSpeed * 0.02` tiles/s while underway; knobs in `VEHICLE_TUNING`.
`stepVehicleKinematics` takes an optional `windMul` (default 1) on its speed target; `stepPowered`
applies the bonus + drift for boats only, after the at-rest early return (a parked boat does not
drift), and the drifted position still goes through the pose-blocked check. (4) Body drying: the
`exposureSystem` dry branch multiplies the dry rate by `(1 + surface.windDryMul * windSpeed /
surface.windDryRefSpeed)` when unsheltered from wind (`sh.wind > 0`); new data knob
`surface.windDryRefSpeed: 12` in `data/environment.json` (+ `defs.ts` surface interface).

**Consequences.** Smoke visibly bends downwind; a fire in a gale spreads downwind twice as fast and
barely spreads upwind; a canoe with the wind behind it is ~25% faster and slides leeward; wet clothes
dry 1.5× faster in a 12-speed wind. No new per-tick scan, no new per-frame work, no new state —
the per-frame smoke loop and the 1 s fire check already ran. Map smoke markers (ADR-453) do not bend
(they sit at the fire's fixed position).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr465_wind.test.ts` 13/13: spread factor calm/downwind/
upwind/crosswind/clamp/same-tile; boat bonus tailwind +25% paddle / +12.5% motor / headwind none /
45° gate / speed scaling / calm none; kinematics windMul raises the speed target 1.25×; wind drying
60 s: windy 0.40 vs calm 0.70 wetness (banded `dryWetness` math). `packages/render/test/adr465_wind.test.ts`
2/2: hearth smoke gains exactly `wind * 0.6` per particle with a deterministic rnd sequence, embers
unchanged; burning-piece smoke drifts the same way.

## ADR-466: Snow that piles up — accumulation, slowing, melt (SurVivaZ)

Snow depth is one `u8` per chunk (0..255 = 0..~30 cm) on the existing `ChunkSurface`, written by
the existing `chunkSurfaceSystem` pass (every 20 ticks, 1 s): +0.02 u8/s at intensity 1 while it
snows (a 3-minute blizzard at intensity 1 lays ~7 units, ~1 cm; a full winter of storms reaches
deep snow), −0.01 u8/s when the seasonal base temperature is above freezing, and each melted
unit adds 0.5 units to chunk wetness — spring is mud season, by design. Deep snow slows
walking off-path: 0.8× at depth ≥ 64 (~7–8 cm), 0.7× at depth ≥ 160 (~19 cm); roads stay fast
(the same `roadSurfaceAt == None` guard as mud) and frozen water is exempt (walking on ice is
already walk speed — the snow multiplier skips tiles where `isFrozenWaterAt` is true, so ice
travel is never double-slowed). Snow does not accumulate on chunks whose centre is water (one
tile read per chunk per pass) — a lake chunk stays a lake. No new art: depth is numeric, and
the existing global snow blanket (season shader, roof snow, snowcaps) already reads as snow on
the ground; the client already receives `ChunkSurface` by replication, so a later depth visual
needs no new plumbing.

The one honest cost is stored state — unlike ADR-450 ice (a pure function of the season mean),
accumulation is history, so it needs the `snow` field. Two implementation notes. (1) The
rates are far below one u8 unit per pass, so the pass carries the fraction in a runtime-only
`SnowRemainderRes` map (`{snow, wet}` per surface entity, never persisted or replicated);
only whole units reach the component. A reload loses at most <1 snow unit and <1 wetness unit
per chunk. Entries are deleted when their surface despawns and pruned in the pass. The melt's
wetness share is released through the same remainder (2 melted snow units = 1 wetness unit),
and the release is a separate write AFTER the pass's rain/dry update — if it were folded into
the same delta, the same pass's drying would eat it and a melted drift would never actually
wet the ground. (2) Float precision: 100 passes of −0.01 lands on 98.99999999999999, and a
bare `Math.floor` reads 98 instead of 99 — the floor carries a +1e-9 epsilon (and the
remainder is clamped to ≥ 0), which absorbs error within 1e-9 of an integer. Found by the
melt test failing, not by inspection.

Knobs: `environment.json` `surface.snowPerSec: 0.02`, `meltPerSec: 0.01`, `meltWetMul: 0.5`;
`movement.json` `snowSlowThreshold: 64`, `snowSlowMul: 0.8`, `snowDeepThreshold: 160`,
`snowDeepMul: 0.7`. Melt needs BOTH gates: seasonal base temperature above freezing AND the
waters not frozen (`isWaterFrozen` — the season-mean predicate, so during the late-fall /
early-spring blends the ground holds its snow even on a mild day). Ice thaws by season mean,
snow melts by temperature + time; no code coupling between the two, just the ordering note
(melt snow first, ice follows). Spring melt is the natural flood trigger — if ADR-467's flood
seeds from heavy rain, "spring melt" is a second seed to decide there, not here; this ADR only
guarantees melt produces wetness, not flood water. Footprints (ADR-455) still stamp on the
global season cover ≥ 0.5; switching the stamp condition to chunk depth is a one-line change
left for later, not required.

Tests: `packages/gameplay/test/adr466_snow.test.ts` 12/12 — `chunkSnowAt` reads / 0 with no
surface; slowdown tiers 0/63 → 1.0, 64/159 → 0.8, 160/255 → 0.7; mud + snow stack
0.85 × 0.7 = 0.595; dirt path in deep snow stays 1.1×; frozen water exempt (winter lake
1.0×, same tile in summer 0.7×); accumulation exactly 1 unit per 50 passes at intensity 1
(and 2 at 100, 3 at 150 — the fraction is not lost); intensity scaling (0.5 → 1 per 100
passes) and blizzards lay snow at the same intensity rate as snow (no separate multiplier);
water-centre chunk stays 0 while a land-centre chunk reaches 2; cap 255; melt 100 → 99 in
100 warm passes and 98 + wetness 1/255 in 200 (2 melted = 1 wetness); no melt below freezing;
clear winter weather neither accumulates nor melts. Revert check: 11/12 fail on pre-change
code (the 1 pass is the dirt-path control — roads were already fast). ADR-449 mud 9/9 and
ADR-450 ice 7/7 still pass (the wetness path is unchanged when there is no snow).

## ADR-467: Rivers that flood — heavy rain and spring melt swell sea-level water onto low ground, then it recedes gradually (SurVivaZ)

- **Status:** Implemented 2026-11-20. Tracey's decision overrules the scope's compliant redesign
  (permanent flood water, option 1): **floods MUST RECEDE OVER TIME — gradual slow drain over
  in-game time, never a single-step clear after the flood.** The flood-tile store tracks the
  gradual recession; flood water is natural-water encoded so it freezes; elevated-lake discs and
  spillway corridors are excluded (waterfall rule). The scope's split-out seasonal lake-level half
  is folded into this ADR (spring +1 tile outward, summer −1 tile inward) to keep the batch at
  15 ADRs. Drain rate is a data knob (`data/flood.json`).
- **Store (`src/flood.ts`, `components.ts`):** one persistent `FloodTile` entity per flooded tile,
  at the tile centre (the `TerrainEdit` pattern): `origTile` (the tile id before flooding, restored
  on drain — the raw height is the bed level and never changes), `drainTick` (when the tile starts
  draining; u32 max = never, for a seasonal tile before summer), `kind` (0 = storm flood,
  1 = seasonal spring band), `dist` (distance from the original water, 1..3). Persistent (a reload
  keeps the flood and its drain schedule) but not networked — the client sees the water through
  the terrain tilemap, and the drain is server-side state. A runtime-only `FloodRes` holds the
  seeded frontier (`tkey -> {dist, kind}`) and the last season seen; it is lost on restart (the
  flood stops advancing, but already-flooded tiles still drain on schedule).
- **Seed (event-driven, no new per-tick scan):** `installFlood` subscribes to `WeatherChanged` (the
  ADR-451 pattern); on a change to Rain (intensity >= `rainIntensityMin` 0.7) or Storm it seeds
  the shore band (land adjacent to original sea-level water, bed <= surface) around each living
  survivor (`seedRadius` 96). The seed scan uses a cheap predicate (`seedable`: O(1) tile lookups
  only — the spatial-index occupancy check runs only at flood time, on the <=64 tiles the advance
  actually processes). Spring melt seeds the same band as a seasonal tile on the season change
  to Spring (the ADR-466 melt raises wetness; the spring season change floods the shore band).
- **Advance (`floodSystem`, every `TERRAIN.flowEveryTicks` = 8 ticks, the flow cadence):** floods
  seeded tiles one tile per step outward, bounded at `TERRAIN.flowPerStep` (64) per step and
  `maxDistance` (3) tiles from the original shoreline. Flood water is NATURAL water (`WATER_TILE`
  with the bed as its raw height — the raw height never changes, so it renders flat at surface 0
  and freezes in winter, ADR-450), never flow-encoded. A tile with a piece / node / crop on it
  never floods (`terrainTileBlocked`, the flow system's occupancy rule, exported from `terrain.ts`
  so the flood reuses it instead of duplicating it); a dug tile belongs to the dug flow. Distance
  is Manhattan, via the 4-neighbour advance (the flow system's neighbour rule).
- **Recession (gradual, never a single-step clear):** storm tiles drain `drainAfterSeconds` (900 s
  = 6 game-hours) after flooding, outermost first (one distance step every `drainStepSeconds`
  300 s = 2 game-hours), at most `drainPerStep` (16) per step — a 3-tile flood shrinks back
  toward the river over 4 game-hours. Seasonal tiles drain in summer, hash-staggered over
  `seasonalDrainDays` (2 game-days), so the spring band thins gradually instead of vanishing at
  once. After recession the ground is wet (chunk wetness 1.0) so the flood leaves mud behind
  (ADR-449). A tile a player fills with earth while flooded drops its flood record (the player's
  edit stands); a tile whose chunk unloaded defers its drain until the chunk loads again (the
  record persists).
- **Seasonal lake levels (folded in):** on the season change to Spring, the +1 shore band floods
  as seasonal tiles (1 tile only — no advance); on the change to Summer, their drainTick is set
  (hash-staggered over `seasonalDrainDays`); fall/winter do nothing. The season is read via
  `worldSeason` on the flood cadence (a pure function of the day count, no scan).
- **Waterfall rule (ADR-383/386):** the flood only spreads from sea-level water (surface 0) and
  never floods a tile adjacent to water whose surface is not 0. An elevated lake and its spillway
  are flow-encoded at their level (`flowWaterRaw`), so `waterSurfaceAt` reads them above 0 and
  the flood stops at least one tile short — it can never connect the two levels. The seed also
  counts ORIGINAL water only (a tile already flooded by an earlier storm is not a source), so a
  second storm during a recession cannot push the flood past the 3-tile cap.
- **Design note:** the flood rides the flow system's cadence and budget shape (8 ticks, 64/step)
  with its own frontier, as a separate `gameplay.flood` system — it does not share the dug flow's
  `FlowRes.frontier` Set, so the two never double-process a tile and the flood code stays in one
  file (`flood.ts`) with no import cycle (`terrain.ts` does not import it; the wiring is in
  `install.ts`). The per-step cost is the same bounded shape as the dug flow.
- **Limits (v1):** seeding is around living survivors (a river far from any player does not flood
  until a player is near it in a storm); a restart mid-storm loses the seeded frontier; the
  spring band is seeded near players, not world-wide. A boat can float onto a flooded field in a
  storm and beach when it recedes (shallow water, `boatWaterMul` 0.55 shallows / 0 land).
- **Tests (`packages/gameplay/test/adr467_floods.test.ts`, 9/9, revert 9/9 fail with the seed +
  advance neutered):** heavy rain seeds the shore and the flood advances to 3 tiles then stops
  (24 tiles; dist-4 stays land; drain stagger outermost-first: dist 1 drains 2 steps after
  dist 3); light rain (0.5) does not seed; a storm seeds at any intensity; high ground (bed 2)
  never floods; a tile with a tree on it never floods and the tree survives; the recession is
  gradual (jumping past the dist-3 drain recedes only the outer ring, the inner rings stay
  flooded; jumping past dist-1 clears it) and leaves the ground wet (wetness 1.0); flood water
  freezes in winter like the lake (`isFrozenWaterAt` true, `isFlowWater` false); the waterfall
  rule (a tile between the lake and a flow-encoded spillway at level 5 never floods, the rest of
  the shore does); seasonal lake levels (spring floods the +1 band as seasonal with drainTick
  never, summer schedules the drain, jumping past the window clears it); a second storm during
  a recession does not push past the cap (still 24 tiles). Test notes: the season check runs
  before the advance in `floodSystem` so a spring band seeds and floods in the same call; the
  seasonal drainTick is `tick + 1 + hash % window` (never in the same call that schedules it).

## ADR-468: Wildfire — fire on vegetation and across terrain (SurVivaZ)

Date: 2026-11-19. Status: implemented (this batch). Scope §4.

Decision: trees, fruit trees and dry grass can burn; a burning vegetation node spreads to
nearby fuel and, when it burns out, depletes like a harvested node (tree → stump for
`stumpSeconds`, then regrows; grass → gone for its respawn). Grove depletion is the stand-in
for a true spreading forest fire — the scope's v1 default, and what this ADR ships: a fire
that runs across a grove and leaves it as stumps that regrow is a visible, bounded wildfire,
not a permanent deforestation event.

Mechanics:
- Fuel predicate `isVegetationFuel(world, kind)` (exported pure, `pvp_pieces.ts`): axe trees
  except `tree_stump`, plus the five fruit trees and `fiber_grass` (explicit non-axe set).
  Berry bushes, cotton/fiber bushes, stumps and `rotten_stump` do NOT burn in v1; crops are a
  separate kind (Crop/GrownPlant, not ResourceNode) and do not burn either.
- `ignite()` gate: a fuel node may ignite (a Burning node decays and depletes — see below);
  anything else still needs BuildPiece or Health. `applyDamage` on a healthless entity no-ops
  safely, but the node branch skips the call for clarity.
- `burningSystem` node branch: no damage (no Health); the node decays 16 per check (same as
  creatures) and, at intensity 0, `burnOutNode` extinguishes it FIRST and then depletes it via
  `depleteNode` (same end state as harvesting: tree → stump + `NodeRegrow` with the def's
  respawn; grass → stumpTicks 0, no stump). Extinguish-before-deplete matters because
  `depleteNode` destroys the entity.
- Spread (node→node only): chance `vegetation.spreadChance` (0.08) × dryness
  `(1 - chunkWetnessAt(candidate tile))` × the ADR-465 `windSpreadFactor` (same shared
  directional factor the piece spread uses — ADR-465's contract: wind first, wildfire second).
  Spread children are plain fires via `ignite()` — never `LightningFire` — so rain quenches
  them even when the parent is an exempt lightning fire.
- Cap: at most `vegetation.maxBurning` (128) concurrently burning vegetation nodes, counted
  once per check from the `Burning` snapshot and incremented on each successful spread ignite,
  so the cap holds within the pass; the spread branch skips entirely once it is reached.
  A dry summer cannot DoS the sim with a runaway fire. Tuning lives in `data/fire.json`
  (`vegetation: { spreadRadius: 2.0, spreadChance: 0.08, maxBurning: 128 }`,
  `FireTuning.vegetation`).
- Lightning (ADR-451 changed): the scope assumes a lightning-struck tree ignites ("the
  lightning-ignited tree keeps the quench exemption", "what one strike can become"), but
  ADR-451's code *depleted* the struck tree immediately — so no burning node would ever
  exist to spread from. This ADR resolves the contradiction the way the scope's design
  assumes: `resolveLightningStrike` now calls `igniteLightning` on the struck tree instead
  of depleting it outright — the tree burns ~8 s (128 / 16 per check), can spread as a
  wildfire, and depletes to a stump when it burns out (the same end state ADR-451's scorch
  produced, now with a visible fire that can spread). A stump is already burnt, so
  `tree_stump` is excluded from the lightning target filter (the old filter,
  `requiredTool === Axe && !oneShot`, matched it, and the new ignite would refuse it — no
  strike would have fired at all).
- Rendering: no render change. `BurningFx.update` already handles a Burning entity with no
  BuildPiece (the `bp` lookup is optional; the piece-scale line returns a 1×1 footprint), so
  a burning tree renders the same flame/smoke it would have rendered as a burning creature
  — the flame sits on the node. That is the scope's §4 default (fire rendering "just works").
- Performance: no new per-tick scan. The spread is a `nearby()` query inside the existing
  1 s fire check, only for burning nodes; the cap is a snapshot count, not a scan.

Tests: `packages/gameplay/test/adr468_wildfire.test.ts` — 12 tests. Fuel predicate
(all axe/fruit trees + grass true; stumps, bushes, unknown kind false); ignite gate (tree
and grass ignite at 128, stump and berry bush refuse); tree decay 16/check → depletes at
check 8 to a stump `NodeRegrow`; grass burns out with no stump; rain quenches a vegetation
fire in ~3 checks (128 → 72 → 16 → 0); a lightning-ignited tree is exempt from storm quench
(after 7 checks in a storm still lit at intensity 16 = 128 − 7×16, where a plain fire would
have burnt out at check 3); spread dry + calm (seed 80, tick-20 draw 0.0056 < 0.08); soaked
ground throttles spread (seed 73, draw 0.0540: spreads dry at 0.08, not at wetness 0.5 /
chance 0.04); wind fans spread (seed 55, draw 0.1110: spreads downwind at 0.16, not calm at
0.08 or upwind at 0.008); a spread child in a storm is quenched (no `LightningFire`) and
burns out in ~3 checks while the exempt parent still burns; the cap (128 burning trees + 1
neighbour: the neighbour does not ignite, 128 Burning total); `fire.json` tuning pins.
The spread seeds were probed once — the `rngFor("fire.spread", entity)` stream is hashed
from (seed, tick, key, entity), so the draw that matters is the one at tick 20, the first
burning check, not the one at tick 0 (an earlier probe at tick 0 gave different draws and
three spread tests failed until the probe was redone at tick 20; creation order player →
burning tree → neighbour must be preserved so the burning tree is entity 2). Revert check:
all 12 ADR-468 tests fail on pre-change code (stash of `fire.json` + `pvp_pieces.ts` only);
the two updated ADR-451 tree tests also fail on pre-change code (14 failed / 5 passed over
the two files — the 5 passing are the ADR-451 non-tree controls).
Updated ADR-451 tests (`adr451_lightning.test.ts`): the tree-strike test now asserts the
tree is alive + burning + `LightningFire` immediately and depletes to a stump `NodeRegrow`
after 8 burning checks; the storm test asserts exactly one tree ignites (the ring trees are
~6 tiles apart, past the 2.0 spread radius, so the fire cannot spread) and it depletes
after 10 s. No other ADR-451 behaviour changed (piece strikes, one strike per storm,
near-survivor placement, rain quench of pieces — all still pass).

Honest cuts / follow-ups (not built):
- Piece→node spread: a burning structure does NOT ignite nearby vegetation in v1
  (node→node only). Recorded as a follow-up in REPORT.md.
- A burning tree's flame renders at the node's 1×1 footprint (the existing `BurningFx`
  null-piece path) — no tree-scale flame art was added; the fire is visible, the flame is
  not scaled to the canopy. If Tracey wants a bigger flame on trees, that is a render follow-up.
- Lightning can still start a wildfire that burns a whole grove to stumps in a dry summer —
  bounded by the 128 cap and by rain, and stumps regrow; whether a grove-fire of that size
  feels right in play is a live play-test question, not a bench one.

## ADR-469: Living forests — wild trees regrow through saplings, saplings can die of drought, lightning fells a grove and leaves fallen logs (SurVivaZ)

- **Status:** Implemented 2026-11-20. Tracey's decision was DEFAULT (no giants; a mature tree is
  the endpoint). Wild regrow goes through sapling stages (no more instant full-size wild trees);
  regrow timing reuses `respawnSeconds` per species, then the planted `growSeconds` (1,680–2,400 s)
  to maturity; wild saplings CAN die of drought (2 in-game days without rain/water, same clock as
  crops); a fallen log spawns on lightning-felled trees only (ADR-451 path); axe-felled trees do
  not leave one; lightning grove: a strike depletes the nearest tree plus other axe-trees within
  3 tiles; `strikesPerStorm` stays 1; giants cut; true spreading forest fire is out of scope.
- **Wild sapling regrow (`systems/gathering.ts`, `farming.ts`):** `respawnSystem` now asks
  `wildSaplingKind(def.key)` — the 1-based plantable kind whose `becomes` is that tree, or 0 —
  and spawns a `Crop` (sapling, stage 0) at the regrow spot instead of a full `ResourceNode`.
  `cropGrowthSystem` grows it through the 3 sapling stages into the mature node (`p.becomes` +
  `GrownPlant`). 11 tree saplings in `data/farming.json` (oak 2,400 s, pine 1,800 s, birch
  1,680 s, maple 2,160 s, willow 1,800 s, palm 1,920 s, apple 1,800 s, pear 1,800 s, cherry
  1,680 s, orange 2,040 s, peach 1,800 s). **Cut: generic `tree` and `resin_tree` have no
  sapling** (their keys never appear as a plantable `becomes`) — they keep instant full-size
  regrow; mapping generic `tree` to an oak sapling would change the species mix over time, and
  a new generic sapling would be new art. No new art was added.
- **Drought death is already built in:** in `cropGrowthSystem`, `if (world.tick > wut + drought)`
  — for `p.type === "crop"` it reverts to bare tilled soil; otherwise (sapling/bush) it DESTROYS
  the entity and emits `PlantDied`. A wild sapling that dries out dies with no change needed.
  Rain re-waters (`wut = tick + wateredSeconds`); water beside the plant also waters. Frost only
  kills `p.type === "crop"` in the Crop loop; saplings are not frost-killed there (the ResourceNode
  frost pass kills fruit trees via `frostKillsNode` — fruit trees die, timber trees and berry
  bushes survive).
- **Chunk tracking (`world.ts`):** `swapChunkNode` moved from `gathering.ts` to `world.ts` (where
  `ChunkNodes` lives) and exported, so both `gathering.ts` and `farming.ts` import it with no
  cycle. `cropGrowthSystem` calls `swapChunkNode(world, e, node)` at maturity, so a wild
  sapling's matured node inherits its chunk tracking. `despawnChunkNodes` now also destroys
  Crops in the chunk list (only wild saplings are ever added — planted crops are never added —
  so any Crop in the list is wild by construction). Consequence: growth progress is lost on
  chunk unload, same as a partially-gathered node resetting on reload.
- **Lightning grove + fallen log (`combat/pvp_pieces.ts`):** in `resolveLightningStrike`, the
  strike now ignites the nearest tree PLUS the other axe-trees within 3 tiles of it (filter, not
  break — the list is sorted by distance to the strike point, not to the nearest tree).
  `strikesPerStorm` stays 1 (one strike igniting several trees). In `burningSystem`, the
  `LightningFire` flag is captured before `extinguish` removes it and passed to `burnOutNode`
  (new optional `struck` param); a lightning-felled tree spawns a `fallen_log` at its position
  via `spawnResourceNode` (full capacity 5, respawnSeconds 600). Wildfire-spread trees do NOT
  leave logs (they carry no `LightningFire`); axe-felled trees do not either. The strike now
  IGNITES the tree (ADR-468) instead of scorching it outright — it burns ~8 s and depletes to a
  stump when it burns out, which calls `depleteNode` (stump + regrow).
- **Wildfire regrow is automatic:** trees depleted by wildfire go through `depleteNode` →
  `NodeRegrow` → `respawnSystem` → sapling, with no extra work (scope: "trees depleted by
  wildfire regrow through saplings with no extra work here").
- **Scope corrections:** the scope's `wildlife.ts` / `migrationSystem` / `migrationDirectionFor` /
  `movePlan` do not exist — the real system is `animalAISystem` in `packages/gameplay/src/population.ts`
  plus the tamed graze path in `skills/husbandry.ts` (not used here); `respawnSystem` is in
  `systems/gathering.ts`, `cropGrowthSystem` in `farming.ts`. The import direction is safe:
  `gathering.ts` → `systems/vitals.ts` → `farming.ts` already exists, so `gathering.ts`
  importing `spawnCrop`/`wildSaplingKind` from `farming.ts` creates no new cycle.
- **Tests (`packages/gameplay/test/adr469_forests.test.ts`, 7/7, revert 7/7 fail):** a depleted
  oak regrows as a stage-0 sapling, grows through stages 0/1/2, and matures into an oak tree
  with `GrownPlant` at the same position (no fallen log); a wild sapling past the 2-day drought
  clock dies with `PlantDied` while a watered one survives; a strike ignites the nearest tree
  plus the axe-trees within 3 tiles and leaves the 4-tile trees unlit; a lightning-felled tree
  leaves a fallen log (full capacity 5) at its position when it burns out; a wildfire-burned
  tree leaves none; generic `tree` and `resin_tree` keep instant full-size regrow; chunk
  tracking — a wild sapling in the chunk list despawns on unload, and its matured node inherits
  the list entry. Test notes: `waterUntilTick` is u32, so a negative "past" value wraps to a
  huge future tick — the drought test sets it to 1 and jumps the world clock past the 2-day
  drought (the ADR-471 tick-jump pattern); `emit` is deferred, so the `PlantDied` delivery
  needs a step after `cropGrowthSystem`.

## ADR-470: Eating well matters — a varied diet earns a bonus, eating the same food carries no penalty (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Freshness scaling shipped; no variety tracking, no food grouping, and no "same food =
weaker" effect existed anywhere. Tracey decided the shape: a bonus for a varied diet (1.1× for 4+
food groups), with NO penalty for eating the same food in a row (1.0× floor) — overruling the
scope's penalty-only default.

**Decision.** One new event-only component, `RecentFoods` (diet-group indices of the last 8 foods
eaten, oldest first, capped at RECENT_MAX = 8; networked + persistent, appended to
GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS after Well) — a plain queue, not a deduped list, so an old group falls off once
8 newer eats have passed. Groups are data in `vitals.json` `dietGroups` (6 groups: meat, fish,
fruit, vegetable, grain, dairy; 94 foods), following the `hotMeals.items` precedent; drinks,
medicines and pet treats are not listed and never count. At the successful-eat point in
`consumeSystem`, the eaten item's group is recorded (`recordRecentFood`) and the distinct-group
count over the window is folded into the nutrition multiplier `k` next to `stage.nutritionMul`: 4+
groups → 1.1×, fewer → 1.0×. Health (`kh`) is untouched. Bots eat through the same `consumeSystem`
path, so they get variety for free.

**Consequences.** A varied diet pays 10% more hunger per eat once 4 groups are in the window; a
monotonous diet is never punished. The window is the last 8 eats — 8 same-group eats push the old
groups out and the bonus lapses.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr470_diet.test.ts` 7/7: bonus on the 4th distinct group
and only then; same food 8× stays 1.0×; drinks and tonics never count; window expiry after 8
same-group eats; queue order/cap; data coverage (every real food in exactly one group, 94 foods;
drinks/medicines/pet treats in none); `dietGroupOf` mapping. Revert check: 7/7 fail on pre-change
code.

## ADR-471: Water you can trust — river risk + wells run low (SurVivaZ)

Drinking straight from a tile (or sipping a raw container) is no longer one flat rate: the
dysentery chance now depends on the water feature under the drinker, read through the existing
`waterFeatureAt` layout — a river is 0.05, a lake or pond keeps the old flat 0.025, an elevated
or great lake is 0.01, and anything else (biome sea, a stray puddle) falls back to the flat
rate. And wells run low: a well piece holds 12 sips, rain recharges +1 sip per 60 s of rain,
and past the 2-day drought clock a well loses 2 sips per further dry day. Drawing at a well
swaps a raw container for its well variant, and well water never rolls dysentery.

Two scope assumptions were wrong on this tree and the build corrects them. First, the scope
says the `WeatherChanged` event carries the rain's duration in `ticks` — it does not: `ticks`
is the INCOMING weather's duration (`environment.ts`), so the recharge is tracked by a
runtime-only `WellWaterRes` resource that records the rain-start tick on `to = Rain/Storm`
and computes the duration when the rain ends. Second, the scope flags checking whether a well
is a lightning target — it is not: `fire.json` `flammableTiers` is `[0, 1]` and the well piece
is tier 2, so no exclusion was needed. `waterFeatureAt` classification is exact in the
starter region and approximate far out (scope caveat, accepted: the drinker's own tile is
checked first, then the 8 neighbours, so the rate follows the water you are actually drinking
from).

Design. New module `packages/gameplay/src/wells.ts`: pure `drinkWaterChance(world, x, y)`
(the layout is computed once per call, not once per tile); new `Well {level: u8}` component
(networked + persistent, appended to `GAMEPLAY_COMPONENTS` after `Carrion`); `wellsOf` /
`nearestWell` / `wellLevel` / `setWellLevel` (lazy-attach at full on first touch, so a well
stamped, placed or loaded before this ADR starts full — no migration); `drawFromWell` (nearest
well within `containerReach + rangeSlack`, the same reach the Boil action uses; the well loses
exactly the sips drawn; a raw container becomes its well variant, a boiled or well container
stays itself); `wellDryCheck` (called from the top of `weatherSystem`, after the authority
guard and before the early return while weather is still running — a few integer comparisons
per tick, the well enumeration only runs on a crossed dry-day boundary); `installWells`
(subscribed on `WeatherChanged` next to `installLightning`). The dry clock is the same
`dayLengthTicks` the 2-day `droughtTicks` crop clock is built from, read directly instead of
importing `farming.ts` — importing it would close a wells → farming → vitals → wells cycle
(`farming.ts` imports `nearWater` from `vitals.ts`, which imports `wells.ts`).

Items. Four raw containers gain `wellTo` (`items.json`); four new well variants
(`well_waterskin`, `well_water_flask`, `well_canteen`, `well_water_bottle`, ids 523–526) with
the same sips/food/weight as their raw form, `safeWater: true`, and `"sprite"` set to the raw
key — no new art, the well variant draws the raw container. `ItemDef` gains `safeWater`,
`wellTarget`, `wellSource`; `RawItem` gains `safeWater?`, `wellTo?`; the loader resolves the
well pairs the same way as the boil pairs and validates them (`wellTo` needs sips; a safe
variant cannot itself map or be boiled). `fillContainer` reverts a treated container on a
refill with untreated water via `boilSource || wellSource`.

Wiring. `vitals.ts` `consumeSystem`: the tile-drink roll uses `drinkWaterChance` at the
drinker's position; the container-sip roll skips `safeWater` containers; the empty-container
branch tries the well draw on dry land when authority (`drawFromWell`) and fails `Empty`
when there is no well in reach or the nearest well is dry. `install.ts` calls
`installWells(world)` after `installCarrion`. Knobs in `packages/gameplay/data`: `diseases.json`
`causes.riverWaterChance: 0.05`, `causes.isolatedWaterChance: 0.01` (lake/pond keep
`rawWaterChance: 0.025`); `environment.json` `wells: {capacity: 12, rainSecondsPerSip: 60,
dryDrainSipsPerDay: 2}`.

Honest cuts. (1) The client renders no text for failed Uses today, so the "Well is dry"
prompt is a client follow-up, not shipped in v1 — the sim emits `ConsumeFailed: Empty`
(testable). (2) The rain/drought clock is runtime-only: it resets on reload, so rain already
falling at load recharges nothing when it ends, and a world loaded already past the drought
clock drains one 2-sip lump (one day's worth, never a catch-up lump for days missed across a
reload). (3) Animals do NOT drink from wells and wells do NOT water crops (v1 defaults).
(4) Low-water well frames (a visual cue for a running-low well) stay a follow-up — v1 is
text-only (the level replicates to the client via the `Well` component for a later HUD read).
(5) A well's level is per-piece, not per-settlement: two wells side by side are two separate
12-sip tanks.

Tests: `packages/gameplay/test/adr471_water.test.ts` 12/12 — drinkWaterChance rates (river
0.05, lake/pond 0.025, elevated 0.01, land fallback); tile-drink dysentery per kind with
deterministic all-1 / all-0 cause tables (river contracts, lake and isolated do not; isolated
contracts when its chance is 1, river does not); well-pair defs (wellTarget/safeWater/
wellSource/sips/spriteKey); draw swaps to the well variant and drops the level 12 → 9 (3
sips); boiled stays boiled; dry well fails Empty; no well in reach fails Empty; rain
recharges +1 per 60 s capped at capacity and 30 s recharges nothing; dry drain 12 → 10 at
day 2, no second drain the same day, 10 → 8 at day 3; well water never rolls dysentery while
raw water does (same all-1 table); refill at untreated water reverts a well container to raw.
Revert check: 11/12 fail on pre-change code (the 1 pass is the no-well-in-reach control,
which is the old behaviour on dry land). `task13_diseases.test.ts` 14/14 (its causes literal
gains the two new fields). Two test facts learned: `addItem` gives a FULL container
(durability = sips), so the draw/refill tests empty the slot via the slots view first; and
there is no great lake within 256 tiles of the origin on seed 42, so the great-lake rate is
covered by the elevated lake through the shared `elevatedLake || greatLake` branch.
`world.set` requires the component already attached — the lazy attach uses `world.add` and
single-field writes use `world.setField`.

## ADR-472: Cold that bites — wet x wind synergy, faster drain in the cold-soaked-gale, and the ADR-458 hot-meal wiring fix (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Felt temperature already subtracted wet chill and wind chill, and dry layers already
mattered — but the two penalties were purely additive (no interaction), and cold drained body
temperature at the same rate whether the victim was dry in still air or soaked in a gale. Worse,
the ADR-458 counterplay — eat a hot meal by the fire, feel warmer — did nothing in live play: the
Insulation +5 buff was written at eat time and never evaluated by any production code.

**Decision.** Three changes, all on lines that already run. (1) Synergy: the felt formula gains
`− windChillPerSpeed × √windSpeed × wet × windWetSynergyMul` (data knob in `environment.json`,
0.5; soaked in a 12-speed gale ≈ −2.6 °C on top of the existing −6 wet / −5.2 wind). Walls block
it like the wind term (`sh.wind`). (2) Bite: in `vitalsSystem`, when felt < `coldBuffBelow` (10 °C
— the dead knob in `environment.json`, zero uses until now, wired rather than adding a new one)
