AND wetness ≥ 0.7 AND windSpeed ≥ 8, `bodyTempChangePerDegreePerSec` is multiplied by
`coldDrain.mul` (1.5; `wetMin` / `windMin` / `mul` in `vitals.json`). All three conditions, not any
one. The bite only speeds arrival at the freezing tier — no second damage channel; hypothermia at
body ≤ 35 °C (`exposureDps` 2.0) stays the only cold damage. (3) ADR-458 fix: `exposureSystem`
evaluates the Buffs stack into the worn-gear insulation —
`evaluate(world, e, Buffs, Stat.Insulation, ins)` — before the `insShift` line, so a hot meal
actually raises felt by +5 in the cold. The only Insulation modifier in production code is the
hot-meal Add, so the evaluate is a no-op without a meal. No per-item wetness, no wind map, no
layer-count bonus (Task 31 / dry-layers decisions stand); enclosed rooms still clamp felt to the
comfort band, so cold that bites is an outdoor mechanic by construction.

**Consequences.** A soaked player in a gale feels ~2.6 °C colder than before and cools 1.5× faster
once all three conditions coincide; a hot meal by the fire now genuinely warms the eater (+5 felt
for 120 s). Bots already respond to cold (`warm_up` / `seek_shelter`), so they feel the bite
through the same felt line.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr472_cold.test.ts` 9/9: synergy delta 8.6 °C (wet 6 +
synergy 2.6) in a 12-speed gale; dry in the same gale loses only the wind term; hot meal raises
felt by +5 in winter cold (same seed/weather/fire in both worlds) and the gain expires after
120 s; cold + soaked + gale drains 1.5× the base rate (1.2 °C vs 0.8 °C over 10 s) while wet-just-
under / wind-just-under each drain at the base rate; 10 s in the bite leaves hp untouched;
tuning knobs in `environment.json` / `vitals.json`. Revert check: 6/9 fail on pre-change code (the
3 passing are controls that hold on both).

## ADR-473: Sleep that restores — a good night leaves you rested, a bad night leaves you groggy (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Sleep already healed (0.5 hp/s) and regened stamina 3×, and all-asleep skipped the
night 30× — but every night was the same: a bed in a sealed dark room felt no different from a
short cold doze in the open. The scope default: score the night at wake time — bed + >= 6
game-hours + warm + dark + quiet room = rested (StaminaRegen x1.25 + HealthRegen +0.25 hp/s for
30 in-game minutes); any of no bed / < 6 h / cold or hot at wake / lit / noisy room (openness >
0.25) = groggy (MoveSpeed x0.85 + StaminaRegen x0.75 for 5 in-game minutes); in between (e.g. an
open door at openness 0.25) is an ordinary night with no buff or penalty. Bots share the hook:
the bot rest edge calls `sleepIn` and every wake path (input, bed destroyed, damage) calls
`wake()`, so a bot in a bed wakes rested or groggy the same way.

**Decision.** Score in `wake()` before the sleeper is moved (the bed position is the sleeping
position: felt, light and openness are all read there) and apply the result as `Buffs` modifiers
(authority only; the stack replicates). Duration is game hours from a sleep-start snapshot taken
in `setMode` when the mode becomes Sleep — not ticks, because `timeSkip` advances game hours
without advancing ticks proportionally, so a tick-derived duration would undercount a skipped
night. Warmth is the ADR-472 felt temperature against the `vitals.json` comfort band [8, 32] °C;
dark is `lightAt` returning nothing; quiet/noisy are `roomOpennessAt` against the `sleepQuality`
tunings in `data/stance.json` (goodHours 6, quietOpenness 0.1, noisyOpenness 0.25, rested
1.25 / +0.25 hp/s / 1800 s, groggy 0.85 / 0.75 / 300 s). A missing sleep-start record (e.g. a
restart mid-sleep) scores ordinary — no buff, no penalty — rather than punishing a night that
cannot be measured. The scope caveat is resolved: floor sleep by the fire does NOT enter Sleep
mode — the bot "sleep" action is stand-still and only the "rest" edge with a bed calls `sleepIn`
— so the no-bed branch is a guard for a sleeper whose bed was destroyed without waking them,
not a reachable play path. No new per-tick scan, nothing per frame: the scoring runs once, at
wake time, on top of the existing `wake()` hook.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr473_sleep.test.ts` 10/10: full good night in a sealed
dark room rests (StaminaRegen 1.25, HealthRegen +0.25, expiry exactly 36000 ticks); 2 h night
groggy (MoveSpeed 0.85, StaminaRegen 0.75, expiry exactly 6000 ticks); cold wake (felt 5 °C),
lit wake (campfire burning nearby), and outdoor bed (openness 1) each groggy after 6 h; an open
door (openness 0.25) is ordinary; one open shutter in the 2-tile test room (openness ~0.1) still
counts as quiet and rests; a sleeper whose bed is gone wakes groggy; a missing sleep-start record
wakes ordinary; a bot-shaped sleeper (clientId 2) wakes rested the same way. Revert check: 10/10
fail on pre-change code. Test note: beds placed in tests need a NetId assigned by hand (ADR-244
pattern) — `placePiece` does not assign one, the NetServer does in live play — and a bed's
centre is its footprint centre (rot 2 puts it at (11, 10.5) inside the 2-tile test room; rot 0/1
puts it on the south wall line, openness 1).

## ADR-474: Tools wear out, and you repair them (SurVivaZ)

Tools and weapons wear: 1 durability per successful gather swing and per landed melee hit. A tool
that reaches 0 is BROKEN but stays in the bag (Tracey: broken tools never vanish, never become a
loot bag) and the hand falls back to the existing bare-hands / fists path, so a broken axe gathers
like fists (a tree still yields, an oak fails WrongTool) and a broken weapon hits like fists (5).
Below 25 % a tool is DULL: one tier lower for the gather bonus only (a dull iron axe on a tree
gives 5 wood where a full one gives 6); WrongTool checks still use the real tier, so dull never
locks the player out. Ranged shots, thrown weapons and explosives wear nothing (the wear hook sits
in the melee fall-through of combatSystem, after the ranged / thrown branches `continue`).

Repair is in place for ~30 % of the tool's own recipe, rounded up per ingredient (the saddle
pattern, mounts.ts): a stone axe costs wood 1, stone 1, fiber 1; a bronze axe planks 1, bronze
ingot 1. First-tier tools (item tier 1: stone, bone) repair anywhere with the resources in the
bag; later tiers (tier 2+: bronze, iron, steel, alloy) need an anvil in range (Tracey). Repair is
one command, `gameplay.itemRepair` { slot: u8 }, with the saddle-shaped `checkItemRepair` /
`repairItem` (item_repair.ts) and a Repair button in the inventory details pane (a plain focusable
button, so touch, D-pad and keys work alike; it shows only while the item is damaged, names the
cost in its title, and is disabled with the blocker — "Needs an anvil nearby" / "Needs …" /
"Needs the skill unlock" — when the check fails). The tooltip says "Broken — repair it" or
"Dull — one tier lower" next to the Durability line. Bots repair too: `fillAgentSensors` sets
`view.repairTool` for a BROKEN tool the bot can repair right now (check included, anvil rule
included), the `tool_repair` behaviour pushes `irepair:<slot>` (throttled 200 ticks, safe-gated),
and `instantChores` pushes the same action for hired workers — same blackboard key, so the two
paths never double-push. Scoped to BROKEN tools only in v1: a dull tool still works, so repairing
it is an optimisation, not a fix. No planner Step kind was added (the planner works on item
counts, not slot durability — a Step would have needed wiring through every Step consumer); the
behaviour-reflex + instantChores pattern (vehicle_service / dye) covers it instead.

Scope corrections (verified in build): there is no hammer tool kind (hammers are weapons; axes are
dual tool+weapon), so wear splits into gather-wear and melee-wear hooks, not a single hook; there
is no whetstone item and no grindstone piece in v1; `spend()` (vehicle_craft.ts) is the OLD break
behaviour (item removed at 0) and was NOT reused — the new `wearDurability` leaves the item in
place at 0. The name `wearSlot` was already taken (combat/arms.ts, the Wear action for clothing),
so the durability helper is `wearDurability`. Skill-gate note: no tool or weapon has an
`item:<key>` unlock node in the skill tree (only the four saddles do), so `itemRepairUnlocked` is
a pass-through for every tool/weapon today — the check follows the saddle pattern and will bind
automatically if a tool is ever gated. First-tier vs later-tier is the item's top-level `tier`
field (stone_axe 1, bronze_axe 2, iron_sledgehammer 3), which covers tools and weapons uniformly.

Files: `packages/gameplay/src/inventory.ts` (`slotDurability`, `isBrokenSlot`, `isDullSlot`,
`wearDurability`), `packages/gameplay/src/systems/gathering.ts` (broken gate in `heldTool`, dull
tier in the bonus, wear after the yields loop), `packages/gameplay/src/combat/combat.ts` (broken
gate in `heldWeapon`, wear after the melee `applyDamage`), `packages/gameplay/src/item_repair.ts`
+ `item_repair_commands.ts` (new), `packages/gameplay/src/input.ts` + `packages/gameplay/src/index.ts`
(register + export, append-only after RAMP_COMMANDS), `packages/gameplay/src/ui/menus.ts`
(`itemRepairIntent`, `itemRepairView`, tooltip note), `apps/client/src/gameplay-panels.ts`
(Repair button), `apps/server/src/protocol.ts` (net bridge + `ITEM_REPAIR_REJECT_REASONS`:
`not_repairable`, `needs_anvil`; `not_damaged` / `cannot_afford` / `skill_locked` / `empty_slot` /
`bad_slot` already existed), `apps/server/src/game.ts` (`installItemRepairCommands`),
`packages/gameplay/src/ai/agent_output.ts` (`irepair:<slot>`),
`packages/gameplay/src/ai/survivor_behaviors.ts` (sensor + `tool_repair` behaviour),
`packages/gameplay/src/ai/autonomy.ts` (`instantChores` line), `packages/gameplay/src/agents.ts`
(`AgentWorldView.repairTool`).

Tests: `packages/gameplay/test/adr474_tool_wear.test.ts`, 15/15 pass (gather wear 1/swing; wear to
0 stays in the bag + bare-hands fallback + WrongTool on an oak; dull = one tier lower, 6 vs 5 wood
in two identical worlds sharing the node's deterministic rng stream; wrong tool / toolless wear
nothing; melee wear 1/hit; wear to 0 + fists fallback, fist hit 5; ranged shot wears nothing;
repair cost 30 %; broken first-tier repair to full in place + cost spent; validation
not_damaged / cannot_afford / not_repairable / needs_anvil; later-tier repair at an anvil; command
round-trip accept + reject; `itemRepairView` data; bot sensor + behaviour + `irepair` mapping;
sensor clear when unaffordable / anvil-needed / only dull). Revert check: 13/15 fail on
pre-change code (wear tests fail on assertions, repair tests fail as "not a function"); the 2
passes are the by-design no-wear controls (wrong tool / toolless, ranged), which pass on old code
because they assert the absence of wear. Gameplay, client and server typechecks EXIT 0. Test
notes: a tree is fist-gatherable (minTier 1 <= bareHands maxMinTier 1), so a broken/wrong tool on
a tree falls back to fists and succeeds — only the oak (minTier 2) gives WrongTool; hp is f32, so
the fist hit reads back 4.9875 — use `toBeCloseTo(5, 1)`; `mk` (arms.test.ts) needs
`installPermissions` for PlayerId, so the dull test uses plain `spawnPlayer`.

## ADR-475: Wild-deer herds graze and move on (SurVivaZ)

Decision: wild deer (animal_deer, animal_red_deer, animal_elk, animal_stag, animal_moose) graze
the grass tiles around their spawn centre and move on when the patch is bare; other animals are
untouched. A herd is a spawn-centre cohort, not a component: deer share a home, and when more
than half the grass within 5 tiles of that home is bare the shared home shifts deterministically
40-100 tiles in the seasonal direction (winter west, summer east; spring/fall a cardinal by hash)
and each deer drifts toward it by wandering. No new per-tick scan: the graze runs inside the
existing animalAISystem loop, the bare-patch check runs only on graze completions and think ticks,
and the rate cap is one graze start per deer per 30 s (a module-level WeakMap, sim-local).

Scope corrections (the scope's migrationSystem / migrationDirectionFor / wildlife.ts / movePlan do
not exist in this tree — the real system is animalAISystem in packages/gameplay/src/population.ts
plus the tamed graze path in skills/husbandry.ts): (1) there are no grass nodes to deplete —
grazing reuses the tamed GrazedTile / Grazing path exactly (same 20 s graze, same 180 s regrow,
same shared tile state, so a tile a deer stripped is bare for a tame herd too and vice versa);
(2) the move is a drift by wandering toward the new home, not the scope's migration machinery;
(3) the scope's "wildlife.ts imports" do not exist — the tunings live in data/ai.json tuning.herd
(grazeCooldownSeconds 30, bareRadius 5, bareFrac 0.5, moveMinTiles 40, moveMaxTiles 100) with a
herdTuning() helper following the animalDrinkTuning() / carrionTuning() pattern, and the AiData
tuning type in ai/population.ts gains the herd block. (4) The new home is deterministic from the
old home + season (hash of floored home + season index), so every deer sharing a home computes
the same new home and the cohort moves as a group; it prefers a grass target and falls back to
any walkable tile (4 rotations, 90 degrees each), and stays put when no walkable target exists.
(5) The grass tile id and the graze timings are duplicated in population.ts (HERD_GRASS_TILE 3,
HERD_GRAZE_SECONDS 20, HERD_GRASS_REGROW_SECONDS 180) with a sync comment rather than imported
from husbandry.ts — husbandry imports population, so population cannot import husbandry (cycle).
A grazing deer stays put on its think tick (threat/flee still override, those branches run
first); a deer that walks off its tile abandons the graze; a deer standing on bare ground checks
the patch on its think tick, which covers the case where a tame herd stripped the patch without
any wild graze completing. A patch with no grass at all never moves (avoids ping-pong in
grassless areas). No new art: deer reuse their existing sprites.

Tests: packages/gameplay/test/adr475_herds.test.ts, 10/10 pass — tuning reads ai.json; patch state
counts grass and live grazed tiles (expired grazed tiles do not count); new home deterministic,
40-100 tiles, winter west / summer east; an Idle deer starts a graze on the first tick and the
tile is bare after 20 s; no second graze within the 30 s cooldown; a bare patch moves the herd on
(home shifts to the deterministic new home, state Wander, goal = new home); a patch that is not
bare keeps the herd; a deer on bare ground checks the patch on its think tick; a rabbit never
grazes; a grazing deer stays put across 20 forced think ticks. Revert check: 9/10 fail on
pre-change code; the one pass is the rabbit control, which passes on both by design (it asserts
the absence of grazing for a non-deer).

## ADR-476: Hordes hunt by sound and by lamplight (SurVivaZ)

Decision: a loud survivor noise re-targets the nearest horde that can hear it to the nearest base
near the noise, and that horde sieges the base for 30 in-game minutes (refreshed by further loud
noise at the same base). While sieging, the horde seeks the base's lights (nearest light within
20 tiles of its target, if that light is on a piece) and its members are exempt from shyGoal light
avoidance. The siege re-targets an existing horde only — it never drafts individual zombies, and
a loud noise in the open (no base within 32 tiles) draws no horde. Tracey's decision overrules
the scope default (lamplight cut from v1): lamplight is IN, but only for hordes already in siege
mode, within 20 tiles, exempt from shyGoal while sieging. Note in the report: lamplight needs a
live play-test (it inverts shipped avoidance for sieging members).

Scope corrections (the scope's "subscribe the director to noise events" does not exist as
written): there is NO noise event and NO noise kind in this tree — NoiseLevel is a decaying
per-entity level (systems/noise.ts) and makeNoise is the one place all noise flows through. So
the director cannot subscribe; instead makeNoise records the peak survivor noise in the noise
module (lastLoudNoise, TTL 100 ticks — the director runs every 20) and the director reads it on
its own cadence. The "player-caused only" gate is exactly "the actor is a living survivor":
thunder never calls makeNoise, animals never call it (footsteps are Survival-gated in
movement.ts), zombie structure hits are not survivors. Vehicle engine noise does not exist (no
makeNoise call for driving), so a driving player draws a horde only by what they do at the
destination. The noise amounts make walk (12) louder than a gunshot (9), so any amount gate that
includes gunshots includes footsteps — the hearing-radius gate (a horde hears what a walker
would hear: 1 tile per noise level) is what keeps a far-away walker from hijacking a horde.
The siege state lives on the HordeMember component (siegeUntil, u32; server-only, not networked)
plus the director's runtime Horde entry — the zombie AI reads the member's field for the shyGoal
exemption, which avoids a hordes<->zombies import cycle (hordes already imports zombies).
The light-seek is a director target selection, not a new AI state: the director re-targets the
siege to the piece the nearest light is on, and hordeSteer + the existing structure-attack path
do the rest. It is self-stabilising (once the target IS a light's piece, the nearest light to it
is itself). Siege expiry is the existing hordeSteer disband path when the base is gone, not a
new mechanism. Tunings in data/roads.json hordes (noiseMin 8 = the gather/chop level, so
gunshot 9 / build 10 / walk 12 / sprint 18 / explosion 27 count and door 5 / swim 7 do not;
siegeMinutes 30, lightSeekTiles 20, noiseTargetRadius 32).

Tests: packages/gameplay/test/adr476_hordes.test.ts, 8/8 pass — tuning reads roads.json;
makeNoise records the last loud survivor noise (zombie noise and quieter noise never overwrite
it; the record expires after its TTL); a gunshot at a base re-targets the nearest hearing horde
and starts a siege (runtime key/target/siegeUntil and every member's HordeMember target/siegeUntil
all move); a door does not re-target and a loud noise in the open draws no horde; a siege
refreshes on further noise at the same base, lapses when jumped past (w.tick = N, the adr238
pattern — stepping the whole siege would let the members destroy the foundation first), and
starts again on fresh noise; a sieging horde re-targets to the lit torch stand; a sieging
member walks into the torch light (min distance < 2) while a non-sieging member stays out
(> 5, the ADR-217 behaviour); a siege never turns an individual zombie into a horde member.
Revert check: 7/8 fail on pre-change code; the one pass is the quiet-noise / open-field
control, which passes on both by design (it asserts no re-target happens).

## ADR-477: Bots get good at things — picks drift toward practiced skills, and practice makes actions slightly faster (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Bots already picked personal wants by personality and mood (`pickWithMood` in
`ai/life.ts`) and already earned XP and bought skill-tree nodes — but the two never met: a bot
that had spent all its points on farming was exactly as likely to tend the garden as a bot that
had never touched a crop, and a master forager gathered at exactly the same speed as a fresh
spawn. Tracey decided bots should get **both better and slightly faster** (overruling the
scope's "better, not faster" default). Two corrections to the scope's map: the scope cites
`planner.ts` for the scoring, but the planner is a fixed ladder (first unmet, reachable goal
wins — no scoring function to add a term to); the only scored bot pick in the tree is
`pickWithMood`. And the scope's "skill level" has no farming / crafting level keys in the tree
(`skillLevelOf` covers the craft professions only), so the branch level is the number of owned
nodes in the branch — the observable measure of practice.

**Decision.** (1) Picks: `pickWithMood` gains `score += branchLevel(world, self, w.skill) * 0.1`
for the want's skill branch, additive after the aspiration / stickiness multipliers, so
personality, mood and aspiration still dominate the pick. The want→skill mapping lives in data
(`ai_life.json`): only `tend_garden` → `farming` and `craft_keepsake` → `crafting` carry a
skill — the other four wants are not skill-driven. `branchLevel` (new in `skills/tree.ts`)
counts owned nodes in a branch. A level-5 farmer scores gardening +0.5 over a level-0 bot:
enough to tip a tie, not enough to lock a bot into one want forever. (2) Speed: new `"speed"`
mod in the `SkillMod` union, granted +0.05 by the four tier-0 practice nodes — `forager`
(survival), `green_thumb` (farming), `tinkerer` (crafting), `carpenter` (building) — all reusing
their existing nodes and icons (`skill_forager` etc.); **no new icons were needed**. The label
in `SKILL_MOD_LABEL` is "action speed (gathering, crafting and building)". `skillMul(world, e,
"speed")` is 1.0 fresh and 1.2 with all four nodes. It divides the gather swing cooldown
(`gathering.ts`), the single timed craft (`systems/crafting.ts` — the player flow; `totalTicks`
is a replicated `Crafter` field, so the client reads the sped-up total from the component), and
the craft queue duration (`craft_queue.ts`, including the `CraftStarted` `totalTicks` so the
announced total matches the real duration). No yield, stamina, ingredient or output changes.
**Build time is not wired: piece placement is instant on this tree**
(`placePiece` has no duration), so there is no build duration for the speed mod to divide; a
builder still benefits through faster gathering and crafting, and the pick term covers the
building branch if a future want uses it. Deeper speed tiers (beyond +20%) would need new
nodes and are a follow-up, not this ADR.

**Consequences.** A bot that practices farming drifts toward the garden over sessions; a bot
that practices crafting drifts toward keepsakes. A practiced player gathers and crafts up to
20% faster (a 0.75 s swing in 13 ticks instead of 15; a 2 s craft in 34 ticks instead of 40).
The drift is gradual — one farming node (+0.1) does not change a pick — and personality still
outweighs skill at the extremes.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr477_bot_skills.test.ts` 8/8: branch levels count
owned nodes per branch (7 farming nodes via the `master_farmer` chain); `speedMul` 1.0 fresh,
1.05 per practice node, 1.20 with all four, 1.0 for a bare entity with no Progression; a lazy
bot (industriousness 0) rests unskilled (rest 0.7 vs garden 0.315), still rests with one farming
node (0.415), and tends the garden with five (0.815); the session-length drift test runs 30 pick
rounds with the skill level rising through practice — 10× rest as a generalist, 10× tend_garden
as a 5-node farming specialist, then 10× craft_keepsake once crafting reaches 7 nodes, proving
the drift is continuous (level-based) and reversible, not threshold-locked; the want→skill mapping is data-only;
gather 15 → 13 ticks; stone_axe 40 → 39 ticks with tinkerer alone, 34 with all four, and the
skilled craft completes 6 steps sooner in live stepping (queue) and 6 steps sooner as a single
timed craft (40 → 34 ticks on the replicated `Crafter` total). The ADR-234 skill audit gained
the `speed` branch (30 s `dry_wet_wood` craft, 600 vs 572 ticks per node): 144/144. The audit
caught a real gap in the first cut — the single timed craft path (`systems/crafting.ts`) had
its own duration and was unwired until the audit forced it. `adr219_skill_desc.test.ts` 7/7 (the
forager pin now expects the added "+5% action speed" line). Revert check: 7 behavioral tests fail
on pre-change wiring (adr219 forager pin, branchLevel/speed, pick flip, session drift, gather,
craft queue, single craft); the 8 controls hold on both, and the ADR-234 audit's 144 pass on revert because
the reverted data carries no speed mod to audit.

## ADR-478: Bots that remember each other — affinity is finally read, not just recorded (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Per-pair trust and affinity memory ships (ADR-444, `ai/social_memory.ts`): shared meals,
working together and helping write affinity, attacks write grudges. But no code ever read affinity —
it was write-only. The scope's defaults were written against a -100..100 scale (-20 grudge cutoff,
>= 30 guard preference); verified in build, the shipped scale is -1..1 for both trust and affinity
(clamped in `social_memory.ts`), so the thresholds translate to grudgeBelow -0.2 and friendAt 0.3.
Two scope claims did not survive contact with the code: there is no `ai/trust.ts` (the memory lives
in `ai/social_memory.ts`), and there is no direct give-food-to-a-bot path with a recipient list —
food sharing is the shared meal's communal store (ADR-446: surplus deposited, foodless bots
withdraw). The guard path is the hired Defend / Follow bot holding its owner's anchor
(`fillHireSensors` + `work_defend`): it already guards a person (Follow: the owner's live position)
or a location (Defend: the owner's base), with the radius trust-modulated by ADR-444 — so the
affinity preference is expressed as guard keenness, not as a person-vs-location pick (the job
assignment, not the bot, picks person vs location).

**Decision.** Add `affinityOf(agent, player)` — the first reader of affinity (0 when unknown) — and
`SOCIAL_AFFINITY` (`grudgeBelow -0.2, friendAt 0.3, friendDefendBonus 4`) in `social_memory.ts`,
next to the existing `SOCIAL_EVENTS` / `SOCIAL_MEMORY` code consts (the file's own convention: these
tunings live in code because they tune bot temperament, not rules). Meal: in
`fillSharedMealSensors`, the bot deposits its surplus into the shared store unless every mate at
the meal is a grudge (affinity < -0.2) — it keeps its surplus instead. The store is communal, so
"friends first" is expressed as sharing whenever at least one mate is not a grudge; a single grudge
never vetoes sharing with the friends present, and a mate with no PlayerId counts as a stranger
(affinity 0), never a grudge. The bot still eats at the hearth with its grudges; it just does not
feed them. Guard: in `fillHireSensors`, the defend radius becomes trust < 0 -> 4 (unchanged ADR-444
gate), else affinity < -0.2 -> 4 (reluctant guard for a grudge), else affinity >= 0.3 -> 12 + 4 = 16
(a friend is guarded more keenly: the bot engages threats further from the friend), else 12. The
trust gate still applies: a distrusted owner is guarded up close no matter the affinity. ADR-478
does not change how affinity is recorded. No new per-tick scan, no new state: both changes read
memory the behaviours already hold, on their existing cadences.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr478_bot_memory.test.ts` 7/7: `affinityOf` reads recorded
affinity (-0.4 after one attack, 0 for unknown) and the threshold constants; neutral mates get the
surplus deposit (3 portions) as before; all mates grudged -> no deposit but the meal still pends;
one grudge + one friend -> deposit still happens; a friend (affinity 0.6) is guarded out to 16
tiles (zombie at 14 defended) while a neutral owner only to 12; a grudge with trust +0.5 is guarded
only up close (8 tiles ignored, 3 defended); a distrusted owner (trust -0.5) is guarded up close
even with affinity 0.6. Revert check: 6/7 fail on pre-change code (the neutral-meal control
passes on both, as it should); a behaviour-only probe (no `affinityOf` calls) passes 2/2 on new
code and fails 2/2 on pre-change code (deposit present when it should be absent; defend missing
when it should be set). The grudge-with-trust case is set by direct record (precedent:
`social_memory.test.ts` validation), because every social event moves trust and affinity the same
way and the two cannot be separated by events alone.

## ADR-479: Sailboat — a wind-driven boat (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Boats were paddle or motor: the wind (ADR-465) pushed them a little, but no boat was
*driven* by it. Tracey approved a sailboat as the 15th ADR of the simulation batch: a new vehicle
class on the water, wind-powered, with its own art in the game's style.

**Decision.** Third boat kind: `sail: true` on the def (class `boat`, fuel null, stamina null —
exactly one of fuel / stamina / sail, enforced by `validateVehicleDefs`; the ADR-422 "never both or
neither" rule now reads "exactly one of the three"). New pure `sailFactor(windDir, windSpeed,
heading)` in `vehicles.ts`: `0.25 + 1.75 * max(0, cos(windDir - heading)) * min(1, windSpeed / 12)`
— a full tailwind at windSpeed 12 doubles the paddle-equivalent maxSpeed (3.0 -> 6.0 t/s), a
headwind, beam wind or calm leaves only the 0.25x paddle crawl, so the driver is never stranded.
Knobs in `VEHICLE_TUNING` (`sailTailMul: 1.75`, `sailPaddleFloor: 0.25`, reusing `windRefSpeed:
12`). `stepPowered` uses the sail factor as the speed-target multiplier for sailboats (the wind IS
the engine) and reuses ADR-465's `boatWindBonus` leeward drift for all boats. No stamina drain, no
fuel burn, no engine/lights: `spawnVehicle` adds no `VehicleState`, engine/lights toggles refuse
with `no_controls`, and the client hides the engine chip (same as a paddle boat). Def appended last
in `vehicles.json` (APPEND ONLY, defId = index + 1): 4 seats (rowboat anchors), maxSpeed 3.0,
footprint 3.6 x 1.5, health 220, storage 8 / 300. Kit `vehicle_kit_sailboat` (item id 522 /
resource 408 in `ids.lock.json`, regenerated via `lock:ids`), dock recipe 120 s (planks 12, wood 6,
cloth 4, rope 4, seat 2 — cloth is the sail), `vehicle_crafting.json` maps `sailboat` to the kit
with fuel `none`; deploy is the ordinary kit flow (water check from `isBoatDef`). Schema
`vehicles.schema.json` gains the optional `sail` boolean (additionalProperties is false).

**Art.** Runtime-painted, in the ADR-421/422 boat family (same dark-plum outline, water shadow,
wake, 2:1 dimetric projection, 4 cols x 6 rows, frame(phase, dir) = phase*8 + dir, idle frame 8):
`SAILBOAT_ART` in `apps/client/src/task421-art.ts` — deep-green painted hull (distinct from the
rowboat's blue, the speedboat's red, the motorboat's white, the pontoon's aluminium), cream trim,
cream canvas mainsail aft + darker jib forward in the u-z plane (broadside from the beam, edge-on
from bow/stern), dark-wood mast + boom, red masthead flag; phases are sail states (0 slack, 1 full,
2 billowing). `boatFrameSize` uses the masthead (4.6 z) as the top, so the frame is 300x228 with
anchor (0.5, 0.6623) — fragment `pack/task479/manifest.task479.json` carries layout only and
declares `idle` [8] + `sail` [0, 8, 16] at 4 fps. Registered three ways (ADR-455 lesson):
`MANIFEST_INDEX` (`packages/assets/src/manifest-index.ts`), the fragment file, vite MOUNTS
(`apps/client/vite.config.ts`), plus `task479AtlasSources()` merged in `view.ts` and the kit menu
icon painted at runtime from the world cell (`installSailboatMenuIcons`, style id
`task479-menu-icons`). The renderer shows one frame per direction (no VAnim, same cut as ADR-421),
so the sail cycle is declared for a future render hook. The sailboat has no oars in art: the
0.25x paddle crawl is a sim fallback with no visible paddle — noted, not faked.

**Consequences.** A sailboat at the dock (120 s, cloth for the sail) sails at up to 6 t/s downwind
and 0.75 t/s into the wind, drifting leeward like every boat; it never strands, never needs fuel
or stamina, and never shows an engine chip. No new per-tick scan, no new state, no new per-frame
work — the wind bonus and the boat drive already ran.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr479_sailboat.test.ts` 12/12: def (sail, boat, no fuel /
stamina, maxSpeed 3.0, 4 seats, storage 8/300); validation (sail + fuel rejected, sail + stamina
rejected, non-boat sail rejected, two-of-three rejected); sailFactor tailwind 2.0 / headwind 0.25 /
beam 0.25 / calm 0.25 / half wind 1.125 / over-ref capped 2.0; kit mapping + dock recipe (cloth 4);
spawn has no VehicleState; engine toggle `no_controls`; driven sailboat reaches ~2x paddle speed
downwind and crawls upwind. `apps/client/test/adr479_sailboat_art.test.ts` 6/6: atlas 1200x1368
(under the 2048 cap), frame 300x228 matching the fragment, 8 distinct direction cells, sail
phases differ, dark-plum outline present, sail-cloth pixels present, fragment declares the atlas
+ sprite with `sail` animation, kit menu icon non-blank, geometry matches `vehicles.json`.

## ADR-480: Mesh rebuild stamp loses diagonal-neighbour changes — stale chunk mesh leaves a side face open to the sky (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Tracey's 2026-11-20 phone photo 1 (live build 8bedc989) shows blue on the side of a
lone 1-level raised tile at a plateau corner. The blue is sky, not water (sampled ~(100, 135, 175),
the daytime sky clear colour; no water colour in code matches), and measuring the original photo
shows the blue region is a TRIANGLE: 53 px wide, ~27 px tall at its left end, tapering to 2 px at
the right end — full height at one vertex, a point at the other. ADR-418 proved the
single-consistent-build model airtight (81 height combos, all sealed), so the remaining hole had to
be cross-build staleness: two different height states disagreeing at a shared vertex.

**Decision.** `TilemapRenderer.stamp` (`packages/render/src/tilemap.ts`) was a floating-point
polynomial hash of a chunk's version and its 8 neighbours' versions. The stamp is ~1.2e21 even in
a fresh world (every version contributes +1), where an IEEE-754 double's spacing is 2^18 =
262,144 — so a +1 increment at the tail of the polynomial rounds away entirely: in a fresh world
a +1 at d3/d4 does not change the stamp; at versions >= 1 a +1 at d2/d3/d4 does not; at versions
>= 100 a +1 at d1..d4 does not (proven by direct evaluation of the exact arithmetic). `sync()`
therefore did not rebuild a chunk's mesh when a diagonal chunk streamed in or was edited, and the
diagonals feed the shared-vertex corner drops (`slope.ts`) — a stale corner drop flips a slope
side into a missing cliff, or leaves the top edge a level above the neighbour's fresh edge, opening
exactly the triangular sky gap in the photo. The stamp is now the exact 32-bit `Math.imul(s, 31)`
mixing already used by `TileTerrain.stamp` (`packages/render/src/terrainTiles.ts`): a +1 at any
of the 9 positions always changes it, at any version (31 is odd, so 31^k is odd). No other stamp
needed changing: the TileTerrain stamp was already exact 32-bit, and the Canvas2D ground-block
stamp is a string. Render-only: no gameplay, balance, touch-input, or graphics-quality change.

**Verification.** `packages/render/test/adr480_mesh_stamp.test.ts` 5/5, all failing on the pre-fix
stamp (revert check): 4 stamp unit tests (all 9 positions move the stamp at versions 0, 1, 100,
1024) and 1 end-to-end repro driving the real `sync()` — a lone raised tile at a chunk corner
whose +x edge is a slope side while the (1,-1) diagonal chunk is unloaded, then the diagonal
streams in with a low tile: on pre-fix code the mesh is not rebuilt and the +x cliff quad is
absent; on fixed code the mesh rebuilds and the quad is present with the exact trapezoid
[5, 4, 4, 3].

**Honest cuts.** The fix guarantees the mesh rebuilds whenever any of the 9 versions changes; it
does not prove this was the only stale-mesh path in the game, only that this path reproduces the
photo's exact triangle shape and is closed. Tracey's phone test on the live build is still the
check that the blue gap is gone in real play.

## ADR-481: Place a liquid container on the ground — a permanent bag, no claim totem (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Tracey's 2026-11-20 request (1): a Place option for liquid containers in inventory so
players and AI humans can place them on the ground outside in the open world without the item
decaying or disappearing for being on the ground, and without requiring a claim totem. Scoping
found the pieces already existed: a permanent LootBag ships (never despawns, cap-exempt); dropped
stacks vanish on a 180 s timer, not spoilage; the claim gate applies to pieces, never drops; rain
fill is held-only by construction (ADR-452). The work is wiring those pieces together, not a new
storage system.

**Decision.** A Place button sits next to Drop in the inventory panel
(`apps/client/src/gameplay-panels.ts`), shown for liquid containers only (`sips > 0`) — a plain
focusable button like Drop, so touch, D-pad and keys work alike. It sends `PlaceItemCmd`
(`gameplay.placeItem`), handled by `placeItem()` (`packages/gameplay/src/pets.ts`): one liquid
container goes into a new permanent LootBag at the actor's feet (`placedBagInit`,
`despawnAtTick = PERMANENT_DESPAWN`, kind `LootSource.Placed` = 6, one container per bag with
`slotCount` 1). No claim totem is required — the loot-bag route never consults claims, and this is
deliberately not routed through pieces. Anyone may pick a placed container back up (only death
bags are owner-locked); the bag vanishes the moment it is emptied, by the existing permanent-bag
rule. Per-player cap 8 (`PLACED_CONTAINER_CAP`): permanent bags are cap-exempt in the despawn
system, so unbounded placement would bloat the save; a hired bot's placements count against its
employer's cap (`placedBagOwnerId`: the player's pid, else the bot's `Worker.owner`). Rain fill YES
in v1: the 20-tick loot pass (`lootBagDespawnSystem`) rolls the same +1 sip per
`rainFillSecondsPerSip` (45) for placed bags, using `shelterAt` for the bag's rain exposure, so a
roofed bag stays dry; held-container behaviour is unchanged, and a boiled container reverts to raw
on refill via `fillContainer`, as in ADR-452. AI trigger: a hired bot carrying a spare full
container (two or more full — one stays for drinking) places it at the home anchor via the
`place_container` behaviour (`packages/gameplay/src/ai/hire_behaviors.ts`, sensor
`view.hire.spareContainer`), sending `PlaceItemCmd` through the net-command path; the server
re-validates item, container and cap. No map markers. Empty containers are placeable. This closes
ADR-452's open gap for placed bags only; storage containers stay out of scope.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr481_place_containers.test.ts` 13/13 and
`apps/client/test/adr481_place_containers.test.ts` 2/2 (15/15): permanent-bag fields, one container
per bag, the player loses the container; a placed bag outlives a dropped bag past `droppedSeconds`;
a non-container is refused (`not_container`); the per-player cap holds at 8 (`cap_reached`, the
9th container stays in the pack); picking the container back up empties the bag and it vanishes
immediately with an `emptied` event; rain fills a placed container in 900 s of rain, not in clear
weather, not under a roof; a boiled container reverts to raw on rain refill; `PlaceItemCmd` is
registered in `PET_COMMANDS` and dispatches through the real handler (rejecting a non-container);
a hired bot's place counts against its employer's cap; the hire sensor reports a spare only with
two full containers; the `place_container` behaviour pushes `PlaceItemCmd` at the anchor and
nothing with no spare. Revert check: 14/15 fail on pre-change code (the label assertion passes
either way — the fallback branch already names single-stack bags).

**Honest cuts.** The AI trigger fires only for hired bots with two or more full containers; an
unhired bot never places, and a bot with a single flask never gives it up. The place lands at the
actor's feet (0.6 tiles ahead) — there is no aiming. Rain fill is probabilistic (~1 sip per 45 s
of rain), so a placed container fills slowly. The live play-test — place, rain, pick up, and a
hired bot placing at its base — still needs Tracey's phone test.

## ADR-482: Bees pollinate 15 tiles from the apiary (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Tracey's 2026-11-20 request (2): bees in apiaries pollinate 15 tiles in every
direction from the apiary. ADR-454 shipped radius 5.

**Decision.** `packages/gameplay/data/farming.json` pollination radius 5 → 15. The check is a
Euclidean circle over the cached apiary list, so there is no tile scan. Everything else is
unchanged: +1 bonus, first yield only, planted crops only, no stacking, wild crops excluded.
Honey-deposit range stays 10 — Tracey did not answer that decision, so the fiction gap is
recorded, not resolved: a bee may now pollinate a crop it never deposits honey near. No guide
surfacing.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr454_bees_pollinate.test.ts` 5/5 (the stale 10-tile
out-of-range case re-based to 16 tiles) and `packages/gameplay/test/adr482_bees_pollinate_15.test.ts`
6/6: axis 15 in / 16 out, diagonal (11,11) in / (12,11) out (circle, not square), two apiaries at
11–15 tiles still +1, wild crops excluded, `apiaryWithin` unit boundary at radius 15. Revert
check: at radius 5, 3/6 adr482 tests fail (the three boundary tests); the other 3 pass as negative
controls.

**Honest cuts.** Honey deposits still land within 10 tiles while pollination reaches 15. No phone
test yet.

## ADR-483: In-game settings are available in the start menu settings (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Tracey's 2026-11-20 request (3): the in-game settings made available in the start
menu settings as well. The menu Settings screen already existed; the in-game-only rows did not.

**Decision.** `apps/client/src/menu.ts` `settings()` gains the graphics-quality `<select>`
(`QUALITY_PRESETS`, `loadPreset()`, live-applies on change via `savePreset` + `setQuality`,
persist-only fallback when no renderer exists, detected-tier line when `qualityInfo` provides it),
the three toggles (toolHints / nameTags / ledgeWarnings, same labels and `data-key`s as in-game),
and the audio + FX rows via the existing standalone builders (`audioSettingsRows`,
`fxSettingsRows`). `menu(opts)` takes optional `audio`, `fx`, `setQuality`, `qualityInfo` (same
types as `GameMenusOptions`); `apps/client/src/main.ts` `boot.menu({...})` passes the mixer, the
same FX adapter as the GameMenus wiring, `setQuality` into the renderer preset, and the same
`qualityInfo` cast. Apply timing: graphics, audio and FX live-apply in the menu, the rest on
Save / next start. Save now also persists the three toggles — this also fixes a pre-existing
menu-save gap, where the old full-replace save dropped toolHints / nameTags / ledgeWarnings
entirely. World-rules readout, tutorial replay and the error log stay in-game only (they need a
live world / debug tool). Scope is existing settings only: no keybindings / language UI, which
exists nowhere and would be new work, not ADR-483. `GameMenus` itself cannot mount in the menu —
the standalone builders only.

**Verification.** `apps/client/test/adr483_menu_settings.test.ts` 6/6: rows present; a graphics
change live-applies and persists (`survivaz.render.quality`); audio volume / mute apply live
through the passed controls; the FX cycle applies live; Save persists the three toggles into
`engine-settings`; without opts the screen still works with persist-only quality. Revert check:
6/6 fail on pre-change `menu.ts` / `main.ts`.

**Honest cuts.** Mixer / FX safety in the menu on a real phone still needs Tracey's phone test —
the gate must confirm it if possible. The three toggles apply on Save / next start, not live.

## ADR-484: AI humans are not shrunk — no bug found, no fix built (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Tracey's 2026-11-20 request (4): make AI humans normal sized if they are shrunk — and
her 2026-11-20 phone photo 2, a little person in the lower left who cannot be interacted with,
measuring ~53 px against her character's ~112 px in the same shot.

**Decision.** NO FIX — no bug was found. Players and bots share one draw path (`view.ts`
`classify`), scale defaults to 1, there is no per-entity scale and no child system: bots are NOT
shrunk. Poses (crouch / sit / sleep / swim) make a real human measure ~half-height at scale 1,
which is the likely explanation for the photo. The figure is almost certainly an unhired AI human
bot in the exact default player outfit (brown bob + green sprout, red shirt, blue trousers —
verified pixel-for-pixel against the packed player sprite; no child NPCs exist in code); it
"cannot be interacted with" because the hire panel only opens within 3 tiles
(`recruitment.ts:463`) and she was ~10 tiles away. The hardening is done once inside ADR-485, so
a missing art key degrades to a similar animal instead of the 0.55x bare-player fallback. No code
was changed for this ADR.

**Verification.** Code inspection only — there is no bug to regress against, so there is no test.
What would prove it: the walk-up Use test (walk within ~3 tiles and press Use — the hire panel
opening means it is a bot), a side-by-side idle screenshot, a `?diag` capture.

**Honest cuts.** The ~0.5x measurement is still unexplained by any code path: if the panel opens
but the figure stays half-size, that is a second bug, still open. Still awaiting Tracey's walk-up
Use test answer.

## ADR-485: Animals draw at realistic readable sizes (SurVivaZ)

**Context.** Tracey's 2026-11-20 request (5): make sure all animals are realistically scaled in
size with the world and players / AI humans. The scoping tree had no pack, so the first step was
measuring the live pack at f40445b5: only 3 of 40 species have own art in TexturePacker atlases
(deer 64 px cell, boar 48 px, wolf 48 px); the other 37 resolve via `nature/manifest.nature.json`
(explicit per-direction trimmed rects), task34 runtime-painted art (bee ~22x13 px, owl ~26x38 px)
or mount sheets (horse / donkey / yak, already true-scale at 52 px = 1.75 m). Measured drawn
heights (idle direction-0 frame 0): deer 42, boar 23, wolf 30, bear 28, bison 30, cow 27, moose 45,
elk 50, stag 48, red_deer 35, alpaca 36, pig 22, sheep 23, goat 26, turkey 28, goose 22, fox 26,
rabbit 26, cats 27, dogs 25–37, chicken 22, duck 16, crow 21, parrot 24, turtle 20 px. Large
animals draw ~0.6x true height (bear, bison, cow); small animals sit in a deliberate readability
band (16–37 px) with mostly-correct relative order. The SCOPE.md fallback ratios assumed base art
was true-scale, which is false — every fallback scale below is recomputed from the measured drawn
heights (base art: boar 23, deer 42, wolf 30, rabbit 26, chicken 22 px).

**Decision.** Three data-only parts, all client view-side, no sim change, cannot desync. (a)
Fallback corrections in `packages/gameplay/data/sprite_fallbacks.json`: deer→boar 1.74,
stag→deer 0.95, red_deer→deer 0.95, elk→deer 1.03, moose→deer 1.41, bear→boar 1.93, fox→wolf 0.40,
hare→rabbit 0.34, squirrel→rabbit 0.28, turkey→chicken 1.21, duck→chicken 0.47, goose→chicken
0.95, goat→deer 0.57, sheep→boar 1.16, cow→boar 1.87, bison→boar 2.33, turtle→boar 0.26,
pig→boar 1.16, alpaca→deer 0.71, wolf→boar 1.10. Snake stays at 0.6: a uniform scale cannot fix a
long, low animal. Horse / donkey / yak are untouched (mount sheets already true-scale). (b)
Safety net for the 13 species with no own art and no fallback entry, so a missing art key degrades
to a similar animal instead of the 0.55x bare-player fallback: dogs→wolf (dachshund 0.25, beagle
0.40, lab / husky / shepherd 0.59), cats→fox 0.62 with tints, parrot→crow 0.50, crow→owl 0.31,
ferret→squirrel 0.35, owl→crow 0.70, bee→crow 0.10. Bee and owl have dedicated task34 runtime art,
so those two entries fire only if the paint path is ever missing (the `task34-art.ts` comment is
updated to say so). Boar, chicken and rabbit have own art and no fallback entry: if that art ever
goes missing they still hit the 0.55x bare-player fallback — deliberate, there is nothing similar
to fall back to. (c) Live-art table `packages/gameplay/data/animal_scales.json` (11 species,
deer-anchored readable policy with deer at 42 px: bear 1.65, bison 1.85, cow 1.65, moose 1.4,
boar 1.35, elk 0.9, wolf 0.9, pig 1.25, sheep 1.2, red_deer 1.2, alpaca 0.85) with
`animalScale()` / `animalDrawScale()` in `packages/gameplay/src/population.ts`, applied by one
multiply in `apps/client/src/view.ts` `classify()`'s animal branch — live-art only (the resolved
key must equal the species' own key) and non-mount only (mounts are already true-scale). A
fallback resolution already carries its own corrected scale from `sprite_fallbacks.json` and must
not be multiplied again. Proportions are readable-game, not true-to-life: a true-scale rabbit is
7 px and a bee under 1 px, so bee and owl stay deliberately over-scale. Babies stay adult-sized.
The dead double-prefix `animal_animal_crow` in `view.ts:1252-1253` was NOT touched — fixing it
would change behaviour; it is a decision, not a drive-by. No sheet was found painted the wrong
size, so no sheets were repainted.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr485_animal_scale.test.ts` 6/6: the live table's exact
values and defaults (1 / undefined for unlisted species); table keys are real animals with no
mounts and no bee / owl; all 20 fallback corrections resolve to the measured target at the
corrected scale (snake pinned at 0.6); all 13 safety-net entries resolve, with the cat tints and
the chained cat→fox→wolf composition (0.62 x 0.40); every animal key with a fallback entry
resolves when its own art is missing, with the boar / chicken / rabbit exception pinned; the
live-art drawn heights come out in the right relative order (bear > boar, bison > cow, moose >
elk, boar > wolf, red deer ~ deer, alpaca < deer). Revert check: 6/6 fail on pre-change code.
`adr110-fallbacks` still 5/5.

**Honest cuts.** The `view.ts` multiply has no isolated test: no harness in the repo reaches the
private `classify` method, so it is verified by typecheck and review — Tracey's eyes on the live
build are the check that animals look right. Fallback scales are true-scale-based while live
scales are readable-policy-based (~5% apart, within the pixel-measurement noise), so a species'
drawn size shifts by that much if its art goes missing and the fallback fires. The pixel heights
were measured on the f40445b5 pack: if a sheet is repainted at a different size, the table must
be re-measured.

## ADR-486: Smell is a sense — blood, rot, and smoke draw zombies (SurVivaZ)

Zombies smell. A zombie that acquires no player investigates the strongest nearby smell the way
noise sends it to Investigate — one bounded spatial query per zombie think tick (every
`ai.thinkTicks`, staggered), beside the sight/noise acquire, never a new scan. Smell sources are
`EmitterKind.Smell = 3` (append-only; `packages/gameplay/src/realism.ts`), sampled by
`strongestSmell(world, x, y)` in `packages/gameplay/src/combat/zombies.ts`, which takes the best
contribution among the 8 nearest Smell emitters when it reaches `ai.smell.threshold` (0.25) and
returns the emitter's position as the Investigate goal. A live stimulus still wins: a player
re-acquired above overwrites the goal, and the Snuffer below overwrites it for light-targeting
zombies. Calm (daytime) zombies do not follow smells, horde members keep their structure march,
and a zombie breaking a structure down does not abandon it for one. Tuning lives in
`packages/gameplay/data/zombies.json` `ai.smell`: threshold 0.25; carcass radius 8 strength 1
(strongest, shortest); rot radius 6 strength 1; kill (loot bag) radius 6 strength 0.8; fire radius
12 strength 1 (widest). All falloffs are linear.

Smell emitters attach at events, never by a scan. A carcass node gets one at spawn
(`spawnResourceNode`, `animal_carcass` only). A kill's loot bag gets one at creation
(`dropAnimalLoot` / `dropZombieLoot`) while it holds spoilable meat or rot; the spoilage pass
(every 20 ticks, the pass that already visits every holder) refreshes it — a ground loot bag smells
while it holds spoilable food or rot, and stops the pass after the meat is gone. The same pass
refreshes carried rot: a player or bot carrying rot smells (radius 6), and stops smelling the pass
after the rot leaves. Stored containers are out of v1 — a storage box full of rot never smells.
Burning vegetation and burning pieces smoke: `ignite` attaches a Smell emitter to a burnable
vegetation node or a BuildPiece, `extinguish` removes it (a burning player, animal, or zombie gets
none — their smell is carried rot). A fired piece smokes through a sibling entity
(`AttachKind.Smell = 6`, mirroring the Light sibling): `placePiece` creates it unlit (strength 0)
and `setEmittersLit` turns it on with the fire and off when the fire goes out; `rehydrate` repairs
a loaded sibling's Emitter the way it repairs light, and `setEmittersLit` grows a missing sibling
for a save from before this ADR when the fire is next lit, so old saves' fires smell too.
Free-standing stations (`spawnStation`, tests/tools only) carry no Smell emitter in v1 — their Heat
emitter already occupies the station entity's one Emitter slot, and a bare sibling would lose its
(non-persistent) Emitter on reload with no rehydrate path to restore it; placed fired pieces (the
real-play path) carry the sibling.

Walls halve a smell instead of blocking it. `structureOcclusion`
(`packages/gameplay/src/building/shelter.ts`) gives Smell a partial transmit of 0.5 per solid cell
and per wall / closed-door edge (`SMELL_TRANSMIT`), so a sealed room still smells faintly of what
burns or rots inside; heat keeps its edge factors and every other kind keeps the binary block. A
`realism.ts` comment that read "0 linear, 1 quadratic" for the EmitterSpec falloff was wrong
against the world's Falloff enum (0 constant, 1 linear, 2 quadratic) and is corrected — the Smell
specs use `Falloff.Linear`, like the fire's Heat.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr486_smell.test.ts` 12/12: the tuning values; the
strongest smell wins over the nearer one and below-threshold smells are nothing; a zombie
investigates a carcass smell it cannot see a player from (goal = the source); a zombie ignores a
below-threshold smell, follows a seen player over a smell, and ignores smell while calm at noon;
carried rot smells and stops when the rot leaves (a storage box of rot never smells); a kill's
loot bag smells while it holds meat and stops when emptied; a carcass node smells and an ordinary
tree does not; burning vegetation smokes and extinguishing clears it (a burning player gets no
emitter); a lit campfire smokes at strength 1 through its sibling and an unlit one reads 0; smell
through one wall is half the open-air value (0.375 vs 0.75 at 3 tiles). Revert check: 9 failed |
3 passed on reverted code — the 3 passing are the vacuous controls (below-threshold, player over
smell, calm daytime), which assert absence and hold without the feature.

**Honest cuts.** Zombies only in v1 — predators need a separate hook (animals have no Investigate
state). No death-spawned carcass node: the kill's loot bag is the fresh-kill source. A lit fired
piece that also catches fire smells twice as strong (the lit-fire sibling plus the burning-piece
emitter) — both are real smoke, so it is left as is. Newly rotted food starts smelling on the next
spoilage pass (<= 1 s later); losing rot stops the smell on the same pass. The smell radii and the
0.5 wall transmit are first-pass tuning, not play-tested — a lived-in world with many rot bags may
want the radii trimmed. No per-frame or per-tick cost: one spatial query per zombie think tick,
emitters maintained by the existing spoilage pass and the existing ignite/extinguish and
lit/unlit events.

## ADR-487: Fog that blinds (SurVivaZ)

Fog and blizzards cut sight. One multiplier in the existing sight check: `fogSightFactor(world)`
(`packages/gameplay/src/combat/zombies.ts`) reads `world.env(Weather).kind` — Fog 0.5, Blizzard 0.35,
anything else 1 — and `acquire()` multiplies the sight range by it (`def.sightRange * moon * fog *
crouchMul`). The tuning lives in `packages/gameplay/data/zombies.json` `ai.sightFogMul` (`{ "fog":
0.5, "blizzard": 0.35 }`, loaded into `AiTuning.sightFogMul` in `packages/gameplay/src/defs.ts`).
Animals get the same treatment in `packages/gameplay/src/population.ts`: `animalAISystem` hoists the
factor once per run and applies it to the aggro range and the flee range in the `wants` / flee
branches; the threat-scan radius itself is unchanged, so nothing re-scans — the fog only shrinks
what counts as seen.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr487_fog_blinds.test.ts` 10/10: the tuning values; the
factor by weather (Fog 0.5, Blizzard 0.35, Clear 1); a walker at 7 tiles acquires in clear weather
and does not in fog (sight 10 × 0.5 = 5); a wolf at 2 tiles acquires in clear weather at night and
does not in fog (aggro 2.5 × 0.5 = 1.25); a deer still flees from a player at 5 tiles in fog
(fleeRange 12 × 0.5 = 6). Revert check: 4 failed | 6 passed on reverted code — the 6 passing are
the non-fog controls (clear-weather acquire, the factor itself, the below-range cases), which hold
without the feature.

**Honest cuts.** `provoker()` is not fogged — a zombie that already saw you keeps coming; the fog
only stops new acquisitions. Blizzard is weight 0 outside winter, so the blizzard multiplier is
winter-only in practice. The wolf tests set night explicitly (`setTimeOfDay(w, 0, 0)`): ADR-495's
activity window makes wolves 0.4× in the daytime, which would have masked the fog effect in the
clear-weather control.

## ADR-488: Humidity that matters (SurVivaZ)

Damp air slows drying and speeds rot. `packages/gameplay/src/systems/environment.ts` gains
`ambientHumidity(world, x, y)` (the `ClimateRes` humidity at the tile, or the 0.5 band default with
no climate), `humidityDryMul(h) = max(0.25, 1 - h)` (drying never stalls completely — the floor
matters: at humidity 1.0 clothes still dry at a quarter rate), and `humiditySpoilMul(h) = 1 + h`
(rot up to twice as fast in saturated air). The exposure pass samples `climateAt` once per occupant
per pass and shares that sample between the drying branch (rate × `humidityDryMul`) and the ambient
line (which now reads `sample.temperature` instead of a per-entity `ambientTemperature` call —
exactly equivalent, one fewer lookup). The spoilage pass does the same: one `climateAt` sample per
holder, temperature from `surface0 ?? sample.temperature`, and the spoilage rate multiplied by
`humiditySpoilMul`. The two formulas are code constants (exported, tested), not `environment.json`
knobs — the scope's suggested defaults are formulas, not knob names.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr488_humidity.test.ts` 5/5: drying orders 0.35 < 0.5
(default) < 0.9 over 800 ticks at wetness 1.0, and the 1.0 floor dries exactly as slowly as 0.9;
spoilage in two identical storage boxes at humidity 0.9 vs 0.35 runs at the 1.9/1.35 ≈ 1.407 ratio
(asserted in [1.38, 1.43], the shared temperature cancelling); a world with no ClimateRes behaves
exactly as before (the 0.5 default). Revert check: 4 failed | 1 passed on reverted code — the
passing one is the no-ClimateRes control, which legitimately passes without the feature. The floor
test was strengthened during the run to also assert 1.0 dries slower than the 0.5 default, since on
reverted code 1.0 == 0.9 == 0.5 vacuously.

**Honest cuts.** Clothes only in v1 — ground drying (`chunkSurfaceSystem`) is untouched. No Guide
line was added (the scope's likely files don't list `guide.json`; the player reads humidity through
wetness and freshness presentation). No new per-tick scan: one `climateAt` sample per occupant or
holder per pass, piggybacking on passes that already run.

## ADR-489: Swimming costs stamina, and deep water can drown you (SurVivaZ)

Swimming is work now. `packages/gameplay/data/vitals.json` gains `swimStaminaDrainPerSec: 4` and
`drownDps: 1.0` (inside the scope's 3–6/s and 0.5–1.0 HP/s bands; 4/s means a 20-tile crossing costs
80 stamina, and drowning runs at the starvation rate); `packages/gameplay/data/movement.json` gains
`exhaustedSwimMul: 0.5`. `packages/gameplay/src/systems/vitals.ts` `stepStamina` gains a `swimming`
parameter: while swimming it drains `swimStaminaDrainPerSec` when stamina is above zero, and — unlike
sprinting — it holds `staminaDelayTicks` even at zero stamina, so a swimmer cannot stop and regen
mid-lake (without that the swimmer would yo-yo: 1 s drowning, ~9 s regen, and almost never drown).
`vitalsSystem` hoists the terrain and shallow radius once per run, computes `swimming` per entity
with the exported `isSwimmingAt(world, x, y, z, terrain, shallowRadius)` (treading water counts;
frozen water reads as land), and the damage section adds `hurt(vt.drownDps * dt,
DamageCause.Drowning)` when swimming with stamina at zero (`DamageCause.Drowning = 14`,
append-only, in `packages/gameplay/src/components.ts`). `predictOwnStamina` shares the same
prediction. The crawl is the second touchpoint: `applyMovementInput` multiplies swim speed by
`exhaustedSwimMul(world, e)` (gated on the stamina read first, so it costs nothing for a fresh
swimmer), and the mount path is deliberately untouched — a rider at zero stamina does not slow
their horse. A Guide line in the seasons-weather section says it plainly.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr489_swimming.test.ts` 8/8: deep water drains 4/s
(100 → ~96 in 20 ticks) while shallow water and land cost nothing; stamina hits 0 and stays 0 over
100 ticks with HP dropping; an exhausted swimmer drowns at 1 HP/s with `lastDamageCause ===
Drowning`; a 5 HP swimmer dies with `Dead.cause === Drowning`; the crawl ratio is ≈ 0.5; a bot
drains (bots spawn via `spawnPlayer` + `setAiHumanPredicate`, so they flow through `vitalsSystem`).
Revert check: 8/8 fail on pre-change code.

**Honest cuts.** The scope allowed gating on `AnimState.Swim`, but that gate was rejected:
`spawnPlayer` never adds `AnimState` — it is added lazily by stance changes, one-shot anims, or
other spawns — so a plain walking player may have no `AnimState` server-side and the gate would
silently never fire. The hoisted-terrain check is used instead. Frozen-water safety is by
construction via `waterDepth` (ADR-450) and was not re-tested.

## ADR-490: Rivers push you downstream (SurVivaZ)

Forced rivers have a current. `packages/gameplay/src/river_current.ts` (new) resolves the river
layout for a position — region-aware, cached in a `WeakMap<World, Map<string, WaterFeatureLayout>>`
(cap 16, the generator's own cap): region size 1536, half 768, feature scale 3 outside region zero,
`fnv1a("rx,ry", seed)`. `riverCurrentAt(world, x, y)` returns the unit downstream direction, or
`undefined` when the floored tile is not a forced river tile; the direction comes from the meander
derivative at the entity's continuous region-local `u` (smooth, no tile-step jumps), +u downstream
by convention. The river math is taken from `packages/world/src/waterFeatures.ts` (`riverLocal`:
`u = tx·cos(angle) + ty·sin(angle)`, `v = −tx·sin(angle) + ty·cos(angle) − offset`, meander
`amp·sin(u/period + phase)`; amp (6 + hash·8)·scale, period (18 + hash·14)·scale, halfLen
(70 + floor(hash·30))·scale, width 1.15–1.7 not scaled, offset ±12·scale). The knob is
`riverCurrentTilesPerSec: 0.3` in `movement.json` — a swimmer swims ~1.45 tiles/s, so 0.3 is
noticeable but fightable, and a boat feels a gentle push. The swimmer hook sits in
`applyMovementInput` as a separate step (it must also apply to an idle swimmer treading water in a
river): inside the moving block and in the idle path, gated on level 0 (ground only) + actually on
a water tile at any depth (`waterDepth !== None` — frozen water reads as land) + a defined current,
applied per axis through `bodyAxisMove` (blocking-aware); dead entities do not drift. The boat hook
sits in `vehicles.ts` `stepPowered` beside the wind drift, so the `boatPoseBlocked` per-axis slide
beaches or slides the boat instead of letting the current push it onto land; it is gated on boat
and not-sailboat (the sailboat is wind-only), and a parked boat gets no current — the same as wind
drift, deliberately.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr490_river_current.test.ts` 8/8: the tuning value; the
unit direction matches the independently-computed meander derivative (dot with the base angle >
0.78, inside the ~38° meander swing), deterministic, undefined on land and on a lake tile; a river
in region (1,0) is found (the default-layout call returns "none" there — the scope's central trap);
an idle swimmer drifts ~0.3 tiles in 1 s; a steering swimmer's downstream + upstream
along-displacements sum to ~0.6 (2 × 0.3 — a sum, not a difference, which the first version got
wrong); land does not drift; a paddle boat underway drifts downstream vs the same boat on a control
lake, a sailboat does not, and a parked boat does not. Revert check: 8/8 fail on pre-change code.

**Honest cuts.** Forced rivers only. The elevated-lake precedence uses the hash disc, while the
generated world's lake may be relocated ±20 tiles — a river tile under a relocated lake's hash disc
reads as lake, not river. Animals and zombies do not drift (they are not moved by
`applyMovementInput`); mounts and riders do not drift (the Driver / Riding branches return early).
The helper is gameplay-side with its own `WeakMap` cache, not a world-side helper (a world-side
helper would need `REGION_SIZE` from `generator.ts` — a cycle) and not `travel.ts`'s generator (the
siting / bands ambiguity). Deterministic: a pure function of (seed, position), no RNG, no new
replicated state. One test assertion was vacuous in the first version (the lake field is `{x, y,
r}`, not `{cx, cy}`) and was fixed to use `.x` / `.y`.

## ADR-491: Wild food follows the seasons (SurVivaZ)

Wild fruit, mushrooms and herbs yield nothing on the last day of fall and all winter. `YieldDef`
gains a required `seasonal: boolean` (`packages/gameplay/src/defs.ts`); `resources.json` flags 31
yields `seasonal: true` across 19 lines — berry_bush mushroom / berry_seeds; blueberry, raspberry,
blackberry and strawberry bushes fruit + seeds; apple, pear, cherry, orange and peach trees fruit
only; tree apple only; wild_mushroom mushroom / mushroom_spores; herb_patch herbs / mushroom /
wild_onion / herbs_seeds; wild_yarrow, wild_ginseng and wild_aloe plus their seeds; rotten_stump,
mossy_log and fallen_log mushroom. Not flagged: plain `berries` (dye → the Claim Flag chain —
zeroing them all winter would starve bot bootstrap), wood / sticks / fiber, fruit-tree saplings
(planting stock), all wild food-crop nodes and wild_garden (seed source), any `crop_*` node.
`gathering.ts` reads `isCropDormant(world)` once per gather action and, in the yield roll, skips a
seasonal yield while dormant (`if (dormant && y.seasonal) return;` — after the bare-hands check,
before the chance roll). Mushrooms flush while it rains: +1 mushroom per successful mushroom roll
while raining. A Guide line in the seasons-weather section says it plainly, including the berries
exception.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr491_seasonal_food.test.ts` 8/8: the flag table (berry
bush mushroom seasonal, plain berries not; apple_tree fruit seasonal, sticks and saplings not);
berry_bush yields nothing in Winter and on the last day of Fall, and yields again in Spring; the
mushroom rain bonus (+1 while raining). Revert check: 8/8 fail on pre-change code.

**Honest cuts.** In Winter the gate's distinct effect is only on frost-proof berry bushes: frost
already kills frost-susceptible wild nodes first (`CROP_EVERY` is 20 ticks, so the frost kill pass
runs inside any multi-step test; Winter's temperature range is always below the 40°F frost kill),
so for frost-susceptible nodes (wild_mushroom, apple_tree, wild_potato) the gate bites on the last
day of Fall on a mild day. `wild_onion` from `herb_patch` is seasonal but from `wild_garden` is
not — per-yield precision, not per-item. The mushroom bonus is while-raining only: no recent-rain
state exists, and none was added (no `lastRainEndTick`). Test-ordering traps found and recorded:
`setTimeOfDay` must run before `setSeason` (setSeason compensates for the current day), and rain on
world day 0 re-rolls at once (the first-day no-rain rule) — the test's `setWeather` helper sets noon
on day 1 first.

## ADR-492: Bleeding wounds (SurVivaZ)

A heavy hit can leave you bleeding, and it will not stop on its own. `diseases.json` gains a
`bleeding` entry (`hpDps: 0.4`, `durationSeconds: 0`, cure `medicated_bandage`, `moveMul: 1`, color
`#A93226`) and a top-level `"bleed": { "chance": 0.25, "minDamage": 15 }` object. The roll sits in
`applyDamage` (`packages/gameplay/src/combat/combat.ts`, after the hp write and the `Damaged` emit,
on the post-armor, post-block, post-share amount): only when the target survives the hit, has
Survival, the cause is Combat / Contact / Fall, the amount is at least 15, and
`world.rngFor("disease.bleed", target).next() < 0.25` does it call `contractDisease(world, target,
"bleeding")`. `applyDamage` gains an optional 7th parameter `nested = false`, passed as `true` by
the mount-share recursion so a rider hit does not roll once for the mount and once for the rider.
A plain bandage staunches it for a minute; a medicated bandage cures it outright: `cureDiseasesForItem`
(`packages/gameplay/src/diseases.ts`) gains `treatBleeding` / `isBleedingStaunched` with
`BANDAGE_BLEED_STAUNCH_SECONDS = 60`. The staunch reuses the disease's `untilTick` field as a
"staunched until" tick — bleeding has duration 0, so its `untilTick` is normally 0 (no auto-expiry);
the drain pauses for 60 s, it does not cure. The expiry loop in
`packages/gameplay/src/systems/diseases.ts` special-cases bleeding: when the staunch tick passes
it clears `untilTick` only and resumes the drain instead of expiring the disease, and the
symptom-drain loop zeroes bleeding `hpDps` while staunched. `medicated_bandage` in `items.json`
now cures `["wound_infection", "bleeding"]`. The Guide gets a cure fact item and a text line; there
is deliberately no duration Guide line for bleeding — `formatDuration(0)` would render "0 s" and
wrongly tell players bleeding lasts 0 seconds (the exhaustion precedent: cure line only for
duration-0 diseases).

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr492_bleeding.test.ts` 10/10: the tuning values and the
loader (chance, minDamage, the medicated cure); a 20-damage hit bleeds at ~25% (statistical, 200
hits); a 10-damage hit never bleeds; a light hit, starvation and fire never bleed; zombies cannot
bleed (no Survival); the drain is 0.4 HP/s while bleeding and 0 while staunched; a plain bandage
pauses the drain for 60 s and it resumes after; a medicated bandage cures; the Guide carries the
cure line and no duration line. Revert check: 7 failed | 3 passed on reverted code — the 3 passing
are the vacuous guard tests (light hits, starvation/fire, zombies can't bleed), which assert absence
and hold without the feature.

**Honest cuts.** Two loader corrections the scope missed. First, `defs.ts` validated `diseases.length
≤ 8` ("need 1..8 diseases (Diseases component width)") — a 9th kind did not fit as written. The
component stores `idx + 1` in a u8 slot, so the encoding supports up to 255 kinds; only the
concurrent-slots cap (8) is real. Validation is widened to 1..16 with that rationale. Second, the
`causes` validator requires every causes entry to be in [0, 1], so `bleedMinDamage: 15` could not
live in `causes` — both bleed knobs moved to the new top-level `bleed` object in `diseases.json`.
The `nested` parameter is defense-in-depth: the Survival guard is what observably prevents mount
bleeding (mounts have no Survival), and no separate mount test was written.

## ADR-493: Fishing from shore and boat (SurVivaZ)

Fish with a rod: stand by the water, face it, and use the rod — the line stays in while you hold
on. The rod is a new item (`fishing_rod`, tool kind `Fishing = 6` append-only in `ToolKind`,
`packages/gameplay/src/defs.ts`; hand-crafted from 2 wood + 1 rope in 2 s, station none; item id
527, recipe id 409 in `ids.lock.json`; durability 150). The cast is tap-to-cast, not hold-to-fish:
`clearIntentsSystem` wipes `PlayerIntent.action` every tick, and the held Gather bit is re-derived
into a Gather intent per tick only in the server's `applyInput` (nodes / loot bags only, no water
knowledge) — so a one-shot Fish command cannot sustain a cast through the intent. One Fish command
(`gameplay.fish`, `IntentAction.Fish = 34`, `packages/gameplay/src/input.ts`) starts the cast; the
cast then holds as `Fishing` state (`{ waitUntilTick, castX, castY }`, transient — server and
predicting client derive it from the same Fish intent and the deterministic per-entity `"fishing"`
rng stream, neither networked nor persistent) while the fisher stands still facing the same water
tile, and reels in when they move, turn, or switch the held item. The bite auto-reels in v1 — no
timing minigame, no new UI. `fishingSystem` (`packages/gameplay/src/systems/fishing.ts`,
registered in the `sys` map and the phase list right after `gameplay.gather` and before
`clearIntents`, so the Fish intent is visible this tick) pays 2 stamina per cast, waits 4–8 s
(`biteDelaySeconds`, × 0.75 at dawn/dusk), then rolls the bite (`biteChance` 0.7 + 0.15 dawn/dusk +
0.1 rain + 0.1 deep water, capped at 1) and the count (1–2 fish, +1 in deep water — the count is
rolled on both peers even on a miss, so the rng streams never diverge; only the authority adds the
fish via `addItem`, emitting `InventoryOverflow` with the lost count when the bag is full). No
`ItemGathered` emit: that event names a ResourceNode (the progression handler reads its kind for
the XP source), and fishing has no node — fishing awards no XP in v1, and the inventory change is
replicated so the catch is visible; a "fish" XP source is a follow-up. The cast point is the tile in front (`plantSpot`); depth comes from `waterDepth` (frozen
water reads as land). The prompt is a `farmPrompt` branch (`Fish`, before the Drink branch — a
rod-holder by the water wants to fish, not drink) that fires only when the exact cast point is
water, and the client `use` handler sends `FishCmd` for it (`apps/client/src/main.ts`). Tuning lives
in `packages/gameplay/data/fishing.json`. A Guide line in the cooking section says it plainly.
The rod art is painted at runtime (`apps/client/src/fishing-rod-art.ts`): a 128×128 icon (diagonal
rod, cork grip, metal reel, hanging line and hook, in the wetwood bark / cut wood / dark metal /
pale line ramps) installed into `ICON_DATA` as `fishing_rod.png`, and a 48×48 × 8-facing held sprite
(the rod held at its butt, angling up-forward along the facing direction, grip anchor (-3, -5) like
the axe) in its own atlas `held_fishing_rod` — the `held` atlas is full (120/120 frames), so the rod
could not go there; `emitHeld` resolves the sprite's own atlas, so that is all it needs. The
fragment (`packages/assets/pack/task493/manifest.task493.json`) carries layout only, registered in
`manifest-index.ts` and the vite allow-list like the footprints / track fragments.

**Verification.** Gameplay 8/8 (`packages/gameplay/test/adr493_fishing.test.ts`): the tuning values,
the rod item and recipe, `FishCmd` in `GAMEPLAY_COMMANDS`, the lock ids; the prompt offers Fish with
a rod facing water and not without a rod or facing land; one Fish command casts, holds without
further intents, and lands fish; no rod / no water means no cast; moving, turning, or switching the
rod reels in; an exhausted fisher (stamina 0) cannot cast; deep water yields more than shallow over
1,200 ticks; a boat driver casts like a shore fisher (a bare `Driver` component — the Driver branch
never touches `PlayerIntent.action`, and `gatherSystem` does not check Driver, so driver-gather was
verified by reading and by test). Client 5/5 (`apps/client/test/adr493_fishing_rod.test.ts`): the
icon paint (diagonal, bark ramp, reads at 24 px), the 8 held frames, the fragment keys / layout /
grip anchors, `rodAtlasSources()` no-op without a canvas, `installFishingRodIcon()` a safe no-op
without a canvas. Revert check: both files fail to collect on reverted code (the gameplay file at
`loadDefs` reading `biteChance` — the reverted `data.ts` no longer passes `fishing`; the client
file at the missing `fishing-rod-art.js`). The revert stashed the code, item, recipe, lock, Guide
and art, but not `defs.ts` — stashing it would break the loader on the ADR-492 diseases data (the
9th disease exceeds the base ≤8 cap); the fishing tuning is inert without the code.

**Honest cuts.** Stamina 2/cast is flavour, not an AFK bound (regen is 15/s): an AFK fisher lands
1–2 raw fish per 4–8 s, slower than gathering a shoal (1–2 per 1.5 s cooldown), so fishing is never
the best way to get fish. The rod's durability 150 is inert in v1 — fishing never wears it (no
`wearDurability` call); that is a follow-up. Touch boat-fishing is blocked in v1: the farm prompt
is hidden while driving, so the touch Use button does not show on a boat — keyboard and gamepad
reach it through QuickUse, which fires the prompt even while driving; showing the prompt while
driving when the action is Fish (or a vehicle-controls fishing button) is the follow-up. The held
rod has no isolated draw test (no harness reaches `emitHeld` in isolation) — Tracey's eyes on the
live build are the check, the same honest cut as the ADR-485 / ADR-496 view multiplies. The fixed
seed's first bite draws miss, so the cast test needs 800 ticks (not 400) to land a fish.

## ADR-494: Wolves hunt in packs (SurVivaZ)

A wolf that sees a packmate hunting joins the hunt. `ArchetypeBehavior` gains `pack?: boolean`
(`packages/gameplay/src/ai/population.ts`); only `animal_wolf` has `"pack": true` in `ai.json` —
the wolf is the only hostile species (the bear is territorial and solitary; dogs are
defensive / tameable-adjacent). `packShareTarget(world, self, kind, tx, ty, radius, animals)`
(`packages/gameplay/src/population.ts`, exported) scans the already-built live list (`cache.live`,
passed in) with store-direct reads and a squared-distance early-out; the radius is measured from
the sharing wolf to the packmate's goal (the prey's position), not to the packmate. The share sits
in the think branch, before the drink / wander logic: `if (def.pack && !tame && !wants && state !==
AnimalState.Flee)` — on a real think tick it scans with radius `def.aggro.leashRange` (7); on a hit
it sets `state = Attack`, `gx` / `gy` to the mate's goal, `thinkAt` to tick + 2–6 s, and `shared =
true`. Between thinks an Attack wolf sets `shared = true` with no re-scan (keep-alive), and the
drink block is gated on `!shared` and the wander block on `!shared && !decided`.

**Verification.** `packages/gameplay/test/adr494_pack_hunt.test.ts` 6/6: the table (wolf pack true,
only wolf, non-boolean pack errors); the `packShareTarget` unit (no mate → undefined; a mate
attacking with prey 6 away → the goal; prey 12 away → undefined; an idle mate → undefined; the self
excluded; an attacking bear → undefined — kind mismatch); the full loop (player at (400, 0), wolf A
at (401, 0), wolf B at (406, 0): B shares, state Attack, within 2 tiles after 60 steps); the
control (B at (410, 0), prey 10 > 7: not Attack, still > 2.5 away after 60 steps); own-target (two
players: B attacks the nearer one, goalX not the first player's); the bear control (a bear at 6
tiles stays out). Revert check: 3 failed | 3 passed — the 3 passing are the controls (out-of-range,
own-target, bear), which assert no-share behaviours that hold with and without the feature.

**Honest cuts.** The keep-alive is a deliberate deviation from the scope's letter: the think
branch runs every tick for Attack wolves, so without it the share would die after one tick and the
joining wolf would re-roll drink / wander on the next tick. The next think re-validates, and a wolf
whose pack stopped hunting falls through to drink / wander and gives up; a wolf in Attack with no
threat keeps pressing toward its last goal for at most one think interval (≤ 6 s) — bounded,
wolf-only, arguably natural. Target-less means `!wants`, not `threat === undefined`: a wolf 6 tiles
from the player has a scanned threat (scan radius 8) but no engagement, so the `threat ===
undefined` form would never fire. A biting wolf's goal is its own position, so a shared goal is at
